More options include a rear-seat audio system, traction control, parking sensors, side-curtain airbags, a tyre-pressure warning system, electronically adjustable pedals and a rear-seat DVD entertainment. Chrysler minivans, in various shapes and names, are best sellers in the United States, but failed to make any headway in this region because minivans are not popular here.

The Korean-built Chevrolet Cruze gets a minor facelift for the 2013 model and was available for the first time in hatchback form. The front-wheel-drive compact features a 1.8-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic, with an independent front and solid-axle rear suspension setup. There are three trim levels. The interior has an attractive "dual-cockpit" design, with seam-stitching colour-matched to the instrument panel, MP3/CD radio with USB port and MP3 jack, optional CD changer, manual or automatic a/c, optional cruise control, optional split-folding rear seat, power windows, keyless entry and optional keyless start. Depending on trim, the Cruze can be had with optional fog lamps, optional sunroof, optional parking sensors and electric mirrors. The basic LS model gets rear drum brakes and 15-inch steel wheels. The higher LT models get four-wheel-disc brakes and either 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels. ABS and dual front airbags are standard, while side airbags are available.

Yet another entry into Daihatsu's sub-compact range, this one is a unique little number. Daihatsu advertising is so poor in this region that we only came across this specialty machine by mistake. Some prefer to call it a mini MPV, but it is really a hatchback. The little boxy car offers oodles of space thanks to the tall shape and long wheelbase. It is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, with a choice of a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic. The rear doors open wide to allow easy entry and exit, and the rear seat can be optioned to slide front and back. Luggage capacity is hihgly flexible, with folding front seats and split-folding rear seats, while pockets are all over the place. This Toyota-derived vehicle has its annoying gauge cluster in the centre, and the interior treatment is all hard plastic, except for interesting touches such as illuminated speakers and handles. Other available features include with a CD/AM/FM radio, power windows, remote central locking, ABS brakes and at least dual front airbags if not more.

The C4 Picasso is a modern replacement for the oddball Xsara Picasso. Based on the C4 compact platform, it is a tall stylish minivan-type vehicle that drives like a car and has the practicality of a big 4WD. It seats only five, and the larger seven-seater Grand Picasso is not offered here. When all five seats are up, has 500 litres of boot space underneath the luggage cover, extending to a maximum 1,734 litres once the rear seats are folded down. Only two 4-cylinder engines are offered, one a 1.8-litre and one a 2.0-litre, with a choice of manual or automatic gearboxes that vary by model. According to trim level, the metal suspension can be replaced with pneumatic suspension on the rear axle on 2.0-litre models. CitroÃ«n has paid close attention to achieving the best levels of acoustic comfort and vibration control, as well as a new air-conditioning system. Its cloth-lined cabin can be outfitted with a variety of options, such as a panoramic glass roof, high-quality stereo system and folding video screens in the back of the front seats. The C4 Picasso has four Isofix seat tethers, audible seatbelt warnings for all seats and seven airbags as standard. Automatic electronic parking brake and Hill Start Assist are also fitted as standard.

Mercedes-Benz GLC replaced the GLK and also added a Coupe model in 2017. Under the hood, the GLC 43 AMG Coupe sports a twin-turbocharged 3.0-litre V6 engine, mated to the 4Matic all-wheel-drive system. Power is delivered via a 9-speed automatic transmission. In 2020, the GLC got a slight facelift and more power. Features include AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The XJ remains the luxury flagship of the Jaguar range. It is a truly handsome large car, with elegant lines rather than the random curves of its German rivals. The XJ-Series comes in regular and long-wheelbase versions, depending on model. While the sportier option would be the standard-wheelbase models, the long-wheelbase models offer enough rear-seat room to recline and watch a movie while having lunch on a tray. The Jaguar XJ8 was launched as an all-new model for 2003, along with the high-performance XJR, offering superior ride and handling to their predecessors thanks to their rigid lightweight aluminium structure and computer-controlled suspension. Other model variations include the XJ6, the XJ8 Sovereign and the Super V8. Engines include the 3.0-litre V6, the 3.6-litre V6, the 4.2-litre V8 and the supercharged 4.2-litre V8, all mated to a six-speed automatic. Standard are leather upholstery, power-adjustable front seats, dual-zone climate control, alloy wheels, and an eight-speaker stereo with CD player.Available features include self-leveling air suspension, adaptive suspension damping, dynamic stability control, xenon headlamps, navigation, power-adjustable foot pedals, an electronic parking brake, and reverse park assist.  Safety features standard on all models include frontal, side-impact and side-curtain airbags, ABS brakes and electronic stability control. The cars were facelifted in 2007 with a mildly-new front end.

An all-new generation Volvo XC90 debuted in the middle of 2015. Under the hood, there are two 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine options, the base engine being the turbocharged T5 unit, while the more powerful model gets a turbocharged and supercharged T6 motor. Both engines are mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The base engine is called the T5 and and the more powerful motor is known as the T6. Introduced in 2019, was the the hybrid model called the T8, which combines the T6 unit with an electric motor. Available features, depending on trim, include integrated rear-door sunshades, illuminated front and rear treadplates, Bowers & Wilkins Premium 19-speaker audio system with USB/AUX inputs and CD player, Bluetooth, heads-up display, navigation, in-car wifi, 4-zone auto a/c with numerous rear vents, power-adjustable front seats, panoramic glass roof, power tailgate with foot-waving opening operation, front and rear parking sensors, smart keyless entry and start, turning LED headlights and foglights, and auto-dimming mirrors. Safety features include City Safety which brakes automatically if a pedestrian runs across the road, driver-alertness detection, blind-spot monitoring with cross-traffic alert, land-departure warning, road-sign detection that displays speed limits on the graphical LCD gauge cluster, whiplash protection, front and side/curtain airbags, and adaptive cruise control that can come to a complete stop and crawl in traffic automatically. Further safety features include a run-off road protection package, which detects what is happening and the front safety belts are tightened to keep the occupants in position, and auto brake at intersection capability.

The Zotye T600 is the Chinese brand's compact SUV offering. Looking a lot like a Volkswagen Tiguan due to the loose copyright laws in China, the T600 features a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard features on the T600 include, standard or optional, include power steering, power windows, central locking, keyless entry, touch screen, multi-functional steering wheel, leather seats, sunroof, automatic A/C and alloy wheels. Safety features include airbags, ABS, brake assist, stability control and traction control.

The Fiat Fiorino is a compact commercial vehicle offering by the Italian brand. The Turkish-built Fiorino comes with a turbocharged 1.4-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed manual. Standard features include power steering, sliding side door, foldable passenger seat, adjustable driver's seat, heat reflecting windows, radio with CD/MP3 player, and ABS. It has 2.8 cubic-metre volume of cargo space with a 600 kg payload capacity.

An all-new model of Chevrolet Traverse came out in 2018. Under the hood, the same 3.6-litre V6 engine is carried over but tweaked with more power and mated to a new 9-speed automatic transmission. The model can be had in either front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. Standard trim available is the "LS", which comes with  black body side moldings, LED daytime running lights, HID headlamps, body color door handles, black rocker moldings, 18-inch aluminum wheels, solar-absorbing glass, LED tail lamps, rear view camera, switchable AWD selector, tri-zone automatic air conditioning, Chevrolet MyLink infotainment system with 7-inch diagonal color touch-screen, keyless entry and push button start. The "LT" trim gets additional front fog lamps, driver seat power lumbar support, multi-directional power driver seat adjuster, leather-wrapped steering wheel, rear park assist, optional side blind zone alert and optional rear cross traffic alert. The "LT leather" adds standard side blind zone alert, rear cross traffic alert, surround vision camera, Bose 10-speaker system, 6-way power front passenger seat adjuster, auto-dimming rearview mirror with wide angle camera modeChevrolet MyLink audio system with 8-inch diagonal color touch-screen with navigation, heated driver and front passenger seats, available 20-inch aluminum wheels and power liftgate. The "LT Premier" option adds D-optic LED headlamps, Intellibeam headlamps, panoramic power sunroof, 20-inch aluminium wheels, power tilt and telescopic steering column, ventilated driver and front passenger seats, driver seat memory settings, heated rear seats, low speed front automatic braking, front pedestrian detection, lane keep assist with lane departure warning, and following distance indicator. The top "High Country" trim adds full speed front automatic braking, twin-clutch AWD, automatic rear locking differential, inductive wireless charging, power folding third row 60/40 split-bench seat, adaptive cruise control with Stop/Go technology and 20-inch aluminium wheels.

The Navigator is the Lincoln-badged luxury version of the Ford Expedition, a full-size 4WD known to be smooth, stable and refined for the most part. Mildly facelifted for 2005, its four-wheel-independent suspension is sophisticated, providing better on-road ride and handling, while low-range gearing is available for off-roading. The standard engine for 2005 onwards was a revised 5.4-litre V8 engine mated to a 6-speed automatic gearbox. What the Navigator does best is move large quantities of people and gear, with its perfectly flat cargo area and third-row seat, with the ability to carry up to eight passengers. The interior was different from its Ford cousin, with faux satin-nickel trim and real wood inserts. Other features include 18-inch wheels, optional power-folding running boards, power liftgate, leather seats and wood trim. Options included a voice-activated touchscreen navigation system, THX audio system, rear-seat DVD player, and HID headlights. Multiple airbags, a tyre-pressure monitor and stability control were standard, with Roll Stability Control an option.

The Passat attempted to reinvent itself back in 2006 with a list of weak base engines. It entered 2008 with a new list of engine choices, and some carrying over, although the latest model still looks the same as the all-new Passat that debuted in 2006. A wagon called the Passat Variant has also joined the lineup. The Passat boasts generous standard content and a high-quality interior mixed with high-tech hijinks. Volkswagen has rolled out a full line of four-door sedans, ranging from  1.8-litre and 2.0-litre 4-cylinder motors, both turbocharged, to the 3.2-litre and 3.6 V6 models, the latter of which is for the body-kitted R36 model. All basic cars are front-wheel-drive, while V6 models get 4Motion all-wheel-drive. V6 models also get a dual-clutch DSG automanual gearbox, while the base cars get standard manuals and autos. All Passats come standard with the latest in safety features and electronics, including power features, front and side airbags, ABS brakes, ESP, tyre-pressure monitoring system and MP3-capable CD player. R-Line package is largely just an expensive bodykit.

The A8 is the most imposing of the Audi range. Most noticeable is the big single-frame grille on all models. Engines available in front-wheel-drive form include the 2.8-litre V6 and the 3.2-litre V6 in this region, while all-wheel-drive Quattro offerings include the 4.2-litre V8, although some dealers do offer the 6.0-litre V12 too. All these models are sold here only in long wheelbase form, but there is also a sweet short-wheelbase S8 model, again only from some dealers, that is powered by a Lamborghini-sourced 5.2-litre V10. Basic features on A8 models include a parking system with graphic display, adaptive front lighting, new 18-inch wheel designs, optional 19-inch performance tyres with the Sport Package, a revamped Driver Information Centre; a glove box lock and a leather interior. The 4.2-litre, 6.0-litre and 5.2-litre models all use Audi's Quattro all-wheel-drive. The A8 uses an all-aluminium frame with a fully pneumatic suspension system. Its aluminium four-link front axle and trapezoidal-link rear axle suspension has air spring struts at each wheel, with sensors that continually monitor and adjust the damping, and automatically level the car. The 3.2-litre uses a CVT automatic transmission, while the rest of the models use a six-speed Tiptronic automatic transmission with manual mode and available wheel-mounted paddles. Audi's Multi Media Interface control system can be used to monitor or control such things as the radio, phone, climate control, stereo or lighting profiles of the LED illumination in the door trim and foot wells. The Quattro models are at least a step in the right direction in combating its German brethren.

The Nissan Sentra remains the same for the 2017 model year, since its introduction in 2013 . It gets a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed manual transmission or a CVT. The 1.8-litre 4-cylinder engine is available in only CVT. Both engines are not available in all GCC countries. The 1.6S and 1.8S gets power steering, power mirrors, power windows, halogen headlamps, rear LED lamps, keyless entry, manual seats, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3/AUX/RDS support and 2 speakers and 15-inch steel wheels. The 1.6SV gets LED accent headlamps, intelligent key with engine push-start button, wood trim and 4 speakers. The 1.6 SV Sports gets fog lamps, leather steering, rear spoiler, 16-inch alloy wheels, rear parking sensors and indicators on side-view mirror.  Both 1.6 SV and 1.8 SV sports have the option of USB/iPod connectivity, bluetooth, navigation, 5.8-inch display, rear view camera and 2 DIN face audio system with CD player. The 1.8 SV gets the same as S but with rear parking sensors and bluetooth. The 1.8 SL gets the same options as 1.6 SV Sports plus rear spoiler with brake lamp, 6 speakers and USB/iPod connectivity. The 1.8 SL Premium gets more features such as leather seats, sunroof, cruise control, dual-zone climate control A/C. The 1.8 SL and SL Premium have the option of adding navigation, 5.8-inch display, rear view camera and 2 DIN face audio system with CD player. Safety features include electronic brake-force distribution (EBD), ABS and Brake Assist (BA), along with driver and passenger front airbags. Only the 1.8 SL Premium gets side and curtain airbags.

Continuing to be based on a joint platform with Mazda, the Focus remains one of the best handling cars in its class, getting a  makeover for the 2008 model year. It comes in two different body styles, namely a sedan and a five-door hatchback. The Focus is a popular car in Europe where it is built, and is fairly well-built at that. Both the versions cost the same, but all are available in various trim levels. The standard motor is an anaemic 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, while the top engine is a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder. Features include electro-hydraulic power steering, and choice of a 5-speed manual transmission and a 4-speed automatic. Standard conveniences include power windows, basic stereo, cloth seating and not much else. Options include LED tail-lights, CD changer, USB audio connector, keyless starter button, Xenon adaptive headlights, tyre pressure monitor, sunroof, fog lights and a 230-volt inverter. Safety features include optional side thorax airbags and inflatable side curtains alongside the standard dual front airbags.

The Peugeot 308 received a facelift in 2012. The same 1.6-litre 4-cylinder and turbocharged 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engines carried over from the previous shape. However, the turbocharged version gets a power boost. From 2012, they get a new 6-speed automatic transmission. Even the most basic model gets driver & passenger airbags, ABS brakes with EBD, trip computer, AM/FM Radio with CD/MP3 player with remote stalk, speed-sensitive power steering, electric windows and mirrors, cooling vent inside the glove compartment, height-adjustable headlights, split-folding rear seats, remote key with central locking, and 15-inch wheels. Moving up to the higher trim levels adds items such as side-curtain airbags, stability control, navigation system, dual-zone automatic a/c with rear vents, CD/MP3 player with bluetooth and AUX input, 5-CD changer, panoramic sunroof with automatic curtain, cruise control, automatic headlights, rain-sensing wipers, leather seats with chrome interior trim, auto-dimming mirror, foldable door mirrors, fog lights, parking sensors, front and rear armrests,  16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and automatic tyre pressure sensors. Inside and out, it is a classy hatchback for its category, making it almost as good as any of the premium-branded compacts.

An all-new Audi S3 sedan came out in 2021 is the performance version of the A3. It comes with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic gearbox. All-wheel drive is standard in the S3. Standard equipment include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, daytime running headlamps, start-stop system, central locking, cruise control, 10.25-inch digital dispaly, LED headlamps, leather seats, automatic A/C, sports seats, headlight washers, sports suspension, fog lights and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment include the 12.3-inch virtual cockpit, LED matrix headlamps, 10.1-inch touch screen in the centre console and 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include electronic stability control, ABS with EBD as well as front and side airbags with knee airbags.

The Toyota Prius was the world's first mass-produced hybrid vehicle when initially launched in 1997. The 2016 Prius retains the 2,700mm wheelbase of the previous Prius, but is 60mm longer overall at 4,540mm, 15mm wider at 1,760mm and 20mm lower. That's about the size of a Corolla. The Prius retains its 1.8-litre VVT-i Atkinson-cycle petrol engine. Features include a heads-up display, wireless charging, 7 airbags, blind-spot monitor and rear cross-traffic alert, ESP and regenerative braking.

The sub-compact Figo is Ford's newest and smallest offering in the GCC. Intended to be a cheaper motoring option than even the Fiesta, the Figo is built in India, based on a shortened older-generation Fiesta, and comes in 5-door hatchback form. It comes with a choice of 1.4-litre 4-cylinder with a manual gearbox and 1.6-litre 4-cylinder with an automatic. All cars get independent MacPherson strut front suspension and a semi-independent rear twist beam. The Figo is available in Ambiente and Trend trims, both getting cloth-upholstered interiors with features that include manual windows, power mirrors, 2-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with USB/AUX ports, power steering, fold-flat second-row seating, intermittent wipers, dual front airbags, soft-touch dashboard and a claimed "best-in-class" manual a/c. Also available on the higher model are 14-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, fog lamps, ABS brakes, front power windows and height-adjustable driver's seat.

An all-new Chevrolet Silverado was released as a 2014 model year. It received a facelift and new transmission for the 2017 model year. It remains the same for 2018. A Z71 package is available which includes stronger shocks, front tow hooks and extra under-body protection. The interior gets a 4.2-inch display on the dashboard. The Silverado pickups has 12-volt outlets, five USB ports and a SD-card slot. There is a 4.3-litre V6, 5.3-litre and 6.2-litre V8 motors. The V6 model gets a 6-speed auto, but the V8 models get a new 8-speed automatic transmission. For improving fuel economy, all engines have cylinder deactivation and direct injection.

The Toyota Land Cruiser Prado has been the same mechanically since 2010, getting few tweaks to the exterior, with the most significant facelift coming in 2018. There are two "VVT-i" engine choices for the Land Cruiser Prado - a 2.7-litre 4-cylinder and a 4.0-litre V6. In Saudi Arabia, additionally a 3.0-litre turbocharged diesel V6 engine on offer. The Land Cruiser Prado are proper off-road cars and all models offer standard all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing and available locking centre-differential. All petrol engines get a 6-speed automatic transmission whereas the diesel motor is mated to a 5-speed automatic. The basic Prado 2.7L, known as TX in KSA and EXR in UAE, comes with 17-inch alloy wheels, front LED fog lamps, black front grille, black power mirrors and door handles, rear spoiler, side steps, mud guards, fabric seating for seven, front and rear manual a/c, CD/MP3 6-speaker stereo,rear parking sensors, ABS with EBD and brake-assist, dual front airbags and floor-mounted spare tyre, a cool box, steering audio controls, USB/AUX ports and Bluetooth. The mid-range Prado 2.7L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, gets 18-inch alloy wheels, front parking sensors, body-coloured trim, leather steering wheel and shift lever, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cool box and more, dual-zone auto a/c, cruise control and rear view camera. The UAE also gets a Prado 2.7L in VXR trim that adds powered front seats, chrome front grille, silver roof rails, leather upholstery and navigation. The basic Prado 4.0L, known as EXR in UAE, comes with a 6-speaker stereo with Bluetooth and USB/AUX ports, steering audio controls, rear parking sensors, LED fog lamps, manual a/c, fabric seats, dual airbags, stability control, ABS, smart key with engine start/stop button, cruise control, side steps and hill start/descent assist. All UAE-bound V6 Prado models have a door-mounted spare tyre. The mid-range Prado 4.0L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, comes with roof rails, sunroof, front bumper guard and uphill/downhill assist on all automatic models. The TXL additionally gets a tow hitch and side mouldings, while the GXR instead gets side/curtain/knee airbags, dual-zone a/c, extra chrome trim, rear camera and navigation. A higher-spec Prado 4.0L trim, known as TXL2 in KSA and VXR in UAE, comes with sunroof, dual auto a/c, rear camera, navigation, auto-levelling LED headlights, sunshades, remote start, leather, front and rear parking sensors and power front seats. The Prado 4.0L in top Limited trim gains 18-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights with daytime running lamps, leather seats, power front seats with memory, front and rear parking sensors with rear camera, side/curtain/knee airbags, 14-speaker JBL stereo with voice control and steering-wheel buttons, multi-touch screen with navigation, remote engine starter, self-leveling KDSS suspension, power-folding third row, ventilated front seats, Multi-Terrain Select with four cameras, rear entertainment system, blind-spot monitor, crawl control and rear cross traffic alert.

The Odyssey is a best-seller in America, but has yet to make an impact in this region, where 4WDs rule. The Odyssey has a car-like ride and handling quality since it is based on the Accord. It is powered by the same fuel-efficient 3.5-litre V6 engine as the MR-V, mated to an automatic. The interior features a clever seating system that can accommodate up to eight passengers. The Odyssey comes standard with side curtain airbags, electronic stability control and ABS brakes, as well as power door locks with remote keyless entry, power windows, 60/40 split fold-down rear seats, power sliding doors, tri-zone climate control, a stowable second-row PlusOne seat, in-dash CD changer, steering wheel audio controls, cruise control, power driver seat controls, alloy wheels and other features. Leather upholstery is available, as is a power moonroof and heated front seats. The Odyssey aims to be more of a luxury cruiser than a basic family or labour hauler.

The aging 9-5 was given a makeover in 2006, which includes a new look inside and out, and some minor mechanical modifications. Sold in Linear, Arc and Aero versions, there is only the four-door sedan form available here, although a SportCombi wagon could probably be ordered. The 9-5 now features two 2.3-litre four-cylinder turbo engines in different states of tune, mated to five-speed manual or optional automatic transmissions. The 9-5 features consist of leather upholstery, sport-tuned suspension, power windows and mirrors, power-adjustable front seats, computer information display, Xenon headlamps, anti-theft alarm, sunroof, CD stereo, aumatic climate control, alloy wheels, parking sensors, keyless entry and more. Safety features are extensive, with an active head restraint system, front and side airbags, ABS brakes, traction control and stability control. This car certainly is loaded with features, but it loses out with an inflated price tag for what is essentially a four-cylinder front-wheel-drive sedan, living only on facelifts since the last millenium.

The Eos is a hard-top convertible version of the Golf hatchback. Facelifted for 2012 with a new front-end, it features a five-piece retractable hardtop. The car can somewhat seat four people, with good luggage room when the top is up. Its four-wheel independent suspension and relatively long wheelbase give it a nice ride along with good stability and handling. The Eos is available in the GCC with only one engine now, namely a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, with a choice of manual or DSG automanual gearboxes, although most dealers are likely to stock the DSG version only. Depending on trim level, the Eos can be outfitted with a touchscreen CD/MP3 stereo, convertible-specific Climatronic a/c, electric windows, alloy wheels, multi-functturning, HID headlights, "ion" display, keyless entry and start, navigation, cruise control, Bluetooth phone and a second-generation Park Assist system with ParkPilot. Safety features include ABS, dual front airbags, side airbags, lateral airbags, a roll-bar safety system and stability control.

The Hyundai Azera, fills the gap between the Sonata and the Genesis sedan. It received a facelift for the 2015 model year. The front-wheel-drive full-size sedan comes with two engine choices, a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder and a 3.0-litre V6, but some GCC markets get only the V6. Both engines get a standard 6-speed automatic. The 2.4-litre version gets smart keyless entry with starter button, mood lighting, available panoramic sunroof, fake wood trim, rear sunshade, CD/MP3 stereo, auto-dimming mirror, electric parking brake with auto hold, leather powered seats, fog lamps, parking sensors, and 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels. The 3.0-litre version additionally gets xenon lights, memory and seat massage for driver, Infinity stereo, heating & cooling for front seats, electric tilt & telescopic steering wheel, Bluetooth, tyre pressure monitoring system, electric folding mirrors, adaptive cruise control, rain sensor and dual-zone a/c. The top model gets a navigation and DVD entertainment system with rear camera. All models get 8 airbags and ABS with EBD, while only the V6 gets stability control.

The all-new Jaguar XK is the long-awaited successor to Jaguar's sports car franchise, and though its new face is decidedly controversial, it is still a very desirable car. The new-for-2007 XK comes as both a coupe and a convertible. Riding on a much longer wheelbase, the new aluminium-built XK offers substantially more interior space than the old model. The XK 4.2 model is powered by the corporate 4.2-litre V8, while the XKR gets a supercharged version of that engine. Both engines are mated to a six-speed manual gearbox with paddle shifters. Its rigid chassis and the latest CATS adaptive suspension aim for a smooth ride and sporty cornering. Standard equipment includes DVD navigation, keyless entry and keyless start, a seven-inch video display, Bluetooth capability, cruise control, a 6-CD/MP3 player, rear park assist, cruise control, and electronic parking brake. Options include adaptive cruise control with a forward-alert system that sounds an audible warning, full soft leather upholstery, and a 520-watt Alpine sound system with eight speakers. Safety feature include front and side airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, dynamic stability control with a track feature, and electronic rollover mitigation.

The Kia Rio is all-new for the 2012 model year. Attractively designed, it is available in 4-door sedan and 5-door hatchback form. The only engine for the GCC is a 1.4-litre 4-cylinder with variable-valve timing, mated to a 4-speed automatic. While mechanically basic, the Rio can be had with a host of features unseen in the sub-compact segment. Standard features include 14-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, manual a/c, CD/MP3 stereo, adjustable steering wheel, central locking, power windows, electric mirrors and only one airbag. The mid-range model gets 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, centre-console armrest, fog lamps, keyless entry, USB port, Bluetooth, steering-wheel audio controls, sun-visor lights, folding mirrors with indicators and a split-folding rear seat. The top model gets rear parking sensors, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, padded leatherette door trim, LED front running lights and tail lamps, 17-inch alloy wheels, more speakers for the stereo, cruise control, cooled glovebox, auto headlights, sunroof, and finally, ABS and a passenger-side airbag in addition to the driver's one. The Rio is offered in Europe and the States with full front-side-curtain airbags and stability control, and has a 5-star crash-test rating in Europe, but that model is not sold in the GCC.

The BMW M3 convertible debuted in 2008 as a sedan, coupe and convertible in the Middle East. It is powered by high revving 4.0-litre V8 engine, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 7-speed automanual dual-clutch transmission. The M3 is the only 3-Series model with features such as electronically-variable suspension and chassis adjustments. The iDrive computer is standard, as are active steering, HID headlights, and 18-inch alloy wheels, or an optional 19-inches. The M3 gets multiple front and side airbags, stability control, ABS and great rear-wheel-drive handling characteristics.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it is not really that good off-road, but gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. It is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. This wagon offers room for five passengers, with the option of two additional rear-facing seats in the luggage area. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, cruise control, electric driver's seat, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, a power front passenger seat,  16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, and WHIPS whiplash protection.

The Opel Astra OPC is the German brand's hot-hatch offering. It is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-litre direct injection engine, mated to a 6-speed manual transmission. Basic options include central locking with remote, power windows, cruise control, daytime running lamps, rear parking sensors, fog lamps, speed sensitive power steering, driver seat manual adjustable, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3/Aux in support, 19-inch alloy wheels, dual zone automatic A/C, leather steering wheel, outside mirror power foldable and flex-ride with continuous damping control. Safety features include driver and passenger front, side and curtain airbags, electronic stability program (ESP) and ABS as standard.

The Porsche Cayman has been completely revamped for 2012 in almost all aspects, with a new exterior design that doesn't rely on leftover 911 parts like before. Rebadged in early 2016, the '718' Cayman have engines that have been downsized to 4-cylinder turbocharged motors, with a choice of 6-speed manual or 7-speed "PDK" automanual. The standard Cayman gets a turbocharged 2.0-litre motor, while the Cayman S gets the turbocharged 2.5-litre unit. Also, the front fascia has been updated with a new headlight design and longer cooling intakes. The 2-seater Cayman comes standard with 18-inch wheels, HID headlights, power windows, keyless entry and not a whole lot else. Everything else costs extra, with a choice of  options such as 19-inch and 20-inch wheel designs, special paint colours, various leather seat styles and upholstery options, cabin trim materials, Bose stereo, CD/DVD changer, multimedia system with navigation and Bluetooth, keyless start, power-folding mirrors, parking sensors, wind deflector and even coloured wheel-caps. Further optional features include speed-sensitive power steering, ceramic brakes, Porsche Torque Vectoring system with mechanically-locking rear differential, Sport Chrono package with launch control, and a variable sports exhaust system. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, fixed roll hoops, ABS, stability control and optional tyre-pressure monitor.

The Toyota Prado got a minor facelift for 2014, and in 2016 all variants got a new 6-speed automatic transmission. The "VVT-i" engine offerings carry over, with a 2.7-litre 4-cylinder and a 4.0-litre V6. All models offer standard all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing and available locking centre-differential. The Saudi market offers both manual and automatic variants on all except the top trim level, while the UAE market only gets automatic versions. The basic Prado 2.7L, known as TX in KSA and EXR in UAE, comes with 17-inch steel wheels, black front grille, black power mirrors and door handles, rear spoiler, mud guards, fabric seating for seven, keyless entry, front and rear manual a/c, CD/MP3 6-speaker stereo, ABS with EBD and brake-assist, dual front airbags and floor-mounted spare tyre. The TX additionally gets side-steps and rear parking sensors, while the EXR instead gets a cool box, steering audio controls, USB/AUX ports and Bluetooth. The mid-range Prado 2.7L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, gets 17-inch alloy wheels, rear parking sensors, chrome front grille, body-coloured trim, side steps, leather steering wheel and shift lever, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cool box and more. The TXL additionally gets front fog lamps, front bumper guard and stability control, while the EXR instead gets dual-zone auto a/c, cruise control and a dealer-installed auto-dimming mirror with rear camera. The UAE also gets a Prado 2.7L in VXR trim that adds powered front seats, side/curtain/knee airbags, stability control and dealer-installed features such as leather upholstery and navigation with rear camera while losing steering-wheel controls. The basic Prado 4.0L, known as EXR in UAE, comes with a 6-speaker stereo withBluetooth and USB/AUX ports, steering audio controls, rear parking sensors, manual a/c, fabric seats, dual airbags, stability control, ABS, smart key with engine start/stop button, cruise control and hill start/descent assist. All UAE-bound V6 Prado models have a door-mounted spare tyre. The mid-range Prado 4.0L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, comes with roof rails, side steps, fog lamps, front bumper guard and uphill/downhill assist on all automatic models. The TXL additionally gets a tow hitch and side mouldings, while the GXR instead gets side/curtain/knee airbags, dual-zone a/c, extra chrome trim, power front seats, rear camera and dealer-installed navigation with no steering controls. A higher-spec Prado 4.0L trim, known as TXL2 in KSA and VXR in UAE, comes with sunroof, dual auto a/c, rear camera and aftermarket audio with navigation. The TXL2 version also gets auto-levelling LED headlights, sunshades and in-car WiFi, while the VXR gets remote start, leather and power front seats. The Prado 4.0L in top VXL trim gains 18-inch alloy wheels, LED-encrusted headlights, leather seats, ventilated front seats, power front seats with memory, front and rear parking sensors with rear camera, side/curtain/knee airbags, "optitron" gauges, 14-speaker JBL stereo with voice control and steering-wheel buttons, multi-touch screen with navigation, remote engine starter and additional exterior trim. The Saudi VXL additionally gets self-leveling KDSS suspension, power-folding third row, Multi-Terrain Select with four cameras, rear DVD screen, blind-spot monitor and a tyre pressure warning system.

The sister-model to the hotly-anticipated Toyota 86, the Subaru BRZ finally made its showroom debut as a mid-2012 model. In 2017, it got a minor facelift. The BRZ is a collaborative effort with Toyota, and therefore versions are available under both nameplates, with only a front bumper different between the two. Usually available in only one trim level in most GCC markets, the front-engine rear-wheel-drive car comes with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder direct-injection boxer engine, mated to a 6-speed manual or automatic transmission. Depending on the dealer, standard features include cloth or leather sports seats, HID headlights, fog lamps, CD/MP3 stereo with USB port, Bluetooth, auto a/c, common power accessories and 17-inch alloy wheels, as well as a stability control system with three modes, ABS and a full set of front, side, curtain and knee airbags. It additionally gets a limited-slip diff, paddle-shifters, smart keyless entry with starter button, extra digital speedo, cruise control and and floor illumination. Specs may vary between different GCC countries, with most offering only the automatic version.

The original B9 Tribeca, Subaru's attempt at a midsize 4WD, has received a facelift for 2008, getting a dull new look instead of the ugly old face. Built on the same all-wheel-drive platform as the Outback, the Tribeca is longer, wider and much inches taller than the Outback, and offers five or seven-passenger seating. The overall styling has been toned down after the previous design was deemed too controversial. The interior attempts to be more modern and upscale than competitive makes, with an amazingly unique design. The oddly-named B9 Tribeca has now dropped "B9" from its name, and is now powered by Subaru's 3.6-litre horizontally-opposed flat six-cylinder "boxer" engine, a rare type of engine design shared only with Porsche. Also standard is a five-speed automatic gearbox. The B9 Tribeca offers power windows, electric mirrors, standard roll sensing system, ABS brakes with Brake Assist, CD stereo, and standard two-position memory system for front driver's seat and more. Options include reverse-assist sensors, remote starter, and rear cargo cover with shade-type functionality. Safety features include dual front and side airbags.

The SQ 5 is the top performance version of the Q5 compact SUV. An all-new model came out in 2018. Under the hood, it comes with a 3.0-litre turbocharged engine, mated to a 8-speed automatic transmission. The four-wheel-drive model gets standard features like power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, Nappa leather interior, cruise control, keyless entry and start, auto headlamps, auto headlight range adjustment, fog lamps, xenon headlamps, LED daytime running lamps, LED taillights, navigation, panoramic glass roof, 3-zone automatic A/C, Bluetooth, Bang & Olufsen sound system, front and rear parking sensors and 21-inch ally wheels. Optional equipment include electric front seats with memory function, electric folding mirrors with heated and memory, side steps, adaptive cruise control, adaptive lights, red brake callipers, dynamic steering, more leather padding and sports seats. Safety features include front, side and head airbags, traction control, brake assist and stability control.

The Dodge Challenger SRT received a minor facelift and new engine upgrades in 2015. The interior has been significantly improved as well. The Challenger utilises retro styling that is largely a rethinking of the original 1970s Challenger's 2-door design. The interior gets upgraded with a bit more gadgetry in the form of an 8.4-inch Uconnect infotainment system and 7-inch customization display between the retro-inspired speedometer and tachometer. With a high-sill center aluminium gauge bezels makes the revamped interior extremely pleasing to the eyes. Through the Uconnect interface, you can now access the all-new Dodge performance pages that allows you to select different driving modes to adjust steering effort, engine and transmission response, electronic stability and traction controls, and standard launch control. It also gets forward collision warning, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring and rear cross path detection. The Challenger SRT gets the 6.4-litre V8. A new addition to the engine lineup is the 6.2-litre supercharged unit for the Challenger SRT Hellcat. The SRT models gets a flat-bottomed steering wheel, bi-xenon headlights, heated and ventilated seats wrapped in Nappa leather and Alcantara and 20-inch aluminium-alloy wheels, along with the usual accessories such as automatic a/c, cruise control and fog lamps. Also available are a sunroof, racing stripes, rear sensors with camera, and the UConnect touchscreen multimedia system with voice controls as well as navigation, hard drive and Bluetooth phone. Safety features include ABS, stability control, front,side and curtain airbags, and SRT-exclusive Brembo brakes.

The Chevrolet Aveo sedan is built in Korea. An all-new model came out in 2017. Under the hood, it gets a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Three trim levels are on offer - a base, LS and LT. The standard model gets steering wheel controls, Bluetooth, radio and phone handsfree controls, driver and passenger dual air bags, 15-inch steel wheels and front power windows. The LS trim gets addtiional 4-way driver seat adjuster, rear park assist, rear seat full folding, 40/60 split, front fog lamps and optional 15-inch alloy wheels. The LT trim gets additional 7-inch MyLinkTM screen with phone integration, 6 speakers and 15-inch alloy wheels.

The popular 7th-generation Lancer, receiving a major facelift in 2004, uses three four-cylinder engines, namely a 1.3-litre and 1.6-litre in the basic models, while a 2.0-litre Ralliart Edition was briefly available before being dropped in 2008. The aging non-Ralliart variants are so popular that they continued to be sold alongside the all-new 2008 Lancer EX. The 1.3-litre has a choice of a five-speed manual and a four-speed automatic. The 1.6-litre has a choice of a manual or automatic. The 2.0-litre came exclusively with an automatic gearbox. None of the engines are particularly sporting. Features, either standard or optional, include driver's & front passenger's SRS dual airbags, simple radio cassette player or a better radio cassette stereo with CD changer and 4 speakers, tachometer, optional rear spoiler, steel wheels with hubcaps or light alloy wheels, ABS with EBD, optional keyless entry system, and a rear seat centre armrest with cup holders. The Ralliart Edition specifically adds a rear spoiler, 15-inch alloy wheels, leather steering wheel, special interior trim, body kit and better brakes. All cars have a cloth interior, with standard power windows and mirrors.

The third-generation Kia Cerato hatchback boasts sleeker styling that is 30 mm longer, 15 mm lower and 5 mm wider than the outgoing car, with a 50 mm extended wheelbase. It also featured an all-new bodyshell, upgraded equipment, a host of additional convenience and safety features, a more spacious cabin with better quality, improved suspension and an upgraded powertrain line-up that delivers class-leading performance and fuel economy. In 2017, the Cerato got a facelift. No changes were made in 2018. Two 4-cylinder engines are offered here -- a 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre, both mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Available options include a colour 4.2-inch LCD information screen, Intelligent Key system with push-start, memory seats, rear-camera, heated and ventilated front seats, dual-zone airconditioning, hill-assist and parking sensors. Safety features include ABS brakes, brake assist, stability control, and two front airbags.

The 599 GTB Fiorano is a new all-aluminium two-seater, named after the circuit Ferrari uses to hone the performance of its track and road cars, while GTB stands for Gran Turismo Berlinetta, after classic Ferrari berlinettas, and 599 reflects the displacement of its V12 engine divided by 10. Talk about overdoing it. The passenger areas of the Ferrari 599 GTB Fiorano are trimmed in leather while the driver area and controls boast more high-tech detailing in carbon-fibre and aluminium. Other standard accessories include front bi-xenon headlamps and rear LED lights, dusk and rain sensors, dual-zone climate control, electrically adjustable steering-wheel column, hideaway radio/CD player and key with integrated volumetric anti-theft device with motion sensors. Accessories include front and rear parking sensors, iPod-friendly set-up, satellite anti-theft system and a luggage set specially tailored to fit this model. Development work for the Ferrari 599 GTB Fiorano focused specifically on the distinctive sound the 6.0-litre V12 makes, to pretty much make it sound like a Ferrari.

An all-new Kia Sportage came out for the 2016 model year. The 2018 Kia Sportage has remained the same. The 2018 Sportage is powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive, or a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder with all-wheel-drive, or a turbocharged 1.6-litre 4-cylinder will all-wheel drive. The naturally-aspirated engines get a 6-speed automatic transmission, while the turbo engine is mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission. The base 2018 Kia Sportage 2.0-litre FWD model comes with power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth seats, fog lamps, manual a/c, rear spoiler, roof rails, CD/MP3 stereo with 6 speakers and USB/AUX inputs, 17-inch steel wheels, ABS and only a single driver-side airbag. Things get better in the higher trim levels, with the top 2018 Kia Sportage 2.4-litre AWD model additionally outfitted with dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, cruise control, smart key with starter button, leather upholstery, power driver-side seat, stereo with subwoofer and iPod cable, rear sensors and camera, chrome door handles, electric folding mirrors, 18-inch alloy wheels, navigation and improved safety features such as ABS with stability control, active headrests and two front airbags, though still no side airbags. The top 2018 Kia Sportage "GT Line" option comes with a different front bumper with four-cube fog lamps, different front grille, front and back skid plates, dual exhaust tips, D-shaped steering wheel and 20-inch alloy wheels

The Volkswagen Jetta received a facelift for 2015. There are two engines on offer, a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine and a 2.5-litre 5-cylinder motor, both mated to a manually-shiftable 6-speed automatic transmission and front-wheel-drive. There are three trim levels, named S for the 2.0, and SE and SEL for the 2.5. The base S model comes with keyless entry, 4-speaker CD/MP3/AUX stereo, power windows, electric mirrors, cloth upholstery and 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps. The SE additionally comes with 8-speakers, 6.5-inch colour touch screen, leather seats, 17-inch alloy wheels, automatic a/c, steering-wheel buttons, cruise control, fog lamps, sunroof, alarm system, rear camera and parking sensors. The top SEL comes with ESP, hill-hold control, xenon headlamps, rear LED lights, front fog lights with cornering lights. All VW Jetta models come with ABS, six airbags and auto hazard lights as standard.

Launched in 2005 and facelifted for 2008, the compact S40 sedan is based on the same front-wheel-drive platform as the Mazda 3 and the Ford Focus, all of which come under the Ford umbrella. Yet Volvo claims that the S40 is a true Volvo, asserting unique premium features only found in the Volvo. The S40 is an obviously small car, but it looks a lot like its larger siblings with its signature new-age-Volvo styling. There are three engine choices, all of them the corporate oddball five-cylinder, except for the base 1.6-litre four-cylinder with manual gearbox. The range includes a basic 2.4-litre, a higher-tuned 2.4-litre and a turbocharged 2.5-litre, all offered with automatic with tiptronic in this region. Markets outside this region get all-wheel-dive models too. The interior has an ultra-slim centre console that seems to be free-floating, with extra storage space behind it. The safety package includes a patented zonal front structure using differing strengths of high-strength steel to disperse force away from passengers in a crash. Dual front airbags, SIPS side impact protection, curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection are all standard.

The Nissan Altima received a minor facelift for the 2010 model year, including a restyled front end, new wheel designs, and new interior options. The Altima will be available with a choice of a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder or a 3.5-litre V6. All versions get the CVT automatic as standard. However, many dealers started offering only the 2.5-litre automatic models from 2011. All GCC-spec Altima models come with a beige interior, in cloth or optional leather. The entertainment system has been upgraded with a optional new Bose premium stereo with nine speakers, optional 4.3-inch colour display, USB port with iPod connectivity, Bluetooth hands-free Phone System, MP3/WMA CD playback, and rear monitor. Also offered is an optional hard-drive navigation system with 6.5-inch VGA colour display, 9.3GB Music Box for music storage and playback, Bluetooth Streaming Audio, DVD player and an RCA input for auxiliary audio/video connectivity. The base 2.5 model gets 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, cloth upholstery, intelligent keyless entry with starter button and manually-adjusted seats. The higher 2.5 models gets 16-inch alloy wheels, Bose stereo, fog lamps, rear camera and cloth upholstery with options such as sunroof and spoiler. And the 3.5 gets 17-inch alloys, power driver's seat, spoiler and optional leather. All Altima models now come with stability control, front and side airbags, and ABS, with options such as side-curtain airbags and a tyre-pressure monitor.

The Mini, heavily updated in 2007, was mildly updated for 2010 in looks, features and power. It is one of the smallest cars on the road and can be parked virtually anywhere. Yet it seats four, though with painfully tight back seats, and it can carry a bit of cargo. Engineered by BMW, the Mini has been given a major overhaul in styling and cabin space for 2007, though the basic underpinnings are still the same. Cabrio convertibles offer an electrically-folding soft-top and pop-up rollover hoops. Models include the Cooper and the turbocharged Cooper S. The Cooper models use a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine in different states of tune, with the S adding a turbocharger. Gearbox choices include a manual and an automatic. Standard features include CD stereo, power windows and electric mirrors, along with a number of airbags, with options such as navigation, sports seats, panoramic glass roof and alloy-wheel choices. Options for the Cooper S include a John Cooper Works (JCW) package that bumps up horsepower and handling, while a Sport package offers DSC, bonnet stripes, 17-inch alloys and xenon headlamps. Originally, the JCW models were only available with a manual gearbox, but automatic versions became available by late 2012. Special edition models are offered from time to time, such as the 50th-anniversary Mayfair Cooper S in 2010. A limited "Inspired by Goodwood" Cooper S model was launched with real leather and other upscale trim, for a lot of money. A limited Cooper S JCW GP edition came in 2013, featuring a bit more power over the regular JCW, Recaro front seats, rear seats deleted, stiffer suspension and unique wheels.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class is essentially the new facelifted M-Class following the German brand's new nomenclature. Mercedes-AMG GLE 63 is the top performance model and got more power and torque in 2016. In 2018, the two variants offered were the standard GLE 63 and then the GLE 63 S. Under the hood, both come with the 5.5-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive. Available features include adjustable air suspension, adaptive cruise control and active parking assist. The exterior features HID headlights, LED running maps and 21-inch cross-spoke AMG alloy wheels. The 5-seater interior offers leather upholstery, mood lighting, HDD navigation, panoramic sunroof, rear entertainment system, keyless start, ventilated power front seats and a split-folding rear seat. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control, ABS and drowsiness monitor, with options such as a rear view camera with parking sensors, active lane assist, blind-spot monitor and automatic pre-crash braking.

The Volvo XC60 was launched with high hopes for the Swedish company, capitalising on the small crossover vehicle market. The XC60 is a 5-seater crossover SUV that is aimed at attracting luxury-brand buyers. The XC60 T6 is powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic with manual-shifting capability, and an all-wheel-drive system without low-range gearing. The XC60 T5 model comes with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder with a 6-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive. The smallest XC model includes safety technology, Volvo's City Safety system, designed to help a driver avoid a collision at under 30 kph, or reduce the speed of impact at higher speeds by hitting the brakes if the vehicle in front suddenly stops and City Safety determines that a collision is likely. Other safety features on the XC60 is Pre-Prepared Restraints that uses a laser sensor that interacts with other technology to control the airbags and adaptive seatbelt load limiters. Other features, depending on trim level, include cloth or leather upholstery, blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, reverse camera, keyless entry, sunroof, alloy wheels, common power accessories and a CD/MP3 stereo. An R-Design body kit is optional. Standard safety features include front and side-surtain airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, and whiplash-protection headrests. A software-based Polestar power upgrade is also offered, adding 20-30 hp, depending on the model.

At first glance, this Chinese-built car looks like nothing more than a cheap copy of the Toyota Corolla, with the rear end of a Honda City mixture, but wearing a fake BMW badge. And it is exactly that, but if you look past the lame attempts at plagiarism, you'll find a package that actually might be a decent deal for a new car. The F3 is powered by a 1.6-litre Mitsubishi-sourced engine, mated to a 5-speed manual Mitsubishi gearbox. It includes an interior that is exactly like that of a last-generation Toyota Corolla, but with softer touchable surfaces. Available features, standard or optional, include 15-inch wheels, leather upholstery, dual front airbags, sunroof, manual air-conditioning, CD player, remote keyless entry, fake wood trim, height-adjustable steering wheel, power windows, ABS brakes and the price tag of a car half its size. Build quality seems to be of passing-grade, although some plastic pieces have an unfinished feel to them. If only they'd try a bit harder and be a bit more original. The price may make up for it though, in the eyes of some cost-conscious buyers.

The Trajet is Hyundai's latest attempt at conquering the world of minivans, but it is a completely typical minivan, with nothing over the competition except a lower price and an underpowered 2.7-litre V6. Standard features include power steering, front and rear a/c, roof rack, front and rear power windows, radio and cassette player with 4 speakers, central door locks, funky tail lights and an automatic transmission. Options include a sunroof, fog lamps, All models come with 15-inch wheels, though the lower model gets steel rims with plastic covers, while the top model gets alloys. Unique features include four forward-opening doors, which is a rarity in the large minivan set. The basic model actually comes with 8-seater capacity, thanks to a bunch of bench seats, but the top model is more of a 7-seater, with more comfortable accommodations. The cabin is of course versatile, with movable and foldable seats to increase or decrease luggage space as needed. Safety features are conspicuously absent in the Middle East model, though overseas versions get all sorts of airbags, traction control and ABS, some of which you could probably special-order.

The Ibiza is based on the VW Polo and is the hatchback variant of the Cordoba. Though similar to the Cordoba, it somehow appears a lot more sporty than the dull Cordoba, and the engine choices here carry forward that notion. In the Middle East, this front-wheel-drive is offered in three-door or five-door body styles, with numerous VW-derived powerplants, including a 1.4-litre, a 1.6-litre and two turbocharged 1.8-litre units, all 4-cylinder engines, with some manual and some automatic transmissions available, depending on model. Standard equipment includes ABS brakes, driver and passenger airbag, power steering, power front windows, electric mirrors, remote central locking, 15-inch to 17-inch wheels, CD stereo, height adjustable front seats, split rear seat, cloth upholstery, traction control and even an optional stability control system. These cars are quite well-packed with features for their size. Sport and FR models get larger alloy wheels, stiffer suspension, body-colour rear spoiler, sports seats and unique exhausts as standard. The limited-availability 3-door Cupra gets the top turbo engine and further sports tuning.

The 407 remains the odd-one-out in the overly-competitive midsize car segment, with styling that still looks good today as it did when the model was launched in 2005. For 2009, the 407 has received a minor facelift comprising on exterior trim add-ons, new tail-lights and mild changes in engine output. Now available in four-door sedan and two-door coupe body styles only, the wagon version has been dropped. There are three engine choices available for the sedan. The entry level engine is a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine combined with a 4-speed automatic with a tiptronic function. Then there is a 2.2-litre 4-cylinder engine with the same 4-speed automatic gearbox. The top model is a 3.0-litre V6 engine with variable valve timing, combined with a 6-speed automatic gearbox with tiptronic. Even the most basic model gets power windows, keyless entry, cruise control, ABS, stability control, power mirrors, fog lights, rear sunblind and automatic climate control. The 407 comes with 16-inch, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, depneding on trim level. All models get eight or more airbags, as well as stability control and ABS.

The Pathfinder can be considered a proper off-roading 4WD. It is built on a fullsize pickup platform, thereby offering good off-road capability but marginal on-road handling. The current Pathfinder is significantly larger than previous models. It offers more interior space and more convenience features. It also offers third-row seating to carry up to seven people. The 4.0-litre V6 that powers the Pathfinder is a larger, retuned version of the engine that powers the 350Z. Its five-speed automatic transmission is geared to use the engine's torque characteristics. The 4WD features optional Hill Descent Control, which limits downhill speed without driver intervention, and Hill Start Assist, which briefly holds the Pathfinder on a slope while the driver releases the brake pedal and applies the accelerator. Standard features include fabric upholstery, cruise control, power mirrors, windows and door locks with keyless remote, CD stereo with six speakers, reclining backs on the middle row seats, front and side airbags, ABS and alloy wheels. Options include power seats, halogen foglights, running boards, roof rack cross bars and leather seating. For 2008, the Pathfinder received a very minor facelift, while gaining new available features such as Bluetooth, navigation, rear-seat DVD entertainment and intelligent keyless entry.

After more than a decade with minimal changes, the Nissan Patrol was redesigned from the ground up for 2010, aiming to regain some of the market-share lost to its rivals. The Patrol can be optioned up with enough features to classify it as a full-fledged luxury vehicle, with some class-leading features and new technology. Engine options include a base 5.6-litre V8 with 5-speed automatic or 6-speed manual, known as the Patrol SE, as well as a brand-new 5.6-litre V8 with more power, direct injection and a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol LE. Depending on trim level, the 7-seater Patrol can be had with standard or optional features such as all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing, hydraulic independent air suspension, computerised terrain response system, climate-controlled leather seats, Arabic-supported HDD navigation, wide WVGA 8-inch touchscreen, multi-screen DVD entertainment system, 9.3GB Music Box hard drive, Bluetooth, power rear liftgate, keyless start, adaptive cruise control, 20-inch alloy wheels, power-folding 3rd-row seat, around-view cameras, and a centre console cool-box that can be opened from both 1st & 2nd-row seats. Also available is an Off-road Monitor that provides real-time information such as tyre conditions involving steer angle, slip and pressure, as well as hill start, hill descent, and an electronically-locking rear diff. Most models get a regular offroad-ready front bumper, while the top trims get a slightly-lower 'city' bumper. Safety features include two front airbags and numerous side-curtain airbags, stability control and ABS, as well as optional lane-departure warning, tyre-pressure monitor and auto-braking systems.

An all-new model of the Kia Cerato came out as a 2019 model year. Two 4-cylinder engines are offered here -- a 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre, both mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Available options include a colour 4.2-inch LCD information screen, Intelligent Key system with push-start, memory seats, rear-camera, heated and ventilated front seats, dual-zone airconditioning, hill-assist and parking sensors. Safety features include ABS brakes, brake assist, stability control, and two front airbags.

The Changan CS75 is a compact SUV from China. It got a facelift in 2019. Under the hood, it gets a turbocharged 1.8-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features in the CS75 "Fashion" trim include power windows, central locking, remote on key, cruise control, manual A/C, radio and single CD player with MP3/WMA support, 8 speakers, multifunctional steering wheel, USB+AUX ports, leather seats, sunroof, fog lamps, parking sensors and LED headlamps. Higher "Elite" trim gets additional 7-inch screen, keyless entry and start and auto climate control.Safety features includes dual front airbags, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD), brake assist (BA), traction control and hill assist. The top option gets addition side curtain airbags.

The Lincoln MKC is the luxury brand's compact SUV offering. It gets two 4-cylinder turbocharged units to choose from, one 2.0-litre and the other 2.3-litre. Both are mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. While the 2.0-litre is available in front-wheel drive, the 2.3-litre gets all-wheel drive. Standard features in the MKC include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, automatic A/C, central locking with keyless entry, pust-start engine, signature push button gear shiftter, leather seats and alloy-wheels. Optional features include panoramic roof and better infotainment system. Lincoln MKC offers advanced technology such as collision warning with brake support, a Lane-Keeping System and driver assist to help drivers avoid common accidents. The collision warning system is designed to alert the driver if it detects a potential front-end crash. The system issues an audible alert in the cabin, a visual alert on the windshield and automatic brake assist sensitivity. MKC has park-out assist technology, a class-exclusive feature that enhances the vehicle's active park assist capabilities. Where active park assist helps guide drivers into tight parallel parking situations, park-out assist steers drivers out of tight parking spots. The vehicle's Lane-Keeping System uses rearview mirror-mounted cameras to identify lane markers and help drivers avoid unintentionally straying from their lane. Dashboard-mounted cameras monitor driver alertness. If the system detects a driver's alertness level dropping below a given threshold, a warning is issued via a chime and a pop-up message appears on the left-hand cluster screen. MKC also offers a Blind Spot Information System, which continuously monitors the vehicle's blind spots with radar sensors, and class-exclusive cross-traffic alert, which detects traffic as the vehicle backs from a parking space. The MKC gets 7 standard airbags, including a class-exclusive driver's knee airbag.

The redesigned 2014 Kia Carens is a seven-seater MPV, smaller than typical minivans. It remained the same for 2017. The Carens can be had with two 4-cylinder engines, one a direct-injection 1.6-litre "GDI" in LX and EX trim, and the other a fuel-injected 2.0-litre "MPI" in LX and two EX trims. All models get a 6-speed automatic, front-wheel-drive, fog lamps, cooled glovebox, CD/MP3 stereo, Bluetooth, roof rack and keyless entry. Base models get 16-inch steel wheels and a vinyl steering wheel. Higher trim levels get 17-inch alloy wheels, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, parking sensors, cruise control and more. Only the top model gets a panoramic glass roof. All models get ABS and only one airbag, except for the top model, which gets two front airbags to go with that glass roof.

The all-new M4 came out as a 2015 model year and is the replacement for the M3 Coupe. Gone is the V8 under the hood, and has been replaced by a highly-tuned twin-turbocharged inline-6, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic. Features include head-up display, a backup camera, parking sensors, ventilated seats, keyless entry, and headlamp washers. The Driver Assistance package adds blind-spot monitoring, lane-departure warning, autonomous braking, and side-view camera.

The redesigned-for-2008 Mondeo is an attractive midsize car built in Europe that shares a Mazda platform. It looks excellent inside and out, but loses out to the Japanese with a weak combination of carryover engines, along with the stigma of expensive dealer maintenance charges. It was facelifted a bit for 2011, with a new front bumper and grille. The Mondeo is largely avaliable as a family sedan, but it is also available in sporty liftback and practical wagon form in some markets. The Mondeo is a tremendous success in Europe though, simply because its handling is outstanding, rivalling more expensive cars like Alfa Romeo, all for an affordable price. The interior is especially attractive and put together well. The base Mondeo is powered by the 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, available with a 5-speed manual. A 2.3-litre 4-cylinder engine is coupled with a 6-speed automatic transmission in the higher model. Various trim levels are available, all with power windows, trip computer, ABS brakes, front airbags, CD stereo with MP3 connector and more. Options include stability control, CD changer, keyless starter button, Xenon adaptive headlights, tyre pressure monitor, sunroof, fog lights, variable suspension settings, hill launch assist and adaptive cruise control.

Opel Astra returned to the UAE and GCC as a 2013 model. Three models will be sold here - Astra Enjoy sedan, the Astra Cosmo hatchback and Astra GTC hatchback. The first two models get the 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, whereas the GTC gets a turbocharged 1.4-litre 4-cylinder motor. They all get a 6-speed automatic transmission. Basic options include a single-zone manual A/C, central locking with remote, power windows, cruise control, daytime running lamps, rear parking sensors, fog lamps, speed sensitive power steering, driver seat manual adjustable, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3/Aux in support and 17-inch alloy wheels. The higher models get dual zone automatic A/C, sunroof, leather steering wheel, outside mirror power foldable, 18-inch alloy wheels, flex-ride with continuous damping control and driver selectable sport/tour modes. The GTC gets 20-inch alloy wheels and a rear spoiler. Safety features include driver and passenger front, side and curtain airbags, electronic stability program (ESP) and ABS as standard on all models.

The redesigned Boxster roadster was introduced in 2005, and it got the upgrated engines from Cayman for the 2007 model year. Considered the entry-level Porsche offering, the cars are powered by a 2.7-litre version of the traditional Porsche flat-six engine in their base trim, while the higher-performance S versions are powered by a 3.4-litre version of the sixer. The model is considered a benchmark for sports-car handling, with rear-wheel-drive and a choice of either a manual or a manually-shiftable automatic. Standard features include power windows, electric mirrors, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, among other luxury options. The Boxster offers head airbags in combination with thorax airbags, concealed on the outer side of the backrest, alongside the usual front airbags. Luggage is space is very limited, with two trunks, one in the front and one behind the mid-mounted engine in the back. The Boxster can be ordered with a removable hard top.

The Genesis GV80 is the South Korean brand's first premium SUV offering. Under the hood, it gets two engine options - a 2.5-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and a 3.5-litre turbocharged V6 motor. Both engines are mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The 2.5-litre model can be had with two-wheel-drive or optional four-wheel-drive whereas the 3.5 model comes only as an all-wheel-drive. Standard options in the GV80 include power steering, power windows, electric folding mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push engine start-stop, leather upholstery, memory and ventilated seats, audio system with AUX/USB support, auto A/C, navigation, auto defog system, rain sensors, sunroof, parking assist system, rear electric curtain, xenon headlamps, LED headlights and taillights with LED daytime running lamps, front and rear camera, air suspension and 20-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include 9 airbags, lane keep assist, adaptive cruise control, ABS, traction control, stability control, brake assist, blind spot detection and autonomous emergency braking (AEB).

The VW Multivan is the range-topping minivan based on the T5 Transporter work-van platform. The outdated front-wheel-drive van is powered by an equally-outdated 3.2-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic. Available with 6 or 7 seats, it has a unique rail feature in which seats can slide forward and backward into any configuration. Offered in base Comfortline and upgraded Highline trim, the Multivan can be had with features such as power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, and a CD stereo. It can be optionally outfitted with cloth or leather seats, HID headlights, wood cabin trim, rear DVD entertainment system, sunroof, alloy wheels and automatic doors. A wide range of accessories are available, like tables and refrigerators which fit onto the rails, all movable. The Multivan has safety features as standard such as front and side-curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it had been somewhat redesigned for 2008, and then mechanically upgraded for 2012. Although it is still not really that good off-road as we know it, the XC70 gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. Available only in T6 trim now, it is powered by a turbocharged 3.0-litre 6-cylinder engine, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, ventilated front seats with perforated leather, 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, an in-dash computer system with USB and Bluetooth support, and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, WHIPS whiplash protection, collision Warning with brake support and emergency brake lamps, adaptive cruise control helps keeping a safe distance to vehicles ahead, hydraulic brake assist, optimised hydraulic brakes and fading brake support. An optional Polestar ECU upgrade is available to bump up the power by 25 hp.

A leader of technology back in the early 90s, the Legend is Honda's forgotten fullsize luxury car, back again for another beating in a tough market that runs on badge snobbery. Completely redesigned a few years ago, it only reached the GCC for the 2008 model year. Powered by a capable 3.5-litre V6, it feeds power to the all-wheel-drive platform through a five-speed automatic that includes paddles for manual shifting. The Legend comes all the usual luxury features such as leather, 17-inch alloys, power accessories, cruise control and the like. Some of the more unique ones include Adaptive Front Lighting (AFS) that swivels the HID headlights up to 20 degrees as the car turns, while the "Super Handling" all-wheel-drive system does extremely well to hide the platform's front-wheel-drive origins. Safety features include stability control, dual front airbags, front-side airbags, and side-curtain airbags over all four doors. Noise reduction technology sends an opposite phase signal through the car's audio system to cancel out engine noise. Too bad the car looks like an economy car, while having to manage with a V6 in a field that takes V8 motors for granted.

The fresh Mazda CX-7 five-seater crossover comes in two trim levels for the GCC market, namely a base model with front-wheel-drive and the top version with all-wheel-drive, both mated to a standard 2.3-litre turbocharged "DISI" 4-cylinder engine. The base 2WD GT model gets black fabric upholstery, CD player, manual a/c, cruise control, 18-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, basic trip computer, dual exhaust tips, rear spoiler, folding 60/40 split rear seats, power windows, electric mirrors and four-wheel independent suspension with disc brakes on all corners. The fully-optioned AWD GTX model additionally gets beige leather upholstery, intelligent keyless entry with starter button, Bose 9-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with changer, colour-screen trip computer, powered driver's seat, automatic a/c, xenon headlights, fog lamps, rain-sensing wipers, sunroof and rear-view camera. All models thankfully get ABS, stability control, front and side-curtain airbags and alarm, Mazda choosing not to skimp on safety features.

The ninth generation Chevrolet Malibu made its debut in the GCC as a 2017 model year. It got a slight facelift in 2019, along with a new base engine and improved tech. Under the hood the base model now gets a turbocharged 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed transmission. The other engine on offer is a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine. That one gets an 6-speed auto transmission. Standard features on the base LS model include power steering, electric windows, central locking, halogen headlamps, LED daytime running lamps, single zone A/C, 6-speaker audio system, 7-inch touch screen with Bluetooth, phone projection and navigation, keyless entry, engine push start, fabric seats, cruise control and 16-inch steel wheels. The LT gets additional remote vehicle starter and 17-inch alloy wheels. The sunroof, 8-inch touch screen, and power seats are optional on the LT. On the Premier, additional features include dual exhausts, HID headlamps, LED tail lamps, auto headlight leveling function, dual-zone A/C, 9-speaker Bose audio system, 8-inch touch screen with navigation, USB charge port, leather seats, power seats and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional features on the Premier include sunroof, rearview camera and adaptive cruise control. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS), and traction control. The Premier gets side airbags as well. Other optional safety equipment include lane-keeping assist, blind spot monitor, forward collision alert and rear cross traffic alert.

The VW Multivan is the range-topping minivan based on the T5 Transporter work-van platform. The outdated front-wheel-drive van is powered by an equally-outdated 3.2-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic. Available with 6 or 7 seats, it has a unique rail feature in which seats can slide forward and backward into any configuration. Offered in base Comfortline and upgraded Highline trim, the Multivan can be had with features such as power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, and a CD stereo. It can be optionally outfitted with cloth or leather seats, HID headlights, wood cabin trim, rear DVD entertainment system, sunroof, alloy wheels and automatic doors. A wide range of accessories are available, like tables and refrigerators which fit onto the rails, all movable. The Multivan has safety features as standard such as front and side-curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.
