Standard safety features include front and side airbags, ABS, stability control and optional tyre-pressure monitor.

The Maybach was originally built for the ultra-rich back before World War II. Mercedes-Benz has revived the brand for the ultra-rich of today, as "a business jet on wheels," according to the company, and quite rightly so. The Maybach is offered in two versions currently. The Maybach 57 is the shorter wheelbase model, which is still very large, and this body style comes in either standard 57 trim with a 5.5-litre turbocharged V12, or in 57 S trim with a 6.0-litre turbocharged V12. Both models utilise a five-speed automatic and rear-wheel-drive. Standard features include massive seats, leather interior and wood all over. The cars can be customised according to fat-cat customer wishes, including real gold interior trim, special paint finishes, TV tuner, DVD player, CD changer, telephone, Dolby surround sound system, panoramic glass roof, and, especially for the 62, reclining rear seats. Safety features include all the requisite equipment, including a multitude of airbags and electronic stability systems.

The Infiniti QX56 full-size luxury SUV, based on the Nissan Patrol, was introduced as a 2011 model. The exterior gives away its Nissan origins, save for unique front and rear ends, as well as some trim bits. The QX comes with a 5.6-litre V8 engine with 'VVEL' variable valve timing and 'DIG' direct injection, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission and four-wheel-drive. A new 'Hydraulic Body Motion Control' system is available, which also includes optional 22-inch wheels and a number of other features. The 2011 QX also offers three-row seating, in a 7-seater or 8-seater configuration, with a reclining 3rd row. Inside, standard and optional features include the usual power accessories, a standard Infiniti Hard Drive Navigation System, Bluetooth, Around View Monitor, Bose 2-channel, 13-speaker Premium Audio System, available perforated semi-aniline leather seating, and available DVD entertainment system with dual 7-inch colour monitors which allows different sources to be played at the same time. Included among the new QX's standard entertainment and technology features are an 8-inch WVGA colour touch-screen display, Infiniti Controller for use with the vehicle information systems and comfort and convenience features. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor, lane departure warning, lane departure prevention, blind spot warning. Options include intelligent cruise control, distance control assist, intelligent brake assist with forward collision warning and front pre-crash seat-belts. For 2013, some dealers may be adding aftermarket LED lights on the front bumper to differentiate it as a new model.

For 2014, the Renault Safrance received a minor facelift but mechanically remains the same. It comes with three Nissan-sourced engines. The base model comes with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine and comes standard with a CVT automatic, dual front airbags, ABS, fog lights, manual a/c, keyless entry, power windows, alarm, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo, Bluetooth phone, Renault key card, cruise control with speed limiter, grey fabric seats and 16-inch steel wheels. The base model can be optioned up with a package that includes a tyre pressure monitoring system, dual front-side thorax and curtain airbags, auto headlights, auto windscreen wipers, electrically adjustable and folding door mirrors, dual-zone climate control, leather steering wheel, air quality ioniser, fragrance diffuser, dark carbon fabric seat trim, 17-inch alloys and a rear spoiler. The mid-range model comes with a 2.5-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic, and additionally features stability control with traction control. The top model comes with a 3.5-litre V6 with a 6-speed automatic, and additionally comes with an athermic windshield, electric mirrors with memory function, auto-dimming rear-view mirror, tri-zone climate control, deadlocking with an anti-intruder device, electric rear windows with anti-pinch, Bose CD/MP3 stereo with 10 speakers, Bluetooth phone, Renault keyless smart card, panoramic sunroof, floor mats, cream leather seats, power front seats with massage, integrated rear sunblind, as well as front and rear parking sensors. Items such as HID headlights, dark leather upholstery, 18-inch alloy wheels and an electronic parking brake are optional in some markets.

The Nissan Altima received a minor facelift for the 2010 model year, including a restyled front end, new wheel designs, and new interior options. The Altima will be available with a choice of a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder or a 3.5-litre V6. All versions get the CVT automatic as standard. However, many dealers started offering only the 2.5-litre automatic models from 2011. All GCC-spec Altima models come with a beige interior, in cloth or optional leather. The entertainment system has been upgraded with a optional new Bose premium stereo with nine speakers, optional 4.3-inch colour display, USB port with iPod connectivity, Bluetooth hands-free Phone System, MP3/WMA CD playback, and rear monitor. Also offered is an optional hard-drive navigation system with 6.5-inch VGA colour display, 9.3GB Music Box for music storage and playback, Bluetooth Streaming Audio, DVD player and an RCA input for auxiliary audio/video connectivity. The base 2.5 model gets 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, cloth upholstery, intelligent keyless entry with starter button and manually-adjusted seats. The higher 2.5 models gets 16-inch alloy wheels, Bose stereo, fog lamps, rear camera and cloth upholstery with options such as sunroof and spoiler. And the 3.5 gets 17-inch alloys, power driver's seat, spoiler and optional leather. All Altima models now come with stability control, front and side airbags, and ABS, with options such as side-curtain airbags and a tyre-pressure monitor.

The Genesis is Hyundai's new rear-wheel-drive flagship sedan. It is designed to take on all sorts of established luxury-sport sedans at their own game. Hyundai's attempt at moving upscale is a solid effort at a reasonable price. For the GCC, it is offered only with one engine, namely a standard 3.8-litre V6 with a 6-speed automatic gearbox. The Genesis sedan offers a host of upscale luxury features including Smart Cruise Control, adaptive HID headlights, air suspension and a Lexicon CD audio system with iPod input and 17 speakers. Further features include a power rear sunshade, automatic electronic parking brake, proximity key and push button starter, leather upholstery, eight parking sensors with optional reverse camera, soft-touch instrument panel with woodgrain accents, Bluetooth hands-free mobile phone interface, rain-sensing wipers, sunroof, and a choice of 17-inch and 18-inch alloy wheels. Safety aspects include front, side and curtain airbags, as well as active head restraints, stability control and big ABS-assisted disc brakes. The Genesis is a full-size luxury sedan competing in price with small and medium-sized models from established luxury marques, but Hyundai not having its own premium brand may be a downer for upscale buyers.

The Jeep Gladiator is a 4-door pickup based on a stretched Wrangler platform. Standard power comes from a 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 mated to an 8-speed automatic and four-wheel-drive. All Gladiator models are Trail Rated. Available features include LED headlights and taillights, an 8.4-inch touchscreen, a nine-speaker Alpine premium sound system, keyless entry, front TrailCam camera, blind-spot monitoring, Rear Cross Path detection, rear parking sensors, Advanced Brake Assist, Full-Speed Forward Collision Warning Plus, Adaptive Cruise Control with Stop, Trail Rail Cargo Management System, spray-in bedliner and trailer towing features. Gladiator Rubicon models are equipped with signature red tow hooks, Rock-Trac 4x4 system, featuring a two-speed transfer case with a 4:1 low-range gear ratio, front and rear heavy-duty Dana 44 axles, Tru-Lok electric front- and rear-axle lockers, segment-exclusive electronic sway bar disconnect, cab and bed rock rails. A limited run of 300 Jeep Gladiator Launch Edition models were made available in the Middle East. Along with a Launch Edition badge, the Gladiator has unique design elements including 17-inch mid-gloss black aluminium wheels, 33-inch BFgoodrich tyres, a wrapped instrument panel mid-bolster painted in Monaco silver and black leather seats with red accent stitching. The Launch Edition also features a body-colour hard top and fender flares.

The new-for-2012 BMW 6-Series Gran Coupe is essentially a 6-Series with four doors on a 5-Series platform. The 640i gets a turbocharged 3.0-litre 6-cylinder, mated to an 8-speed automatic with paddle-shifters. The 650i with the 4.4-litre turbocharged V8 and 8-speed auto came at the end of 2012. Some of the wide range of sophisticated driving and comfort features offered in the new BMW 6-Series include Dynamic Drive Control with four modes, namely comfort, normal, sport and sport +, as well as Comfort Start, Head-Up Display, Multi-Channel Audio System, Rear Seat Entertainment, Four-Zone Automatic Air Conditioning and BMW iDrive control. BMW ConnectedDrive also offers a unique range of driver-assist technology functions for enhanced comfort and safety. BMW claims the Gran Coupe is a 4+1 seater, but the rear middle seat offers zero legroom. Aside from the usual power accessories, leather upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo and other common items, available features include Surround View cameras, night vision with pedestrian recognition, Park Assistant, heads-up display, BlackBerry smart phone access via iDrive, Bluetooth interface for phone and e-mails, navigation, turning HID headlights, adaptive cruise control, run-flat tyres, 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels with optional 20-inchers, electronic parking brake, power-adjustable seats with optional ventilation, active steering, standard Drive Dynamic Control to choose from a range of pre-programmed suspension settings, Adaptive Drive for stability, multiple airbags, ABS, traction control, tyre-pressure monitor and more.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG made its debut as a 2014 model year. Slightly taller and wider, the new S65 features a front fascia with a bigger front radiator grille and a slanting rear end. The Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG comes with a twin-turbocharged 6.0-litre V12 engine. Inside, the traditional instrument cluster from the previous generation is gone and is replaced by two high-resolution 8:3 format colour displays, 12.3-inch in size, for controlling comfort settings and infotainment purposes. Seats are fitted with 14 actuated air bladders in the backrest with six different massage programs. For safety the S65 AMG gets "beltbags", which are airbags in the seatbelt webbing, and "cushionbags", which prevent occupants from sliding under the belt. A new climate control, called "thermotronic" features improved filtering of outside air and also an "active perfuming system" for customising the smell of the interior. The new S65 AMG gets "Magic Body Control" which uses cameras to scan the road in advance and adjust the suspension accordingly. Safety features include Active Parking Assist, Active Lane Keeping Assist, Night View Assist Plus, Distronic Plus with Steering Assist, Brake Assist Plus with Cross-Traffic Assist and Pre-Safe Brake with pedestrian recognition.

An all-new Chevrolet Tahoe was released as a 2015 model year. The exterior gets a complete redesign and also technical improvements, which includes a stronger frame. Under the hood is the same 5.3-litre V8 engine, but has been slightly updated for more horsepower and torque. Power is delivered through a 6-speed automatic transmission. In 2019, a Tahoe RST was revealed with a 6.2-litre engine, mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission. Features include a new electric power steering system, power windows, electric mirrors, 12 device-charging locations, AM/FM radio with MP3/AUX/USB support, 4.2-inch display between the instrument panel, an optional 8-inch screen with MyLink infotainment system and alloy rims. The rear seats can fold down flat, allowing for more luggage space. The Tahoe RST gets magnetic ride control, optional Brembo performance brakes, Borla performance exhaust, illuminated black Chevrolet bowties, 22-inch gloss black aluminium wheels and RST badges. Safety features include a front-seat center air bag, forward collision alert, front park assist, lane departure warning, lane change assist, rear cross traffic alert and adaptive cruise control. An advanced anti-theft system can be added which shuts down key systems to make the it almost impossible to move or start.

Toyota introduced an all-new Camry for 2007. The carryover model has been facelifted for 2010, with a new grille, reshaped headlights, LED-style tail lamps and new wheel designs. The Camry remains the same on the inside however. The engine choice remains the same, with the existing 2.4-litre 4-cylinder that dates back to the 2003 version, while the 3.5-litre V6 option is reserved only for the Aurion sedan. The 4-cylinder can be had with a 5-speed manual or a 5-speed automatic. Among various trim levels, the Camry is available with cruise control, electrically-adjustable seats, the usual power accessories, a multi-function driver information display, a decent AM/FM/CD/MP3 stereo, power tilt/slide moonroof, cloth or leather, a keyless entry system, front and optional side airbags, and either steel or alloy wheels. The SE version, known as Touring in some markets, made a comeback in 2011 with a body kit and firmer sports suspension. The Toyota Camry continues to define the commuter-class midsize 4-door sedan segment and should remain competitive, even with its rising base price.

The Ford Escape gets a completely new design for the 2013 model. Slightly longer than the previous model and ditching the V6 motor, the new shape will arrive in the GCC with just the 2.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission and only front-wheel-drive for now. The interior will also receive a major upgrade as it will have the Microsoft SYNC entertainment system we have all come to expect in all Fords. The  Escape comes standard with cloth seats, power door locks, windows and mirrors, tilt steering column, speed controls on the steering wheel, 17-inch alloy wheels and electric power steering.  Upgrades include premium cloth upholstery or leather, power front seats, a power moonroof, cruise control, fog lamps, 18-inch alloy wheels and parking sensors. Escape comes standard with front, side and curtain airbags, ABS brakes and AdvanceTrac with Roll Stability Control. It might get all-wheel-drive in the future, and has decent ground clearance, but it will not have the low range gearing to tackle serious turf.

The BAIC BJ40 is the Chinese brand's offroad-capable SUV. Sharing a lot of design cues from the Jeep Wrangler, the BJ40 Plus is a 5-door version. Under the hood is 2.3-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, radio with USB/AUX, remote key, CD player with touch screen, 6 speakers, leather seats, parking sensors, rearview camera, cruise control and auto headlights.They come with standard front two airbags, ABS brakes and electronic brake distribution (EBD).

The Jaguar XK received a face-lift for 2012. The XK Convertible are powered by a 5.0-litre V8 direct-injection engine, while a supercharged version of the same V8 powers the high-performance XKR. Both engines are mated to a six-speed automatic gearbox with paddle shifters. An even more powerful XKR-S was released in 2012 with the same supercharged 5.0-litre engine but producing even more horsepower. Changes include a new wider front grille, enlarged vents in the lower grille with chrome accents, LED daytime running lights and slightly thinner headlamps. Its rigid chassis and CATS adaptive suspension aim for a smooth ride and sporty cornering. Standard equipment includes DVD navigation, keyless entry and keyless start, a seven-inch video display, Bluetooth capability, cruise control, a 6-CD/MP3 player, rear park assist, cruise control, and electronic parking brake. Options include adaptive cruise control with a forward-alert system that sounds an audible warning, full soft leather upholstery, and a CD stereo system. Safety feature include front and side airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, dynamic stability control with a track feature, and electronic rollover mitigation.

The Chevrolet Camaro Convertible received a facelift for the 2014 model year. Aside from the pointier front-end, the generic tail lamps, the functional new bonnet vents and optional Recaro seats, there aren't any other visible changes. Powered by a 3.6-litre V6 or a 6.2-litre V8, it rides on a shortened rear-wheel-drive Lumina SS platform, with four-wheel independent suspension and 2+2 seating. The Camaro comes in V6 LT and V8 SS trims. The V6 is only available with a 6-speed paddle-shifted automatic in the GCC. The SS gets a choice of two V8 engines, each customised for use with a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic. The automatic V8 features cylinder deactivation to improve fuel economy. StabiliTrak traction control and front-side airbags are standard, while Brembo brakes are available on the SS version. The SS also gets stiffer suspension and adjustable Competitive/Sport modes for stability control and Launch Control on manual models. The ZL1 gets a supercharged 6.2-litre V8 with a 6-speed manual or automatic. The hard-plastic cabin comes with cloth or leather interior, with standard blue LED lighting and optional glow-in-the-dark trim panels. Standard features include air conditioning, power windows and lock, and keyless entry. Available features include heads-up display and a new MyLink entertainment system which includes touchscreen navigation. Standard rims include 18-inch wheels for the V6 and 20-inch ones for the V8. Safety features include front airbags, side airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Kia Sportage was redesigned from the ground up in 2011, and continues largely unchanged for 2015 aside from a very minor facelift. Based on Hyundai underpinnings, it is powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive, or a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder with all-wheel-drive, both engines mated to a 6-speed automatic. The base 2.0-litre FWD model comes with power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth seats, fog lamps, manual a/c, rear spoiler, roof rails, CD/MP3 stereo with 6 speakers and USB/AUX inputs, 17-inch steel wheels, ABS and only a single driver-side airbag. Things get better in the higher trim levels, with the top 2.4-litre AWD model additionally outfitted with dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, cruise control, smart key with starter button, leather upholstery, power driver-side seat, stereo with subwoofer and iPod cable, rear sensors and camera, chrome door handles, electric folding mirrors, 18-inch alloy wheels, navigation and improved safety features such as ABS with stability control, active headrests and two front airbags, though still no side airbags. The Sportage received high ratings in European crash tests, but keep in mind that they apply to a model with six airbags. Some markets have dropped the 2.0-litre model.

The Outback is a crossover wagon heavily based on the Legacy, but with distinct visual and mechanical differences. Like all Subarus, the Outback features permanent all-wheel-drive. Originally introduced as a Legacy trim years ago, it is now a separate model, with higher ground clearance, fender flares and a more utilitarian demeanour. The Legacy-based Outback was completely redesigned for 2005, and only features a facelift for the 2007 model year. Engines include the 2.5-litre four-cylinder in the 2.5i trim, and the 3.0-litre six-cylinder in the 3.0R trim. Both are boxer engines mated to automatic gearboxes. All Outback models feature a MP3/WMA CD stereo, 6-disc CD changer, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, ABS brakes, dual front airbags, alloy Wheels, fog lamps, climate control, cruise control and cloth upholstery. The fully-optioned trim, includes a Vehicle Dynamics Control system, eight airbags, self-levelling rear suspension, dual sunroof, and a leather interior with power seats.

The Ford Expedition is a full-size 4WD that's carried on virtually unchanged since 2007, but started gaining ground in some markets after the demise of the Crown Victoria in 2012. It's smooth, stable and refined for the most part, and this new version goes head-to-head with Chevrolet's non-descript Tahoe for top honours among American 4WDs. Its four-wheel-independent suspension is unusually sophisticated in this class, providing better ride and handling, on-road and off. In 2015, the Expedition comes with turbocharged 3.5-litre V6 engine mated to an automatic gearbox. Expedition is loaded with safety features, and offers an available Roll Stability Control system, which is designed to sense an approaching rollover situation then take action to help prevent it. What the Expedition does best is move large quantities of people and gear, with its perfectly flat cargo area and available PowerFold third-row seat that folds perfectly flat with the press of a button. Able to carry up to eight passengers, the second row features a small center seat that slides forward to give parents in the front seat access to a small child. Options include a rear-seat DVD system and the reverse sensors, among the many standard power features. The longer Expedition EL model has a stretched wheelbase to offer more space.

The Volkswagen Toureg got a facelift in 2015. The petrol engines on offer in this 5-seater is a carryover 3.6-litre V6, and a 4.2-litre V8, both mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel-drive. This VW is a crossover, with independent four-wheel-suspension and a simple terrain-select system. Largely optional features include cloth or leather upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo, navigation, Bluetooth phone, intelligent keyless entry, starter button, panoramic sunroof, real wood trim, power-folding rear seat, adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go function, lane departure warning system, blind-spot monitor, pre-crash system with full automatic emergency braking, ABS, a full set of front and side airbags, parking assist with four cameras, adaptive air suspension with continuous damping control and adaptive roll compensation, LED tail lamps, HID headlights, power-adjustable front seats with memory, seat heaters and a choice of 18-inch, 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels.

The Picanto is one of the smallest cars plying the Middle East's aggressive roads. Powered by a tiny 1.1-litre four-cylinder, it is smaller than a family-size Coke bottle, mated to either a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic. The tall styling makes sure there is fair headroom, though legroom is conservative at best. Standard features include 14-inch steel wheels with full wheel covers, radio cassette player with roof antenna and 4 speakers, manual air-conditioning, combination vinyl-cloth cabin, variable intermittent front wipers, front cup holder, seat belts and, thankfully, a tachometer. Available features in higher trim levels include a rear wiper and washer, rear shelf cover over the luggage area, body-coloured exterior trim pieces and bumpers, a luggage net, and not much else. We believe most markets do not get anything more than seat belts as safety features, although a few markets do get the front-wheel-drive Picanto with all sorts of optional airbags. Anyone who chooses to pilot a Picanto in public is a brave man indeed.

The Japanese-built Tiida has been replaced by a Mexican-built version for the 2011 model year, the benefits of which include a lower price and more available features. Available as a 5-door hatchback or a 4-door sedan, the new-for-2011 Tiida is available with a standard 1.8-litre four-cylinder engine, with a 6-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic. There is good head room and even tall passengers will find rear seat legroom as good as that in many much larger cars. Two trim levels are available, namely the 1.8S and the 1.8SL. Standard features on the 1.8S include electric power steering, tilt steering column, 60/40 split folding rear seats, keyless entry, 15-inch steel wheels, a/c with micro filter, trip computer and a CD/MP3 stereo with AUX input. Moving up the range to a 1.8SL adds cruise control, front fog lamps, power door mirrors and windows, leather-wrapped steering wheel and a wood-grain interior finish and optional 16-inch alloy wheels, among other items. On the safety front, only a driver-side airbag is standard, while ABS, EBD, Brake-Assist, passenger-side front airbag and side-curtain airbags are all extra-cost options.

The Veyron 16.4 was a long-running pet project by Volkswagen to create the fastest production car in the world at the time, reintroducing the Bugatti badge in style. Goofy looks notwithstanding, the styling is an essential part of the design to ensure total stability at top speed. In 2009, a removable roof model was added to the lineup, called the Veyron Grand Sport. The car is powered by an 8.0-litre quad-turbo W16 engine derived from Volkswagen designs, mated to all-wheel-drive and a seven-speed direct-shift automanual gearbox. The fully customisable interior is covered in leather and metal, with numerous features such as CD stereo, navigation and more. The single-piece carbon-fibre monocoque does well in crash tests, while airbags give the driver and passenger additional protection. The high-speed tyres designed specially for the Veyron 16.4 incorporate the PAX System that ensures safe handling even after sudden pressure loss. Another safety element is the rear spoiler that acts as a "˜parachute brake' during emergency braking. A second key must be engaged when stopped to initiate "top speed" mode, when the rear spoiler sets itself to a lower position, the front air diffusers close and the vehicle lowers to further improve aerodynamic downforce. A limited-to-150-pieces Grand Sport model was released in mid-2008 with a removable targa-roof panel.

Maxus G10 is a the Chinese brand's MPV offering. Under the hood, there are two engines. The cargo vans get a naturally aspirated 2.4-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed manual gearbox, while the people carrier gets a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features in the G10 people carrier include power steering, power windows, central locking, electric mirrrors, keyless entry, manual dual-zone A/C, radio with MP3/AUX support and 6 speakers, halogen headlights, front & rear foglights, sliding doors, lift tailgate and 16-inch wheels. The higher models gets LED headlamps, LED taillamps, dual-sliding doors, rear panorama sunroof, leather seats,  7-inch touch screen with DVD system, rearview camera and 18-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD), stability control and traction control.

The Picanto is one of the smallest cars plying the Middle East's aggressive roads. Powered by a tiny 1.1-litre four-cylinder, it is smaller than a family-size Coke bottle, mated to either a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic. The tall styling makes sure there is fair headroom, though legroom is conservative at best. Standard features include 14-inch steel wheels with full wheel covers, radio cassette player with roof antenna and 4 speakers, manual air-conditioning, combination vinyl-cloth cabin, variable intermittent front wipers, front cup holder, seat belts and, thankfully, a tachometer. Available features in higher trim levels include a rear wiper and washer, rear shelf cover over the luggage area, body-coloured exterior trim pieces and bumpers, a luggage net, and not much else. We believe most markets do not get anything more than seat belts as safety features, although a few markets do get the front-wheel-drive Picanto with all sorts of optional airbags. Anyone who chooses to pilot a Picanto in public is a brave man indeed.

The Dodge Durango was completely redesigned in 2011. Mildly facelifted for 2014 with a whole lot of LED lighting, the three-row crossover SUV is based on a stretched Jeep platform. There are now three trim levels, namely the base SXT V6 and SXT Plus V6, the Limited V6 and Limited V8, the R/T V8 and the Citadel V8. The carryover engines, a 3.6-litre V6 and a 5.7-litre V8, all now get a new 8-speed automatic with tiptronic as standard. The base model can be had in rear-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. All higher trim levels are all-wheel-drive, although only the V8 Hemi models get low-range gearing. The SXT model gets 18-inch alloy wheels, tri-zone automatic a/c with rear vents, power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, built-in rechargeable torch, cargo cover, 6-speaker CD/DVD/MP3 touchscreen stereo with 30GB hard drive and audio jack, fog lamps, automatic headlights, hill-start assist and keyless entry. The Limited adds LED running lamps, leather steering wheel, remote start, front power seats with memory, Bluetooth, navigation, auto-dimming rear-view mirror, 9-speaker stereo with subwoofer, power liftgate, chrome roof rails, chrome mirrors with indicators, chrome exhaust tip, rear parking sensors, tyre pressure display, intelligent keyless entry with starter button, and rear-view camera. The R/T model adds leather seats, 20-inch wheels, power-adjustable steering wheel, heated first and second-row seats, HID headlights, body-colour exterior trim, sports suspension, rain-sensitive wipers and more. The top Citadel model adds 20-inch chrome alloys, bigger brakes, heated steering wheel, Nappa perforated leather, ventilated front seats, HID headlights, sunroof, blindspot monitor & cross-path detection, forward collision warning and adaptive cruise control. Some of the Citadel's features seem to be optionally available on the lower trim levels. Standard safety features include front airbags, side and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, rain brake support, anti-theft alarm, active headrests and a tyre-pressure monitor.

The new-for-2011 Mitsubishi ASX is a 5-seater sub-compact crossover based on the Outlander platform and actually shares the exact same wheelbase, but is shorter at the front and especially the rear. The standard engine is a 2.0-litre DOHC 4-cylinder with MIVEC variable valve timing, CVT transmission and either front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. The all-wheel-drive has 2WD, 4WD and 4WD Lock modes. The base model comes with 16-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, cloth seats, soft-touch dash and front door surfaces, CD/MP3 player with AUX and USB ports, ABS-assisted disc brakes, four-wheel independent suspension, up to seven airbags including a knee bag, and an optional panoramic glass roof with mood lighting along the sides. The top model gets 17-inch alloys, a front lip spoiler, intelligent entry with starter button, HID headlights, leather upholstery and a 7-speaker stereo with subwoofer, among other items. Available safety features include the aforementioned airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, hill start assist and emergency braking blinkers.

Launched here in 2005 and facelifted in 2007, the Scorpio is the first Indian consumer vehicle to grace Middle East roads since the disastrous Padmini. Unlike the Fiat-derived outdated Padmini, this 4WD wagon is mostly an original inhouse design and arguably more modern, though not quite up to current standards. Yet, it is good enough to win multiple Indian "Car of the Year" awards. This Mahindra & Mahindra product is available here only in top trim, complete with leather seats, possibly fake wood trim, power windows, central locking, power steering, keyless entry, CD stereo and rear a/c vents. It was restyled lightly for 2007. Interesting features include a low-range transfer case, seating for seven and a Renault-derived engine. However, this 2.0-litre four-cylinder is too weak to move a compact car, let alone this heavyweight 4WD. And even in top trim, there is an obvious lack of safety features other than its perceived bulk. Five of the seven passengers manage with seat belts only, with nothing for the last two inward-facing seats.

The Kyron is this Korean carmaker's entry into the hotly-contested traditional soft-roader category, only they do it with a real 4WD using truck underpinnings and low-range gearing. Two adults will have no trouble fitting in either front or second row. Behind them is plenty of room for their luggage too. The bench seat also folds down nearly flat to accommodate big, awkward loads like bicycles. The weak part is the 2.3-litre four-cylinder engine. The engine is mated to a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic, and power reaches the road through a four-wheel-drive system that even includes low-range gearing. The drive system offers a choice of two-wheel drive, four-wheel high, or four-wheel low. The suspension utilizes double wishbones at the front and a multilink design at the rear. Available electronic aids include ABS, hill descent control, traction control, and brake assist. Available features include cloth or leather upholstery, alloy wheels, CD player, keyless entry, power windows, cruise control and more. Safety features include dual front airbags with optional side airbags.

The new Commander is the first Jeep that offers three-row seating and the ability to carry seven passengers. Available with either a 4.7-litre V8 or a 5.7-litre Hemi V8, they are both mated to a five-speed automatic transmission, and both offer similar fuel economy. Standard is Jeep's Quadra-Trac I, which is an automatic full-time all-wheel-drive system enhanced by electronic traction control. Other standard features on the Commander include AM/FM stereo with CD player, power windows, power mirrors, power eight-way driver's seat, flipper glass on the liftgate with remote control, all-terrain tyres on 17-inch aluminium wheels, tyre-pressure monitoring, and cruise control. The higher-trim Commander comes with the Hemi V8 with fuel-saving Multi-Displacement System technology, a full-time active 4WD system known as Quadra-Trac II, that has a two-speed transfer case with front and rear electronic limited-slip differentials, dual-zone temperature control, leather-trimmed bucket seats with memory, power adjustable pedals, power sunroof,  power front seats and a six-disc in-dash CD player with MP3 capability. Options include rear DVD and 17-inch chrome wheels. Safety includes ABS, electronic stability control, Brake Assist, and numerous airbags.

The Ferrari Roma is the Italian luxury brand's front-engine grand tourer model. Under the hood is a 3.9-litre turbocharged V8 motor, mated to a 8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard features on the car include power windows, keyless entry, power mirrors, central locking, engine push start, leather seats, leather dashboard with stitching, automatic AC, navigation system, xenon headlamps and 20-inch alloy wheels. Options are endless from different leather, Alcantara and carbon-fibre options for the interior, carbon-fibre accessories for the exterior, better stereo system, sports seats, and different wheel options. Safety features include airbags, stability control, traction control, ABS brakes and brake assist.

The Lumina remains the only rear-wheel-drive sedan in the affordable midsize segment. The available 3.6-litre V6 and 6.0-litre V8 motors offer value no one can match. Built in Australia alongside the Caprice, it is brand new from the ground up, and comes in four-door trim only. The Lumina comes in four variants, namely the LS, LTZ, S and SS. The power for the LS, LTZ and body-kitted S comes from the Alloytec 3.6-litre V6 engine with an automatic transmission. The 6.0-litre V8 does its work in the SS sedan with either a 6-speed manual or new 6-speed automatic that replaced the old 4-speed automatic since 2008. The base LS and LTZ models fulfil the basic needs of a commuter car that doubles as a family vehicle, with decent space and adequate power, while the SS models merge muscle-car attitude with a traditional sedan. Available features, standard or optional depending on model, include an MP3-capable CD stereo, CD changer, stability control, ABS brakes, traction control, 16-inch, 17-inch or 18-inch wheels, comfort or sports suspension, trip computer, Bluetooth, cloth or leather upholstery, and various power features.

An all-new Chevrolet Tahoe was released as a 2015 model year. The exterior gets a complete redesign and also technical improvements, which includes a stronger frame. Under the hood is the same 5.3-litre V8 engine, but has been slightly updated for more horsepower and torque. Power is delivered through a 6-speed automatic transmission. Features include a new electric power steering system, power windows, electric mirrors, 12 device-charging locations, AM/FM radio with MP3/AUX/USB support, 4.2-inch display between the instrument panel, an optional 8-inch screen with MyLink infotainment system and alloy rims. The rear seats can now fold down flat, allowing for more luggage space. Safety features include a front-seat center air bag, forward collision alert, front park assist, lane departure warning, lane change assist, rear cross traffic alert and adaptive cruise control. An advanced anti-theft system can be added which shuts down key systems to make the it almost impossible to move or start.

The Audi RS 5 Sportback is being sold, but mostly only on special order. It made its debut in the GCC in 2020. It gets a twin turbocharged 2.9-litre V6 engine with a 8-speed automatic. Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control. The exterior gets more aggressive bumpers to differentiate from the standard A5 Sportback.

The goofy B-Class is touted as a Compact Sports Tourer, when it really is a tall hatchback. Though the A-Class is still in production, its sale seems to have been cancelled here, with this one taking its place. Mercedes-Benz is also touting their the sandwich concept, to which it credits the space-saving arrangement of the engine and transmission partly in front of and partly beneath the passenger cell, which in turn offers the interior spaciousness of larger saloons and estate cars despite its compact external dimensions. There is a height-adjustable load compartment floor, an asymmetrically divided, folding and removable rear seat unit plus an optionally removable front passenger seat, all of which allows conversion from a comfortable touring car to a practical van. Models include the B 150, the B 170, the B 200 and the B 200 Turbo, all four-cylinder, rear-wheel-drive, and available with a choice of manual or CVT automatic, plus all the creature comforts and safety features of a Mercedes-Benz.

The second-generation Peugeot 308 went on sale in the GCC in 2015. The same  is turbocharged 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engines carried over from the previous shape, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. In 2019, it got a slight facelift and interior upgrades. Even the most basic model gets driver & passenger airbags, ABS brakes with EBD, trip computer, AM/FM Radio with CD/MP3 player with remote stalk, speed-sensitive power steering, electric windows and mirrors, cooling vent inside the glove compartment, height-adjustable headlights, split-folding rear seats, remote key with central locking, and 15-inch wheels. Moving up to the higher trim levels adds items such as side-curtain airbags, stability control, navigation system, dual-zone automatic a/c with rear vents, CD/MP3 player with bluetooth and AUX input, 5-CD changer, panoramic sunroof with automatic curtain, cruise control, automatic headlights, rain-sensing wipers, leather seats with chrome interior trim, auto-dimming mirror, foldable door mirrors, fog lights, parking sensors, front and rear armrests,  16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and automatic tyre pressure sensors. Inside and out, it is a classy hatchback for its category, making it almost as good as any of the premium-branded compacts.

In addition to a sedan version, the Impreza has now become a hatchback for 2008, with interior and exterior styling solidly in the mainstream of conservative design. It remains the only car in its class with standard full-time all-wheel drive. Subaru likes to tout their rally heritage, but none of the Middle East models are anywhere near rally cars. The models offered here are the new 1.5-litre, known as the 1.5i, and the 2.0-litre, known as the 2.0R. Both have flat 4-cylinder "boxer" engines, and both mated to either a 5-speed manual or an outdated 4-speed automatic. Base models have a standard AM/FM stereo system, cloth upholstery, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking and steel wheels, along with dual front airbags. The full-spec 2.0R model features the same full power options, alloy wheels, rear spoiler, ABS brakes, dual front airbags, fog lamps, sunroof and not much else. Western and Eastern world markets receive turbocharged WRX sports models, but local dealers do not officially offer them in the GCC.

The Abarth 595 Competizione is based on the Fiat 500. The front end was redesigned with a much larger air scoop to improve heat management in the engine compartment and increase cooling capacity by 18%. The extractor is quite pronounced on the rear bumper. To enhance its looks, specific bumper inserts have also been created with the Tar Cold Grey finish on the 595 Competizione. It has polyelliptical headlights and LED daytime running lights as standard equipment. Xenon headlights, on the other hand, are available on request. The standard flat-bottomed steering wheel, as well as other striking interior details, on the Competizione version is made of technical materials, such as carbon and Alcantara. Abarth 595 Competizione is equipped with a 1.4-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine mated to an Abarth sequential gearbox and fits the new Record Monza Attivo exhaust. The 595 Competizione is equipped with supporting shell-shaped "Abarth Corsa by Sabelt" seats. Braking is secured by a Brembo system with 4-piston aluminium monobloc fixed callipers paired with self-ventilating, perforated 305 mm discs. Koni FSD (Frequency Selective Damping) shock absorbers are standard on both front and rear. The Sport button can be used to adjust various parameters of the car, such as torque delivery and power steering calibration, as well as managing the exhaust. Furthermore, the system adjusts engine response to the accelerator pedal and the TFT instrument panel switches to racing configuration. Safety standards are high with the Abarth 595 equipped with seven airbags as standard equipment. It also gets ABS with electronic brake distribution (EBD), electronic stability control (ESC), anti-slip regulation (ASR) system, the Hill Holder devices and hydraulic brake assistance (HBA) to help with emergency stops.

The Sorento is an attractive entry into the crowded affordable 4WD market. Offering either a 2.4-litre four-cylinder with a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic, or a 3.5-litre V6 with a 4-speed automatic in early models and a 5-speed automatic since 2005, the Sorento offers decent off-road ability and a fair bit of interior space, making it a good buy, given its price. Standard features include 16-inch alloy wheels, radio cassette with antenna and 6 speakers, manual air-conditioning, power steering, 8-way adjustable driver seat, 4-way adjustable passenger seat, power windows, 60/40 split folding rear seat, battery saver, driver airbag, proper rear lift gate, power door locks, and limited slip differential. Available features in higher models include a CD player with power antenna and 8 speakers, ABS brakes, power folding mirrors and cruise control. Four-wheel independent suspension and four-wheel disc brakes make it a good road cruiser, unlike truck-based 4WDs, although it is still no sports car.

Toyota has finally launched the 2011 Scion tC in the GCC, only it will be known as the Toyota Zelas in the GCC, and will come standard with an aggressive body kit. The all-new 5-seater Zelas is powered by a Camry-derived 2.5-litre VVT-i 4-cylinder engine, with front-wheel-drive and a standard 6-speed automatic with tiptronic. The two-door coupe has four-wheel-independent suspension with MacPherson struts up front and double-wishbone rear, as well as four-wheel-disc brakes, vented at the front and solid rear. The Zelas comes in only two trim levels. The rather-loaded base trim comes with an 8-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with USB port and 6-disc CD changer, Bluetooth, keyless entry, cloth upholstery, manual a/c, power windows, folding electric mirrors, ABS, stability control, front and side airbags, spilt-folding rear seat, fog lamps, 17-inch alloys with 215/50 tyres, parking sensors, leather steering wheel with controls, rear spoiler and the body kit. The top version adds leather upholstery, cruise control, paddle shifters and smart keyless entry with starter button. Curiously, neither a sunroof nor a manual gearbox is available. Toyota says they are going to promote it as a tuner car.

The 206 is one of Peugeot's more popular models, with a wide range of body styles, trim levels and engine choices. Its design has changed little since its launch in 1999, although new derivatives such as the 206 CC Cabriolet joined the line-up in 2001. There are various petrol engines in the range, although after 2006, the local offerings had decreased. The standard five-door hatchback can be had with a 1.4-litre or a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine with either a manual or an automatic. The 206 CC coupe-cabriolet can only be had as a 1.6-litre automatic in the later years, although the manual 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre CC models were available here for a few years in between. There is a more powerful 2.0-litre engine with a manual offered in three-door RC hatchback form, which is a true sporting contender. The tuned RC debuted in 2003, replacing the competent GTi 2.0-litre model. All models come with front power windows, a cloth interior, driver's airbag and other basics as standard. Comprehensive safety equipment such as ABS with electronic brakeforce distribution, Emergency Brake Assist, ESP and traction control, along with passenger front airbag, were all optional. Available features included a CD player, alloy wheels and more.

The F-150 delivers all the manly attributes of toughness, strength, and imposing size, but does anyone who isn't involved in a job with physical labour need one? The fully-loaded models of the F-150 is sold here as more of a lifestyle vehicle, offering interior design and comfort that would rival some luxury cars. Properly equipped, it can haul more than a tonne in its bed. The F-150 is comfortable as well, with a quiet and refined ride. It comes with dual frontal airbags, cloth seats, a CD player, and air conditioning as standard. A host of power and luxury options are available too. For all these reasons, the F-150 has sadly been America's best-selling full-size pickup for 28 consecutive years. It is the most most profitable vehicle Ford makes. It is available in various trim levels, variations, and specialty models, including quad cab, single cab and dual cab model, with various bed sizes. At the bottom of the lineup is a V6 work truck, though the only options apparently offered here are the 4.6-litre V8 and the 5.4-litre V8 engines, with automatic trannies.

Released in 2003, and ever so slightly redesigned for 2006, the Mazda 6, also known as the grammatically-incorrect Mazda6, is the sportiest among the current crop of front-wheel-drive midsize family cars, but only in terms of handling. The Mazda 6 was originally designed for the driving enthusiast, with choices of V6 and turbocharged engines, but the Middle East market only gets a pathetic 2.0-litre and a reasonable 2.3-litre engine, both of which are four-cylinder and come with a choice of manual or automatic. The 2.0-litre comes in the four-door sedan and an attractive five-door station wagon body style, while the 2.3-litre comes in the four-door sedan shape as well as a sporty five-door liftback , as long in length as the sedan. Standard features include power windows, central locking, basic stereo system with 4 speakers, dual airbags for driver and front passenger, and available ABS brakes with Electronic Brakeforce Distribution. Options include a full body kit, rear spoiler, fog lamps, 6 CD changer, cruise control, alloy wheels, sunroof and leather seats.

The Hyundai Azera, newly-redesigned for 2012, fills the gap between the Sonata and the Genesis sedan. The front-wheel-drive full-size sedan comes with two engine choices, a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder and a 3.0-litre V6, but some GCC markets get only the V6. Both engines get a standard 6-speed automatic. The 2.4-litre version gets smart keyless entry with starter button, mood lighting, available panoramic sunroof, fake wood trim, rear sunshade, CD/MP3 stereo, auto-dimming mirror, electric parking brake with auto hold, leather powered seats, fog lamps, parking sensors, and 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels. The 3.0-litre version additionally gets xenon lights, memory and seat massage for driver, Infinity stereo, heating & cooling for front seats, electric tilt & telescopic steering wheel, Bluetooth, tyre pressure monitoring system, electric folding mirrors, adaptive cruise control, rain sensor and dual-zone a/c. The top model gets a navigation and DVD entertainment system with rear camera. All models get 8 airbags and ABS with EBD, while only the V6 gets stability control.

The redesigned Jaguar XK was the long-awaited successor to Jaguar's sports car franchise back in 2007. For 2010, the Jaguar XK Convertible is powered by a new 5.0-litre V8 direct-injection engine, while in 2011, a new supercharged version of the same V8 powers the high-performance XKR Convertible. Both engines are mated to a six-speed automatic gearbox with paddle shifters. Other changes include a new front bumper, new side mirrors with integrated LED side repeater, rear bumper spoiler, rear LED lights and colour-coded side vents. Its rigid chassis and the latest CATS adaptive suspension aim for a smooth ride and sporty cornering. Standard equipment includes DVD navigation, keyless entry and keyless start, a seven-inch video display, Bluetooth capability, cruise control, a 6-CD/MP3 player, rear park assist, cruise control, and electronic parking brake. Options include adaptive cruise control with a forward-alert system that sounds an audible warning, full soft leather upholstery, and a CD stereo system. Safety feature include front and side airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, dynamic stability control with a track feature, and electronic rollover mitigation.

The Volvo XC60 was launched with high hopes for the Swedish company, capitalising on the small crossover vehicle market. The XC60 is a 5-seater crossover SUV that is aimed at attracting luxury-brand buyers. In 2017, only the T5 model was offered in the region, which comes with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder with a 8-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive. The smallest XC model includes safety technology, Volvo's City Safety system, designed to help a driver avoid a collision at under 30 kph, or reduce the speed of impact at higher speeds by hitting the brakes if the vehicle in front suddenly stops and City Safety determines that a collision is likely. Other safety features on the XC60 is Pre-Prepared Restraints that uses a laser sensor that interacts with other technology to control the airbags and adaptive seatbelt load limiters. Other features, depending on trim level, include cloth or leather upholstery, blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, reverse camera, keyless entry, sunroof, alloy wheels, common power accessories and a CD/MP3 stereo. An R-Design body kit is optional. Standard safety features include front and side-surtain airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, and whiplash-protection headrests. A software-based Polestar power upgrade is also offered, adding 20-30 hp, depending on the model.

The Ford Tourneo Custom is the commercial van offering for carrying passengers. It can seat up to 8 people, offers 2 roof heights (low and high) and two wheelbases (SWB and LWB). The 2021 Ford Tourneo Custom comes with a 2.2-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder diesel engine. Standard features include power steering, power windows, power windows, keyless entry, AM/FM radio with 4 speakers,  SYNC, 3.5-multifunctional display, Bluetooth and AUX, halogen headlamps, manual A/C, fabric seats and 16-inch steel wheels. Safety features on the 2021 Ford Tourneo Custom include Electronic Stability Program (ESP) ,ABS, roll movement intervention, emergency brake assist [EBA], hill hold assist [HHA], traction control, tire pressure monitoring system and emergency brake light flashers.

The Freestar is a capable full-size minivan that is a solid performer, but is outclassed by newer entries. However, it is well-equipped, easily hauling seven passengers, and has a deep well behind the third row that is perfect for groceries. Fold the third-row seat into the floor, and the Freestar holds four passengers and offers a big, flat cargo area behind the seats. The third row can flip around to function as a tailgate seat, while options include a power rear liftgate and dual power sliding doors. On the highway, the Freestar is smooth and quiet, moved along by either a 4.2-litre V6. It doesn't feel as refined as the best and newest of the minivans, but it's strongest suit is safety, with dual-stage driver and front-passenger air bags standard, while the optional Safety Canopy airbags can help protect against head injuries in a rollover or side impact. The Freestar comes standard with ABS brakes with electronic brake-force distribution, a tyre-pressure monitor is standard and optional AdvanceTrac electronic stability control.

The Genesis G90 is the the first model to be released after its parent company Hyundai decided to make Genesis a separate luxury brand. The G90 is their flagship sedan and it comes in the GCC with three engine options. The base engine is the 3.8-litre V6 which was found in the Centennial, while the other two new additions are the turbocharged 3.3-litre V6 motor and the 5.0-litre V8. Standard options in the G90 include power steering, power windows, electric folding mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push engine start-stop, leather upholstery, memory and ventilated seats, audio system with AUX/USB support, auto A/C, navigation, auto defog system, rain sensors, sunroof, parking assist system, rear electric curtain, xenon headlamps, LED headlights and taillights with LED daytime running lamps, front and rear camera, air suspension and 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include 9 airbags, lane keep assist, adaptive cruise control, ABS, traction control, stability control, brake assist, blind spot detection and autonomous emergency braking (AEB).

An all-new model of the BMW X4 came out for the 2019 model. The X4 20i and X4 xDrive30i feature a turbocharged 2.0-liter 4-cylinder engine, with two different tunes. Both are available with a standard 8-speed sport automatic. The X4 M40i is available with a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 cylinder motor, mated to an 8-speed auto transmission as well. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, leather seats, automatic A/C and FM radio and entertainment system with USB/iPod/Bluetooth support. Optional features include a new generation of BMW Navigation System, full-color BMW Head-Up Display, Driving Assistant Plus which warns the driver of a potential collision with a pedestrian and BMW Active Cruise Control with Stop & Go. Safety features are always good with BMW and standard equipment include driver and passenger airbags, ABS and dynamic stability control (DSC).

The Dodge Challenger received a minor facelift and new engine upgrades in 2015. The interior has been significantly improved as well. The Challenger utilises retro styling that is largely a rethinking of the original 1970s Challenger's 2-door design. The interior gets upgraded with a bit more gadgetry in the form of an 8.4-inch Uconnect infotainment system and 7-inch customization display between the retro-inspired speedometer and tachometer. With a high-sill center aluminium gauge bezels makes the revamped interior extremely pleasing to the eyes. Through the Uconnect interface, you can now access the all-new Dodge performance pages that allows you to select different driving modes to adjust steering effort, engine and transmission response, electronic stability and traction controls, and standard launch control. It can also be optioned with a forward collision warning, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring and rear cross path detection.Sharing its platform, engine and mechanicals with other fullsize rear-wheel-drive Chrysler cars, the Challenger can be had with a 3.6-litre V6 or a 5.7-litre V8. Standard features in the V6 include sporty suspension, cloth upholstery, alloy wheels, keyless entry with starter button, CD/MP3 stereo, power accessories and not much else. Also available are a sunroof, racing stripes, rear sensors with camera, and the UConnect touchscreen multimedia system with voice controls as well as navigation, hard drive and Bluetooth phone. Safety features include ABS, stability control, front,side and curtain airbags.

The all-new Kia Stinger came out as a 2018 model year and is the Korean brand's grand tourer model on offer. Under the hood, it gets two engine choices - the standard engine is a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder motor and the higher option is the 3.3-litre turbocharged V6 unit. Both engines are mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The Stinger comes as rear-wheel drive standard and optional all-wheel-drive. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, remote locking, central locking, leather seats, and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment include real leather upholstery, 8-inch screen with navigation, 19-inch alloy wheels, heads up display, ventilated front seats and remote start. Safety features include front, side and knee airbags, ABS, ESP, traction control and brake assist. Optional safety features include blind spot monition, front collision warning, parking distance warning front and back and rear cross-traffic alert.

All A5 versions feature a loudmouth grille framed by rectangular headlights, a very thick C-pillar, frameless windows, and a waistline that flows upwards around the wheel arches. The Audi A5 Cabriolet is powered by either a 1.8-litre 4-cylinder turbo engine, 2.0-litre turbo 4-cylinder or a 3.0-litre V6 supercharged engine. Power is delivered through a CVT transmission for the front-wheel-drive 1.8-litre version, and a 7-speed tiptronic auto transmission for the Quattro all-wheel-drive versions. Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The latest ScÃ©nic is based on the Megane platform. It is what could be called a compact people carrier, with a longer seven-seater version also available, called the Grand ScÃ©nic, with a longer wheelbase and rear overhang, and with two small child-sized seats in the enlarged luggage area. It is available in the region with a 2.0-litre four-cylinder with an automatic. The Scenic employs Renault's new corporate styling cues and technology, such as the Renault Card keyless immobiliser and an automatic parking brake on some trim levels. Features include folding front passenger seat with integrated table, automatic headlights and windscreen wipers, 'child minder' mirror, and front and rear electric windows. An optional upgrade enables all the exterior body mouldings to be painted to match the bodywork. Safety features include dual front airbags, front lateral airbags, side curtain airbags, and ABS brakes with Electronic Brakeforce Distribution and Brake Assist.

The BMW 8-Series nameplate came back to the line-up in 2019. The 8-Series Convertible came to the GCC in 2020. Under the hood, it comes with a 4.4-litre turbocharged V8 engine, coupled with an 8-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive. Some of the wide range of sophisticated driving and comfort features offered in the new BMW 8-Series include Dynamic Drive Control with four modes, namely comfort, normal, sport and sport+, as well as Comfort Start, Head-Up Display, Multi-Channel Audio System, Rear Seat Entertainment, Four-Zone Automatic Air Conditioning and BMW iDrive control. BMW ConnectedDrive also offers a unique range of driver-assist technology functions for enhanced comfort and safety. The BMW 8-Series comes with a Parking Assistant, an optional feature that facilitates the process of parking, as well as Active Cruise Control, Surround View and Rear View Camera, Lane Departure Warning, Lane Change Warning and BMW Night Vision with pedestrian recognition.

The Gen2 is probably the most competitive model in Proton's line-up. Its chassis is engineered with the help of Proton-owned sports car maker Lotus, with engines derived from Mitsubishi. Powered by a 1.6-litre four-cylinder, this five-door hatchback can be had with either a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic. The car is available with cloth upholstery, front power windows, trip computer, 60/40 split folding rear seats, keyless entry, 15-inch alloy wheels, central locking and CD stereo with four speakers and steering wheel-mounted controls. Options include a 10-disc CD changer, rear power windows, rear spoiler, cruise control, leather seating, fog lamps and metallic paint. Safety features include optional ABS brakes, dual front airbags and seat-belts for all seating positions. The Gen2 is not available in all Middle East markets. As far as we know, it is only available in a handful of GCC countries, and might not offer all the optional extras. It first came to Saudi Arabia in 2007, and UAE in late 2011.

The F-150 delivers all the manly attributes of toughness, strength, and imposing size, although it is largely sold here as a fashion statement for tiny men. Redesigned for 2009 and updated in 2011, the fully-loaded F-150 crew-cab is sold here as more of a lifestyle vehicle, offering interior design and comfort that would rival some luxury cars. Properly equipped, it can haul more than a tonne in its bed. The F-150 is comfortable as well, with a quiet and refined ride. It comes with dual front and side airbags, cloth or leatherette seats, CD/MP3 stereo, and air conditioning as standard. Other available features include an optional 4.2-inch LCD screen, hill descent control, electronic locking differential settings and stability control. A host of power and luxury options are available too. For all these reasons, the F-150 has been America's best-selling full-size pickup for nearly 30 consecutive years. It is the most most profitable vehicle Ford makes. It is available in various trim levels, variations, and specialty models, including quad cab, single cab and dual cab model, with various bed sizes. New engines redefined the line-up for 2011, with a new 3.7-litre V6 and a new 5.0-litre V8, both from the Mustang, and fitted with automatic transmissions and a choice of rear-wheel-drive or four-wheel-drive. The top version is called the Platinum, while a special Harley-Davidson trim is also available. The F-150 SVT Raptor also became available on special-order, in 6.2-litre V8 form, and identifiable by its unique body mods and aggressive offroad suspension.

The new Audi Q5 is the smallest offering in the German manufacturer's limited SUV range, peddling its entry in the compact luxury 4WD field. The Q5 is available in the GCC with either a 2.0-litre turbocharged FSI 4-cylinder or a 3.2-litre FSI V6, both lifted from other VW products. Both versions come standard with an 'S-tronic' 7-speed dual-clutch automanual transmission. Also standard is Audi's Quattro all-wheel-drive system, and will be available with the Audi 'Drive-Select' system to change its settings. Features include LED running lights and taillights, alloy wheels of up to 20 inches in size, seating for five with folding rear bench and a foldable front seat, and the usual power accessories. The Q5 will be available in several different trim options, including an 'S-Line' trim option with aggressive body mouldings and mesh foglight grills, while a faux 'Offroad' exterior package includes front and rear underbody protection panels, along with flared fender and door sill protection. Other available features, whether standard or optional, include a roof load sensor to adjust the stability control for the higher centre of gravity, rearview camera, navigation, high-beam assistant that automatically switches between the high and low beams, blind-spot monitor, adaptive cruise control, triple-zone climate control, intelligent keyless entry, electric parking brake, multiple airbags, MMI multimedia with speech control system, Bluetooth telephone, a DVD drive and TV tuner, an iPod interface and MP3 capability.

In 2013, the Audi R8 Spyder got a facelift. The R8 is Audi's two-seat, mid-engine sports car that incorporates technology from Audi's Le Mans-winning R8 prototype to build on its racing success for the street. The production version of the Audi R8 sports car debuted at the Mondial de l'Automobile in Paris in the fall of 2006, with the dramatic design remaining very true to the Le Mans quattro concept car first seen in 2003. The Audi R8 goes for the supercar look with its wide lowered stance, mid-engined setup and air-intake overkill. Based on the Lamborghini Gallardo platform, Audi added their own weird ideas of design, such as out-of-place "blade" of carbon fibre on each side, the gaping front end and LED headlight elements. The convertible made its debut in 2011. The standard Audi R8 is powered by a 4.2-litre aluminium V8 with FSI direct fuel injection and quattro all-wheel drive. There is also a more powerful 5.2-litre V10 engine. The power is delivered through either a 6-speed manual or a R-tronic sequential manual gearbox that uses the same transmission and clutch but operates the clutch and changes gears automatically. The cabin is outfitted to luxury standards, with leather upholstery, power features and decent space. Luggage compartments are in the front and in the back. Safety features include the usual airbags and electronic nannies.

The Gullwing is back for 2010 on a completely new and unique platform, paying homage to the original 1954 Mercedes-Benz 300SL Gullwing. But the Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG is supposed to be an everyday-use supercar, ditching McLaren in favour of in-house development by AMG. The car's trademark feature is the set of 'gullwing' doors that open upwards, requiring less room to open than conventional coupe doors. Underneath the long bonnet is the usual AMG-built 6.2-litre V8 engine, retuned and mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automanual gearbox in this application. A lightweight structure molded largely from carbon-fibre and aluminium double-wishbone suspension form the basics of the SLS. Among other things, the centre console incorporates the AMG DRIVE UNIT, which enables SLS owners to customise their vehicle set-up, while the AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT 7-speed sports transmission is operated by means of the E-SELECT lever. Beyond the usual power accessories and comfort features such as automatic a/c and cruise control, the simplistic interior can be customised in various colours, and can be fitted with options such as sports seats, metal trim, various leather choices, nicer paint and carbon-fibre appliquÃ©s. Further options include different 19-inch and 20-inch alloy wheels, carbon-ceramic brakes, pricey Bang & Olufsen stereo and a sports steering wheel.

The Maxima was a hot car when it was first unveiled in this iteration. However, Nissan's GCC division chose to let this model stagnate to the point where it was easily overshadowed by the newer Altima, even when the Maxima was redesigned in other markets and transformed into a luxury cruiser. The GCC-spec Maxima also still uses Nissan's older version of the corporate V6, with a displacement of 3.0-litre, combined with front-wheel-drive, and with a choice of five-speed manual and four-speed auto gearboxes. Performance is very respectable even after all these years. It comes with automatic air-conditioning, CD player, power windows, power mirrors, power locks with remote keyless entry, ABS-assisted disc brakes, cloth seats, front airbags and many wheel choices, depending on model. The basic model gets 15-inch steel wheels, while higher models get 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels. Options include an in-dash CD changer with subwoofer, cruise control, sunroof, rear electric sunshade and leather cabin trim. Changes from year to year largely involve a new grille style every few years.

The Mondeo is a midsize front-wheel-drive built in Europe that is based on a Mazda platform. It loses out to the Japanese with a combination of engines that lag behind in power, its smaller size and its expensive dealer maintenance charges. The Mondeo actually a good family sedan, but its image is also diluted due to fleet sales as taxis. The Mondeo is a tremendous success in Europe though, simply because its handling is outstanding, rivalling more expensive cars like Alfa Romeo, all for a very affordable price. The interior is fairly attractive and put together well. The Mondeo does have a sizeable interior for its size. The base Mondeo is powered by the 2.0-litre four-cylinder engine, available with either a manual or an automatic transmission. A 2.5-litre V6 engine is coupled with a five-speed automatic transmission in the higher model. The sporty Mondeo ST220, a great car, is powered by a 3.0-litre V6 engine and a six-speed manual transmission. The Mondeo can also be had as a wagon.

The BMW 5-Series Gran Turismo received a facelift for the 2014 model year. The 5-Series GT is supposed to be a coupe-like crossover vehicle that aims to appeal to markets where the 5-Series wagon is ignored. The 'F07' platform features a unique "bi-modal" trunk which may be opened in traditional sedan fashion, or the entire hatch may open like a hatchback. The 2014 model gets a new front air intake, while the back has been extended rearwards to give it a lower slung appearance. Also boot capacity has been increased by 60 litres to total up to 500 litres. Tech features include four-wheel multilink suspension, standard 8-speed automatic gearboxes and turbo engines, namely the 3.0-litre inline-6 for the 535i GT and the 4.4-litre V8 for the 550i GT. Depending on trim level, the 4-seater GT can be outfitted with features such as leather upholstery, 4-zone automatic a/c, Bluetooth, navigation, USB/iPod port, CD/MP3 stereo with 80 GB hard disc, rear DVD entertainment system, heads-up display, panoramic glass roof, adaptive cruise control with stop-&-go feature, blind spot monitor, lane departure warning system, night vision, active steering, rear-wheel steering, rearview camera, side-view cameras, parking sensors, run-flat tyres and keyless button-start, among others. Also included are various selectable driving modes, adjustable air suspension, stability control and numerous airbags. The niche vehicle is almost as long as the 7-Series and has as much headroom as the X5.

Mercedes-Benz GLC replaced the GLK and also added a Coupe model in 2017. It has remained the same for the 2018 model year. Under the hood, the GLC Coupe 250 gets a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine. Power is delivered via a 9-speed automatic transmission. Features include AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Ford Tourneo Custom is the commercial van offering for carrying passengers. It can seat up to 8 people, offers 2 roof heights (low and high) and two wheelbases (SWB and LWB). The 2020 Ford Tourneo Custom comes with a 2.2-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder diesel engine. Standard features include power steering, power windows, power windows, keyless entry, AM/FM radio with 4 speakers,  SYNC, 3.5-multifunctional display, Bluetooth and AUX, halogen headlamps, manual A/C, fabric seats and 16-inch steel wheels. Safety features on the 2020 Ford Tourneo Custom include Electronic Stability Program (ESP) ,ABS, roll movement intervention, emergency brake assist [EBA], hill hold assist [HHA], traction control, tire pressure monitoring system and emergency brake light flashers.

The 3008, a crossover in the truest sense of the word, first debuted in Europe back in 2009 before making its way to the GCC in 2010 as a 2011 model. It got a facelift in 2014. The 3008 is Peugeot's attempt to fill a vague niche, somewhere between a compact SUV and a midsize sedan. Only a 1.6-litre turbo 4-cylinder with a 6-speed automatic is offered here. Despite minivan looks, it seats just five, with a split tailgate, split-folding rear seat, rear-seat floor storage compartment, foldable front passenger seat and a two-level cargo hold. Features include tinted glass, 17-inch alloy wheels, rear wiper, dual-zone automatic a/c with rear ducts, panoramic roof with electric curtain, CD/MP3 stereo with Bluetooth and USB port, automatic headlights and wipers, one-touch power windows, electric foldable mirrors with indicator lights, adjustable leather steering wheel, cruise control, cooled front storage compartment, cargo net, fog lamps, speed-sensitive power steering, parking sensors, keyless entry, rear-seat 12V plug-point, heads-up display and a detachable map-reading torch in the boot. Safety features include six airbags, ABS with EBD, stability control and emergency braking assist.

Combining extreme power and a chop-top body, the all-new Dodge Charger delivers an experience like no other, except maybe for its sibling, the Chrysler 300C. Available with a 3.5-litre "High-Output" V6 engine or the infamous 5.7-litre HEMI V8 engine, but the SRT-8 6.1-litre HEMI V8 has been left out of the GCC. The Dodge Charger races into the local market with contemporary, provocative styling and substance with all the conveniences of a modern sedan. The 5.7-litre HEMI V8 engine comes with the Multi-Displacement System, also known as MDS, that seamlessly deactivates four cylinders in just 40 milliseconds when full V8 power is not needed, improving fuel economy by as much as 20 percent, though fuel economy is still far from impressive. Either engine is mated to a fully automatic five-speed transmission with AutoStick. In addition to the Charger's aggressive design, features include standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP), ABS brakes, all-speed traction control and optional DVD entertainment. Some dealers offer an expensive upgrade kit to make the R/T look like a faux SRT-8.

The Cadillac XT5 debuted in 2017 as an all-new model and is considered a luxury midsize crossover. Under the hood, it gets a 3.6-litre V6 engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The V6 engine features cylinder deactivation and engine stop/start when idle to improve fuel economy. A 2.0-litre turbocharged engine could debut later. The all-wheel-drive is powered by a "twin-clutch" system which is capable of sending 100-percent torque to the front or rear axle. Standard features include power windows, power mirrors, LED headlights and tail lamps and fog lamps. Optional equipment include Cadillac's CUE entertainment system with BOSE speakers, magnetic ride control, alloy wheels and adaptive forward lighting. Safety features include ABS and traction control, sensors to warn driver of potential dangers, safety seat alert which sends immediate impulse through the seat cushion from the direction of the potential hazard.

The Dodge Challenger debuted in 2008, went on sale in the GCC by 2010, and has already been upgraded for the 2011 model year. The Challenger utilises retro styling that is largely a rethinking of the original 1970s Challenger's 2-door design. From this version, the Challenger became available in V6-powered base trim in the GCC. Sharing its platform, engine and mechanicals with other fullsize rear-wheel-drive Chrysler cars, the Challenger packs either a 3.6-litre V6 mated to a 5-speed automatic. Standard features in the V6 include sporty suspension, cloth upholstery, alloy wheels, keyless entry with starter button, CD/MP3 stereo, power accessories and not much else. Also available are a sunroof, racing stripes, rear sensors with camera, and the UConnect touchscreen multimedia system with voice controls as well as navigation, hard drive and Bluetooth phone. Safety features include ABS, stability control, front and side airbags.

The Jaguar XJ is generally available in four trim levels in SWB and LWB versions. The UAE and some other GCC markets will only see the Premium Luxury, Portfolio and SuperSport versions, all in LWB form. The XJ Premium Luxury and the Portfolio will be available with a 5.0-litre naturally-aspirated V8. The XJ Portfolio can also be optioned up with a 5.0-litre supercharged V8. The SuperSport comes exclusively with a higher-tuned 5.0-litre supercharged V8. Finally a supercharged 3.0-litre V6 engine completes the line-up. All models are rear-wheel-drive mated with 8-speed automatic gearboxes. Features include an aluminium body, air suspension, "Adaptive Dynamics" continuously-variable damping, adaptive cruise control, keyless entry and start, "Active Differential Control" and quick-ratio power steering. Customers can have their choice in colours, veneers and leathers. Inside the car, there is a 12.3-inch LCD with virtual Instruments, Dual-View 8-inch touchscreen, navigation, optional 1200W Bowers & Wilkins system, hard drive and connectivity for portable audio and video devices via a "Media Hub." Other available features include a panoramic glass roof, power accessories, automatic climate control, electric seats with ventilation, turning headlights and more. Safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, stability control, ABS, pre-charged braking technology, blind-spot monitoring, tyre pressure monitor and more. The V6 is available in regular or long-wheelbase form, while the V8 is only available in long-wheelbase form, with regular-wheelbase models available upon request.
