Power produced by the powerful 3.5-litre V6 goes to the front wheels, originally via a smooth 5-speed automatic. A 6-speed automatic replaced the previous unit from 2008 onwards. Inside is a comfortable cabin lavished with tasteful materials and ergonomically-designed controls that makes this car a pleasant and cheap alternative to a Lexus. This newest Avalon is significantly larger than previous models. The front seats are roomy and comfortable and special attention was paid to back-seat comfort. The Avalon is smooth and comfortable, quiet and serene, as the suspension was tuned for ride comfort. Trim variations are limited to accessories. Standard features include a premium AM/FM/CD/cassette stereo with nine speakers, remote keyless entry, multi-function information display for audio, climate control, temperature and trip computer, among other things.

The Vectra is Opel's attempt at the upper end of the midsize car market, although more conservative pricing would've helped it compete against the larger Japanese midsize sedans. The Vectra was the first European application of GM's front-wheel-drive Epsilon platform, shared with the Saab 9-3. This architecture uses aluminium in the suspension and bonnet, magnesium in the dashboard cross member and lots of high-tensile steel. The Vectra, available as a sedan or a liftback, received a new front end during the 2006 model year. The largish interior can hold five people, and luggage space can be increased by folding down the rear bench seat. The extensive range of engines available in Europe has been cut down to a single 2.2-litre four-cylinder in the Middle East, mated with only a five-speed automatic transmission. Features include power windows, cloth or leather upholstery, alloy wheels, CD stereo, cruise control, keyless entry and more. The rigid passenger cell is complemented by standard safety equipment including front airbags, side airbags for driver and front passenger, as well as curtain airbags in front and rear. Also available are active head restraints in front with lumbar supports to reduce whiplash injury.

PGO proclaims itself to be a 'French automobile craftsman' to highlight their hand-crafted aspect and small-scale production. The range expands from the Speedster II with the addition of the CÃ©vennes. Both share the same technical foundation and differ only in style, with the CÃ©vennes looking more modern with restyled bumpers and trim. Indeed, the overall styling is still based on the 1950s Porsche 356. However, it is powered by a recent 2.0-litre 4-cylinder Peugeot engine, with no additional tuning. The rear-mounted motor is mated to a rear-wheel-drive platform and a choice of 5-speed manual or 4-speed automatic. While the car is very basic and very expensive, customisation options offer 15 paintjobs, 8 soft-top colours, 14 types of leather and 10 types of carpet. Standard features include a basic a/c, power windows, 17-inch alloy wheels, CD/MP3 stereo with 2 speakers, keyless entry, electric mirrors, black manual soft top and a set of eight instrumentation gauges. Options include chrome wheels, two-tone leather, CD changer, alarm and more.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it is not really that good off-road, but gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. It is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. This wagon offers room for five passengers, with the option of two additional rear-facing seats in the luggage area. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, cruise control, electric driver's seat, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, a power front passenger seat,  16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, and WHIPS whiplash protection.

For 2014, the Mercedes-Benz E-Class gets a redesign. The four headlights have been removed after 17 years and replaced with one-piece LED headlamps. Like most of their new models, for the interior they have incorporated the "Direct Select" lever for the gear instead of the console-mounted shifter. A lot of new technology is borrowed from the 2014 S-Class which includes Stereo Multi-Purpose Camera, Active Parking Assist and a 360-degree camera for a bird's-eye view to aid parking.

This generation of the Genesis G80 sedan debuted in 2015 model year as the Hyundai Genesis, before the rebranding in 2017 as a separate marque. The Genesis can be had with a choice of either a 3.8-litre V6 or 5.0-litre V8. Both engines are mated to a Hyundai-designed 8-speed automatic transmission. Rear-wheel-drive is standard in both models. An "Intelligent Drive Mode" system offers Normal, Eco, Sport and Snow settings that alter transmission mapping, throttle responsiveness, stability control to suit driving conditions. The Genesis V8 can be optioned with an adaptive damping suspension that promises both sportier roadholding and a cushier ride. It, too, can be controlled by Intelligent Drive Mode.  The Genesis 3.8 is fitted as standard with leather upholstery, 12-way power-adjustable front seats, a navigation system with an 8.0-inch screen, a seven-speaker AM/FM/CD radio stereo with AUX and USB input jacks, auto on/off headlight, LED headlight accents, LED taillights, rain-sensing windshield wipers, automatic climate control, Bluetooth connectivity, cruise control, hands-free trunk opening capability, a 4.3-inch instrument cluster TFT LCD display and 18-inch alloy wheels. To those features, the Genesis 5.0 adds or substitutes a Lexicon Discrete Logic 7 surround sound system with 14 speakers, premium leather upholstery, genuine matte wood trim, 16-way power adjustable front seats, HID headlights with auto-leveling, high-beam assist, LED fog lights, a rear-view camera, front and rear parking sensors, automatic emergency braking, blind spot detection with rear cross traffic alert and lane change assist, lane departure warning system with lane keep assist, a 7.0-inch instrument cluster TFT LCD display, manual rear side window sunshades, a power rear sunshade, memory functionality for power driver's seat and outside mirrors and steering column, adaptive cruise control and 19-inch alloy wheels. Much of the 5.0's features can be added to the 3.8 in the form of optional extras. All Genesis models come with dual front, front side, rear side and full-length side curtain airbags in addition to a driver's knee airbag and traction and stability control systems. Optional equipment includes an automatic emergency braking system that applies the brakes if it detects an impending collision; a blind spot warning system with a rear cross traffic alert system that warns the driver of approaching traffic in backup situations; a lane departure warning system with lane keep assist setup that warns the driver if the Genesis begins to wander into an adjacent lane and provides slight steering corrections to bring the sedan back on course; and an emergency steering support mode that automatically changes the setting of suspension and electronic stability control in the direction suitable for emergency steering, to help avoid frontal crash situations.

The Renault Koleos is a compact SUV designed by Renault and developed by Nissan. It is manufactured by Renault Samsung Motors, a subsidiary of Renault, at its plant in South Korea. Based on a Nissan platform, the Koleos uses a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder mated to a 6-speed manual or CVT automatic gearbox. Though it may look like an offroader, this mildly-lifted crossover comes standard with front-wheel-drive, while optional is a basic all-wheel-drive system with 50:50 lock but without low-range gearing. Available equipment, depending on trim level, includes cruise control, alloy wheels, CD/MP3 sound system, automatic air-conditioning, rain-sensing wipers, automatic headlights, rear parking sensors, power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and an automatic electronic parking brake. Stability control, ABS, front airbags and side-curtain airbags helped the Koleos achieve a 5-star crash test rating in Europe.

The H3 is the smallest addition to the Hummer line-up. Based on the Chevrolet Trailblazer platform, it is a midsized, five-passenger 4WD wagon that carries the military design cues and off-road capabilities of the Hummer H1, but puts them in a smaller and ultimately more affordable package. The H3 provides a good level of off-roading equipment, with luxury features to boot, and at a very good price. With rising petrol prices, the H3 is awkwardly marketed by touting its improved fuel economy for a Hummer, though still hardly impressive. The first-year 2006 models, built in USA, came with a 3.5-litre inline-5 briefly. The South-African-built 2007-onwards models come with a new 3.7-litre five-cylinder engine, with a standard five-speed manual or an optional four-speed automatic. The H3 delivers serious off-road capability, with low-range gearing and good ground clearance. The base price includes cloth seating for five, power windows and locks, remote keyless entry, a CD audio system, cruise control and all-terrain tyres on 16-inch wheels. Safety features include ABS brakes, traction control, frontal and side-impact airbags and a tyre-pressure monitoring system. Options include leather seating, chrome wheels, in-dash six-CD changer, navigation, a power sunroof and more.

The Altima received a face-lift for the 2013 model. They still get the same 2.5-litre 4-cylinder and 3.5-litre V6 engine from the previous shape, along with CVT transmissions. Some GCC markets don't offer the 3.5-litre version. Features included in the base 2.5 S include ABS, traction-control, vehicle stability control, remote keyless entry with Push Button Ignition, radio with CD player with Aux-in and 4 speakers, audio controls on steering wheel and dual airbags. The 2.5 SV adds to that cruise control, 6-speaker audio system with 5-inch display, bluetooth, USB port with iPod connectivity, rear-view camera, auto-headlamps, parking sensors, fog lamps and 17-inch alloy rims. Moving up to 2.5 SL,  additional features include 6-way power seats, dual zone auto A/C, side and curtain airbags and remote engine start. For the V6, the 3.5 SV is the same options as 2.5 SV but included are paddle shifters on the steering column. The 3.5 SL gets leather seats, driver 8-way power seat, lumbar support, Bose audio system with 9 speakers, sunroof, xenon head lamps and LED tail lamps. The top SL versions can be specced out with a navigation system.

The Lamborghini Aventador LP-700 4 is the Italian supercar maker's latest flagship model, replacing the 10-year old Murcielago. For 2013, a Roadster version was introduced. The all-wheel drive Aventador gets a 6.5-litre V12 engine, Lamborghini's only second 12-cylinder plant. The transmission is a 7-speed, single clutch semi-automatic, capable of doing gear shifts in 50 milliseconds. The interior gets a LCD screen, through which you can control audio controls and the navigation system. Driving aids include ABS, electronic brake distribution, anti-slip control, speed-dependent servo-tronic steering, hill start assist and ESP stability control. The rear spoiler and the side air intakes are electronically controlled. The Drive Select System enables vehicle characteristics (engine, transmission, differential, stability control, steering) to be set in three modes Strada (road), Sport and Corsa (track).

The redesigned Jaguar XK was the long-awaited successor to Jaguar's sports car franchise back in 2007. For 2010, the Jaguar XK Convertible is powered by a new 5.0-litre V8 direct-injection engine, while in 2011, a new supercharged version of the same V8 powers the high-performance XKR Convertible. Both engines are mated to a six-speed automatic gearbox with paddle shifters. Other changes include a new front bumper, new side mirrors with integrated LED side repeater, rear bumper spoiler, rear LED lights and colour-coded side vents. Its rigid chassis and the latest CATS adaptive suspension aim for a smooth ride and sporty cornering. Standard equipment includes DVD navigation, keyless entry and keyless start, a seven-inch video display, Bluetooth capability, cruise control, a 6-CD/MP3 player, rear park assist, cruise control, and electronic parking brake. Options include adaptive cruise control with a forward-alert system that sounds an audible warning, full soft leather upholstery, and a CD stereo system. Safety feature include front and side airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, dynamic stability control with a track feature, and electronic rollover mitigation.

An all-new Subaru Impreza made its debut in 2017 in the GCC. The engines carry over from the previous model, which is either a 1.6-litre or a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder boxer engine, although only the 2.0-litre is offered in some markets from 2018. Both are mated to a CVT automatic and all-wheel-drive. Standard features in the 1.6i model include 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, power windows and mirrors, multi-function display, automatic a/c, audio system with 6.5 inch screen, 4 speakers, Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, 60/40 folding rear seats and cloth upholstery. The 2.0i model adds the larger engine, 17-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, fog lamps, 6 speakers, faux paddle-shifters and a rear-seat centre armrest with cup-holders. Standard safety features include front dual airbags, knee airbags, stability control and ABS with EBD, along with the all-weather traction of asymmetrical all-wheel-drive.

Introduced in late 2016, the Bentley Bentayga is the British luxury brand's first SUV model. In 2021 it got a facelift. Initially offered with a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 model with an 8-speed automatic, a twin-turbocharged 6.0-litre W12 engine, connected to an 8-speed automatic transmission was offered later. It gets a variable displacement system, which shuts down half of the engine under defined conditions. Intake and exhaust valves, fuel injection and ignition are all shut down on defined cylinders for improved efficiency. Other notable features include LED headlights, a front skid-plate, front fender vents, aluminium roof-rails, panoramic glass roof and 20 to 22-inch alloy wheels. The interior is, as expected, nothing short of luxury, with its premium leather upholstery, metallic accents, an infotainment system with an 8-inch display and 22-way adjustable front seats with heating, ventilation and massage functions. Bentley is also offering a 4-seat variant with each seat having its own set of power controls and massage functions. The seats are divided by a small centre-console which consists of cup holders, storage compartments and USB charging ports. Other optional equipment include a high-end premium audio system and entertainment Android tablets with 4G, WiFi and Bluetooth connectivity, and even a self-winding Breitling dash-clock option that costs as much as the base price. A Mulliner specification adds more customisability in terms of paint, leather and wood.

An all-new GLS-63 AMG model came out in 2020. The GLS uses 4MATIC, the permanent Mercedes-Benz four-wheel drive system, with special off-road features such as Downhill Speed Regulation (DSR), hill-start assist and off-road ABS assist. The package includes a two-speed transfer case with a low range ratio and 100 percent differential locks for the transfer case and the rear axle. The GLS 63 AMG comes with a 4.0-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 9-speed automatic transmission. The performance of the V8 biturbo engine is enhanced by a further 16 kW courtesy of the integrated starter-alternator - resulting in impressive torque. Equipped with the third-row individual seats, the GLS-Class is a full-size seven-seater. Either one or both seats can be electrically folded to create a continuously level load floor. All the usual Mercedes-Benz safety and luxury power features are included in this one too.

The TrailBlazer is powerful and capable midsize off-road vehicle, which is just the right size to not be a pain on the roads. Launched in 2002, it received a minor facelift in 2006. It has a rigid chassis, good off-road suspension, powerful brakes and a spacious enough interior to compete in this class. It is stable at high speeds, wobbly around curves, and comfortable over rough surfaces, while being quite capable off-road, thanks to a proper four-wheel-drive system with low-range gearing. The TrailBlazer also comes in an EXT trim with an extended wheelbase that adds a third row seat. The early TrailBlazer comes with a Vortec 4.2-litre inline 6-cylinder engine that generates very respectable numbers, similar to the V8 motors of some competitors. And then there is 5.3-litre V8 engine that can be had as an option only on the EXT. The V8 is equipped with GM's Displacement on Demand technology as standard which deactivates four cylinders under certain driving conditions to aid fuel efficiency, returning the full complement of power once the controller senses vehicle speed or load requires additional power. Both engines use a Hydra-Matic 4-speed auto transmission.

The CMC Z7, new in the GCC, is actually an iteration of a Taiwanese model called the Mitsubishi Zinger, and sharing a chassis with the Mitsubishi Nativa. The Z7 people-carrier is powered by a Mitsubishi-sourced 2.4-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic. Features include four forward-opening doors with a rear tailgate, eight seats, cloth upholstery, parking sensors, keyless entry, power windows, power locks, power steering, rear spoiler and 18-inch alloy wheels. Higher trim levels get climate control, HID headlights and leather upholstery. Safety features include ABS and one standard airbag, with a second one optional. Local dealers are offering long warranties.

The Audi RS Q3 is the top performance trim for the sub-compact SUV. Under the hood, it gets a turbocharged 2.5-litre 5-cylinder engine, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. A higher performance version with more horsepower was introduced later on. Standard features in the RS Q3 include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push start-stop button, multi-functional steering wheel, 6.5-inch display screen, MMI entertainment system, aluminium look pedals, black cloth headlining, dual-zone electric climate control, sports seats with leather upholstery and 20-inch alloy wheels. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, ABS, anti-slip regulation (ASR), electronic differential lock and electronic stability control (ESC).

The Chevrolet Trailblazer received a significant facelift and power upgrade for the 2017 model year. The Trailblazer comes in LT and LTZ trim levels. The Isuzu-based pickup chassis is modified to have an independent rear suspension while under the hood, it has a 3.6-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic gearbox, available in both two-wheel-drive and four-wheel-drive setups. The LT 2WD & LT 4WD trim gets 18-inch alloy wheels, 7-inch touchscreen with Chevrolet MyLink and Apply CarPlay phone integration, Bluetooth, USB, and AUX connections, rear fog lamps, rear park assist, front and underbody skid plate (4WD only), steering wheel audio controls and cruise control. The Chevrolet Trailblazer LT Z71 4WD gets all LT options, plus 18-inch black alloy wheels, black hood decals, black body side moldings, black door handles and mirrors and Z71 emblems. The  LTZ 2WD & 4WD gets an  8-inch touch screen with Chevrolet MyLink, Apple CarPlay phone integration and navigation,  7-speaker, premium sound system, 18-inch alloy wheels, leather interior, remote engine start, automatic climate control, LED daylight running lights, front and rear fog lamps, front and rear park assist, front and underbody skid plate (4WD only), and safety features like forward collision alert lane departure warning and blind spot alert. The LTZ Z71 4WD gets all LTZ options, 18-inch black alloy wheels, black hood decals, black body side moldings, black door handles and mirrors and Z71 emblems interior and exterior.

The S80 is the flagship of Volvo range, and though it looks big in size, it is actually more of a large midsize sedan than a true fullsize sedan. The only model available in most GCC markets now is a front-wheel-drive S80 T5 model with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and 6-speed automatic with manual-shift capability. The model underwent an unnoticeable facelift for 2011 which added more chrome to the exterior and some minor design changes to the interior. Features include the wafer-thin centre console that houses the digital climate controls and the Dolby Pro-Logic II surround sound system. The car is filled to the brim with the usual luxury features such as power windows, mirrors and seats, leather trim, 16-inch and 17-inch alloy rims, adaptive cruise control, Bluetooth, sunroof and more. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection, as well as Pedestrian Detection, Collision Warning with Full Auto Brake, Driver Alert Control, Lane Departure Warning and Active Bending Lights.

The Rexton II is the latest version Ssangyong's attractive original Rexton. It was launched in the Middle East alongside two other now-defunct 4WDs back in 2002, and has survived with a facelift for 2007. The five-door Rexton can seat up to seven people and comes with a host of features. The most significant of these is the 3.2-litre inline-six engine built under license from Mercedes-Benz, based on a ten-year-old design. The engine is mated to a five-speed automatic with manual shift capability, and power reaches the road through a four-wheel-drive system that even includes low-range gearing. Available features include cloth or leather upholstery, fake wood trim, alloy wheels, CD player, keyless entry, power windows, cruise control and more. Safety features include dual front airbags with available side bags. The four-wheel disc brakes are assisted by ABS with Automatic Braking Differential, while traction control is also available.

The all-new M4 Convertible came out as a 2015 model year and is the replacement for the M3 Convertible. Gone is the V8 under the hood, and has been replaced by a highly-tuned twin-turbocharged inline-6, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic. Features include head-up display, a backup camera, parking sensors, ventilated seats, keyless entry, and headlamp washers. The Driver Assistance package adds blind-spot monitoring, lane-departure warning, autonomous braking, and side-view camera.

The Veyron 16.4 was a long-running pet project by Volkswagen to create the fastest production car in the world at the time, reintroducing the Bugatti badge in style. Goofy looks notwithstanding, the styling is an essential part of the design to ensure total stability at top speed. In 2009, a removable roof model was added to the lineup, called the Veyron Grand Sport. The car is powered by an 8.0-litre quad-turbo W16 engine derived from Volkswagen designs, mated to all-wheel-drive and a seven-speed direct-shift automanual gearbox. The fully customisable interior is covered in leather and metal, with numerous features such as CD stereo, navigation and more. The single-piece carbon-fibre monocoque does well in crash tests, while airbags give the driver and passenger additional protection. The high-speed tyres designed specially for the Veyron 16.4 incorporate the PAX System that ensures safe handling even after sudden pressure loss. Another safety element is the rear spoiler that acts as a "˜parachute brake' during emergency braking. A second key must be engaged when stopped to initiate "top speed" mode, when the rear spoiler sets itself to a lower position, the front air diffusers close and the vehicle lowers to further improve aerodynamic downforce. A limited-to-150-pieces Grand Sport model was released in mid-2008 with a removable targa-roof panel.

The C8 is an interesting new addition to the midsize people mover market. It drives like a car and has the utility of a 4WD. The regional market gets a 2.0-litre four-cylinder engine, mated to an automatic. Available features include twin sliding anti-trap rear side doors than can be electronically controlled individually from the key fob, a panoramic interior mirror for viewing the interior, seatback tables, up to three individually controllable climate zones, power outlets for running TVs and Playstations, and numerous other storage holes. It has a walk-through cabin that allows front passengers to snake their way between the front seats to the back. The seats are versatile, and you can fold them, remove them or move them around. The dashboard is a funky design, with main dials are in the centre and the tripmeter on the steering column. There are numerous airbags, seven three-point belts and enough safety features to make the C8 a safe bet.

The 407 is an oddity in the midsize car segment, with bold styling that puts form over function, and the 2-door coupe version goes even further. Standard is a 3.0-litre V6 engine with variable valve timing, combined with an all-new 6-speed automatic gearbox with tiptronic. Basic features include power windows, keyless entry, cruise control, ABS, stability control, power mirrors, fog lights, rear sunblind, automatic climate control, and as many as nine airbags.

The Jimny is a longstanding Suzuki 4WD dating back to the 1980s Samurai. With its rounded 1999 facelift, it entered the modern age in with a lot of enthusiasm. Powered by a 1.3-litre four-cylinder engine, it can be had with either a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic. For what it's worth, the manual version is much quicker than the automatic one, though both are still painfully slow. Off-road, the Jimny holds its own against bigger 4WD vehicles. A separate chassis means that the Jimny has been constructed with serious off-road use in mind. Four adults can be carried on short journeys as long as they don't bring any luggage, but even then, front seat occupants will probably be called upon to sacrifice some legroom. When carrying rear passengers, the luggage area behind them is tiny. It is better to think of this vehicle as a two-seater with a fold-down rear bench. Driver and passenger airbags are available, as are ABS brakes. The Jimny is outdated, but finding another off-roader at this price is an unrealistic idea.

The Porsche Cayenne was redesigned for 2011, and continues with minor changes for 2013. The entry-level Cayenne gets a 3.6-litre V6 engine, the Cayenne S gets a 4.8-litre V8 engine, whereas the Turbo gets a 4.8-litre V8 with twin-turbochargers. New for 2014 is a Turbo S model with an upgraded turbo engine. A hybrid model, the Cayenne S Hybrid, is fitted with a 3.0-litre supercharged engine and electric motor. There is also a Cayenne Diesel model now with a 3.0-litre turbodiesel V6. By 2013, a Cayenne S Diesel model was introduced with a 4.2-litre turbodiesel V8. The Cayenne GTS, a lowered sporty model powered by a higher-tuned 4.8-litre V8, came in mid-2012. All the models get a new 8-speed Tiptronic S automatic transmission and an Automatic Start-Stop function. Only the base V6 can be had with a 6-speed manual. There were Platinum versions for the V6 and Diesel models, which were simply special trim choices. Porsche claims the Cayenne is a capable off-roader, but there isn't even a low-range gearing option any more. A feature called Porsche Traction Management manages the permanent all-wheel-drive, self-locking centre differential, automatic brake differential, stability control and on-demand hill control. A PASM air suspension controls the damping firmness, and available as standard or optional, depending on model. As usual, everything on a Porsche is largely optional, with few exceptions. Features available on the Cayenne include a 7-inch TFT touchscreen, optional two-tone or body-colour leather upholstery, 40:20:40 split rear seat with front-back movement, power front-seat adjustment with optional memory feature, optional adaptive sports seats, cruise control, navigation, Bluetooth, cruise control with optional distance-control function, optional lane-change monitor, parking sensors with optional back-up camera, wheel sizes from 18-inch to 21-inch, and a choice of an optional 14-speaker BOSE CD stereo or an optional 16-speaker Burmester CD stereo, both with USB and iPod support. Safety features are thankfully standard, including front and side airbags, tyre pressure monitor, ABS and stability control, with various other optional electronic aids.

European motorcycle-maker KTM, introduced their first ever car with the X-Bow. KTM basically transferred its principles from two wheels to four, with a track-biased car that can be driven on the street. But KTM developers have kept the weight of the vehicle extremely light by removing everything that is not needed, including body panels, doors and a windshield. Parts of the suspension are intentionally visible. Built on a carbon-fibre chassis, a 'crash box' in the front nose absorbs collision energy, while roll bars are integrated into the structure, which is all good considering there are no airbags. An options kit is available on request which includes having additional struts mounted at designated points. The Audi-sourced 4-cylinder FSI turbo engine is made of aluminium and mated to a 6-speed manual or an optional 6-speed DSG automanual transmission. Brembo brakes, a limited-slip differential, and four-point seat-belts round out the standard package. There are no electronic driving aids, no power steering and no roof, although a cloth tarpaulin is available to cover the interior when not in use.

The Pajero is a true off-roader, and a legend in its own right. It received a massive revamp for 2007, with an all-new interior, and can be had in either three-door or five-door body styles. Powered by either a 3.0-litre V6 mated to a 4-speed automatic, or a 3.8-litre V6 engine mated to a 5-speed auto. The standard package includes ActiveTrac four-wheel-drive with rear-wheel, full-time all-wheel and 4WD high and low range with locked centre differential. The short-wheelbase three-door Pajero holds five passengers, while the long-wheelbase model holds seven, with a third-row seat that can be folded into a well in the cargo area floor, or removed entirely. Standard features include an RV meter showing external temperature, time, date, compass, pressure, altitude and maintenance intervals. Also standard are a radio cassette player with 6 speakers, automatic a/c, front dual airbags, keyless entry, power windows and mirrors, and alloy wheels. Higher models get a 6-disc CD changer, fake wood interior trim, sunroof, front and rear automatic a/c, traction control, ABS with EBD, cruise control, cool box and leather seats. Only the top-level 3.8 models get side airbags.

An all-new GMC Yukon was released as a 2015 model year. The exterior gets a complete redesign and also technical improvements, which includes a stronger frame. Under the hood is the same 5.3-litre V8 engine, but has been slightly updated for more horsepower and torque. Power is delivered through a 6-speed automatic transmission. The more luxurious Denali version, identified by its chrome grille and trimmings, gets a 6.2-litre V8 debuting initially with a 6-speed automatic, but later upgraded to an 8-speed auto in late 2014. Features include a new electric power steering system, power windows, electric mirrors, 12 device-charging locations, AM/FM radio with MP3/AUX/USB support, 4.2-inch display between the instrument panel, an optional 8-inch screen with MyLink infotainment system and alloy rims. The rear seats can now fold down flat, allowing for more luggage space. Safety features include a front-seat center air bag, forward collision alert, front park assist, lane departure warning, lane change assist, rear cross traffic alert and adaptive cruise control.

The Nissan Altima received a minor facelift for the 2010 model year, including a restyled front end, new wheel designs, and new interior options. The Altima is available with a choice of a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder or a 3.5-litre V6 in the coupe. All versions get the CVT automatic as standard, although the 2.5 coupe can actually be had with a 6-speed manual in some markets. All GCC-spec Altima models come with a beige interior, in cloth or optional leather, but red upholstery is optionally available for the coupe. The entertainment system has been upgraded with a optional new Bose premium stereo with nine speakers, optional 4.3-inch colour display, USB port with iPod connectivity, Bluetooth hands-free Phone System, MP3/WMA CD playback, and rear monitor. Also offered is an optional hard-drive navigation system with 6.5-inch VGA colour display, 9.3GB Music Box for music storage and playback, Bluetooth Streaming Audio, DVD player and an RCA input for auxiliary audio/video connectivity. The 2.5 models gets 16-inch alloy wheels, Bose stereo, intelligent keyless entry with starter button, manually-adjusted seatsfog lamps, rear camera and cloth upholstery with options such as sunroof and spoiler. And the 3.5 gets 17-inch alloys, power driver's seat, spoiler and optional leather. All Altima models now come with stability control, front and side airbags, and ABS, with options such as side-curtain airbags and a tyre-pressure monitor.

The Peugeot Boxer is the French company's large commercial van offering. It got a facelift in 2018. Only the turbocharged 2.2-litre 4-cylinder diesel engine is offered in the GCC. They all come with a 6-speed manual transmission. Only the high roof version is sold in the GCC region. There are two different versions, each with a different length. Standard options include power windows, power steering, central locking, air-conditioning, AM/FM radio with CD player and 16-inch steel wheels. Safety options include ventilated front and rear brake discs, and ABS with electronic brake force distribution (EBFD).

Looking to ring bells in the midsize-SUV market is the BYD S6. Entering the GCC market, the S6 fights for space alongside dominant Japanese and Korean rivals. Under the hood, it gets a 2.4-litre engine. However, it is coupled to a dated 4-speed automatic. The interior is pretty plush for its price range though, and on offer is a 4.2-inch TFT speedometer, multi-information display screen, leather steering wheel with mounted controls, dual-zone A/C and Smart key system. Tick a few more boxes and the S6 receives a DVD system with a 7-inch touch screen and 9-speaker audio system. As for safety, the S6 comes standard with ABS and EBD and dual front airbags. Higher models get curtain airbags, rear parking sensors and rear-view camera parking system. The S6 is only on offer in select countries across the GCC including UAE, Oman and Kuwait.

The Jimny is a longstanding Suzuki 4WD dating back to the 1980s Samurai. With its rounded 1999 facelift, it entered the modern age in with a lot of enthusiasm. Powered by a 1.3-litre four-cylinder engine, it can be had with either a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic. For what it's worth, the manual version is much quicker than the automatic one, though both are still painfully slow. Off-road, the Jimny holds its own against bigger 4WD vehicles. A separate chassis means that the Jimny has been constructed with serious off-road use in mind. Four adults can be carried on short journeys as long as they don't bring any luggage, but even then, front seat occupants will probably be called upon to sacrifice some legroom. When carrying rear passengers, the luggage area behind them is tiny. It is better to think of this vehicle as a two-seater with a fold-down rear bench. Driver and passenger airbags are available, as are ABS brakes. The Jimny is outdated, but finding another off-roader at this price is an unrealistic idea.

The six-seater R-Class, the so-called Grand Sports Tourer from Mercedes-Benz, is certainly a trendsetter. This unprecedented vehicle concept attempts to mesh the qualities of a sporty saloon, a wagon, a minivan and a 4WD. All we see is a very sleek-looking minivan. Packed under the hood are rather powerful engines, but that hardly makes it a sporting vehicle. Models include the R 350 L and the R 500 L, both available only in long-wheelbase trim here, and then there is the shorter R 63 AMG. Amazingly, it is very hard to tell the difference between long and short models. Boasting ample spaciousness, exemplary standards of safety and impeccable comfort for up to six passengers, the new R-Class enthrals with its beguiling styling. Sadly, few on the road recognise its eccentricity and price tag, so it gets as much respect in public as a typical cargo hauler. Features include a 7-speed automatic transmission, cruise control with variable speed limiter, automatic climate control and all-wheel-drive. Options include a panoramic sunroof and navigation.

The Previa is roomy, comfortable and does everything well. It is easy to live with if you learn how to park it, and it comes loaded with features that make life easier and more convenient. Everything operates exactly as expected, so equipment struggles are rare. Its smoothness and convenience allows the vehicle to fade into the background while you go about your life, even though it looks like a space ship. On the road, the Previa delivers a smooth ride and decent handling. Its 2.4-litre four-cylinder engine and four-speed automatic transmission offer adequate throttle response and fuel economy, though given its weight, it is far from quick. The 3.5-litre V6 with six-speed automatic, new for 2007, improves straight-line power. Standard features include seating for either seven or eight, a radio cassette player, power windows, cloth seats, keyless entry and central locking, along with ABS and two airbags. Optional features include HID headlamps with adaptive light system and auto leveling, front fog lamps, 17-inch alloy wheels, CD player with 6 speakers, cruise control and automatic rear doors.

The LX 470 offers luxurious comfort with outstanding off-road capability, but it is so obviously based on the Toyota Land Cruiser that few both to upgrade to this Lexus version. The eight-seater LX 470 is powered by a 4.7-litre V8, mated to a five-speed automatic transmission. The LX is available as one fully loaded model, with full-time four-wheel drive, a locking center differential and four-wheel traction control. It also comes with an adaptive suspension with variable-rate damping and adjustable height control, and big tyres on 18-inch alloy wheels. Standard is a leather interior, automatic climate control front and rear, power seats, door locks, windows and moonroof, a DVD-based navigation system, reverse camera, keyless entry and a Mark Levinson stereo system with a six-disc DVD/CD auto changer, automatic sound leveling and a separate rear-seat controls. Active safety features include Vehicle Stability Control, ABS brakes and traction control, as well as six airbags.

The CCX is the latest mid-engined supercar from Swedish manufacturer Koenigsegg. It is an evolutionary design that replaced the original Koenigsegg CCR. The removable roof can be stored in the front cargo area of the carbon-fibre and kevlar-reinforced body. This new model has been designed to be more practical, so its scissor-doors reveal a cabin with Sparco sports seats and decent headroom. While previous Koenigsegg models were powered by a Ford Modular V8 engine sourced from America, the CCX engine was designed in-house, based on the Ford Modular architecture and assembled by Grainger & Worrall, a British outfit that produces drivetrain components for Formula 1 cars. The engine is a 4.7-litre V8 boosted by two centrifugal superchargers and mated to a 6-speed manual. A vortex-generator behind the seats and a flat underbelly improve downforce, while a rear spoiler is optional. Large 19-inch front and 20-inch rear magnesium-alloy wheels are standard. Also standard are electronically-adjustable ride height, climate control, electric mirrors, leather interior, central locking, power windows, alarm with immobilizer, toolkit, driver-side airbag, power steering, ABS brakes, traction control and a CD stereo. Options include custom-colour leather, custom paint, parking sensors, navigation, rearview camera, carbon-fibre wheels and fitted luggage. CCX is an abbreviation for Competition Coupe X. The X refers to the 10th anniversary of the completion and test drive of the first Koenigsegg vehicle in 1996.

The attractive GranCabrio is convertible version of the GranTurismo, derived from a shortened Quattroporte platform. The sizeable GranTurismo is offered with a 4.7-litre V8, mated to a 6-speed MC-Shift automanual. The cloth roof drops electrically in 28 seconds and this can be done on the move at speeds of up to 30 kph. Everything can be customised, including the interior, which can be had in a choice of 10 colours, accented by either wood or body-colour trim. It is equipped with an adaptive control system which adjusts the gear-shifting mode to the driving style and conditions. All cars get a full suite of luxury features, such as power windows, premium CD stereo, electric mirrors, power-adjustable leather seats, alloy wheels, multiple airbags, ABS brakes, stability control and more.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it is not really that good off-road, but gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. It is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. This wagon offers room for five passengers, with the option of two additional rear-facing seats in the luggage area. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, cruise control, electric driver's seat, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, a power front passenger seat,  16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, and WHIPS whiplash protection.

Mercedes-Benz GLC replaced the GLK back in 2016. It gets a whole new exterior design. The interior gets a wide centre console and a screen sticking out on top of the A/C vents. It is said to be more spacious than the GLK, thanks to the 11.8 cm longer wheelbase. It is also 80 kg lighter than the GLK, thanks to a mix of different materials used to make the body which includes aluminium and high-strength steels. In 2020 it got a slight facelift and a better infotainment system. Under the hood, the GLC200 and GLC 300 get a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine with two different tunes, both available only in four-wheel drive (4Matic). Power is delivered via a 9-speed automatic transmission. In 2020, the engine became a mild hybrid, due to the addition of a small battery to aid performance and fuel economy. Features include AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Bentley Continental GT received a facelift for the 2012 model. Also a new turbocharged V8 model was added to the line-up, to join the W12 engine. It now comes with an 8-speed automatic transmission which gives better fuel economy numbers and ever so slight increase in acceleration figures. The Bentley does not skimp on luxury, with a handcrafted wood and leather interior, complete with all the requisite gadgets such as navigation and a killer stereo. Instrumentation is provided by classic dials that live in deep recesses ahead of the steering wheel, while a small screen directly in the driver's line of sight monitors all relevant in-car systems. The two-door Continental coupe is equipped with the full suite of passive safety equipment, including two front airbags, four side airbags and two side curtain bags. And the GT Speed coupe, with the same W12 engine adds more power, reduced weight and an aluminium cabin trim package, while improving performance and handling.

The Optima is a credible entry into the midsize field. Not as big as the usual Japanese models, it still offers good interior space and a comfortable drive. This front-wheel-drive offers much improved quality over previous Kia creations, and its derivative actually looks pleasant. Powered by either a weak 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic, or a respectable 2.7-litre V6 with a 5-speed automatic, both cars offer a fair bit of standard equipment. Available features, standard or otherwise, include basic air-conditioning, glass-integrated antenna, AM/FM radio cassette player with CD and MP3 capability, audio remote controls on the steering wheel, luggage net hook and luggage net for the spacious trunk, optional electric sunroof, keyless entry with alarm, cloth or leather seats, ABS brakes, dual front airbags, dual power mirrors, power windows, front fog lamps, battery saver, 60/40 split-folding rear seat and 16-inch alloy wheels.

This iteration of the Honda Jazz was launched in the GCC for the 2009 model year, and facelifted for 2012 with a few minor mechanical upgrades. The 'New Jazz' is powered by an upgraded 1.5-litre 4-cylinder i-VTEC engine. In a move to deter true enthusiasts, a 5-speed automatic gearbox with optional paddle-shifters is the only choice. For 2012, the suspension has been retuned to ease the firm ride a bit, while retaining the tight handling. The speedometer features a large LED display providing of a broad range of information, including current fuel economy and range indications. An integrated single-CD stereo is fitted on all models, with MP3/WMA capability and speed-dependent volume adjustment. Features include four speakers, two tweeters and a USB adaptor in the centre console storage box. The Jazz is also equipped with the latest version of Honda's 'Magic Seats' in the back that can fold up or fold down in one motion. All models get power-folding mirrors, air-cooled double glovebox, keyless entry, alarm, 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, and front power windows. The EX adds rear power windows, paddle shifters, faux-leather steering wheel with audio controls, 16-inch alloy wheels and cruise control. A panoramic sunroof and fog lamps are standard on the top version. The Jazz also comes in several bright colours. All Jazz models are equipped with ABS and Electronic brake-force distribution and dual front airbags as standard, with optional side airbags.

The BMW M5 is the performance version of the 5-series and a new model debuted in late 2011 with a highly-tuned 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard equipment include head-Up display, multi-channel audio system, four-zone automatic air conditioning and BMW iDrive control. The M5 gets a unique body kit, hydraulic steering, and simpler sports suspension. The redesigned BMW 5-Series comes with a parking assistant, as well as active cruise control, surround view and rear view camera, lane departure warning, lane change warning and night vision with pedestrian recognition.

The Edge is an all-new softroader from Ford that debuted for the 2007 model yearand is aimed to compete in the hot crossover market. The Edge features a bold three-bar corporate grille, a raked windshield, a fast-sloping back window, a high-mounted rear spoiler, a high beltline and wheels that are pushed to the far corners to deliver an aggressive stance. The interior features seating for five and cargo space can be maximised when the rear seats are folded. The Edge is powered by a new 3.5-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Available with front-wheel-drive or an intelligent all-wheel-drive system, the Edge is not equipped with low-range gearing. The interior features a centre console that can fit a laptop computer and a number of options including a panoramic Vista Roof, an MP3 audio jack and six-way power-adjustable front seats. Standard safety features include Advance Trac with Roll Stability Control, seat-mounted side airbags and Safety Canopy air curtain system with rollover detection and side-curtain airbags.

The Continental GT is the first new model to come out of the Bentley since it separated from Rolls-Royce under VW ownership. The Continental is smaller and less expensive than any past Bentley, but it still remains out of reach for pretty much anyone who doesn't have a seven-figure bank account. It is also their first model ever to feature all-wheel drive, which is no surprise, since it uses the same platform as the ill-received VW Phaeton. However, this Bentley does not skimp on luxury, with a handcrafted wood and leather interior, complete with all the requisite gadgets such as navigation and a killer stereo. Instrumentation is provided by classic dials that live in deep recesses ahead of the steering wheel, while a small screen directly in the driver's line of sight monitors all relevant in-car systems. The two-door Continental coupe is equipped with the full suite of passive safety equipment, including two front airbags, four side airbags and two side curtain bags. And the GT Speed coupe for 2008 adds more power, reduced weight and an aluminium cabin trim package, while improving performance and handling. Also introduced in 2009 is the Continental GT Supersports with even more power and capable of running on both petrol and biofuel. The Supersports had a more aggressive exterior, while mechanically it had revised suspension settings to make it more sporty, bigger ceramic brakes and an automatic retractable spoiler.

The Ford Expedition is a full-size 4WD that's carried on virtually unchanged since 2007, but started gaining ground in some markets after the demise of the Crown Victoria in 2012. It's smooth, stable and refined for the most part, and this new version goes head-to-head with Chevrolet's non-descript Tahoe for top honours among American 4WDs. Its four-wheel-independent suspension is unusually sophisticated in this class, providing better ride and handling, on-road and off. The Expedition comes with a 5.4-litre V8 engine mated to an automatic gearbox. Expedition is loaded with safety features, and offers an available Roll Stability Control system, which is designed to sense an approaching rollover situation then take action to help prevent it. What the Expedition does best is move large quantities of people and gear, with its perfectly flat cargo area and available PowerFold third-row seat that folds perfectly flat with the press of a button. Able to carry up to eight passengers, the second row features a small center seat that slides forward to give parents in the front seat access to a small child. Options include a rear-seat DVD system and the reverse sensors, among the many standard power features. The longer Expedition EL model has a stretched wheelbase to offer more space.

The Kia Sorento has been completely redesigned from the ground up for 2010. Originally a proper 4x4 with low-range gearing, the Sorento is now a road-going crossover SUV with seating for five or optionally seven, four-wheel independent suspension, and featuring the new Kia corporate grille. The available engine for the GCC is a 3.5-litre V6 with a 6-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive, and a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder joined later, with a 6-speed automatic and a choice of front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. The interior is available in four colours, with cloth or leather upholstery. The new Sorento CUV can be equipped with a 6-speaker or 8-speaker audio system with MP3, USB and iPod connectivity, plus a built-in or external amplifier. Depending on model, available tech features on higher models include hands-free keyless entry and engine start button, in-mirror reversing camera, navigation, automatic a/c, LED indicators on the mirrors, fold-flat 3rd-row seat and a panoramic glass sunroof. Lower models get 17-inch alloy wheels while higher trims get 18-inch ones, and all get standard four-wheel disc brakes. The Sorento is also available with features such as standard ABS with electronic brake-force distribution, and optional stability control, while passive safety is limited to a stiffened structure and two front airbags, with side and curtain airbags only on the top model.

The CLK underwent a minor facelift for 2007, along with receiving a new range of modern engines. Available in both luxury convertible and pillar-less coupe models, the CLK-Class is an attractive extension of the C-Class platform. It packs the usual comfort and safety features typical of Mercedes-Benz, either standard or optional. Standard features include front and side airbags, ABS with Brake Assist and Electronic Stability Programme, common power features, pneumatically operated retractable rear head restraints, alloy wheels, good stereo and a host of upholstery options. The model range includes the 1.8-litre supercharged CLK 200 Kompressor, the 3.0-litre CLK 280, the 3.5-litre CLK 350, the 5.5-litre CLK 500 and the 6.2-litre CLK 63 AMG rocketship. Only the lower models have a manual gearbox option in addition to the automatic, though they make have to be special order. A new optional AMG package adds a sporty body kit, suspension and wheels to any CLK model. Other options include keyless start, navigation, an even better stereo and parking sensors.

Changan Alsvin is the Chinese brand compact sedan offering. In 2020, it got a facelift along with an engine and gearbox update. Under the hood it gets a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard features of the Alsvin include power windows, power steering, central locking, keyless entry, front fog lamps, radio with CD/AUX/USB, 4 speakers, manual A/C, fabric seats, halogen headlamps and 15-inch alloy wheels. The higher models get leather seats, engine push start, 6-speakers, sunroof and parking sensors. Safety features include front airbags, hill-start assist, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD), brake assist (BA), traction control (TCS) and stability control (ESC).

When the new Nissan Patrol was launched in 2010, the carmaker elected to keep producing the older-generation Patrol Safari alongside the new one. The long-running Safari continues to be Nissan's best four-wheel-drive model. For 2010, it only became available as a 5-door model with the 4.8-litre inline 6-cylinder engine as standard, with the choice of a 5-speed automatic with tiptronic or a proper 5-speed manual. By the middle of 2011, a 3-door short-wheelbase model became available with the same drivetrain, as a 2012 model. Straight-line drive transfer allows on-the-fly shifting from 2WD to 4WD with one touch of a lever. The Patrol also has a decent interior featuring quality materials, wood trim, cloth upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo, manual a/c, fog lamps, 16-inch wheels and other equipment. Along with two foldout cargo-area seats, the wagon model has room for seven. Front airbags and ABS are standard, among other features.

The Brilliance FRV Cross is the Chinese company's sub-compact SUV offering. The FRV Cross has been around since 2009, but only made its debut in the UAE in 2013. It comes with 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic. Standard features in the FRV Cross include power steering, power windows, fabric seats, radio with single CD player and MP3/USB support, and steel wheels. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, ABS and electronic brake distribution (EBD).

For 2012, the Mercedes-Benz E 63 AMG received the new twin-turbocharged 5.5-litre V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. A multimedia computer is  awkwardly integrated into the dashboard, with a controller on the centre console. All the usual luxury and safety features are available, such as power windows, electric seats, sunroof, HID headlights, front airbags, side-curtain airbags, LED running lights, leather upholstery, Bluetooth phone, adaptive cruise control, and more. It also features over 70 sensors whose sole purpose is to ensure the driver's physical well-being, such as drowsiness monitors, night-vision, automatic braking and other electronic gimmickry.

An all-new model of Nissan Altima was revealed for 2019. The sixth generation model features an upgraded 2.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, but the V6 has been replaced with a 2.0-litre turbocharged motor. Both engines are connected to a CVT automatic and front-wheel-drive platform. The platform itself has gained wheelbase length, which translates to more cabin space. The 2022 Altima will be offered in a range of trim levels – S, SV and SL in the 2.5L and SV, SL grades in 2.0L Turbo, although not all trims may be offered in all GCC markets. Available new features include upgraded seats with added bolstering, an updated infotainment system with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as well as an 8-inch multi-touch colour display, blind-spot monitoring with Rear Cross Traffic Alert, Automatic Emergency Braking with Pedestrian Detection, Lane Departure Warning and High Beam Assist, aside from the usual smart keyless entry and start, full set of airbags, ESP, tyre-pressure monitor, the usual power accessories and more. The SL has added Nissan ProPilot from 2022, which aids in keeping the car in the middle of the lane while in cruise control, as well as provide auto-parking.

The new GL-Class, built in USA, was intended to be the replacement for the classic Gelaendewagen, but criticism from the general public killed that idea. The GL-Class is now a separate model, supposedly a state-of-the-art luxury 4WD that offers typical Mercedes-Benz luxury with true off-road capability. The GL uses 4MATIC, the permanent Mercedes-Benz four-wheel drive system, with special off-road features such as Downhill Speed Regulation (DSR), hill-start assist and off-road ABS assist. The package includes a two-speed transfer case with a low range ratio and 100 percent differential locks for the transfer case and the rear axle. In addition to the newly developed 5.5-litre V8 in the GL 500, the second model is the GL 450 with a 4.6-litre V8. Both come exclusively with a 7-speed automatic. Equipped with the third-row individual seats, the GL-Class is a full-size seven-seater. Either one or both seats can be electrically folded to create a continuously level load floor. All the usual Mercedes-Benz safety and luxury power features are included in this one too.

The BMW M5 is the high performance version of the 5-series and debuted in 2006 with a high-revving 5.0-litre V10 engine, mated to 7-speed automanual transmission. It was the first production sedan to feature a V10 engine, said to have been made as a tribute to the Formula 1 V10 era. It was the fastest production sedan in the world at the time of its release. It also has a launch control function. Standard options include power windows, climate control, active cruise control, head-up display, active steering, Harman Kardon Logic7 stereo system, ESP, Dynamic Stability Control (DSC), voice control, adaptive headlights, night vision, active headrests, xenon headlights, run-flat tyres, active cruise control, LED rear lights, lane departure warning and brake force display.

The Lincoln MKC is the Ford-owned luxury brand's compact SUV offering. It gets two 4-cylinder turbocharged units to choose from, one 2.0-litre and the other 2.3-litre. Both are mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. While the 2.0-litre is available in front-wheel drive, the 2.3-litre gets all-wheel drive. Standard features in the MKC include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, automatic A/C, central locking with keyless entry, pust-start engine, signature push button gear shiftter, leather seats and alloy-wheels. Optional features include panoramic roof and better infotainment system. Lincoln MKC offers advanced technology such as collision warning with brake support, a Lane-Keeping System and driver assist to help drivers avoid common accidents. The collision warning system is designed to alert the driver if it detects a potential front-end crash. The system issues an audible alert in the cabin, a visual alert on the windshield and automatic brake assist sensitivity. MKC has park-out assist technology, a class-exclusive feature that enhances the vehicle's active park assist capabilities. Where active park assist helps guide drivers into tight parallel parking situations, park-out assist steers drivers out of tight parking spots. The vehicle's Lane-Keeping System uses rearview mirror-mounted cameras to identify lane markers and help drivers avoid unintentionally straying from their lane. Dashboard-mounted cameras monitor driver alertness. If the system detects a driver's alertness level dropping below a given threshold, a warning is issued via a chime and a pop-up message appears on the left-hand cluster screen. MKC also offers a Blind Spot Information System, which continuously monitors the vehicle's blind spots with radar sensors, and class-exclusive cross-traffic alert, which detects traffic as the vehicle backs from a parking space. The MKC gets 7 standard airbags, including a class-exclusive driver's knee airbag.

An all-new Porsche 911 Turbo Cabriolet made its debut back in 2007. In 2010 it received power upgrades and a new automatic gearbox. Under the hood, is the same 3.6-turbocharged flat-6 engine, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 7-speed "PDK" automatic transmission. The power unit of the Porsche 911 Turbo features an exhaust gas turbocharger with variable turbine geometry (VTG), which helps increase power. It also gets an updated all-wheel drive management system. Standard features include power windows, power mirrors, central locking, electric seats, leather upholstery, automatic AC and 19-inch alloy wheels. the Porsche 911 Turbo comes standard with Porsche Communication Management (PCM), including DVD-based navigation. The standard BOSE Surround Sound System comprises 13 speakers and a seven-channel digital amplifier. As an option, PCM may be upgraded through the addition of a telephone module. The PCM also gets a 5.8-inch display. An MP3-compatible CD player is fitted just above the display. Additional standard features on the 911 Turbo include rear-view mirrors with an automatic anti-dazzle function, and a theft warning system monitoring the car with radar sensors for the interior and contact sensors for all the door and lid latches. The Porsche 911 Turbo can be further personalized by additional features including the Park Assistant. Another option in the Porsche 911 Turbo is the Sports Chrono Package Turbo, which includes an Overboost function for even quicker acceleration. By depressing the dash-mounted button to activate the Sport mode, the driver is able to temporarily boost turbocharger pressure in the medium speed range for up to 10 seconds by approximately 2.9 psi (0.2 bar). Safety features include front and side curtain airbags for driver and passenger, traction control, ABS and stability control.

The Jimny is a longstanding Suzuki 4WD dating back to the 1980s Samurai. With its rounded 1999 facelift, it entered the modern age in with a lot of enthusiasm. Powered by a 1.3-litre four-cylinder engine, it can be had with either a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic. For what it's worth, the manual version is much quicker than the automatic one, though both are still painfully slow. Off-road, the Jimny holds its own against bigger 4WD vehicles. A separate chassis means that the Jimny has been constructed with serious off-road use in mind. Four adults can be carried on short journeys as long as they don't bring any luggage, but even then, front seat occupants will probably be called upon to sacrifice some legroom. When carrying rear passengers, the luggage area behind them is tiny. It is better to think of this vehicle as a two-seater with a fold-down rear bench. Driver and passenger airbags are available, as are ABS brakes. The Jimny is outdated, but finding another off-roader at this price is an unrealistic idea.

The Ferrari 488 GTB replaced the 458 Italia in late 2015. Under the hood, the 488 GTB gets a twin-turbocharged 3.9-litre V8, and power is delivered via an updated 7-speed dual clutch automatic transmission. The exterior is still pretty similar to the 458, but gets a few visual updates, most of which have been added to improve aerodynamics and performance. The interior is quite similiar to the 458 with minor tweaks such as angled air vents and improved graphics on the infotainment and instrument panel, as well as keyless start. The LCD displays in the gauge cluster serve as screens for everything from telematics to navigation. Other available features include front/rear parking sensors, cruise control, power windows and mirrors, ceramic brake discs, and selectable drive modes using the dial on the steering wheel, which loosens up the ESP to various degrees. Optional features include front and rear cameras, and an automated front-lift system to avoid scrapes.

The Freestar is a capable full-size minivan that is a solid performer, but is outclassed by newer entries. However, it is well-equipped, easily hauling seven passengers, and has a deep well behind the third row that is perfect for groceries. Fold the third-row seat into the floor, and the Freestar holds four passengers and offers a big, flat cargo area behind the seats. The third row can flip around to function as a tailgate seat, while options include a power rear liftgate and dual power sliding doors. On the highway, the Freestar is smooth and quiet, moved along by either a 4.2-litre V6. It doesn't feel as refined as the best and newest of the minivans, but it's strongest suit is safety, with dual-stage driver and front-passenger air bags standard, while the optional Safety Canopy airbags can help protect against head injuries in a rollover or side impact. The Freestar comes standard with ABS brakes with electronic brake-force distribution, a tyre-pressure monitor is standard and optional AdvanceTrac electronic stability control.

The original Continental by Bentley is a large, expensive, luxury coupÃƒÂ© made by Rolls-Royce for a 10-year run. It was the first Bentley in 25 years to not feature a body shared with a Rolls-Royce model. It was also the first Bentley to use a GM  4-speed automatic transmission to work Bentley's long-running twin-turbo 6.8-litre V8. Power output of the earliest models are unknown, as Rolls Royce was too snobby to reveal numbers. But back then, the Continental was still the quickest, most expensive, and most powerful Bentley ever. The convertible version was called the Bentley Azure, launched in 1995. The cabin featured usual Bentley traits such as acres of wood, leather and chrome. The standard model was known as the Continental R, but 1994 saw production of a severely-limited Continental S, and then the shortened Continental T was introduced in 1996 as a performance model. Mulliner editions, which started in 1999, added performance upgrades on both the R and the T. A handful of Continental SC models were built in 1999, with a huge lift-out glass sunroof.

The unique Infiniti FX "crossover" 4WD has been given a makeover as well as some mechanical upgrades for the 2009 model year. Most prominent are the sharky new face and the upgraded interior. The engine range gets a revamp too, with an uprated 3.5-litre V6 in FX35 trim and a new 5.0-litre V8 in FX50 trim, both with 7-speed automatics with paddle shifters. Built on the all-wheel-drive front-midship platform, the new FX features an extensive list of available equipment. Available features include Continuous Damping Control, Rear Active Steer, and 21-inch lightweight aluminium-alloy wheels designed by Enkei. Inside, the new FX interior  has available "sport" seating and advanced audio, optional navigation and technology ranging from an 11-speaker BoseÂ®-developed audio system to the intelligent key, available active cruise control and available around-view monitor system. The new FX offers numerous safety and convenience technologies such as intelligent brake assist, distance control assist, adaptive front lighting system, standard HID headlights, integrated fog lights, rear LED taillights, functional side air vents, aluminium roof rails, leather and wood trim, sunroof, "self-healing" clearcoat paint finish, stability control, and the usual power accessories and multiple airbags.

The Citroen C5 is the midsize offering from the French brand. Only one engine is offered in the GCC, which is a turbocharged 1.6-litre 4-cylinder unit. Standard features on the C5 include power steering, power windows, power-foldable mirrors, steering wheel with multi-functional controls, automatic A/C, stereo radio/MP3 compatible CD player, cruise control, Bluetooth system with USB, automatic rain-sensitive windscreen wipers and automatic illumination of headlamps, front fog lamps, cornering lights, daytime runnings LEDs, rear parking sensors and 17-inch alloy wheels. The higher model gets Hydractive 3+ suspension, hill-start assist, automatic electric parking brake, electric front seats, chrome linings, part leather seats, interior mood lighting, sunroof, xenon headlamps and different 17-inch alloy rims. Standard safety features are good with front and passenger airbags, knee airbags and curtain airbags, ABS with Electronic Brakeforce Distribution (EBD), Electronic Stability Programme (ESP) with traction control and Emergency Braking Assistance (EBA).

The Nissan Patrol was redesigned from the ground up for 2010, and has been mildly facelifted for 2014. In 2017, the major change was the new V6 engine and no manual option was available. In 2018, everything was pretty much the same. In 2019, the Patrol got a host of new accessories which include fender flares, front and rear diffusers and different roof rails. Engine options include a base 4.0-litre V6 with a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol XE or SE, as well as a 5.6-litre V8 with direct injection and a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol LE. Depending on trim level, the 7-seater Patrol can be had with standard or optional features such as all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing, hydraulic body motion control system for the suspension, computerised terrain response system, climate-controlled leather seats, Arabic-supported HDD navigation, wide WVGA 8-inch touchscreen, multi-screen DVD entertainment system, 9.3GB Music Box hard drive, Bluetooth, power rear liftgate, keyless start, adaptive cruise control, 20-inch alloy wheels, power-folding 3rd-row seat, around-view cameras, and a centre console cool-box that can be opened from both 1st & 2nd-row seats. Also available is an Off-road Monitor that provides real-time information such as tyre conditions involving steer angle, slip and pressure, as well as hill start, hill descent, and an electronically-locking rear diff. Most models get a regular offroad-ready front bumper, while the top Platinum "City" trim gets a slightly-lower unique bumper. For the Desert Edition, it gets bead-lock wheels, skid plates and more, built from the base Patrol LE model. Safety features include two front airbags and numerous side-curtain airbags, stability control and ABS, as well as optional lane-departure warning, tyre-pressure monitor and auto-braking systems.

The Audi A4 received its first major redesign for its second generation. Available as a sedan from 2001 and as a convertible from 2003, the wagon is not offered here, for obvious reasons. Engines for the sedan include a 2.0-litre normally-aspirated four and a 1.8-litre turbocharged four, along with a 3.0-litre V6. The sedan could also be ordered in hot S4 form from a few dealerships, which adds a V8 engine and sporting suspension, among other goodies. The cabriolet can be had in this region with a 3.0-litre V6 as well as the 1.8-litre turbo four. There is a choice of a manual for all engines, though not officially offered on most models. Standard on the front-wheel-drive models is the Multitronic CVT automatic. The all-wheel-drive models get a traditional automatic. Changes over the previous first-gen model include a new look, better suspension, upgraded engines and brighter front lighting. Features include aluminium or wood trim, six-CD changer, auto door locking, a bunch of airbags, a tyre pressure monitoring system and an optional S-Line body kit. The S4 or even the 3.0-litre sedan are rare models.

The Clio was completely redesigned in 2006, but this new version is only available in the GCC in sporting form. The Renault-Sport Clio now has bumped-up power, so it is called the Clio 200 now. The Clio Renault-Sport 200 models will be sold in limited numbers across the GCC, due to low demand rather than to maintain exclusivity. Derived from the basic New Clio available in Europe, both the Renault-Sport cars are powered by a highly-tuned 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with a 6-speed manual gearbox. Renault says the cars were apparently tested locally to ensure suitability for local driving conditions, and fitted with air-conditioning systems to suit the local heat. The car will be available in various funky colours and now has a better interior. Features include sports suspension, upgraded brakes, 17-inch alloy wheels and racing-bucket seats. There is no spare tyre due to the dual-exhaust setup. Safety features include stability and traction control with "off" switch, ABS brakes, up to eight airbags, and energy-absorbing head restraints.

The Cadillac SRX aims more for road-going luxury than any sort of off-roading ability. There's a standard power rear liftgate, reduced step-over for easy exiting, stylish 17-inch and 18-inch wheels and an enhanced optional wood package, all of which signify its intentions. Bigger than a wagon but not quite a 4WD, the SRX is one of the rare vehicles that truly deserves the "crossover" designation. It uses GM's Sigma platform serving the Cadillac CTS. Engine choices are a 3.6-litre V6 and a 4.6-litre Northstar V8, both of which use a five-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission. Both engine sizes can be optioned up to all-wheel-drive. Standard features include fog lights, heated mirrors, roof rack side rails, rear wiper/washer, 17-inch painted aluminium wheels, automatic dual-zone climate control, auto-dimming rearview mirror, leather-wrapped wheel with controls for audio and voice recognition systems, express up/down on all windows, leather interior, eight-way power driver's seat, 60/40 folding rear seat, CD player with seven speakers, automatic headlamps, and rear parking assist. The V8 model adds driver's side auto-dimming exterior mirror, 18-inch aluminum wheels, CD changer and more. The SRX handles like a car rather than a lumpy 4WD, and the optional Magnetic Ride Control, which automatically adjusts the shocks to compensate for any road imperfections, makes it even smoother on the roads, where it belongs.

An all-new GMC Sierra was released as a 2014 model year and received a facelift in 2016. Exterior-wise, the styling carries pretty much the same DNA as the previous model but the new front fascia seems more imposing now. That is because they have added bigger headlights and a huge grille. GM consciously kept the design similar as, unlike the UAE where big pickup trucks are more of a statement, in the U.S. market it is a high volume seller among conservative buyers. A Z71 package is available which includes stronger shocks, front tow hooks and extra under-body protection. The interior is where the main changes will be, with the new 4.2-inch display on the dashboard. More soft-touch material has been added around the cockpit. The new Sierra pickups will have 12-volt outlets, five USB ports and a SD-card slot. A new 4.3-litre V6 engine adds to the family of 5.3-litre and 6.2-litre V8 motors. They will all be mated to a six-speed automatic. For improving fuel economy, the V8 engines have cylinder deactivation and direct injection.

The 2015 Mitsubishi Pajero received a facelift. The Pajero is a true off-roader, and a legend in its own right. Powertrain options were either a 3.5-litre V6 mated to a 5-speed automatic, or a 3.8-litre V6 engine mated to a 5-speed auto. The standard package includes ActiveTrac four-wheel-drive with rear-wheel, full-time all-wheel and 4WD high and low range with locked centre differential. The long-wheelbase model holds seven passengers, with a third-row seat that can be folded into a well in the cargo area floor, or removed entirely. Standard features include an RV meter showing external temperature, time, date, compass, pressure, altitude and maintenance intervals. Also standard are a radio cassette player with 6 speakers, automatic a/c, front dual airbags, keyless entry, power windows and mirrors, and 16-inch alloy wheels. Higher models get a multimedia entertainment system, fake wood interior trim, sunroof, front and rear automatic a/c, traction control, ABS with EBD, cruise control, cool box, leather seats and 17-inch wheels. Only the top-level 3.8 models get side airbags as standard.

This generation of the Audi A6 was first launched in 2005, and continues for 2009 with a minor facelift. It is available as a sedan and a wagon in this region, along with the RS6, although the wagons seem popular only for fleet duty. The engine range continues to get exceedingly confusing. Available in the front-wheel-drive platform are the 2.0-litre turbocharged inline-4 for the 2.0T as well as the 2.8-litre V6 for the 2.8 model. The Quattro all-wheel-drive platform came the new 3.0-litre supercharged V6 for the 3.0T, while the 4.2-litre V8 and the 5.2-litre S6 are not available in the GCC. The RS6 sedan also joined the range in 2009, with a twin-turbo 5.0-litre V10. The standard transmission on Frontrak front-wheel-drive models is either a CVT with simulated 7-speed functionality, while the all-wheel-drive Quattro models will get a 6-speed automatic, but a manual gearbox will not be offered in the GCC. The S-Line sports package is available on the higher-end sedan models. Other features include a Bose surround sound, adaptive cruise control, MMI multimedia interface, reverse camera, and adaptive air suspension, as well as 17-inch or 18-inch rims. The A6 attempts to offer a blend of comfort and performance, and the Quattro models certainly do well here.
