Among the three rows of seats, the second row moves front and back offering adjustable legroom, while the foldable third row seats can be tucked away to increase luggage space. Standard features include keyless entry, 18-inch wheels, CD player, trip computer, rear air-conditioning, power windows, doors, locks and mirrors, and an eight-way power driver's seat with memory. Available features also include leather seats, a power front passenger seat, memory mirrors, a power moonroof, upgraded audio with a six-CD changer, turning HID headlights and self-leveling rear suspension. An R-Design sports package adds 19-inch rims, redesigned upholstery, extra cabin trim and unique 19-inch wheels.stiffer suspension. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, WHIPS whiplash protection, and a rollover protection system.

The Pilot is Honda's midsize 4WD replacement for the MR-V. The new-for-2009 SUV increases a bit in size while attempting to move slightly upscale with its available luxury options. An all-new look features slab-sided styling, and a weird new standard grille which can be replaced by an optional better-looking grille. The longer wheelbase adds second-row and third-row legroom as well as additional cargo space. It can supposedly seat eight people. New to the Pilot is Variable Cylinder Management (VCM) which allows the 3.5-litre V6 engine to operate on half the cylinders when power is not needed, improving fuel economy. Also standard is a 5-speed automatic. Based on the same platform as the Odyssey minivan, the Pilot claims to be an off-roader, but only succeeds moderately, with an all-wheel-drive system that can lock itself in a 50:50 front/rear power split, but with no low-range gearing. Standard safety features include ABS, traction control, stability control, front-side airbags and curtain airbags. A power tailgate, front and rear obstacle detection, rear-view camera, side-mirror indicators, leather upholstery, side-steps, power-adjustable front seats and sunroof are all optional.

The aging 9-5 was given a makeover in 2006, which includes a new look inside and out, and some minor mechanical modifications. Sold in Linear, Arc and Aero versions, there is only the four-door sedan form available here, although a SportCombi wagon could probably be ordered. The 9-5 now features two 2.3-litre four-cylinder turbo engines in different states of tune, mated to five-speed manual or optional automatic transmissions. The 9-5 features consist of leather upholstery, sport-tuned suspension, power windows and mirrors, power-adjustable front seats, computer information display, Xenon headlamps, anti-theft alarm, sunroof, CD stereo, aumatic climate control, alloy wheels, parking sensors, keyless entry and more. Safety features are extensive, with an active head restraint system, front and side airbags, ABS brakes, traction control and stability control. This car certainly is loaded with features, but it loses out with an inflated price tag for what is essentially a four-cylinder front-wheel-drive sedan, living only on facelifts since the last millenium.

The 206 is one of Peugeot's more popular models, with a wide range of body styles, trim levels and engine choices. Its design has changed little since its launch in 1999, although new derivatives such as the 206 CC Cabriolet joined the line-up in 2001. There are various petrol engines in the range, although after 2006, the local offerings had decreased. The standard five-door hatchback can be had with a 1.4-litre or a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine with either a manual or an automatic. The 206 CC coupe-cabriolet can only be had as a 1.6-litre automatic in the later years, although the manual 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre CC models were available here for a few years in between. There is a more powerful 2.0-litre engine with a manual offered in three-door RC hatchback form, which is a true sporting contender. The tuned RC debuted in 2003, replacing the competent GTi 2.0-litre model. All models come with front power windows, a cloth interior, driver's airbag and other basics as standard. Comprehensive safety equipment such as ABS with electronic brakeforce distribution, Emergency Brake Assist, ESP and traction control, along with passenger front airbag, were all optional. Available features included a CD player, alloy wheels and more.

The Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class is a sub-compact 4-door sedan. The CLA-Class will only be offered in one version, the CLA 250, powered by a direct-injection 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder mated to a 7-speed "DCT" dual-clutch automanual and a front-wheel-drive platform. The 5-seater is offered in one loaded "Sport" spec that includes 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The 2022 Land Cruiser LC300 is claimed to be an all-new model. The full-size SUV utilises the latest TNGA platform, although the wheelbase mysteriously remains the same. The new Land Cruiser sheds 200 kg from the previous model, which ran for 14 years with numerous facelifts. The interior has been completely revamped as well, although the design remains unremarkable. The screen can be as big as 12.3-inches in the higher trims, while a 9.0-inch screen is offered as standard. The 2022 Land Cruiser is packed with modern features like Android Auto, Apple CarPlay, wireless charging, heads-up display, 360-degree camera, powered tailgate, and even a fingerprint authentication system for some reason. The third row of seats can now be folded down into the floor. For the Middle East market, the 4.0-litre V6 carries on, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Gone is the V8, now replaced with a 3.5-litre V6 turbocharged motor, mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission. It goes without saying, four-wheel drive is offered as standard, complete with three differential locks. The approach and departure angles measure 32 degrees and 26.5 degrees, respectively. It gets a ground clearance of 230 mm. Toyota has also added an Adaptive Variable Suspension (AVS) to the LC300, along with an upgraded Electronically Controlled Kinetic Dynamic Suspension Stabilisation (E-KDSS) system. There is an advanced Multi-Terrain System as well, with additional Deep Snow and Auto modes. An underbody camera gets thrown into the mix, as a part of a Multi-Terrain Monitor system. The exterior GR Sports package offers a honeycomb grille, front and rear off-road bumpers, GR 18-inch off-road alloy wheels and signature GR Sport interior design elements.

An all-new Nissan Maxima came out in 2016, featuring the company's "V-Motion" front end, boomerang lights and floating roof look. The new chassis is lighter and more rigid than the previous generation. In 2019, the Maxima got a slight facelift. The American-built front-wheel-drive midsizer is powered by the same 3.5-litre V6 as the previous model but updated with 60% new parts. The engine is mated to a CVT transmission with redundant paddle shifters. Inside, the 2020 Nissan Maxima gets a flat-bottomed steering wheel, Alcantara accents and a centre console that is angled 7-degrees toward the driver. It also gets 7-inch Advanced Drive Assist Display in the instrument cluster that can be paired with an optional 8-inch screen with multi-touch control. Other options include HID headlights, 18-inch or 19-inch wheels, panoramic glass roof, cloth or leather upholstery, Android Auto, Apple CarPlay and more. The 2020 Nissan Maxima comes standard with ABS, front airbags, side-curtain airbags and stability control, with options such as blind-spot monitoring, around-view parking cameras and adaptive cruise control with auto-braking. Equipment packages between trim levels change slightly, depending on market.

The Volkswagen Golf GTI always had a good following here, even though hatchbacks were never so popular in this region. The 4-cylinder turbocharged 2.0-litre GTI is satisfyingly fast and features a dual-clutch automanual gearbox that is still rare in any class of car that was affordable at the time. The Golf comes standard with available safety features such as front and side-curtain airbags, ABS brakes and optional ESP, alongside available convenience features like power windows and CD stereo.

The American-built Honda Odyssey minivan received a facelift for the 2014 model year. The upmarket minivan is aimed at big families, and is longer, wider and lower than the previous version. It comes in LX, EXL and Touring trim levels. Mechanical specs include a 3.5-litre V6 with cylinder-shutoff technology, a 6-speed automatic, MacPherson strut front and double-wishbone rear suspension, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and an 80-litre fuel tank. Depending on trim, features include three rows of seating for up to eight people, adjustable 2nd-row seats that can space outwards to fit three baby seats, 3rd-row "magic" seats that can flip forwards or backwards, power-adjustable driver's seat with optional powered passenger seat, optional HID headlights, optional rear DVD screen that is ultra-wide to play a movie and a video game at the same time, ports for USB and even HDMI, optional navigation with Bluetooth phone, optional 15GB hard drive or 2GB flash drive to store CDs instead of needing a CD changer, front and side airbags with three-row side-curtain airbags, stability control, power windows front and rear, cruise control, sunroof, cooler box, remote-controllable power tailgate and rear sliding doors, variable power steering, ABS and 15 bottle and cup holders.

From 2014, the Infiniti JX35 became the QX60 to follow the Japanese brand's new naming structure, and it received a facelift for 2016.  It has remained the same for the 2017 model year. Powered by a 3.5-litre V6 mated to a CVT automatic and all-wheel-drive, the Infiniti QX60 is aimed at the family crowd. With three-row seating, leather upholstery and a touchscreen multimedia computer, all models are generously equipped as luxury vehicles, unlike the cloth-wearing base models peddled as premium vehicles by German competitors. Depending on trim level, available features include smart keyless entry and start, tri-zone auto a/c with air purifier, 15-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with USB port and Bluetooth, powered front seats with memory and ventilation, split-folding second and third-row seats, wood trim, hard-drive navigation, around-view parking cameras, parking-guidance system, blind-spot monitor, multiple airbags, lane departure warning and prevention, adaptive cruise control with collision warning, cross-traffic alert and auto braking, rear DVD screens, pre-crash seatbelts, ABS and stability control. The 2016 QX60 also adds Forward Emergency Braking with pedestrian detection.

The new Toyota Yaris hatchback was released as a 2015 model year. It got a facelift for 2018. The Thai-built Yaris has two 4-cylinder engines to choose from. The base SE gets a 1.3-litre, whereas higher SE+ model gets a 1.5-litre in the UAE. In KSA, there is only one 1.5-litre Sport model. They all get a CVT automatic transmission for 2017. Standard features in the Toyota Yaris 1.3 SE hatchback include power steering, power windows, fabric seats, manual A/C, radio with AM/FM/CD/AUX/USB support with 4 speakers, keyless entry, 14-inch steel wheels and halogen lamps. The 1.5 SE gets 15-inch alloy wheels, fog lamps, red stitching and steering-mounted audio buttons. The Saudi Sport S additionally gets parking sensors. The SE+ get automatic air-conditioning, smart entry and push-button start system, 6 speakers, split-folding rear seat, projector headlights and better-quality seat fabric. Standard safety features on the Toyota Yaris include front driver and passenger airbags, ABS, brake assist and Electronic Brake-Force Distribution (EBD). In the UAE, tyre-pressure monitor, stability control and rear fog lamps are now standard on non-fleet models. Some dealers offer additional accessories such as Bluetooth and parking sensors. TRD-branded accessories such as lowering springs, body kits and wheels are also available.

A classic if there ever was one in this modern world, the Arnage stands as a symbol of what Bentley once was, before the VW-based Continental came along. Bentley claims an unrivalled heritage thanks to a skill-set handed down through three generations working on the same site, and an ability to tailor cars to precise customer wishes. Every Arnage is built to order, and over half are further modified by Bentley's coachbuilding arm, Bentley Mulliner. Bentley also claims that the Arnage is the culmination of over 80 years continual experience of building Grand Touring Limousines. It is odd though that at least in the last decade, the Arnage, in R, T and RL trims, has remained largely untouched, except for a minor facelift. Bentley also likes to brag about one regular customer, who said that determining the specification of an Arnage is like having your own private car company. An exclusive club for sure, but we have to wonder what they pay for. The impressive 6.8-litre turbo V8 engines are massive and yet they are easily surpassed in power and economy by, of all people, the Americans. Changes in 2007 included a switch from the old 4-speed automatic to a new 6-speed auto, as well as a bump-up in power due to new Mitsubishi turbochargers. The higher-tuned engine is reserved for the sportier T model.

The Indica is an outdated hatchback launched in India back in 1998, spawning variants such as the Indigo sedan and the Indigo Marina station wagon. They went on sale in the GCC for the first time from 2008 onwards, but only in select countries such as Saudi Arabia. The Indica and Indigo were considered India's first indigenously-developed passenger cars. In reality, the engine and engineering came from within India, but the exterior styling was largely handled by an Italian design firm. Italian styling would've been cool if it wasn't out-of-date by a decade. The five-seater is powered by a 1.4-litre 4-cylinder engine that is consumes less fuel than larger cars in general, but nowhere near as efficient as modern Japanese subcompacts. Standard features include a 5-speed manual and not much else. However, it can be outfitted with power steering, basic a/c, alloy wheels, power windows, keyless entry, disc brakes, four-spoke steering wheel, tinted windows, fog lamps, rear spoiler with integrated LED stop lamp, two-tone interior colours, chrome exterior trimmings, tachometer, child lock on rear doors, ABS and front airbags.

The Mitsubishi Mirage hopes to take on the sub-compact category currently being dominated by its Japanese rivals. The hatchback has a tiny 1.2-litre 3-cylinder engine under the hood. The base model has a 5-speed manual, with the option of a CVT in the higher models. Standard features will include cloth seats, AM/FM Radio with a CD-player, painted bumpers and 14-inch steel wheels. Available options on higher-level versions include 15-inch alloy wheels, body-colour exterior trim, electric power steering, trip computer, split-folding rear bench, power windows, keyless entry, rear wiper, fog lamps and two types of CD/MP3 stereo with optional USB port. Standard safety features include ABS and a driver-side front airbag, with a passenger-side one available in higher trims.

The second generation Porsche Panamera came out as a 2017 model year. The trims available in the GCC include the base Panamera, along with the, Panamera 4, Panamera 4 E-Hybrid Turbo S E-Hybrid. The base model and the Panamera 4S gets a turbocharged 3.0-litre V6,  while the Panamera Turbo gets a turbocharged 4.0-litre V8. The Turbo S E-Hybrid gets a V8 4.0-litre turbo unit combined with an electric motor. Some updates on the new generation include an improved adaptive air suspension system and optional rear-axle steering. Inside, the interior gets a new instrument cluster with two 7-inch displays. The centre console gets a 12.3-inch touch screen, while the rear passenger get their own set of infotainment and climate controls. Safety features include the usual cocoon of airbags, electronic stability control and ABS.

The Mercedes-Benz A35 AMG 4Matic joined the lineup for the first time in 2019. It is a new performance variant, sitting below the A45 AMG. It uses the same 2.0-litre turbocharged engine as the standard version, but tuned to produce more horsepower. Power is delivered via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The 5-seater hatchback's features include 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

Introduced in late 2016, the Bentley Bentayga is the British luxury brand's first SUV model. It is powered by a twin-turbocharged 6.0-litre W12 engine, connected to an 8-speed automatic transmission and four-wheel drive system. It gets a variable displacement system, which shuts down half of the engine under defined conditions. Intake and exhaust valves, fuel injection and ignition are all shut down on defined cylinders, with the engine running as a 6-cylinder for improved efficiency. A 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 model was introduced for 2018, also with an 8-speed automatic. Other notable features include LED headlights, a front skid-plate, front fender vents, aluminium roof-rails, panoramic glass roof and 20 to 22-inch alloy wheels. The interior is, as expected, nothing short of luxury, with its premium leather upholstery, metallic accents, an infotainment system with an 8-inch display and 22-way adjustable front seats with heating, ventilation and massage functions. Bentley is also offering a 4-seat variant with each seat having its own set of power controls and massage functions. The seats are divided by a small centre-console which consists of cup holders, storage compartments and USB charging ports. Other optional equipment include a high-end premium audio system and entertainment Android tablets with 4G, WiFi and Bluetooth connectivity, and even a self-winding Breitling dash-clock option that costs as much as the base price. A Mulliner specification adds more customisability in terms of paint, leather and wood.

The Korean-built Chevrolet Spark is the smallest offering from the American brand. An all-new model came out in 2016. Under the hood of the 2021 Chevrolet Spark, it gets a 1.4-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a CVT.  Options for the higher-spec models include aluminium-alloy wheels, coloured door handles, fog lamps, cruise control, steering wheel with audio and cruise control buttons, push start button, chrome grille, parking sensors, and CD player with MP3 support and USB port. Safety features in the 2021 Chevrolet Spark include front airbags for both driver and passenger, tyre pressure monitoring system and stability control.

The new L200 offers versatility combined with a tough new look that makes it seem more like a lifestyle vehicle than a commercial pickup. It obviously is tough enough to be a commercial pickup. Available in two-wheel-drive form with a 2.4-litre petrol engine or a 2.5-litre turbodiesel, or in four-wheel-drive form with the diesel engine only, it is an interesting proposition on-road, and even off-road, if equipped. Only the five-speed manual is offered here. The spacious interior places the L200 firmly in the midsize class, unlike the previous compact model. The L200 is an ideal choice for small to medium type of business application. Choices in body styles include double cab or single cab along with a variety of work and handling packages. Mitsubishi's new L200 delivers good everyday performance, thanks to willing, if somewhat weak, engines, ventilated disc brakes at the front and drum rear brakes, and available ABS and Electronic Brakeforce Distribution. The brakes, the rear axle, the steering gear and the chassis have all been substantially beefed up for the new L200, while interior features include vinyl seats and a radio cassette player.

The Lexus LS has been completely overhauled for 2018, featuring major changes inside out. The handsome exterior and extravagant interior aside, this new LS will be the first Lexus LS ever to sport a V6 engine, deviating from the customary V8 application since the first LS rolled off into the international market during the 90's. There will be two models available initially - the LS 500 which sports a twin-turbo V6 engine mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission, and a LS 500 h hybrid model sporting a naturally-aspirated Atkinson-cycle V6 engine mated to two electric motors, and an industry-first hybrid automatic transmission, which is a combination of the traditional 4-speed automatic with a CVT. There will also be the F-Sport versions available, which are essentially the short wheelbase versions of the standard LS, sporting a unique body kit, chassis management system, and 20-inch alloys. Standard features include Bi-Xenon HID+halogen headlamps with AFS and daytime running lamps, Smart Entry & Start system, 19-inch alloy wheels, moonroof, blind spot monitor, leather seats, cruise control, HDD navigation system. The F-Sport further gets air suspension, paddle shifters, rear-seat entertainment system with Blu-Ray player, lane discipline system and night vision. The higher models get the options of massage seats and a pre-crash safety system.

An all-new Skoda Octavia came out in 2014 in the GCC. Compared to its predecessor, the Octavia has grown significantly in length and width. The new model is 90 mm longer and 45 mm wider than the second-generation Skoda Octavia. At the same time, the wheelbase has grown by 108 mm, mainly benefiting the interior and space on the rear seats. There are three 4-cylinder turbocharged engines to choose from, the 1.4-litre, the 1.8-litre and the 2.0-litre. The base Octavia Ambition model comes with 16-inch steel wheels, fabric interior, rear mud flaps, automatic A/C, electric adjustable, heated & foldable door mirrors, electric windows, parking sensors, radio with CD player and MP3 support,  4 speakers, remote central locking, fog lights and front & side front airbags. The Octavia Elegance model gets additional 17-inch alloy wheels, leather and fabric interior, cruise control, 8 speakers, LED rear lights and curtain airbags. The Elegance Plus model gets 18-inch alloy wheels, leather interior, sunroof and xenon headlamps. The Octavia RS gets 19-inch alloy wheels, carbon-fibre inlays for dashboard and door panels, boot spoiler, red brake calipers, sports suspension, Bluetooth and Apple connectivity.

The Lotus Elise is a super-light sports convertible. In 2017, two 4-cylinder engines were available, a naturally aspirated 1.6-litre and a supercharged 1.8-litre engine. Both are available with a 6-speed manual transmission. It gets go-kart like handling, thanks to its light weight, as well as its aerodynamics and aluminium chassis. The soft-top is standard on the Elise, with the option of a hard-top as well. Standard options include light weight aluminium passenger foot-rest, proBax seats, plain black leather sun-visors, light weight aluminium foot-well divider, black leather steering wheel, black leather gear lever gaiter, polished aluminium gear-knob and hand break sleeve, radio and single CD/MP3 player with 4 speakers, immobiliser with remote activated alarm and central door locking. Upgrade packages are offered for the Elise - the Touring Pack offers leather ProBax seats, leather door panels, perforated leather door inserts, leather trimmed centre console, handbrake gaiter, black carpet mats with embroidered Elise logo, noise insulation paneling, auxiliary driving lights, iPod stereo connection, trinket tray divider and cup holder. The Sport Pack offers Bilstein sports dampers, twin oil coolers, 7-twin-spoke ultra light weight forged alloy wheels and ProBax sports seats. Safety features include driver and passenger front airbags, traction control system (TCS) and torque-sensing limited slip differential.

The new Skoda Yeti is a sub-compact crossover SUV, and it comes standard with a 1.8-litre turbo 4-cylinder engine coupled to a 6-speed DSG automatic gearbox and an all-wheel-drive system that adapts for driving on rough terrain. Available in Comfort and Adventure trim levels, features are largely similar between the two. On the Comfort, these include 17-inch alloy wheels, fabric seating, black roof rails, auto a/c, cruise control, electric mirrors, folding table on rear-seat centre armrest and on the rear of front seats, cooled storage compartment, rear parking sensors, CD/MP3 stereo, Bluetooth and turning fog lamps. The Adventure gets different 17-inch wheels, silver roof rails, 6-CD changer with SD card reader, and a panoramic glass roof. Safety features include standard front airbags, side-curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, hill-descent assist, and a whole host of electronics.

The Nissan Patrol Nismo debuted in the GCC in 2016 and gets a whole host of upgrades. The 5.6-litre V8 engine has been upgraded to produce slightly more power. The exterior gets a bodykit which includes Nismo sports headlights, 22-inch forged-alloy wheels, chrome-plated radiator grille, front and rear sports bumpers. The interior gets a sportier design for the leather upholstery with Nismo logos. The suspension has been upgraded with Nismo-tuned Bilstein shock absorbers. The rest of the features you will find similar to the Patrol Platinum edition which includes Arabic-supported HDD navigation, wide WVGA 8-inch touchscreen, multi-screen DVD entertainment system, 9.3GB Music Box hard drive, Bluetooth, power rear liftgate, keyless start, adaptive cruise control, power-folding 3rd-row seat, around-view cameras, and a centre console cool-box that can be opened from both 1st & 2nd-row seats. Safety features include two front airbags and numerous side-curtain airbags, stability control and ABS, as well as optional lane-departure warning, tyre-pressure monitor and auto-braking systems.

The GMC Terrain got a minor facelift in 2016. There is a choice of two engines, namely a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder and a 3.6-litre V6, both featuring "SIDI" direct injection, a 6-speed automatic, and either front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. The interior features ambient lighting, clever storage spaces, a closed compartment under the center armrest for a notebook binder, four power outlets, optional power liftgate, basic keyless entry with optional remote start, single-zone a/c, CD/MP3 stereo with USB support, optional 8-speaker premium audio with available 10GB hard drive with DVD and navigation, optional DVD rear-seat entertainment with two screens, optional power driver's seat, standard rear camera, optional sunroof, common power accessories, cloth or leather upholstery, and a choice of 17-inch, 18-inch and 19-inch alloy wheels. A Denali version was offered from 2013, with a chrome grille and some additional chrome trim. Safety features include stability control, traction control, six standard airbags and ABS disc brakes.

Big and conservative, the Kia Mohave is supposed to strengthen Kia's "family" SUV line-up and brand image in the world market. With a 3.8-litre V6 engine mated with the 5-speed automatic transmission and a 4.6-litre V8 available with a 6-speed auto in some GCC markets such as Qatar, the Kia Mohave is characterized by fully-independent air suspension and its various safety systems, including the ABS brakes, electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD), brake assist, stability control, traction control, and front and side airbags. Furthermore, the Mohave is equipped with Downhill Assist Control, keeping the vehicle's speed steady while going down straight and strong slopes, while a Hill-Start Assist Control is also available. The Mohave comes with a 600W stereo with six-CD changer, seven-seater capability, cloth or leather trim, DVD player, reverse camera and all the usual power accessories. The Mohave rides on a truck-like body-on-frame platform and comes with four-wheel-drive and low-range gearing, which allows it to be classified as an off-road vehicle by default.

With the Sharan, VW properly wets its feet in the minivan segment, though it is falling behind the modern competition nowadays, considering its 1995 origins. The Sharan is not a true VW, being based on a Ford minivan, and also sold as a rebadged Seat. Revamped in 2000, and facelifted for 2004, it provides ample room for the driver and six adult passengers to sit back, relax and enjoy their individually formed 'business class' seats. The Sharan offers the flexibility of removing the rear seats to open up a massive 2,610 cubic litres of storage space. Powered by two aging VW engines, namely the 1.8-litre turbo four-cylinder and the 2.8-litre VR6 units, they can be had with a manual or an automatic. Built in Portugal, the Sharan comes standard with five removable rear seats, ABS brakes with electronic brake-pressure distribution, electronic climate control both front and rear, alarm with interior protection and remote central locking, front side airbag system, driver's and front passenger's airbags, electric front windows, electrically adjustable door mirrors, radio/CD stereo with 10 speakers, and seat belts for all three rows of seating.

The 3 is a fairly roomy and affordable compact car, with the sportiest handling and the poorest engine in this class of cars. The Mazda 3, or Mazda3 as company likes to call it, is available as a four-door sedan in this region, while a five-door has been released from 2006 onwards, all with only the base engine available. The 3 has an interesting rounded shape that hides the height which is necessary for a roomier cabin. The Mazda 3 features a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine, with five trim levels, of which only the base version has a standard manual gearbox, with the rest having a five-speed automatic with manual shift capability. Available features, depending on trim level, includes leather, sunroof, and a premium sound system with a CD changer. As with the engine choices, safety options are limited in the Middle East too. Available airbags only include a standard driver side and an optional passenger-side bag. And ABS brakes are standard only on the higher models. Available on all but the base model are power windows, mirrors, central locking and keyless entry. A sporty appearance kit is optional.

European motorcycle-maker KTM, introduced their first ever car with the X-Bow. KTM basically transferred its principles from two wheels to four, with a track-biased car that can be driven on the street. But KTM developers have kept the weight of the vehicle extremely light by removing everything that is not needed, including body panels, doors and a windshield. Parts of the suspension are intentionally visible. Built on a carbon-fibre chassis, a 'crash box' in the front nose absorbs collision energy, while roll bars are integrated into the structure, which is all good considering there are no airbags. An options kit is available on request which includes having additional struts mounted at designated points. The Audi-sourced 4-cylinder FSI turbo engine is made of aluminium and mated to a 6-speed manual or an optional 6-speed DSG automanual transmission. Brembo brakes, a limited-slip differential, and four-point seat-belts round out the standard package. There are no electronic driving aids, no power steering and no roof, although a cloth tarpaulin is available to cover the interior when not in use.

The rugged Xterra debuted in the GCC during late 2007 and got a facelift for the 2009 model year. The Xterra is a simple but capable alternative to the Pathfinder, incorporating as much off-road gear while originally forgoing most luxury features, but Nissan did add a few conveniences in 2009 due to customer demand. The five-seater Xterra is powered by the Pathfinder's 4.0-litre V6 engine, with four-wheel-drive, low-range gearing and either a six-speed manual or a five-speed automatic. All 2009 Xterra trims now have a redesigned front end featuring two new grilles, namely sandblast aluminium finish on X, S and Off-Road models, and satin chrome finish for Xterra SE models. New features include rear a/c ducts, new audio package including six-disc in-dash changer, redesigned centre cluster, push-button a/c, Bluetooth handsfree phone and iPod connectivity. Side steps and cloth upholstery are standard on the S model, while leather seats and illuminated steering-wheel switches are standard on the SE model. A new Off Road model includes body side molding, unique two-tone seat fabric, rear differential lock, heavy duty Bilstein shock absorbers, and BF Goodrich off-road tyres on new 16 inch alloy wheels. A GPS navigation system is also available. All models feature power windows and mirrors, power steering, CD audio system, remote keyless entry, alloy wheels, low tyre-pressure indicator, 60/40 split folding rear seat, available fold-down front passenger seat, and a leather-wrapped steering wheel. Standard safety features include dual front airbags, ABS brakes with brake-force distribution and brake assist, although side-curtain airbags may be available in some markets. Key exterior styling features include large flared fenders, big roof rails and a rear bumper design with side steps for easy access to the roof rack.

The Tesla Model S is a fully electric sedan, which combines high performance and zero emission. Dropping rear-wheel-drive models altogther, all versions are now all-wheel-drive with air suspension as standard for 2018 -- 75D, 100D and P100D, with the numbers indicating the size of the battery. Standard features include power steering, power-folding heated side mirrors, LED headlamps, LED fog lamps, automatic keyless entry, 17-inch touch screen, AM/FM radio with Bluetooth, and USB, leather seats, reverse camera, Wifi and internet connectivity, power liftgate and 19-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment include, self-driving capability, enhanced autopilot, higher quality leather interior, Alcantara, higher quality exterior paint, better sound system and 21-inch alloy wheels. Standard safety features include six airbags, collision avoidance, automatic emergency braking, blind spot detection and lane departure warning. Optional safety features feature traffic-aware cruise control, autosteer and autopark.

The Escape is Ford's smallest sport-utility 4WD. It offers comfortable seating for four and plenty of space for stuff. Folding down the rear seats reveals a moderate cargo area with a flat floor. Its smooth ride and car-like handling make for easy driving, helped by its compact dimensions. A 2.3-litre four-cylinder engine comes standard while a 3.0-litre V6 is optional. The 2.3-litre can be had with either a manual or an automatic, while the 3.0-litre only gets an automatic. The Escape comes standard with cloth seats, illuminated remote entry, power door locks, windows and mirrors, tilt steering column, speed controls on the steering wheel, 15-inch steel wheels and AM/FM/6CD stereo. Upgrades include premium cloth upholstery or leather, power front seats, a power moonroof, cruise control, 16-inch aluminium wheels, various premium audio system choices and parking sensors. Available safety features include front-and-side airbags along with ABS. It has all-wheel-drive and decent ground clearance, but it does not have the low range gearing to tackle serious turf.

The BMW 5-Series Gran Turismo received a facelift for the 2014 model year. The 5-Series GT is supposed to be a coupe-like crossover vehicle that aims to appeal to markets where the 5-Series wagon is ignored. The 'F07' platform features a unique "bi-modal" trunk which may be opened in traditional sedan fashion, or the entire hatch may open like a hatchback. The 2014 model gets a new front air intake, while the back has been extended rearwards to give it a lower slung appearance. Also boot capacity has been increased by 60 litres to total up to 500 litres. Tech features include four-wheel multilink suspension, standard 8-speed automatic gearboxes and turbo engines, namely the 3.0-litre inline-6 for the 535i GT and the 4.4-litre V8 for the 550i GT. Depending on trim level, the 4-seater GT can be outfitted with features such as leather upholstery, 4-zone automatic a/c, Bluetooth, navigation, USB/iPod port, CD/MP3 stereo with 80 GB hard disc, rear DVD entertainment system, heads-up display, panoramic glass roof, adaptive cruise control with stop-&-go feature, blind spot monitor, lane departure warning system, night vision, active steering, rear-wheel steering, rearview camera, side-view cameras, parking sensors, run-flat tyres and keyless button-start, among others. Also included are various selectable driving modes, adjustable air suspension, stability control and numerous airbags. The niche vehicle is almost as long as the 7-Series and has as much headroom as the X5.

BMW's American-built 4WD has been completely redesigned for the 2007 model year, and comes in two models in this region, namely the 3.0si with a 6-cylinder engine, and the 4.8i with a V8, with trim levels such as Business, Sports and Exclusive. The X5 has all-wheel-drive without low-range gearing, but does come with ABS and traction control. The new X5 mates the two engines to a revised chassis and a more responsive 6-speed automatic transmission. Redesigned to be longer, wider and taller than its predecessor, the X5 now offers optional 7-passenger seating, increased interior room and a host of new features, including standard 18-inch wheels, a tyre-pressure monitor, new occupant-detection sensor in front passenger seat and a new rear differential. The all-new interior features include more space, 10-way power front seats, new leather colour schemes and improved cargo area. Options include active steering, automatic tailgate, aluminium stepping boards, third-row seating, and rims all the way to 21-inch alloys. The X5 is far from an off-roader, but it has built up a reputation for excellent on-road driving dynamics, and has become popular with rich people who like to terrorise other road users. However, the improved xDrive all-wheel-drive system is supposed to offer better off-road capability. An M-Sport package is optional, and includes a body kit.

The Jaguar F-Type is a two-seater convertible based on a shortened XK platform. From 2018, it came with one 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, two supercharged engine choices - a 3.0-litre V6 and a 5.0-litre V8. The V8 only comes in R form. The F-Type comes standard in rear-wheel drive from, but from 2016, the R versions were available in optional all-wheel-drive and later on only as all-wheel-drive. It gets adaptive dampers and adjustable suspension settings, several aluminium body bits, rear-wheel-drive and a unique 8-speed automatic with paddle-shifters. The roof is said to close or open in 12 seconds. Standard options include engine start/stop function, bi-xenon headlamps, power windows, LED daytime running lights, 8 or 10-speaker entertainment system, USB port, Bluetooth phone and streaming, several airbags and a retractable rear wing spoiler. Further available features include optional sports seats, dual-zone a/c, customisable colours for cabin trim, power-adjustable seats and steering, cruise control and more.

The Jaguar XE is the smallest car offering from the British brand. The XE is offered with two engines - a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbocharged motor and a 3.0-litre V6 supercharged unit. The turbocharged engine is offered in two different tunes. All models get the 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard options in the XE include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, central locking, dual-zone AC, smart key system with keyless start, 8-inch display screen, 6 speakers, cloth seasts, paddle shifters and 17-inch alloy wheels. The higher option models get leather seats, sunroof, ventilated seats, xenon headlights, adaptive cruise control, head-up display, bodykit, and 18 to 19-inch rims. Safety features include All Surface Progress Control (ASPC), Torque Vectoring by Braking (TVbB), ABS, dynamic stability control (DSC), lane departure warning, closing vehicle sensing, autonomous emergency braking, driver and passenger front and side airbags.

The Ford Mustang received a GT500-inspired facelift for 2013, along with a few mild tweaks. All Ford Mustang models get a new front-end with revised lower air intakes and a new splitter. HID headlights are now standard on all versions, while GT models get a new bonnet with functional air extractors as well as optional HID foglamps. New body-coloured side-skirts and rear lower bumper as well as new 17-inch, 18-inch and 19-inch wheels are also available. There is now a high-gloss black panel in the rear between the redesigned taillamps. The side mirrors have LED lamps in them that project the Mustang pony logo onto the ground when the doors are unlocked. New colours include new shades of green and blue. The 5.0-litre V8 engine also receives a slight increase in horsepower. The Mustang is offered in metal-top coupe and glass-roof versions. Only the metal-top coupe will be offered with the manual gearbox with either engine, while the glass-roof ones will only be sold with an automatic. The interior comes in cloth or leather, a soft-touch dashboard and aluminium trim, though some hard plastics remain. Standard equipment includes four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, stability control, dual exhausts, power mirrors, front and side-curtain air bags, power locks with remote keyless entry, power windows, cruise control, optional reverse camera, rear spoiler, power driver's seat and optional panoramic roof on the coupe. Roush models are available in the UAE for both the V6 and V8. Few Boss 302 models, which comes with a higher tuned 5.0-litre V8 engine, were sold in the UAE, and comes only with a 6-speed manual transmission.

The Mini Coupe is the latest edition for 2012 to the ever-expanding Mini line-up. Based on the standard Mini, the only real difference is in the upper half. While the regular hatchback had tight back seats, the Coupe still features a rear hatch, albeit more sloping, and ditching the rear seats completely in the process. Models include the Cooper, the turbocharged Cooper S, and the upgraded turbocharged John Cooper Works. The Cooper uses a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine, with the S adding a turbocharger, and the JCW featuring an upgraded turbocharger. Gearbox choices include a manual and an automatic for all except the JCW, which only comes with a manual. Standard features include CD stereo, power windows and electric mirrors, along with a number of airbags, with options such as navigation, sports seats, panoramic glass roof and alloy-wheel choices. The John Cooper Works package bumps up the horsepower and handling. Further options on all Minis include bonnet stripes, 17-inch alloys and xenon headlamps.

The Tata Xenon is the Indian manufacturer's answer to commercial vehicles which is currently dominated by the Japanese. Featuring a 2.2-litre 4-cylinder diesel engine, the Xenon comes standard with power steering, power windows and air-conditioning. Unlike the name, it does not come with xenon headlamps. The Xenon can be had in either single cab or double cab, with the option of two-wheel drive or four-wheel-drive.

The Escalade is all-new for 2007, but still based on the latest version of the Chevrolet Tahoe. The King of Bling is back, bigger, gaudier, more powerful and more fuel efficient than before. Available in either standard five-door 4WD body, ESV long-wheelbase 4WD body or a retarded EXT long-wheelbase 4WD pick-up body, the Escalade ups the ante when it comes to showing off on the streets. The Escalade boasts a massive grille, tighter panel gaps, and a more streamlined exterior, which enables it to get better fuel mileage despite having a more powerful, 6.2-litre V8 engine that makes 403 hp and a whopping 565 Nm of torque. The Escalade models come with standard 18-inch wheels and tyres, but buyers can opt for 22-inchers. Stability control is standard and now incorporates a program to help avoid rollovers, while front side air bags are standard and a full-length head curtain system is available. Other features include automatic dual-zone climate control, tyre pressure monitoring system, auto-dimming rearview mirror, power-adjustable pedals, leather and wood steering wheel with audio controls, leather interior, 14-way power seats, six-CD/cassette stereo with nine speakers and rear-seat audio controls, four ventilated brake discs, speed-sensitive steering, automatic rear level control system, and rear parking assist. All off-roading equipment from the Chevy version has been stripped out in this one.

The third generation Mercedes-Benz SLK Roadster received a redesign for the 2012 model, with the front end looking more like their SLS model. The range starts with the SLK 200 and SLK 250, both with two 4-cylinder 1.8-litre turbocharged units. Then comes the SLK 350 with a 3.5-litre V6 and finally a high-powered SLK 55 AMG model fitted with a naturally aspirated 5.5-litre V8 engine. Only the SLK 200 gets the six-speed manual, while the rest of the models is mated to a seven-speed automatic. The traditional mechanically folding hardtop continues in the SLK, with this time having the option of combining it with a panoramic glass roof. Standard equipment include automatic engine start/stop function, driver and passenger front airbags, ABS, acceleration skid control(ASR), electronic stability control (ESP), cruise control and radio with AUX/USB support. Optional extras include steering wheel with shift paddles, parking sensors, LED daytime running lights, rain sensor, headlamp cleaning system, Harmon Kardon surround sound system, navigation, memory seats and AMG bodykits. The SLK 55 AMG has a cylinder deactivation system, which switches off four cylinders to achieve impressive fuel economy numbers.

A tribute to the discontinued Hummer H1 which was based on the military Humvee, the 6.0-litre V8-powered Hummer H2 is based on the Chevrolet Tahoe platform. Technically larger than the original H1, the H2 platform has actually been modified for proper off-road duty in keeping with the Hummer name. In 2005, the Hummer H2 wagon was joined by a second model called the SUT, or Sport Utility Truck. The SUT version, as its name implies, looks like a pickup, characterized by its unique tailgate, short pickup bed, and tailgate-mounted full-size spare tyre, which makes it a few inches longer than the wagon overall. Features include air suspension, roof rack crossbars, an AM/FM 6-disc CD changer, leather seats, onboard air compressor, ESP, ABS brakes, numerous airbags and a first aid kit. Options include exterior chrome appearance package, 17-inch chrome wheels, chrome tubular assist steps, navigation and a third-row seat for the wagon. The Hummer H2 offers truly impressive off-road capabilities. However, its size makes us wish it was banned from on-road use.

The MKT is Lincoln's full-size luxury crossover that is based on the Ford Flex, with three rows of seating and tons of space. According to Lincoln, the "T" in MKT, stands for Touring. Larger than the MKX midsize crossover and more efficient than the Navigator, the MKT is offered in the UAE with the turbocharged 3.5-litre "EcoBoost" V6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive. Offered in either 6-seater or 7-seater configurations, a second-row 60/40 split folding bench seat, optional power "fold and tumble" second-row bucket seats include heating, cooling and power lumbar adjustment, and an available 5-quart refrigerator in the centre console, alongside all the usual features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, power-adjustable front seats, CD/MP3 stereo and Bluetooth phone. A fixed-glass panoramic roof with power-assisted front and rear sunshades is standard and an opening panoramic sunroof is optional. Safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, as well as ABS and stability control.

For 2009, an underwhelming Audi S5 Quattro coupe model debuted, with a 4.2-litre V8 mated to a 6-speed manual or an automatic. Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

Porsche is offering a "new" Boxster model from 2009, and while the facelift is barely noticeable, the real changes are under the bonnet. Still available in base and S versions, both models feature more horsepower, new gearbox choices and modern multimedia options. A new lightweight Boxster Spyder model debuted in 2010. The base Boxster now has a 2.9-litre flat-6, while the Boxster S has a 3.4-litre flat-6 with direct fuel injection technology. The Spyder uses the 3.4-litre engine, with slightly more power. While a 6-speed manual is standard on both, the optional new 7-speed Porsche Doppelkupplungsgetriebe (PDK) dual-clutch automanual gearbox is also available, which actually improves acceleration and fuel economy. Cosmetic changes from 2009 include new headlights and tail lamps, larger front intakes with integrated running lights, and an altered lower rear-end with twin diffusers. Both models can be fitted with a never-ending list of optional features, which can drive up the total price by 30% or more. While the basic models are very bare on features, the car can be optionally outfitted with a hardtop, various types of expensive cloth or leather sports seats, different 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheel designs, a new Porsche Communication Management System (PCM) with a touchscreen, Bluetooth, TV tuner, DVD changer, metallic paint, stickers, wind deflector, roll bars, headlamp cleaners, Xenon headlights, rear parking sensors, and a cabin that can be trimmed with carbon-fibre, aluminium, alcantara or wood.

The Jimny is a longstanding Suzuki 4WD dating back to the 1980s Samurai. With its rounded 1999 facelift, it entered the modern age in with a lot of enthusiasm. Powered by a 1.3-litre four-cylinder engine, it can be had with either a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic. For what it's worth, the manual version is much quicker than the automatic one, though both are still painfully slow. Off-road, the Jimny holds its own against bigger 4WD vehicles. A separate chassis means that the Jimny has been constructed with serious off-road use in mind. Four adults can be carried on short journeys as long as they don't bring any luggage, but even then, front seat occupants will probably be called upon to sacrifice some legroom. When carrying rear passengers, the luggage area behind them is tiny. It is better to think of this vehicle as a two-seater with a fold-down rear bench. Driver and passenger airbags are available, as are ABS brakes. The Jimny is outdated, but finding another off-roader at this price is an unrealistic idea.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it is not really that good off-road, but gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. It is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. This wagon offers room for five passengers, with the option of two additional rear-facing seats in the luggage area. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, cruise control, electric driver's seat, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, a power front passenger seat,  16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, and WHIPS whiplash protection.

The Ibiza is based on the VW Polo and is the hatchback variant of the Cordoba. Though similar to the Cordoba, it somehow appears a lot more sporty than the dull Cordoba, and the engine choices here carry forward that notion. In the Middle East, this front-wheel-drive is offered in three-door or five-door body styles, with numerous VW-derived powerplants, including a 1.4-litre, a 1.6-litre and two turbocharged 1.8-litre units, all 4-cylinder engines, with some manual and some automatic transmissions available, depending on model. Standard equipment includes ABS brakes, driver and passenger airbag, power steering, power front windows, electric mirrors, remote central locking, 15-inch to 17-inch wheels, CD stereo, height adjustable front seats, split rear seat, cloth upholstery, traction control and even an optional stability control system. These cars are quite well-packed with features for their size. Sport and FR models get larger alloy wheels, stiffer suspension, body-colour rear spoiler, sports seats and unique exhausts as standard. The limited-availability 3-door Cupra gets the top turbo engine and further sports tuning.

The compact V50 wagon and its S40 sedan sibling are based on the same front-wheel-drive platform as the Mazda 3 and the Ford Focus, all of which come under the Ford umbrella. Yet Volvo claims that the V50 is a true Volvo, asserting unique premium features only found in the Volvo. The V50 is an obviously small car, but it looks a lot like its larger siblings with its signature new-age-Volvo styling. There are three engine choices, all of them the corporate oddball five-cylinder, except for the base 1.6-litre four-cylinder with manual gearbox. The range includes a basic 2.4-litre and a higher-tuned 2.4-litre, all offered with automatic with tiptronic in this region. Markets outside this region get all-wheel-dive models too. The interior has an ultra-slim centre console that seems to be free-floating, with extra storage space behind it. The safety package includes a patented zonal front structure using differing strengths of high-strength steel to disperse force away from passengers in a crash. Dual front airbags, SIPS side impact protection, curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection are all standard.

The Gelaendewagen stands out anywhere, even in the heart of the urban jungle. Facelifted slightly for 2013 and getting more power in 2016, its classic beefcake looks have remained untouched for over 20 years apart from the interior where the comfort levels have been repeatedly upgraded. The trademark clean-cut, square-jawed lines have already made the G-Wagen a cult classic. The G-Class represents pure off-road driving pleasure. It is among the elite few off-roaders that combine comfortable surroundings with a complete suite of off-road equipment. The model range includes a five-door wagon, a three-door wagon and a two-door soft-top version of the three-door. The twin-turbochared 5.5-litre V8 G63 AMG is fitted with a 7-speed automatic transmission. The AMG models get a unique front bumper with large intakes as well as side-exit exhaust tips. Interior features include various leather trim and wood choices, power-adjustable front seats, redesigned large multimedia screen, navigation, Bluetooth, CD/DVD/MP3 and all that. Standard specifications include permanent four-wheel-drive with an off-road reduction gear plus the electronically controlled traction system 4ETS, the Electronic Stability Program and three differential locks which can be operated at the push of a button. The G-Class is built for Mercedes-Benz by Magna Steyr in Austria, and has been since 1979.

The Volvo S90 debuted as an all-new model in 2017, introduced to compete in the premium midsize luxury segment. The new S90 adopts Volvo's latest corporate look from the XC90, and a clean rear featuring elongated taillights and dual exhaust tips. In 2021, the S60 Recharge model was introduced, which is hybrid model. It gets a 2.0-litre turbocharged engine connected to an electric motor. Power is delivered via an 8-speed automatic transmission. Interior features include the usual leather, wood and aluminium trim choices and power accessories as well as a portrait-style multimedia touchscreen. Volvo is incorporating ‘Pilot Assist’ as a standard feature that will track lane-markings on the road, and accelerate, brake and steer at speeds up to 128 kph depending on obstacles. Other safety features include the City Safety pedestrian-braking system, ESP, ABS, blind-spot monitor, tyre-pressure monitor, anti-whiplash headrests and a full set of airbags.

The Genesis is Hyundai's new rear-wheel-drive flagship sedan. It is designed to take on all sorts of established luxury-sport sedans at their own game. Hyundai's attempt at moving upscale is a solid effort at a reasonable price. For the GCC, it is offered only with one engine, namely a standard 3.8-litre V6 with a 6-speed automatic gearbox. The Genesis sedan offers a host of upscale luxury features including Smart Cruise Control, adaptive HID headlights, air suspension and a Lexicon CD audio system with iPod input and 17 speakers. Further features include a power rear sunshade, automatic electronic parking brake, proximity key and push button starter, leather upholstery, eight parking sensors with optional reverse camera, soft-touch instrument panel with woodgrain accents, Bluetooth hands-free mobile phone interface, rain-sensing wipers, sunroof, and a choice of 17-inch and 18-inch alloy wheels. Safety aspects include front, side and curtain airbags, as well as active head restraints, stability control and big ABS-assisted disc brakes. The Genesis is a full-size luxury sedan competing in price with small and medium-sized models from established luxury marques, but Hyundai not having its own premium brand may be a downer for upscale buyers.

The Nissan Maxima was all-new back in 2010, and has continued since then with only minor changes in the grille area. The America-built front-wheel-drive midsizer has moved upscale and aims to be a budget 'sports' sedan, although betrayed by its drivetrain layout. It is powered by a 3.5-litre V6, mated to a CVT transmission with redundant paddle shifters. The entry-level Maxima S model comes with an auto-dimming mirror, cloth upholstery, cruise control, CD stereo, Bluetooth, power windows, intelligent key with starter button, power front seats, fake wood trim, sunroof, 19-inch rims, and dual-zone automatic a/c with rear vents. The Maxima SV adds power outside mirrors with LED turn signals, digital compass, HID headlights, fog lights, power-adjustable steering column with memory, power-adjustable pedals, front and rear parking sensors. The top Maxima SR gets additional features such as auto-dimming driver-side mirror, leather seats, driver's seat thigh support extension and ventilation fans, rear bucket seats, rear-window power sunshade, navigation system touchscreen with rearview camera, and a rear spoiler. All come standard with ABS, front airbags, side-curtain airbags and stability control. Equipment packages between trim levels change slightly, depending on market.

The Musso is a sleek Korean 4WD with a Mercedes-Benz heart. It comes with a Mercedes-Benz 3.2-litre inline-6, with the choice of a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic, with power transmitted to all four wheels. The cabin seats five, or seven with the optional third-row bench. Standard features include power windows and mirrors, driver's airbag, CD player, ABS-assisted disc brakes, independent front suspension, limited-slip differential, central locking, engine immobilizer, auto antenna, cloth upholstery, fake wood trim, adjustable steering, and a rear spoiler. Also standard is a full-time 4WD system with low-range gearing. Interestingly, the Musso was originally launched during 1993 in its home market of South Korea. Even more interesting is that it was on sale in Australia as a Mercedes-Benz GX320, in the days before the German company had a 4WD of its own. The final year with its original face was 1999, when bankrupt Ssangyong was purchased by Daewoo, marked with a major facelift.

The Superb is an upper-medium segment car, with an extended wheelbase to increase interior room. The Superb name first appeared on a Skoda in 1934 and is the company's flagship model. The modern-day version Superb is available in various trim levels, with names like Classic, Comfort and Elegance. The Superb offers many of the benefits of a luxury car, with large rear doors and optional rear-seat DVD entertainment. The rear passenger space is exceptional for a vehicle in this segment and high quality trim materials are used throughout the model range. Customisation options include a sunroof and a host of alloy wheel designs and sizes. In the Middle East, the Superb is available with two petrol engines, namely the entry-level turbocharged 1.8-litre four-cylinder and the 2.8-litre V6. Both are coupled with a 5-speed automatic gearbox to drive the front wheels. Standard safety features include ABS brakes, front and side airbags, and even curtain airbags, while the V6 model gets electronic stability control as standard.

Based on a stretched version of the latest 'B6' Passat platform, the redesigned Skoda Superb is a 5-door liftback sedan, with an innovative tailgate that can open as a regular sedan boot or as a full liftback boot, known as 'Twin-Door.' Various VW-derived engines are available, although the only engines available for the GCC is the 1.8-litre turbo 4-cylinder, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automanual and front-wheel-drive, along with a 3.6-litre V6 that debuted in late 2010 with a 7-speed automanual and all-wheel-drive. The Superb 1.8 TSI is available with power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, 17-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, sunroof, CD/MP3 stereo with six-disc CD changer and a 6.5-inch touchscreen, SD card and AUX inputs, automatic climate-control a/c, and a choice of upholstery. The Superb 3.6 adds various other luxuries. Available features include a Bluetooth phone, pull-up rear sun blinds, parking sensors with visual aid and a 'Park Assist' automatic parallel-parking system. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control and ABS. The Superb may not be available in all markets in the GCC.

The Magna was an all-new model back in 1997, replacing Mitsubishi's Sigma as their top-of-the-line sedan. Competing in the near-luxury segment against upscale brands, it never stood a chance, but soldiered on anyway unchanged right up to 2003, at which point it got a facelift. The Magna features a standard 3.5-litre V6 engine, a 4-speed automatic gearbox, a modern-at-the-time dashboard, decent suspension tuning and improvements in body structure that promise fair handling. Offered only as a sedan, the fairly-large Magna rode on a front-wheel-drive platform, and didn't overlap with the more-popular Galant, which was originally in between a compact and a midsize at that time. The Magna was available in essentially two flavours, namely a standard model and a sportier VR-X version. The Magna VR-X upgrades include a mesh grille, colour-keyed rear spoiler, aerodynamic side skirts, wheel lip moldings, sport-style bucket seats, unique seat fabric, and possibly sportier suspension tuning with slightly-increased engine power. Standard features on this redesigned sedan include dual airbags, 16-inch alloy wheels, tinted glass, a power driver seat, an AM/FM stereo with cassette and CD player, remote keyless entry, optional leather, optional ABS and a security system. A minor facelift came for 2000, before the major one in 2004.

The Lexus LS has been completely redesigned for 2013. However, mechanically it remains the same. There are two models, the LS 460 and the hybrid LS 600h. The LS 460 are all rear-wheel drive and LS 600h is all-wheel drive. The LS 460 has  five models - Premier, F Sport, Prestige, Platinum and Titanium. The Premier and F Sport are the short-wheel base versions, whereas the Prestige, Platinum and Titanium are the long-wheel base models. The all-wheel drive LS 600h has Platinum and Titanium model options. The LS 460 gets a 4.6-litre V8 mated to an eight-speed transmission and the LS 600h has 5.0-litre V8 engine connected to an electric motor and mated to a CVT transmission. Base options include Bi-Xenon HID+halogen headlamps with AFS and daytime running lamps, Smart Entry & Start system, 19-inch alloy wheels, moonroof, blind spot monitor, leather seats, cruise control, HDD navigation system with 12.3-inch screen and DVD player with 10 Speakers. The F-Sport gets bodykit, air suspension, paddle shifters, 19-speaker Mark Levinson audio/DVD system, rear-seat entertainment system with Blue Ray player, lane discipline system and night vision. The higher models get the options of massage seats and a pre-crash safety system.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class is essentially the new facelifted M-Class following the German brand's new nomenclature. This midsize SUV comes in two versions, namely the GLE 350 with a 3.5-litre V6 and the GLE500 with a 4.7-litre V8, both with 7-speed automatics and all-wheel-drive with no low-range gearing. Available features include adjustable air suspension, adaptive cruise control and active parking assist. The exterior features HID headlights, LED running maps and a choice of 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels. The revamped 5-seater interior offers, depending on trim level, leather upholstery, wood trim, mood lighting, Harmon-Kardon Logic7 surround sound, HDD navigation, optional panoramic sunroof, rear entertainment system, optional keyless start, optional ventilated power front seats and a split-folding rear seat. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control, ABS and drowsiness monitor, with options such as a rear view camera with parking sensors, active lane assist, blind-spot monitor and automatic pre-crash braking. An AMG package is optional, and it adds a body kit and sportier suspension. The ML 63 also option of AMG performance package which adds even more power.

The bulbous new-for-2010 Prado is available with two petrol and two diesel engines. The GCC-spec Prado 5-door will be available in VXL, VX and TX trim levels, with the choice of a 4.0-litre V6 with a 5-speed manually-shiftable automatic or a 6-speed manual, or an underpowered 2.7-litre 4-cylinder with a 4-speed automatic or a 5-speed manual. The two diesel choices include a 3.0-litre 4-cylinder and a turbocharged 3.0-litre 4-cylinder. All models get 17-inch aluminium wheels, except for the VXL, which gets 18-inch ones. All models also have four-wheel ventilated disc brakes, independent front and live-axle rear suspension, and on higher-spec models, a "KDSS stabiliser" system to reduce body roll. The interior is available with three grades of upholstery. Basic models get fabric and mid-range versions get a better fabric, while the VXL gets leather along with wood trim and thicker-bolstered front seats. The top VXL version also gets features such as three-zone automatic a/c, 17-speaker JBL stereo with AUX input, keyless entry and starter button, front and rear parking sensors with display, electrically-operated last-row seating, Bluetooth and rear-seat DVD entertainment. Also available are front, side-curtain and knee airbags, as well as stability control and turning HID headlights. The 7-seater 5-door Prado finally gets a fold-flat third-row seat, while a 9-seater configuration is optional. The top tech feature is the optional multi-terrain system in the VX-L, with settings for mud and sand, rock, and loose surfaces, mated with air suspension, locking centre and rear diffs, four cameras and adjustable air suspension. Lower models have to cope with "active" traction control and rear diff lock, all with low-range gearing. The VX-L can also be optioned with a Pre-Crash system to hit the brakes when an imminent crash is detected, but it cannot be had with the multi-terrain option.

The Patrol is Nissan's most capable 4WD in its lineup. It is smaller than the Armada, but still big enough to qualify as a big 4WD. It has garnered a reputation as an excellent off-road vehicle in the Middle East, even though it has been fighting a losing battle with the overrated Toyota Land Cruiser for decades now. It is also popular for its smooth on-road ride, though its handling leaves a lot to be desired. The latest engine is a 4.8-litre inline six-cylinder, alongside the older 4.5-litre inline-six which eats more fuel, and the frugal diesel 4.2-litre inline-six. A new five-speed automatic with manual sequential shift facility is available on petrol models alongside the manual. The latest updates give the Patrol an edgier new front end and freshened rear end. Straight-line drive transfer allows on-the-fly shifting from 2WD to 4WD with one touch of a lever. The latest Patrol has an all-new interior featuring better quality materials and more equipment. Along with two foldout cargo-area seats, it has room for seven. Front airbags are standard, among other features. After the launch of the all-new 2010 model, this older version continued to be sold briefly in a stripped-down format at a lower base price.

Based on a stretched version of the latest 'B6' Passat platform, the redesigned Skoda Superb is a 5-door liftback sedan, with an innovative tailgate that can open as a regular sedan boot or as a full liftback boot, known as 'Twin-Door.' Various VW-derived engines are available, although the only engines available for the GCC is the 1.8-litre turbo 4-cylinder, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automanual and front-wheel-drive, along with a 3.6-litre V6 that debuted in late 2010 with a 7-speed automanual and all-wheel-drive. The Superb 1.8 TSI is available with power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, 17-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, sunroof, CD/MP3 stereo with six-disc CD changer and a 6.5-inch touchscreen, SD card and AUX inputs, automatic climate-control a/c, and a choice of upholstery. The Superb 3.6 adds various other luxuries. Available features include a Bluetooth phone, pull-up rear sun blinds, parking sensors with visual aid and a 'Park Assist' automatic parallel-parking system. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control and ABS. The Superb may not be available in all markets in the GCC.

The Lexus LC is the Japanese luxury brand's first attempt at a grand tourer model. The 2-door coupe gets two engine choices - the LC500 gets naturally aspirated 5.0-V8 engine, mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission, the other a 3.5-litre V6 coupled with an electric motor, with power transmitted via a hybrid transmission, which is a combined 4-speed automatic and CVT. Standard features on the LC 500 include power steering, power windows, electric foldable mirrors, cruise control, LED headlamps, smart entry and start system, front and rear corner sensors, panoramic roof, leather seats, 10-way power front seats, Mark Levinson surround sound system, DVD player, 2 USB ports, Bluetooth, 13 speakers, navigation, head up display, LED interior lighting package, seat ventilation and 21-inch alloy wheels. There is a "Carbon" edition available for the V8, with carbon moon roof, carbon scuff plates, sports seats and Lexus Dynamic Handling, which is the luxury brand's 4-wheel steering wheel system. Safery features include pre-crash safety systems, lane keeping assist, automatic high beams system, blind spot monitor, rear cross traffic alert, ABS, traction control, vehicle stability control and front, side & knee, curtain airbags.

Standard options in the GV80 include power steering, power windows, electric folding mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push engine start-stop, leather upholstery, memory and ventilated seats, audio system with AUX/USB support, auto A/C, navigation, auto defog system, rain sensors, sunroof, parking assist system, rear electric curtain, xenon headlamps, LED headlights and taillights with LED daytime running lamps, front and rear camera, air suspension and 20-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include 9 airbags, lane keep assist, adaptive cruise control, ABS, traction control, stability control, brake assist, blind spot detection and autonomous emergency braking (AEB).

The Mercedes-Benz AMG GT, or Mercedes-AMG GT as the marketeers like to call it now, is the first car entirely developed in-house by AMG. Four variants of the AMG GT will be available as of 2017, all with the same V8 4.0-litre twin-turbocharged engine but with different tunes. Power is delivered in both variants through a 7-speed dual clutch automatic transmission. The standard AMG GT gets a mechanical rear-axle locking rear differential while the AMG GT C gets an electronic locking rear differential. The GT C also has an AMG RIDE CONTROL suspension with electronically controlled dampers with three different modes - Comfort, Sport and Sport Plus. The AMG GT R comes with more power, modified suspension and more aerodynamic thanks to exterior mods. The GT R also gets all-wheel steering for better handling performance. For the 2020 model year, Mercedes released the AMG GT R Pro version, The AMG GT doesn't weigh so much for its size, thanks to the body structure being built through a mixture of steel, aluminium and magnesium. Safety standards are high in the AMG GT with front and side airbags, traction control, ABS brakes and stability control. In 2021, an AMG GT Black Series joined the lineup with much more power and even sportier suspension setup. A lot of carbon-fibre has been used for the body parts and the aerodynamic kit.

The Kia K900 is the flagship model of the Korean brand. Under the hood, it gets 2 engine options. One is a 3.8-litre V6 engine, while the top model gets a 5.0-litre V8 motor. Both engines are mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power windows, power steering, power mirrors, keyless entry, engine push start, leather seats, memory seats, digital instrument cluster, 12.3-inch screen with rotary dial controller, premium sound system with AUX and USB, wireless charging, triple-zone climate control, rear ac controls, sunroof, ventilated seats and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment include rear-seat entertainment,  rear seat ventilation, and 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, front knee airbags, and front and rear passenger side airbags, stability control, brake assist, ABS, adaptive cruise control, tyre pressure monitor, blind spot monitor and auto parking.

Based on a stretched version of the latest 'B6' Passat platform, the redesigned Skoda Superb is a 5-door liftback sedan, with an innovative tailgate that can open as a regular sedan boot or as a full liftback boot, known as 'Twin-Door.' Various VW-derived engines are available, although the only engines available for the GCC is the 1.8-litre turbo 4-cylinder, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automanual and front-wheel-drive, along with a 3.6-litre V6 that debuted in late 2010 with a 7-speed automanual and all-wheel-drive. The Superb 1.8 TSI is available with power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, 17-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, sunroof, CD/MP3 stereo with six-disc CD changer and a 6.5-inch touchscreen, SD card and AUX inputs, automatic climate-control a/c, and a choice of upholstery. The Superb 3.6 adds various other luxuries. Available features include a Bluetooth phone, pull-up rear sun blinds, parking sensors with visual aid and a 'Park Assist' automatic parallel-parking system. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control and ABS. The Superb may not be available in all markets in the GCC.

The Mercedez-Benz GLS-Class is the new name for the GL-Class. In 2016, it received a facelift, along with mechanical updates. The GLS uses 4MATIC, the permanent Mercedes-Benz four-wheel drive system, with special off-road features such as Downhill Speed Regulation (DSR), hill-start assist and off-road ABS assist. The package includes a two-speed transfer case with a low range ratio and 100 percent differential locks for the transfer case and the rear axle. The GLS 63 AMG comes with a 5.5-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. Equipped with the third-row individual seats, the GLS-Class is a full-size seven-seater. Either one or both seats can be electrically folded to create a continuously level load floor. All the usual Mercedes-Benz safety and luxury power features are included in this one too.

The Jeep Patriot got a new transmission and minor interior and exterior upgrades in 2014. The Patriot is a compact all-wheel-drive 4WD that, like the Compass, is based on the Dodge Caliber and features Jeep styling cues such as a seven-slot grille and round headlights. Unlike the Compass, the Patriot attempts to retain some features of a traditional 4WD, such as decent ground clearance and short overhangs. The all-wheel-drive Patriot is powered by a 2.4-litre four-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. The Patriot is available in very bare Sport trim and loaded Limited trim. The full-time active four-wheel-drive system includes a "Lock" mode for use on low-traction surfaces. Standard equipment includes side-curtain airbags, ESP, traction control and a fabric interior. Other features include a built-in flashlight, flip-down rear speakers in the tailgate, 17-inch alloy wheels and power features.

The Chrysler 300 got a facelift in 2015. The new 300 is rear-wheel-drive and gets a 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 version, mated to an 8-speed automatic with manual capability. The base model gets cruise control, cloth upholstery, 18-inch alloy wheels, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with 4.3-inch touchscreen and USB port, auto headlights, intelligent keyless entry and other standard features. Higher trim levels additionally come with an 8.4-inch touchscreen, stereo amplifier, auto a/c with rear vents, power seats, heated/cooled cup-holders, leather, remote start, Bluetooth, HID headlights, sunroof and more. The 5.7-litre Hemi V8 model, with an 8-speed automatic with manual capability, comes in three trim levels. Standard features include cruise control, 18-inch alloy wheels with optional 20-inch wheels, CD/MP3 stereo with touchscreen and USB port, auto headlights, intelligent keyless entry with starter button. Other available features, depending on trim level, includes an 8.4-inch touchscreen, stereo amplifier, auto a/c with rear vents, power seats, heated/cooled cup-holders, leather, remote start, Bluetooth, HID headlights, sunroof and more.
