The top model includes 19-inch alloy wheels, reverse camera, bi-xenon headlights, daytime running lights, 11-speaker Bose sound system, dual-zone automatic a/c with rear vents and a sunroof. Navigation and adaptive cruise control can be further added to the top-spec version, but they're not offered in all GCC markets. Standard safety features include dual front airbags with optional side-curtain airbags, stability control, and ABS with EBD.

An all-new Skoda Octavia came out in 2014 in the GCC. Compared to its predecessor, the Octavia has grown significantly in length and width. The new model is 90 mm longer and 45 mm wider than the second-generation Skoda Octavia. At the same time, the wheelbase has grown by 108 mm, mainly benefiting the interior and space on the rear seats. There are three 4-cylinder turbocharged engines to choose from, the 1.4-litre, the 1.8-litre and the 2.0-litre. The base Octavia Ambition model comes with 16-inch steel wheels, fabric interior, rear mud flaps, automatic A/C, electric adjustable, heated & foldable door mirrors, electric windows, parking sensors, radio with CD player and MP3 support,  4 speakers, remote central locking, fog lights and front & side front airbags. The Octavia Elegance model gets additional 17-inch alloy wheels, leather and fabric interior, cruise control, 8 speakers, LED rear lights and curtain airbags. The Elegance Plus model gets 18-inch alloy wheels, leather interior, sunroof and xenon headlamps. The Octavia RS gets 19-inch alloy wheels, carbon-fibre inlays for dashboard and door panels, boot spoiler, red brake calipers, sports suspension, Bluetooth and Apple connectivity.

The Sirion is Daihatsu's entry in the sub-compact segment, packed with features and space. It received a minor facelift for the 2008 model year, along with a bigger 1.5-litre engine. The little Sirion offers a generous amount of space for the front passengers, including a fair bit of room between the driver seat and the front passenger seat. Rear passengers aren't so lucky, but they still get reasonable amounts of leg space between front and rear seats. The rear doors open wide to an angle of around 80 degrees, allowing easy entry and exit, and the tailgate eases handling of large luggage. There is a full 630 litres of luggage space with two people on board and the rear seats folded down. With five on board, it still has 225 litres. The top of the back door has decent head clearance and a pull handle also makes it easy to close the door. A luggage room lamp adds convenience, along with the CD/AM/FM Radio, power windows, central locking, front airbags, cup holders in the doors and the centre console, and split rear seats that are 60:40 foldable. It is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder motor, the Sirion shifts gears using a 4-speed automatic, as the manual is not offered here. 14-inch steel wheels are standard, while alloys are optional, among other things.

The sleek new-for-2008 EX35 is what Infiniti likes to call a coupe-crossover, although it is really a compact five-door wagon. Powered by a 3.5-litre V6, it comes with a standard five-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive. It has an excellent leather interior, power front seats, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, sunroof, automatic headlamps, Bluetooth hands-free phone system, power tilt and telescopic wheel, six-CD/MP3 Bose stereo, power mirrors, stability control,  and an advanced front-side-curtain airbag system. There is no low-range gearing as the EX35 sits low and the chassis is tuned for on-road dynamics. The EX35 also comes with nifty features such as intelligent keyless entry and start, as well as a seven-inch colour display with Infiniti controller for the trip computer and additional vehicle information, including the Infiniti DVD navigation system. But the most interesting feature by far is the around-view parking system that uses four cameras to simulate a 360-degree image of what is around the vehicle, thereby making parking easier in tight spots.

The Subaru Impreza got a complete redesign for 2012, and is only offered in sedan form in the GCC. Interestingly, the WRX versions have spun off into a separate model line and continue unchanged from their pre-2012 forms, at least until 2014. The Impreza is now offered with either a 1.6-litre or a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder boxer engine, both mated to a CVT automatic and all-wheel-drive. Standard features in the 1.6i model include 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, power windows and mirrors, multi-function display, automatic a/c, CD/MP3 stereo with AUX port, 60/40 folding rear seats and cloth upholstery. The 2.0i model adds the larger engine, 16-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, fog lamps, faux paddle-shifters and a rear-seat centre armrest with cup-holders. Standard safety features include front dual airbags, stability control and ABS with EBD, along with the all-weather traction of asymmetrical all-wheel-drive.

The Carnival, also known as Grand Carnival or Sedona in some markets, is undoubtedly Kia's largest non-commercial vehicle, being a full-size minivan. With three rows of seats, there is no shortage of space. Powered by a 3.8-litre V6, it comes with limited standard features, which include 16-inch alloy wheels, AM/FM radio with CD, front and rear a/c with tri-zone control, battery saver, electric mirrors, central door locks, ABS brakes, power windows with driver-side auto down, variable intermittent wipers, hidden radio antenna, power sunroof and an automatic gearbox. Higher trim levels get additional features such as an AM/FM radio with cassette player, CD and MP3, automatic light control system, audio remote controls on the steering wheel, reverse warning system, electric folding mirrors, cruise control, keyless entry system, roof rack, front fog lamps, power sliding doors and tailgate, 8-way power driver's seat and finally, dual front airbags. Safety features are surprisingly limited to only ABS brakes, the optional airbags and an energy-absorbing steering column.

The second-generation SLK, a hard-top convertible, boasts a better-looking design than its limited competition from Germany. Several details take their cue from Formula 1, like its arrow-shaped nose. The range starts with the 1.8-litre supercharged SLK 200 Kompressor, and goes up to V6 models such as the 3.0-litre SLK 280 and the new 3.5-litre SLK 350, while Mercedes-AMG builds the top 5.4-litre SLK 55 AMG. Standard equipment includes light-alloy wheels of various sizes, projection-beam headlamps, LED tail-lights, manual six-speed transmission on non-AMG models, stability control, remote control locking system and cruise control. Options, standard on high-spec models, include 18-inch alloy wheels, AMG bodystyling, Designo upholstery, sports suspension, speed-sensitive power steering, steering wheel gearshift buttons for the optional automatic transmission, bi-xenon headlamps with cornering light, parking sensors, electric seats with memory function, infrared remote control for the vario-roof, COMAND navigation system with DVD player, and a Harman/Kardon LOGIC7 surround-sound system with 11 speakers.

The Fiat Linea is a compact sedan, targeted mainly to sell as a fleet model. It comes with a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed automatic. Available in three trim levels, features in the basic model include 15-inch steel wheels, front power windows, keyless entry, power steering, CD stereo, manual a/c with rear ducts, body-coloured bumpers, cloth upholstery, trip computer, dual front airbags and ABS. The mid-range model adds 15-inch alloy wheels, 60/40-split rear seats, rear headrests, rear power windows,, electric mirrors, extra storage pockets and additional external trim. The top model gets 16-inch alloys, steering-mounted controls, Bluetooth, USB-port, electric driver's seat, rear sun blinds, extra chrome trim, front/rear armrests, automatic a/c with rear vents, side airbags, rear parking sensors, fog lights and more. Optional equipment include leather upholstery, rain-sensing wipers, auto-dimming mirror, auto headlights, 17-inch alloys, even more chrome trim and several other features.

In 2015, the Audi A7 Sportback got a facelift. Almost 5 metres long with a low roofline, the Audi A7 Sportback is a full-sizer riding on 18-inch to 20-inch wheels, and as with all Audi sedans,  really rides a front-wheel-drive platform, with optional 'Quattro' all-wheel-drive tacked onto the higher trim levels. Three engines are on offer - 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder, 2.8-litre V6 and a 3.0-litre supercharged unit, all of which are mated to an 'S-tronic' 7-speed automatic transmission. Standard options include 4-zone automatic air-conditioning, reverse-camera, MMI touch-sensitive navigation system, 10-speaker audio system. Optional equipment include interior leather packages for the seats and door trim, sports suspension, air suspension, front and reverse camera, park assist, side assist, night-vision, lane-assist and BOSE surround sound.

The Volvo XC60 was launched with high hopes for the Swedish company, capitalising on the small crossover vehicle market. The XC60 is a new 5-seater crossover SUV that is aimed at attracting luxury-brand buyers. The XC60 T6 is powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic with manual-shifting capability, and an all-wheel-drive system without low-range gearing. For 2010, an XC60 T5 model was introduced, with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder with a 6-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive. The smallest XC model includes new safety technology, debuting Volvo's new City Safety system, designed to help a driver avoid a collision at under 30 kph, or reduce the speed of impact at higher speeds by hitting the brakes if the vehicle in front suddenly stops and City Safety determines that a collision is likely. Another new safety featured being introduced on the XC60 is Pre-Prepared Restraints that uses a laser sensor that interacts with other technology to control the airbags and adaptive seatbelt load limiters. Other features, depending on trim level, include cloth or leather upholstery, blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, reverse camera, keyless entry, sunroof, alloy wheels, common power accessories and a CD/MP3 stereo. An R-Design body kit is optional. Standard safety features include front and side-surtain airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, and whiplash-protection headrests.

The Audi A5 originally debuted for 2008 in the GCC as a four-seater coupe based on the latest stretched A4 platform, with the range later diluted by the addition of a 5-door model. All A5 versions feature a loudmouth grille framed by rectangular headlights, a very thick C-pillar, frameless windows, and a waistline that flows upwards around the wheel arches. For 2010, the A5 Sportback 5-door liftback model joined the range, with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbo engine, a 7-speed DSG automanual and all-wheel-drive. Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control. The new platform moves the engine more rearward in relation to the front axle for better balance and handling, but ultimately the car loses out on the fun factor in any form, either due to its front-driven underpinnings or to its overly-safe Quattro system.

The Geely Emgrand 8 or EC8 is the Chinese brand's midsize sedan offering. Two 4-cylinder engines are offered for the GCC market, the 2.0-litre and the 2.4-litre, with both motors coupled to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard options on the EC8 include power steering, power windows, central locking, manual seats, remote entry key, halogen headlamps, auto A/C, rear air outlets, AM/FM radio with CD player, Bluetooth and 4 speakers, leather seats, rear sensors and 16-inch alloy wheels. Higher models get fog lamps, electric seats, 17-inch alloy wheels, auto A/C with dual-area control, LED lights, cruise control, sunroof, DVD player and 6 speakers. Safety features include driver and passenger side airbags, while the top model gets side airbags as well. ABS and electronic brake distribution (EBD) is standard.

JAC M5 is the Chinese brand's large minivan offering. It features a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed manual or 5-speed automatic. Standard features include power steering, power mirrors, electric windows, central locking with keyless entry, trip computer, fabric seats, automatic A/C, AM/FM radio with CD/USB/AUX support and 7-inch screen, 6 speakers, sunroof and alloy wheels. Optional equipment include a better entertainment system, rearview camera, folding mirrors. leather seats and xenon headlamps. Standard safety features include airbags, ABS brakes, brake assist (BA) and electronic brake distribution (EBD).

The CLS-Class "four-door coupe" was completely redesigned for the 2012 model year and facelifted for 2015. Based on the latest E-Class platform, the CLS continues the trend of offering a repackaged midsize luxury sedan in a prettier suit. Models on offer include the CLS 400 with a turbocharged 3.5-litre V6 and the CLS 500 with a 4.6-litre twin-turbo V8. The V6 model gets a 7-speed automatic transmission, while the V8 model gets a new 9-speed automatic gearbox. Standard features on all models include leather upholstery, active parking assist, memory electric front seats, COMAND multimedia system, electric rear-window blinds, automatic a/c and LED exterior running lamps. Some models gets a standard sunroof, active shape-shifting front seats with fans, rear camera, intelligent keyless entry and start and a sports package for the non-AMG models. Options include metallic paint, nicer leather, wooden steering wheel, night vision, various 18-inch and 19-inch alloy-wheel designs, DVD changer, Harman Kardon stereo, TV tuner and more.

The Toyota Land Cruiser Prado has been the same mechanically since 2010, getting few tweaks to the exterior, with the most significant facelift coming in 2018. There are two "VVT-i" engine choices for the Land Cruiser Prado - a 2.7-litre 4-cylinder and a 4.0-litre V6. In Saudi Arabia, additionally a 3.0-litre turbocharged diesel V6 engine on offer. The Land Cruiser Prado are proper off-road cars and all models offer standard all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing and available locking centre-differential. All petrol engines get a 6-speed automatic transmission whereas the diesel motor is mated to a 5-speed automatic. The basic Prado 2.7L, known as TX in KSA and EXR in UAE, comes with 17-inch alloy wheels, front LED fog lamps, black front grille, black power mirrors and door handles, rear spoiler, side steps, mud guards, fabric seating for seven, front and rear manual a/c, CD/MP3 6-speaker stereo,rear parking sensors, ABS with EBD and brake-assist, dual front airbags and floor-mounted spare tyre, a cool box, steering audio controls, USB/AUX ports and Bluetooth. The mid-range Prado 2.7L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, gets 18-inch alloy wheels, front parking sensors, body-coloured trim, leather steering wheel and shift lever, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cool box and more, dual-zone auto a/c, cruise control and rear view camera. The UAE also gets a Prado 2.7L in VXR trim that adds powered front seats, chrome front grille, silver roof rails, leather upholstery and navigation. The basic Prado 4.0L, known as EXR in UAE, comes with a 6-speaker stereo with Bluetooth and USB/AUX ports, steering audio controls, rear parking sensors, LED fog lamps, manual a/c, fabric seats, dual airbags, stability control, ABS, smart key with engine start/stop button, cruise control, side steps and hill start/descent assist. All UAE-bound V6 Prado models have a door-mounted spare tyre. The mid-range Prado 4.0L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, comes with roof rails, sunroof, front bumper guard and uphill/downhill assist on all automatic models. The TXL additionally gets a tow hitch and side mouldings, while the GXR instead gets side/curtain/knee airbags, dual-zone a/c, extra chrome trim, rear camera and navigation. A higher-spec Prado 4.0L trim, known as TXL2 in KSA and VXR in UAE, comes with sunroof, dual auto a/c, rear camera, navigation, auto-levelling LED headlights, sunshades, remote start, leather, front and rear parking sensors and power front seats. The Prado 4.0L in top Limited trim gains 18-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights with daytime running lamps, leather seats, power front seats with memory, front and rear parking sensors with rear camera, side/curtain/knee airbags, 14-speaker JBL stereo with voice control and steering-wheel buttons, multi-touch screen with navigation, remote engine starter, self-leveling KDSS suspension, power-folding third row, ventilated front seats, Multi-Terrain Select with four cameras, rear entertainment system, blind-spot monitor, crawl control and rear cross traffic alert.

The M is a car very similar to the G35, only slightly larger in size. Ever so lightly facelifted for 2008, it is offered with either a 3.5-litre V6 or a 4.5-litre V8 mated to the usual five-speed automatic transmission with manual-shift mode and a rear-wheel-drive chassis. The M35 and M45 are also a little more luxurious than the G35, by virtue of its extra cabin space. The suspension is independent double-wishbone in front and multi-link independent rear. Rear Active Steer adjusts the geometry of the rear suspension, according to steering input and vehicle speed, to enhance low-speed manoeuvrability and high-speed stability. Standard features on the M35 sedans include heated and cooled leather seats, ten-way power driver's seat, six-way power passenger seat, intelligent key with pushbutton ignition, Bluetooth, 18-inch wheels, six-CD/MP3 Bose stereo, vehicle information system with seven-inch screen, xenon headlamps with adaptive front lighting, and power sunroof. Optional features include surround sound with 14 speakers, DVD-based navigation system with eight-inch colour monitor, DVD entertainment system, and laser-based intelligent cruise control.

The F-150 delivers all the manly attributes of toughness, strength, and imposing size, although it is largely sold here as a fashion statement for tiny men. Redesigned for 2009 and updated in 2011, the fully-loaded F-150 crew-cab is sold here as more of a lifestyle vehicle, offering interior design and comfort that would rival some luxury cars. Properly equipped, it can haul more than a tonne in its bed. The F-150 is comfortable as well, with a quiet and refined ride. It comes with dual front and side airbags, cloth or leatherette seats, CD/MP3 stereo, and air conditioning as standard. Other available features include an optional 4.2-inch LCD screen, hill descent control, electronic locking differential settings and stability control. A host of power and luxury options are available too. For all these reasons, the F-150 has been America's best-selling full-size pickup for nearly 30 consecutive years. It is the most most profitable vehicle Ford makes. It is available in various trim levels, variations, and specialty models, including quad cab, single cab and dual cab model, with various bed sizes. New engines redefined the line-up for 2011, with a new 3.7-litre V6 and a new 5.0-litre V8, both from the Mustang, and fitted with automatic transmissions and a choice of rear-wheel-drive or four-wheel-drive. The top version is called the Platinum, while a special Harley-Davidson trim is also available. The F-150 SVT Raptor also became available on special-order, in 6.2-litre V8 form, and identifiable by its unique body mods and aggressive offroad suspension.

The compact V50 wagon and its S40 sedan sibling are based on the same front-wheel-drive platform as the Mazda 3 and the Ford Focus, all of which come under the Ford umbrella. Yet Volvo claims that the V50 is a true Volvo, asserting unique premium features only found in the Volvo. The V50 is an obviously small car, but it looks a lot like its larger siblings with its signature new-age-Volvo styling. There are three engine choices, all of them the corporate oddball five-cylinder, except for the base 1.6-litre four-cylinder with manual gearbox. The range includes a basic 2.4-litre and a higher-tuned 2.4-litre, all offered with automatic with tiptronic in this region. Markets outside this region get all-wheel-dive models too. The interior has an ultra-slim centre console that seems to be free-floating, with extra storage space behind it. The safety package includes a patented zonal front structure using differing strengths of high-strength steel to disperse force away from passengers in a crash. Dual front airbags, SIPS side impact protection, curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection are all standard.

An all-new Chevrolet Silverado was released as a 2014 model year. Exterior-wise, the styling carries pretty much the same DNA as the previous model but the new front fascia seems more imposing now. That is because they have added bigger headlights and a huge grille. GM consciously kept the design similar as, unlike the UAE where big pickup trucks are more of a statement, in the U.S. market it is a high volume seller among conservative buyers. A Z71 package is available which includes stronger shocks, front tow hooks and extra under-body protection. The interior is where the main changes will be, with the new 4.2-inch display on the dashboard. More soft-touch material has been added around the cockpit. The new Silverado pickups will have 12-volt outlets, five USB ports and a SD-card slot. A new 4.3-litre V6 engine adds to the family of 5.3-litre and 6.2-litre V8 motors. They will all be mated to a six-speed automatic. For improving fuel economy, the V8 engines have cylinder deactivation and direct injection.

The Renault Duster, a rebadged Dacia, released an all-new model for 2019. This sub-compact SUV comes with a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine mated with a CVT or a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, available in either a two-wheel-drive or in an all-wheel-drive, mated to a 4-speed automatic transmission. Interestingly, the 2WD model comes with a torsion-beam rear suspension, while the 4WD model gives up some boot space to make way for an independent rear suspension. The rear seats fold down as standard, and split-folding on all but the base model, while you can transport longer items if the front passenger seat is folded down as well. The basic PE version comes with two-wheel-drive, 4-speed automatic, cloth upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo with USB port and Bluetooth with buttons behind steering wheel, unpainted bumpers, 16-inch steel wheels, front power windows, keyless entry, folding rear bench seat, power steering and manual a/c. All models have two standard airbags. The higher-spec SE can be had in 2WD automatic or special-order 4WD manual drivetrains, and adds standard fog lamps, trip computer, ABS with Emergency Brake Assist, extra front-passenger airbag, rear power windows, electric mirrors, 16-inch alloy wheels, painted bumpers, leatherette steering wheel and extra chrome trim. The SE version can be further upgraded with leather seats with additional pyrotechnic pre-tensioners on the front seatbelts as well as side airbags. The exterior package on the SE version also adds standard chrome door mirrors, longitudinal roof rails, front/rear skid plates and side-skirt covers. Extra tinted rear windows, rear quarter glass and rear windscreen round up the list, as is a split-folding rear seat, height adjustable driver's seat and height-adjustable steering wheel. A comprehensive range of accessories,including wind reflectors, side steps, wheel arch mouldings, chrome exhaust trim and mudflaps, is also available.

The original Continental by Bentley is a large, expensive, luxury coupÃƒÂ© made by Rolls-Royce for a 10-year run. It was the first Bentley in 25 years to not feature a body shared with a Rolls-Royce model. It was also the first Bentley to use a GM  4-speed automatic transmission to work Bentley's long-running twin-turbo 6.8-litre V8. Power output of the earliest models are unknown, as Rolls Royce was too snobby to reveal numbers. But back then, the Continental was still the quickest, most expensive, and most powerful Bentley ever. The convertible version was called the Bentley Azure, launched in 1995. The cabin featured usual Bentley traits such as acres of wood, leather and chrome. The standard model was known as the Continental R, but 1994 saw production of a severely-limited Continental S, and then the shortened Continental T was introduced in 1996 as a performance model. Mulliner editions, which started in 1999, added performance upgrades on both the R and the T. A handful of Continental SC models were built in 1999, with a huge lift-out glass sunroof.

The bulbous new-for-2010 Prado SWB gets only a single base petrol engine. The GCC-spec Prado 3-door gets a 2.7-litre 4-cylinder with a 4-speed automatic or a 5-speed manual. It comes with four-wheel ventilated disc brakes, independent front and live-axle rear suspension. It comes with "active" traction control and rear diff lock, all with low-range gearing. Standard features for the interior include power steering, power windows, manual A/C, keyless entry, rear parking sensors, fabric upholstery, chrome door handles, tilt-telescoping steering column, dual front airbags, stability control and ABS with EBD and brake-assist.

European motorcycle-maker KTM, introduced their first ever car with the X-Bow. KTM basically transferred its principles from two wheels to four, with a track-biased car that can be driven on the street. But KTM developers have kept the weight of the vehicle extremely light by removing everything that is not needed, including body panels, doors and a windshield. Parts of the suspension are intentionally visible. Built on a carbon-fibre chassis, a 'crash box' in the front nose absorbs collision energy, while roll bars are integrated into the structure, which is all good considering there are no airbags. An options kit is available on request which includes having additional struts mounted at designated points. The Audi-sourced 4-cylinder FSI turbo engine is made of aluminium and mated to a 6-speed manual or an optional 6-speed DSG automanual transmission. Brembo brakes, a limited-slip differential, and four-point seat-belts round out the standard package. There are no electronic driving aids, no power steering and no roof, although a cloth tarpaulin is available to cover the interior when not in use.

The Sierra range is GMC's line of full-size pickup trucks, and covers everything from passenger pickups to big honking diesel monsters with six wheels and more. The Sierra 1500 pickup is the identical twin of the second-best selling truck in the United States, namely the Chevy Silverado. The Sierra 1500 light pickup version is about the only vehicle that you can drive from this range without offending everyone around you with your show of excess, while the Sierra 1500 HD trucks should best be used if you work at a place that requires regular hauling. The Sierra is available in three cab lengths, 2-door short cab, 3 or 4-door extended cab, and front-hinged 4-door crew cab. Three cargo beds are available, including a short box, a standard box, and a long box. The short box is only available with the extended or crew cab, and is the only option on the 4-door. Engines include a 4.3-litre V6, a 4.8-litre V8 and a 5.3-litre V8, all with 4-speed automatics. A luxury Sierra Denali version was introduced in 2009, with a 6.2-litre V8 mated to a 6-speed automatic. All versions come in either rear-wheel-drive or four-wheel-drive form. Along with leather and special exterior trim, the Denali gets standard features such as Bluetooth, power-adjustable pedals, auto-dimming inside mirror, dual-zone auto a/c, rain-sensing wipers, remote starting system, rear parking sensors, MP3-capable stereo with a six-disc in-dash CD changer, Bose premium speakers, rear-seat audio, power-sliding rear window, navigation, sunroof and an optional DVD rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include at least front airbags and ABS brakes, while higher trim levels get side-curtain airbags and stability control, among other options.

Opel Astra returned to the UAE and GCC as a 2013 model. Three models will be sold here - Astra Enjoy sedan, the Astra Cosmo hatchback and Astra GTC hatchback. The first two models get the 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, whereas the GTC gets a turbocharged 1.4-litre 4-cylinder motor. They all get a 6-speed automatic transmission. Basic options include a single-zone manual A/C, central locking with remote, power windows, cruise control, daytime running lamps, rear parking sensors, fog lamps, speed sensitive power steering, driver seat manual adjustable, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3/Aux in support and 17-inch alloy wheels. The higher models get dual zone automatic A/C, sunroof, leather steering wheel, outside mirror power foldable, 18-inch alloy wheels, flex-ride with continuous damping control and driver selectable sport/tour modes. The GTC gets 20-inch alloy wheels and a rear spoiler. Safety features include driver and passenger front, side and curtain airbags, electronic stability program (ESP) and ABS as standard on all models.

The Volvo V60 Polestar is the top performance trim of the little wagon. Under the hood, it gets a turbocharged and supercharged 2.0-llitre inline-4 cylinder engine for 2017, along with a new 8-speed automatic transmission, revised electric steering, slightly redesigned wheels and retuned suspension. The cabin features extensive soft-touch materials and Volvo's trademark 'floating' console. Standard features include power windows, electric mirrors, alloy wheels, CD/MP3 stereo, front and side-curtain airbags, keyless entry with starter motor, leather, navigation, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitor, adaptive HID headlights, sunroof and more. Volvo's unique 'City Safety' feature is standard, whereby the system brakes by itself to avoid hitting cars and pedestrians. It is available at very few GCC dealers.

An all-new Ford Explorer came out in 2020. The new chassis has gone back to becoming a proper SUV instead of a crossover, so off-road ability has improved. Under the hood, the standard engine gets a 2.3-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine. Then there is a hybrid model which gets a 3.3-litre V6 engine combined with an electric motor. The top model is the 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 engine. All engines are mated to an 10-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, tri-zone A/C, LED auto headlamps, 8-inch infotainment system, 6 speakers Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, cloth seats, 8-way adjustable power driver's seat, power liftgate reverse camera and 18-inch alloy wheels. The higher models get leather seats, hand's free liftgate, 20 and 21-inch wheels, digital instrument cluster, and better audio system. Standard safety features include 7 airbags, ABS, brake assist, pedestrian detection, blind spot monitor, forward-collision warning and post-collision braking. Higher models get lane centering and evasive steering assist.

The fifth generation Honda Odyssey came out in 2018, featuring a new design and improvements in technology and safety. The Odyssey is still the same size, but improvements have been made to the structure to improve efficiency and safety. In 2021, it received a facelift and updated interior and safety features. Under the hood, the 3.5-litre V6 engine is carried over, connected to a new 10-speed automatic transmission, for better performance and fuel efficiency. Standard features on the 2021 Honda Odyssey include power windows, power mirrors, central locking, electric sliding doors, fabric seats, halogen headlamps, LED daytime running lamps, LED tail lights, 8-inch touchscreen display audio, Apple CarPlay, USB, AUX, Bluetooth, 6 speakers and subwoofer, cruise control, push start button, and 18-inch alloy wheels. Higher models get 10.2-inch screen rear entertainment system, navigation, 11 speakers, leather seats, wireless phone charging, automatic AC,  and 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include front, side, curtain and knee airbags, ABS, traction control, stability control, hill-start assist, electronic brake distribution and tyre pressure monitoring system. Higher trims get additional blind spot monitor and Honda Sensing.

Toyota created the IMV platform to serve its budget-oriented lineup, and one of the products of this venture is the Innova. The IMV platform consists of a body-on-chassis setup, offering more refinement in its larger vehicles. The Innova received its second facelift for the 2012 model-year. The minivan attempts to resemble a 4WD in height, with a high waistline and four forward-opening doors, but it ends up looking like a van. The only engine is a 2.7-litre four-cylinder straight from the Fortuner, offered with a 4-speed automatic in the UAE, but a 5-speed manual is offered as a base model in Saudi Arabia and other GCC markets. All versions are well-equipped, seat eight people and get a rear seat slide mechanism to improve legroom, along with infinitely-configurable seats. Standard features include new CD/MP3 stereo with 4 speakers and USB port, dual-zone manual a/c, power & tilt steering, power windows, keyless entry, central locking, multi-information display, fabric seats, fake wood trim, 15-inch steel wheels, fog lamps, airbags for driver and front passenger, and ABS brakes. The top trim gets rear parking sensors, auto-dimming mirror, 15-inch alloys, 6-speaker stereo, auto a/c, leatherette steering wheel, chrome door handles and faux wood. Incidentally, the Innova is considered a luxury vehicle in third-world markets.

The Jaguar XK received a face-lift for 2012. The XK Convertible are powered by a 5.0-litre V8 direct-injection engine, while a supercharged version of the same V8 powers the high-performance XKR. Both engines are mated to a six-speed automatic gearbox with paddle shifters. An even more powerful XKR-S was released in 2012 with the same supercharged 5.0-litre engine but producing even more horsepower. Changes include a new wider front grille, enlarged vents in the lower grille with chrome accents, LED daytime running lights and slightly thinner headlamps. Its rigid chassis and CATS adaptive suspension aim for a smooth ride and sporty cornering. Standard equipment includes DVD navigation, keyless entry and keyless start, a seven-inch video display, Bluetooth capability, cruise control, a 6-CD/MP3 player, rear park assist, cruise control, and electronic parking brake. Options include adaptive cruise control with a forward-alert system that sounds an audible warning, full soft leather upholstery, and a CD stereo system. Safety feature include front and side airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, dynamic stability control with a track feature, and electronic rollover mitigation.

The Opel Corsa is the smallest offering from the German manufacturer in the Middle East market. It received a significant update to the exterior in 2015. The base model comes with a 4-cylinder 1.4-litre engine, mated to a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic transmission. There is a 3-door and 5-door hatchback version to choose from. Standard options include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, manual A/C, AM/FM radio, cloth upholstery and steel wheels. The higher models get a better entertainment system with a CD player and MP3/iPod/AUX support, and alloy wheels. All Corsa variants are also equipped with ABS brakes, featuring brake assist and electronic brakeforce distribution.

The Lexus GS received a facelift back in 2016 and gained a new entry-level model, the 200t, which replaced the GS 250. Later on, they renamed it to GS 300 which is currently sold only in some markets. Other models include the GS 350 and the GS 450h hybrid. The GS 300 comes with a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The GS The GS 350 comes with a 3.5-litre direct-injection V6, also with a 8-speed paddle-shiftable automatic. The GS 450h comes with a 3.5-litre engine mated to a compact, water-cooled electric motor powered by a nickel-metal hydride battery pack, and a CVT automatic. Identifiable by its Lexus trademark 'spindle' grille and LED running lamps, the GS comes in various trim levels. The base model comes with 18-inch alloys, smart keyless entry and start, moonroof, fabric upholstery, powered front seats and steering wheel adjustment, rear camera, 12-speaker CD/MP3/DVD stereo with USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cruise control, bi-xenon headlights, parking sensors, dual-zone auto a/c, and a "dynamics management" system. Higher trim levels add ventilated front seats, leather seats, and an 8-inch screen with hard-drive navigation. The GS 350 also comes in various trim levels, the basic version getting all the features of the top GS 200t, as well as a card-type key. Higher trim levels include turning headlights, nicer leather, further-adjustable front seats, 17-speaker stereo with a 12.3-inch screen, radar cruise control, adaptive variable suspension, heads-up display, pre-crash safety system, and lane-change assist. The top GS 350 comes with an F-Sport package that includes 19-inch wheels, special upholstery, four-wheel-steering and a body kit. The GS 450h, available in only a few GCC markets such as the UAE, comes only in fully-optioned F-Sport trim. Standard safety features include front, side, curtain and knee airbags, as well as stability control, and ABS with EBD and brake-assist.

The long-running Mercedes-Benz Sprinter van has been facelifted for the 2014 model year. It can be classified as one of the largest "light" commercial vehicles on offer in the GCC market. It comes with a range of petrol and diesel engines, with three roof heights, various wheelbase lengths, and several body trims, including panel-van, pickup and crew-bus styles. Apparently, this German-built van holds three times as much cargo as its Japanese rivals, with standard safety features to boot, such as airbags, ESP and three-point seatbelts for all passengers, and with 40,000 km service intervals for the diesel models, it ends up offering reasonable overall value. Optional safety features include lane-keeping assist, blind-spot assist, collision-prevention assist and high-beam assist.

A new generation Ford Mustang was introduced in 2015. In 2018 it received a facelift and some power upgrades. There is no more V6 engine offered, with only 2.3-litre turbo and the V8 engines carrying over. All engines can be had with either a 6-speed manual transmission or a new 10-speed automatic transmission. The interior gets the MyFord infotainment system with SYNC 3. For the first time, Ford has introduced independent rear suspension for this generation Mustang, which helps improve handling. Standard features include power windows, power steering, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, manual A/C, fabric seats, paddle shifters and alloy rims. The higher models get navigation, rear-view camera, leather seats, more speakers, engine push-start and automatic A/C. Safety standards include driver and passenger airbags, electronic stability control, ABS brakes and traction control.

The Mercedes-Benz Vito is a midsize commercial van that can be outfitted as a cargo carrier or as a passenger transport. The cargo vans can be had with three turbocharged 2.1-litre 4-cylinder diesel engines with different states of tune, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 5-speed automatic transmission. The UK-built luxury passenger carrier version gets a 3.5-litre V6 engine, mated to a 5-speed automatic. All models are rear-wheel-drive. Basic options include power steering, front power windows and central locking with remote control. Safety features include ESP, driver-side airbag, third brake light and three-point seatbelts for all seats.

The YRV has been billed as a young and innovative car, posing as a direct rival to models in a niche that no one wants to deal with. It's cheap to own, easy to drive and offers a similar package to the Toyota Yaris hatchback, with which it shares an engine, all for a cheaper price. The car has adequate space for two adults in the front, while the back may accomodate two adults in tight settings, or maybe three kids comfortably. The car is a comfortable cruiser on long journeys, although it will lose this advantage when the roads get slightly bumpy. The 1.3-litre 4-cylinder, with the manual or auto, lacks power for swift overtaking manouevres, but is fine for town traffic driving, as it is exceptionally light and easy to handle, paticularly when parking. Features include a radio cassette player, power windows, central locking, rear foldable seat, 14-inch steel wheels and not much else. It has a 40-litre fuel tank, which should last a while as the car is very frugal indeed. It looks like a little van though, which can put many buyers off.

Mercedes-Benz GLC replaced the GLK back in 2016. It gets a whole new exterior design. The interior gets a wide centre console and a screen sticking out on top of the A/C vents. It is said to be more spacious than the GLK, thanks to the 11.8 cm longer wheelbase. It is also 80 kg lighter than the GLK, thanks to a mix of different materials used to make the body which includes aluminium and high-strength steels. In 2020 it got a slight facelift and a better infotainment system. Under the hood, the GLC200 and GLC 300 get a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine with two different tunes, both available only in four-wheel drive (4Matic). Power is delivered via a 9-speed automatic transmission. In 2020, the engine became a mild hybrid, due to the addition of a small battery to aid performance and fuel economy. Features include AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it is not really that good off-road, but gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. It is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. This wagon offers room for five passengers, with the option of two additional rear-facing seats in the luggage area. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, cruise control, electric driver's seat, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, a power front passenger seat,  16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, and WHIPS whiplash protection.

The SQ 5 is the top performance version of the Q5 compact SUV. Under the hood, it comes with a 3.0-litre supercharged engine, mated to a 8-speed automatic transmission. The four-wheel-drive model gets standard features like power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, Nappa leather interior, cruise control, keyless entry and start, auto headlamps, auto headlight range adjustment, fog lamps, xenon headlamps, LED daytime running lamps, LED taillights, navigation, panoramic glass roof, 3-zone automatic A/C, Bluetooth, Bang & Olufsen sound system, front and rear parking sensors and 21-inch ally wheels. Optional equipment include electric front seats with memory function, electric folding mirrors with heated and memory, side steps, adaptive cruise control, adaptive lights, red brake callipers, dynamic steering, more leather padding and sports seats. Safety features include front, side and head airbags, traction control, brake assist and stability control.

The Mitsubishi Xpander is actually an MPV, guised as an SUV. Under the hood, is a small 1.5-litre engine, mated to a CVT. Standard features include third-row seating, power steering, power windows, power mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, cruise control, manual AC, rear cooler, fabric seats, halogen lamps, rear parking sensors, rearview camera and 16-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, hill-start assist, tyre pressure monitor, stability control, ABS and brake assist.

The Mercedes-Benz Vito is a midsize commercial van that can be outfitted as a cargo carrier or as a passenger transport. Changes were made in 2015 which included standard Attention Assist and Crosswind Assist, optional Intelligent Light System which included LED indicators, LED daytime running lamps, LED low-beam headlamps, and main beam with cornering light function. It remained the same for 2016. The cargo vans can be had with three turbocharged 2.1-litre 4-cylinder diesel engines with different states of tune, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 5-speed automatic transmission. The UK-built luxury passenger carrier version gets a 3.5-litre V6 engine, mated to a 5-speed automatic. All models are rear-wheel-drive. Basic options include power steering, front power windows and central locking with remote control. Safety features include ESP, driver-side airbag, third brake light and three-point seatbelts for all seats.

The Volkswagen Teramont is the German brand's first entry into the seven-seater SUV market. While it is longer than the Touareg, it is not their flagship SUV. It is built in the United States and sold as the Atlas over there. VW felt the demand for SUVs and 7-seaters in this region was healthy enough to be introduced here. Teramont continues the tradition of naming their SUV line-up starting with a "T". Under the hood, the crossover has two engine options. The standard engine is a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder unit, which is available in FWD and AWD, while there is the optional 3.6-litre V6 motor available only as AWD. Largely optional features include cloth or leather upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo, navigation, Bluetooth phone, intelligent keyless entry, starter button, panoramic sunroof, real wood trim, power-folding rear seat, adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go function, lane departure warning system, blind-spot monitor, pre-crash system with full automatic emergency braking, ABS, a full set of front and side airbags, parking assist with four cameras, LED tail lamps, LED headlights, power-adjustable front seats with memory, seat heaters and a choice of 18-inch, 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels.

The redesigned Ssangyong Korando made its debut in the Middle East in 2013, as a sub-compact crossover. Only the petrol engine will be sold here, which is a 4-cylinder 2.0-litre motor, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. It can be had in either two-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. Standard features include power steering, air conditioning, electric windows, electronic stability control, CD/MP3 player, Bluetooth, cruise control, reverse sensors, 16-inch alloy wheels and a leather steering wheel. The higher models get 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels.

Big and conservative, the Kia Mohave is supposed to strengthen Kia's "family" SUV line-up and brand image in the world market. With a 3.8-litre V6 engine mated with the 6-speed automatic transmission, the Kia Mohave is characterized by fully-independent air suspension and its various safety systems, including the ABS brakes, electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD), brake assist, stability control, traction control, and front and side airbags. Furthermore, the Mohave is equipped with Downhill Assist Control, keeping the vehicle's speed steady while going down straight and strong slopes, while a Hill-Start Assist Control is also available. The Mohave comes with a 600W stereo with six-CD changer, seven-seater capability, cloth or leather trim, DVD player, reverse camera and all the usual power accessories. The Mohave rides on a  truck-like body-on-frame platform and comes with four-wheel-drive and low-range gearing, which allows it to be classified as an off-road vehicle by default.
For 2021, an all-new Mercedes-Benz S-Class came out.

The Ford Flex received a facelift and new engines for the 2013 model. Touted as a crossover, it is more of a boxy-shaped minivan alternative. Offered in various trim levels, the Flex is powered by either a 3.5-litre V6 or a turbocharged 3.5-litre "EcoBoost" V6 engine, mated with a 6-speed automatic transmission and a choice of front-wheel-drive or all-wheel drive. Airy and spacious, It offers four forward-opening doors, seating for six or seven depending on chosen options, and can be had with a refrigerator, dual panoramic sunroofs, cruise control, common power accessories, capless fuel-filler, HID headlights and LED tails, two-tone paintjob, programmable interior LED lighting, 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels, 10-speaker Sony stereo, and Ford's new Sync multimedia system which can connect and control any Bluetooth phone or USB music player. Safety features include Advance Trac with Roll Stability Control, multiple front and side airbags and ABS brakes.

The Ferrari 458 Italia is the successor to the F430. Going on sale in 2010, the 458 has a new mid-mounted 4.5-litre V8 engine, incorporating direct injection and mated only to a 7-speed dual-clutch automated manual gearbox that shifts in 0.05 seconds. Technology includes an E-Diff differential and an F1-Trac skid control system. The brakes feature a new system called "˜prefill' so when the driver's foot lifts off the throttle, the pistons in the calipers move the pads towards the discs to reduce the stopping distance. The 458 Italia's body and chassis are all aluminium, with a Pininfarina-designed exterior. The Vehicle Dynamic Assistance monitors the operating parameters of the most important areas of the car engine/gearbox, tyres and brakes. The VDA offers various settings that enables the driver to tune the car for the ideal operating conditions. The 458 is also available with modern conveniences like Bluetooth, CD stereo, rear camera, navigation, stability control and ABS, as well as a full set of front and side airbags.

For 2013, an Audi S5 Quattro coupe debuted, with a 3.0-litre supercharged engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic. Audi has also introduced a new rear diffuser that appears to be more cosmetic than the one found on previous models.Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Lexus GS received a facelift back in 2016 and gained a new entry-level model, the 200t, which replaced the GS 250. Later on, they renamed it to GS 300 which is currently sold only in some markets. Other models include the GS 350 and the GS 450h hybrid. The GS 300 comes with a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The GS The GS 350 comes with a 3.5-litre direct-injection V6, also with a 8-speed paddle-shiftable automatic. The GS 450h comes with a 3.5-litre engine mated to a compact, water-cooled electric motor powered by a nickel-metal hydride battery pack, and a CVT automatic. Identifiable by its Lexus trademark 'spindle' grille and LED running lamps, the GS comes in various trim levels. The base model comes with 18-inch alloys, smart keyless entry and start, moonroof, fabric upholstery, powered front seats and steering wheel adjustment, rear camera, 12-speaker CD/MP3/DVD stereo with USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cruise control, bi-xenon headlights, parking sensors, dual-zone auto a/c, and a "dynamics management" system. Higher trim levels add ventilated front seats, leather seats, and an 8-inch screen with hard-drive navigation. The GS 350 also comes in various trim levels, the basic version getting all the features of the top GS 200t, as well as a card-type key. Higher trim levels include turning headlights, nicer leather, further-adjustable front seats, 17-speaker stereo with a 12.3-inch screen, radar cruise control, adaptive variable suspension, heads-up display, pre-crash safety system, and lane-change assist. The top GS 350 comes with an F-Sport package that includes 19-inch wheels, special upholstery, four-wheel-steering and a body kit. The GS 450h, available in only a few GCC markets such as the UAE, comes only in fully-optioned F-Sport trim. Standard safety features include front, side, curtain and knee airbags, as well as stability control, and ABS with EBD and brake-assist.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class came out in 2019. The exterior and interior have been completely changed to incorporate their new design language, first seen on the Mercedes-Benz A-Class. New engines now power the CLS-Class which includes a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbo for the CLS 350, the 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 motor for the CLS-450 and the 3.0-litre turbo inline-6 engine coupled with an electric motor for the CLS-53 AMG. All of them get the 9-speed automatic transmission. The CLS 450 and CLS 53 AMG are available only in all-wheel-drive. Standard features are aplenty which include leather seats, keyless entry, central locking, engine stop-start button, digital instrument cluster, infotainment system with Bluetooth/USB support, cruise control, LED headlights and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment includes air suspension and a widescreen cockpit consisting of two 12.3-inch displays on the dashboard. An AMG line is also available and includes AMG body styling, a diamond pattern radiator grille, 19-inch alloy wheels, and a flat-bottomed sports steering wheel.

The Renault Clio RS got a new model in 2014 and started making its way to the GCC as a 2015 model year. It gets 1.6-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed EDC automatic gearbox with paddle shifters. The standard RS model gets remote central locking, auto A/C, LED daytime running lamps, power windows, power-foldable door mirrors, rain sensing wipers, cruise control, leather steering wheel and gear knob, sports front seats, automatic headlamps, rear sensors, radio and entertainment system with Bluetooth, USB & iPod connectivity and jack plug, navigation system,  handsfree entry and start system, 18-inch alloy wheels, rear bumper air diffuser with twin exhausts and rear spoiler. The RS+ model gets additional leather front bucket seats with red-stitching and rear-view camera. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, ABS with electronic brake distribution (EBD) and electronic stability program (ESP) with anti-skid regulation (ASR).

The Ford Mustang received a GT500-inspired facelift for 2013, along with a few mild tweaks. All Ford Mustang models get a new front-end with revised lower air intakes and a new splitter. HID headlights are now standard on all versions, while GT models get a new bonnet with functional air extractors as well as optional HID foglamps. New body-coloured side-skirts and rear lower bumper as well as new 17-inch, 18-inch and 19-inch wheels are also available. There is now a high-gloss black panel in the rear between the redesigned taillamps. The side mirrors have LED lamps in them that project the Mustang pony logo onto the ground when the doors are unlocked. New colours include new shades of green and blue. The 5.0-litre V8 engine also receives a slight increase in horsepower. The Mustang is offered in metal-top coupe and glass-roof versions. Only the metal-top coupe will be offered with the manual gearbox with either engine, while the glass-roof ones will only be sold with an automatic. The interior comes in cloth or leather, a soft-touch dashboard and aluminium trim, though some hard plastics remain. Standard equipment includes four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, stability control, dual exhausts, power mirrors, front and side-curtain air bags, power locks with remote keyless entry, power windows, cruise control, optional reverse camera, rear spoiler, power driver's seat and optional panoramic roof on the coupe. Roush models are available in the UAE for both the V6 and V8. Few Boss 302 models, which comes with a higher tuned 5.0-litre V8 engine, were sold in the UAE, and comes only with a 6-speed manual transmission.

Introduced in late 2016, the Bentley Bentayga is the British luxury brand's first SUV model. It is powered by a twin-turbocharged 6.0-litre W12 engine, connected to an 8-speed automatic transmission and four-wheel drive system. It gets a variable displacement system, which shuts down half of the engine under defined conditions. Intake and exhaust valves, fuel injection and ignition are all shut down on defined cylinders, with the engine running as a 6-cylinder for improved efficiency. A 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 model was introduced for 2018, also with an 8-speed automatic. Other notable features include LED headlights, a front skid-plate, front fender vents, aluminium roof-rails, panoramic glass roof and 20 to 22-inch alloy wheels. The interior is, as expected, nothing short of luxury, with its premium leather upholstery, metallic accents, an infotainment system with an 8-inch display and 22-way adjustable front seats with heating, ventilation and massage functions. Bentley is also offering a 4-seat variant with each seat having its own set of power controls and massage functions. The seats are divided by a small centre-console which consists of cup holders, storage compartments and USB charging ports. Other optional equipment include a high-end premium audio system and entertainment Android tablets with 4G, WiFi and Bluetooth connectivity, and even a self-winding Breitling dash-clock option that costs as much as the base price. A Mulliner specification adds more customisability in terms of paint, leather and wood.

The MG 350 is the Chinese-owned brand's attempt to enter into the competitive compact sedan segment. Under  the hood, it gets a 1.5 litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a five speed manual or a 4-speed automatic. Standard features in the 350 include power windows, power mirrors, radio with CD/MP3/USB/AUX support, fabric seats with manual adjustment, folding rear seats, fog lamps, front and rear disc brakes, and steel wheels. As we go higher up the range, features include climate control, leather seats, electric seats, DVD entertainment system, sunroof, rear parking sensor,bluetooth connectivity and 16-inch alloy rims. Standard safety features include ABS, electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD) and cornering brake control (CBC).

The MKT is Lincoln's full-size luxury crossover that is based on the Ford Flex, with three rows of seating and tons of space. According to Lincoln, the "T" in MKT, stands for Touring. Larger than the MKX midsize crossover and more efficient than the Navigator, the MKT is offered in the UAE with the turbocharged 3.5-litre "EcoBoost" V6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive. Offered in either 6-seater or 7-seater configurations, a second-row 60/40 split folding bench seat, optional power "fold and tumble" second-row bucket seats include heating, cooling and power lumbar adjustment, and an available 5-quart refrigerator in the centre console, alongside all the usual features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, power-adjustable front seats, CD/MP3 stereo and Bluetooth phone. A fixed-glass panoramic roof with power-assisted front and rear sunshades is standard and an opening panoramic sunroof is optional. Safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, as well as ABS and stability control.

The Audi A6 is available as a sedan and a wagon in this region, along with the sporting S6, although the wagons seem popular only for fleet duty. The engines available in the front-wheel-drive platform are the 2.0-litre inline-4 turbo, as well as the 2.4-litre and the 3.2-litre V6 powerplants, and in the Quattro all-wheel-drive platform, the 3.2-litre V6, the 4.2-litre V8, and for the S6, a 5.2-litre V10. The transmission of choice in these cars is either the CVT or the traditional six-speed automatic, depending on model. The S-Line sports package is available on 3.2 and 4.2 sedans. Other features include a Bose surround sound standard on the 4.2, adaptive cruise control and adaptive air suspension are available, and 17-inch wheels are standard on the 3.2, while the 4.2 gets 18-inch rims. The A6 attempts to offer a blend of comfort and performance, and the Quattro models certainly do well here. The 3.2 does a good job of lugging passengers around, while the 4.2 and S6 are pure muscle. The front-wheel-drive models are purely for cosmetic purposes, considering the wrong wheels put the power down, unlike rear-wheel-drive offerings from BMW and Mercedes-Benz.

The MG RX8 is the brand's midsize SUV offering. Under the hood, it gets the 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features on the base model include power steering, power windows, central locking, electric folding mirrors, LED headlamps and taillamps, LED daytime running lamps, cruise control, single zone electric A/C, fabric seats, driver seat manual lumbar adjustment, mechanical instrument cluster, 10.1-inch touch screen with USB ports, Bluetooth, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto and 6 speakers, front and rear fog lamps, roof rails, and 18-inch alloy wheels. The higher models gets all-wheel drive, leather seats, front driver and passenger powered seats, ventilated seats, 7-inch virtual instrument cluster screen, dual-zone automatic A/C, wireless charger, rear climate control, panoramic sunroof and 20-inch alloy wheels. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, side airbags, curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, hill assist control, and tyre pressure monitor. The higher models get additional blind spot monitor and lane departure warning.

The Uplander is a new attempt by General Motors to conquer the world of minivan by offering something different. It is a minivan that tries to look a little like a 4WD, and hopes that people won't notice that it is indeed just a minivan. This new seven-passenger minivan is a front-driver that is about 90 percent minivan, and the other 10% could become a quasi-4WD with the optional Versatrak all-wheel-drive, but this option is apparently not offered here. GM is calling their new line a crossover sport van. Power came from a 3.5-litre V6 powerplant in the early models, while a 3.9-litre V6 was later offered optionally, only to become the only choice since 2007. Interior features include fold-down second and third row seating, ceiling rail storage system with DVD and other entertainment features, along with a series of in-floor rear storage bins. The van still utilizes a walkthrough between seats and sliding doors for inner access, while the back has a lift-up tailgate. This van is effectively a replacement for the unloved Venture minivan, which few people knew even existed. The only Uplanders visible on the road seems to be airport taxi vehicles.

The Hyundai Sante Fe comes to the UAE and GCC as a seven-seater version. While it competes with compact crossover SUVs, it is only slightly smaller than most midsize SUVs. It comes with a choice 2 engines - the 'Theta' 4-cylinder 2.4-litre and the 'Lambda' V6 3.3-litre. Two-wheel drive is standard in the 2.4-litre base model, while all the other trims are in four-wheel drive in the higher 2.4-litre and 3.3-litre models. Some of the optional features include panoramic sunroof, 8-inch touchscreen with navigation, reverse camera, leather seats, memory seats with cooling & heating for front passengers, memory package for mirrors with auto folding, smart key with engine start, automatic lights and rain sensing wipers. Safety features include ABS, electronic brake distribution(EBD) and traction control.

The Changan Eado is a compact sedan offering from the Chinese brand. Under the hood, it gets a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic transmission. Standard features in the Eado include power windows, central locking, remote control on key, manual A/C, radio and single CD player with MP3/WMA support, 4 speakers, leather steering wheel with audio controls, USB+AUX ports, sunroof, fog lamps, parking sensors and hologen headlamps. Safety features includes front dual airbags, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD), brake assist (BA), traction control and hill assist.

This generation of the popular S-Class debuted in 2006, and was facelifted for 2010 with a mildly different grille, a revised bumper and optional LED marker lights. Almost all models offered in the GCC are the long-wheelbase version, which include the S 350 L, the S 500 L and the S 600 L, all with automatic gearboxes. A new entry-level S 300 short=wheelbase model and an S 400 HYBRID model both debuted for 2010, while the S 500 4MATIC all-wheel-drive model is also now offered in the GCC. The new model features new steps in road safety with the second generation of the PRE-SAFE occupant protection system that predicts accidents and prepares the car's occupants for the crash by initiating safety measures such as pre-tensioning seatbelts, raising seat backs to the optimum position and even closing the sunroof. In addition, it also has optional Night View Assist which is an advanced after-dark vision system. Other features include enhanced COMAND system with 8-inch display and a controller on the centre console, Airmatic adaptive suspension and adaptive brake lights. Options include a reversing camera, panoramic sunroof, AMG bodystyling and either 19-inch or 20-inch light-alloy wheels.

The rear-wheel-drive H1 is marketed as a contender in the minivan market for families, assuming you are looking just for obscene lot of space. It received a major makeover for 2008, and while its cabin has improved considerably, it appeals more to corporate groups as staff transportation rather than the jalopy of choice for large families who would like to travel in style and comfort. Still, Hyundai is promoting it as such. Powered by a 2.4-litre four-cylinder, it is available in various configurations, ranging from a 3-seater all the way to a 12-seater. The top spec is actually a 9-seater with power front windows, electric mirrors, an automatic gearbox and a two-tone paint job. The other models don't get any of those features, and manage with a manual gearbox. All trims get power steering, radio cassette player and air-conditioning with rear vents. Boasting uniquely configurable seats and extensive luggage space, other standard features include cloth seat coverings, while options include central door locks and front fog lamps. A driver's airbag is optional, and only the top 9-seater trim gets dual airbags.

The Jimny is a longstanding Suzuki 4WD dating back to the 1980s Samurai. With its rounded 1999 facelift, it entered the modern age in with a lot of enthusiasm. Powered by a 1.3-litre four-cylinder engine, it can be had with either a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic. For what it's worth, the manual version is much quicker than the automatic one, though both are still painfully slow. Off-road, the Jimny holds its own against bigger 4WD vehicles. A separate chassis means that the Jimny has been constructed with serious off-road use in mind. Four adults can be carried on short journeys as long as they don't bring any luggage, but even then, front seat occupants will probably be called upon to sacrifice some legroom. When carrying rear passengers, the luggage area behind them is tiny. It is better to think of this vehicle as a two-seater with a fold-down rear bench. Driver and passenger airbags are available, as are ABS brakes. The Jimny is outdated, but finding another off-roader at this price is an unrealistic idea.

An all-new model of Nissan Altima was revealed for 2019. The sixth generation model features an upgraded 2.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, but the V6 has been replaced with a 2.0-litre turbocharged motor. Both engines are connected to a CVT automatic and front-wheel-drive platform. The platform itself has gained wheelbase length, which translates to more cabin space. The 2019 Altima will be offered in a range of trim levels – S, SV and SL in the 2.5L and SV, SL grades in 2.0L Turbo, although not all trims may be offered in all GCC markets. Available new features include upgraded seats with added bolstering, an updated infotainment system with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as well as an 8-inch multi-touch colour display, blind-spot monitoring with Rear Cross Traffic Alert, Automatic Emergency Braking with Pedestrian Detection, Lane Departure Warning and High Beam Assist, aside from the usual smart keyless entry and start, full set of airbags, ESP, tyre-pressure monitor, the usual power accessories and more.

Porsche released a facelifted 991.2-generation 911 GT3 sometime in early 2017. Changes made from the earlier 991.1-generation 911 GT3 are the engine and the spoiler, which is 20% taller along with the front bumper and the exhaust system. The engine is a naturally-aspirated 4.0-litre racing engine, upgraded to have the same power as the previous GT3 RS. In 2019, the GT3 RS was released with more power. Another change from the 991.1 is the introduction of the spoiler-less touring version that includes a manual transmission, along with the regular version that has a choice between manual and PDK transmissions. It also has rear-axle steering and Porsche Torque Vectoring Plus with fully variable rear axle differential lock. The regular GT3 comes with a full interior, including a touchscreen multimedia system, auto a/c, a full set of airbags and other safety features.

In 2021, the all-new Genesis G80 made its debut in the GCC. The Genesis can be had with a choice of either a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder turbocharged engine, or a 3.5-litre turbocharged V6 motor. Both engines are mated to a Hyundai-designed 8-speed automatic transmission. Rear-wheel-drive is standard in both models.

The Lincoln MKS is an all-new full-size luxury sedan produced by Ford's upscale division, continuing the brand's confusing new letter-based naming system. And although it can be considered the marque's technological flagship sedan, it still falls behind leaders in the wider market. For starters, it is based on a front-wheel-drive platform shared with the Ford Taurus. But while this can be overlooked thanks to all-wheel-drive being standard on all GCC-spec models, the main engine for this full-sizer is a new 3.7-litre V6, instead of a V8. It rides on fully-independent suspension and 20-inch polished aluminium wheels. Features include a 6-speed manually-shiftable automatic, keyless entry and start, adaptive cruise control, SYNC voice-activated multimedia system, Bluetooth, rain-sensing windshield wipers, a rearview camera system, front and rear park assist, a THX sound system with full 5.1 surround sound, vented power seats, sunroof, HID headlights, LED taillamps, wood and leather interior trim, and Ford's capless fuel-filler system. Safety features include standard front, side and curtain airbags, stability control and ABS brakes.

The compact V50 wagon and its S40 sedan sibling are based on the same front-wheel-drive platform as the Mazda 3 and the Ford Focus, all of which come under the Ford umbrella. Yet Volvo claims that the V50 is a true Volvo, asserting unique premium features only found in the Volvo. The V50 is an obviously small car, but it looks a lot like its larger siblings with its signature new-age-Volvo styling. There are three engine choices, all of them the corporate oddball five-cylinder, except for the base 1.6-litre four-cylinder with manual gearbox. The range includes a basic 2.4-litre and a higher-tuned 2.4-litre, all offered with automatic with tiptronic in this region. Markets outside this region get all-wheel-dive models too. The interior has an ultra-slim centre console that seems to be free-floating, with extra storage space behind it. The safety package includes a patented zonal front structure using differing strengths of high-strength steel to disperse force away from passengers in a crash. Dual front airbags, SIPS side impact protection, curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection are all standard.

The 5th-generation 3-Series coupe was introduced in 2007 in its current iteration, but received a facelift as well as new engines for 2010. Models currently available in some, but not all, GCC countries include the 320i with higher-tuned 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, the 325i with a 2.5-litre 6-cylinder, the sharp 330i with a 3.0-litre 6-cylinder and the hyper 335i with a 3.0-litre turbo 6-cylinder engine. They all came in 7-speed dual-clutch automanual transmissions. Manual models are not actively imported by many GCC dealers. All cars come equipped with keyless entry, cloth or leather upholstery, manual or powered front seats, electric mirrors, power windows, CD stereo and optional sunroof. The optional iDrive computer is available on all models, as are active steering, HID headlights, and alloy wheels in various sizes. All cars get multiple front and side airbags, stability control, ABS and great rear-wheel-drive handling characteristics.

The Golf R debuted in 2011 with a higher-tuned turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, DSG automanual and all-wheel-drive. The interior is very similar to the previous Golf, but some new bits include the steering wheel, 'climatronic' a/c and better noise reduction.It features sports seats, standard XDS electronic differential lock, turning HID headlights, automatic parking assist, 19-inch alloys, optional navigation, rear camera, sunroof, adaptive cruise control, usual power accessories and optional DCC adjustable suspension. Safety features include seven airbags including a knee airbag, stability control, traction control and ABS brakes,

The XC90 is Volvo's first proper 4WD vehicle, and a fairly good one at that. The seven-seater is powered by either a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, a 3.2-litre V6 or a 4.4-litre V8, all with an automatic with tiptronic function. The V8 came only in 2005. Among the three rows of seats, the second row moves front and back offering adjustable legroom, while the foldable third row seats can be tucked away to increase luggage space. Standard features include keyless entry, 17-inch wheels, CD player, trip computer, rear air-conditioning, power windows, doors, locks and mirrors, and an eight-way power driver's seat with memory. Available features also include leather seats, a power front passenger seat, memory mirrors, a power moonroof, upgraded audio with a six CD changer, 18-inch alloy wheels and self-leveling rear suspension. A sports package adds 19-inch rims, stiffer suspension and some trim pieces. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, WHIPS whiplash protection, and a rollover protection system.

The new Avalon is Toyota's rendition of the traditional big car. The Avalon was designed, engineered and built by the Toyota Technical Center in the United States. Its understated styling is more distinctive than any previous-generation Avalon, presenting a quiet look of grace. There was a very minor facelift in 2008, though no one noticed. Power produced by the powerful 3.5-litre V6 goes to the front wheels, originally via a smooth 5-speed automatic. A 6-speed automatic replaced the previous unit from 2008 onwards. Inside is a comfortable cabin lavished with tasteful materials and ergonomically-designed controls that makes this car a pleasant and cheap alternative to a Lexus. This newest Avalon is significantly larger than previous models. The front seats are roomy and comfortable and special attention was paid to back-seat comfort. The Avalon is smooth and comfortable, quiet and serene, as the suspension was tuned for ride comfort. Trim variations are limited to accessories. Standard features include a premium AM/FM/CD/cassette stereo with nine speakers, remote keyless entry, multi-function information display for audio, climate control, temperature and trip computer, among other things.

The Lexus LS has been completely overhauled for 2018, featuring major changes inside out. The handsome exterior and extravagant interior aside, this new LS will be the first Lexus LS ever to sport a V6 engine, deviating from the customary V8 application since the first LS rolled off into the international market during the 90's. There will be two models available initially - the LS 500 which sports a twin-turbo V6 engine mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission, and a LS 500 h hybrid model sporting a naturally-aspirated Atkinson-cycle V6 engine mated to two electric motors, and an industry-first hybrid automatic transmission, which is a combination of the traditional 4-speed automatic with a CVT. There will also be the F-Sport versions available, which are essentially the short wheelbase versions of the standard LS, sporting a unique body kit, chassis management system, and 20-inch alloys. Standard features include Bi-Xenon HID+halogen headlamps with AFS and daytime running lamps, Smart Entry & Start system, 19-inch alloy wheels, moonroof, blind spot monitor, leather seats, cruise control, HDD navigation system. The F-Sport further gets air suspension, paddle shifters, rear-seat entertainment system with Blu-Ray player, lane discipline system and night vision. The higher models get the options of massage seats and a pre-crash safety system.

The Peugeot 2008 is a five-seater crossover loosely based on the 208 hatchback. Available only with a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a 4-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive, it is designed to be a city-runner rather than a beach-goer. Available features include tiptronic gear-shifting, panoramic glass roof, cloth upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo, multimedia LCD display, 16-inch alloy wheels, split-folding rear seats, keyless entry, cruise control with speed limiter, power windows, eletric mirrors, front airbags and ABS, among other options.

Daihatsu aims to boost sales with its new Terios 4WD. With short front and rear overhangs, a long wheelbase and wide track, it looks like it can go off-road, but not with any real verve. It's apparently aimed at people looking for the traditional 4x4 qualities of high seating position, bad-weather traction and versatility combined with small car running costs and manoeuvrability. It is longer and wider than the previous model. The interior is about the same size as a mid-sized hatchback, with a split fold-and-tumble rear seat that frees up luggage space supposedly long enough to take a mountain bike. The front floor cross-member, tunnel, sills, B-pillars and roof-side rails are all strengthened to secure the cabin. With the rear seat in use the boot capacity is 380 litres.
