Available in the GCC with two engine choices, the entry-level V60 T4 model comes with a 1.6-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder mated to a 6-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive. The higher-spec V60 2.0T model comes with 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine mated to a 6-speed automatic as well. Later on the more powerful V60 T5 2.0-litre turbocharged engine came was offered. The cabin features extensive soft-touch materials and Volvo's trademark 'floating' console in a choice of wood, metal and graphite colours. Base features include cloth upholstery, power windows, electric mirrors, alloy wheels, CD/MP3 stereo, front and side-curtain airbags, keyless entry with starter motor and more. The higher model gets larger wheels, leather, navigation, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitor, adaptive HID headlights, sunroof and more. Volvo's unique 'City Safety' feature is standard, whereby the system brakes by itself to avoid hitting cars and pedestrians. Very few were sold in the GCC.

The redesigned Boxster roadster was introduced in 2005, and it spawned the fixed-top Cayman for the 2006 model year. Considered the entry-level Porsche offering, the cars are powered by a 2.7-litre version of the traditional Porsche flat-six engine in their base trim, while the higher-performance S versions are powered by a 3.4-litre version of the sixer. The model is considered a benchmark for sports-car handling, with rear-wheel-drive and a choice of either a manual or a manually-shiftable automatic. Standard features include power windows, electric mirrors, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, among other luxury options. The Cayman offers head airbags in combination with thorax airbags, concealed on the outer side of the backrest, alongside the usual front airbags. Luggage is space is very limited, with two trunks, one in the front and one behind the mid-mounted engine in the back.

The Cordoba is designed to appeal to sedan customers who like the Ibiza hatchback. Though similar to the Ibiza, it somehow appears a lot more conservative than the Ibiza, and the engine choices here carry forward that notion. It is keeping pace in the market with variations of the original car, by adding new Seat styling features to what is essentially the same car that was launched ages ago. In the Middle East, it is offered with only a VW-derived 1.4-litre four-cylinder engine, with an automatic transmission. Standard equipment includes ABS brakes, driver and passenger airbag, power steering, front power windows, remote central locking, 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, CD radio with six speakers, height adjustable front seats, split rear seat, cloth upholstery, height and reach adjustable steering wheel, double headlamps, three-point rear seatbelts and three rear headrests, among others. Stability system with brake assistance is an option, as are rear power windows, alloy wheels and what not.

The Mercedes-AMG C63 and C63 S are the sports variants of the C-Class. In 2017, an all-new C63 and C63 S Coupe made its debut. Under the hood, they get twin-turbocharged 4.0-litre V8 engines, mated to 7-speed automatic transmission, with the C63 S having the slightly higher power rating. Standard equipment includes power steering, power windows, automatic A/C, cruise control, xenon headlamps, radio with MP3/iPod/USB/AUX support, navigation system and leather sports seats. The C63 gets AMG RIDE CONTROL sports suspension with electronically controlled shock absorbers and the AMG DYNAMIC SELECT drive programmes. It also gets 3-stage RIDE CONTROL sport suspension, the 3-stage ESP and the optional button for the performance exhaust system with flap control. Standard safety equipment includes front drive and passenger airbags, curtain airbags, drowsiness warning system ATTENTION ASSIST and COLLISION PREVENTION ASSIST PLUS, which helps to avoid rear-end collisions.

In 2013, the Audi A5 Sportback received a facelift and new engine options. All A5 versions feature a loudmouth grille framed by rectangular headlights, a very thick C-pillar, frameless windows, and a waistline that flows upwards around the wheel arches. The 4-door A5 Sportback comes with three engine options; a 1.8-litre 4-cylinder turbocharged engine, a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder motor and a 3.0-litre V6 supercharged unit. Power is delivered through a CVT automatic for the front-wheel-drive 1.8-litre version, and a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic is mated to the Quattro all-wheel-drive versions. Available technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, smart keyless entry and start, and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Veyron 16.4 was a long-running pet project by Volkswagen to create the fastest production car in the world at the time, reintroducing the Bugatti badge in style. Goofy looks notwithstanding, the styling is an essential part of the design to ensure total stability at top speed. The car is powered by an 8.0-litre quad-turbo W16 engine derived from Volkswagen designs, mated to all-wheel-drive and a seven-speed direct-shift automanual gearbox. The fully customisable interior is covered in leather and metal, with numerous features such as CD stereo, navigation and more. The single-piece carbon-fibre monocoque does well in crash tests, while airbags give the driver and passenger additional protection. The high-speed tyres designed specially for the Veyron 16.4 incorporate the PAX System that ensures safe handling even after sudden pressure loss. Another safety element is the rear spoiler that acts as a "˜parachute brake' during emergency braking. A second key must be engaged when stopped to initiate "top speed" mode, when the rear spoiler sets itself to a lower position, the front air diffusers close and the vehicle lowers to further improve aerodynamic downforce. A limited-to-150-pieces Grand Sport model was released in mid-2008 with a removable targa-roof panel.

The Hyundai Sonata has received a complete makeover for the 2015 model-year, taking a more conservative approach to its styling while retaining mostly the same mechanical specs. All models come with a carryover 2.4-litre 4-cylinder mated to a 6-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive. A new turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder was introduced later in 2015. The base model, known as Sonata GL in UAE, comes with 16-inch steel wheels, power windows and mirrors, fog lamps, keyless entry, rear camera, cruise control, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with Bluetooth, ABS and one only airbag. The GL can be optioned up with 16-inch or 17-inch alloys, rear parking sensors, panoramic sunroof, leatherette steering, electric folding mirrors and a second passenger airbag. The top-spec Sonata GLS comes with auto a/c, subwoofer, front parking sensors, smart key with starter button, chrome door handles, blind-spot monitor, navigation, rear and side-rear sunblinds, electric parking brake, auto-dimming mirror, HID headlights with auto-levelling and washers, leather seats with front heating/ventilation, puddle lamps, solar glass, stability control and a total of 6 airbags. The Turbo Sport gets sports suspension, 18-inch alloy wheels and dual twin-tip exhaust mufflers. The front-grille is slightly different and it also gets LED daytime running lights. The interior gets a new 3-spoke steering wheel, gear knob, instrument cluster and interior trim, along with Turbo stitching.

The Accord may not be best in class for every little thing, but its all-rounder package makes it popular among consumers. The Accord was enlarged and redesigned for the 2008 model year, and now offered in an American-built coupe form as well. The coupe debuted in the middle of 2008. It's offered with either a 2.4-litre four-cylinder or a 3.5-litre V6. The 2.4-litre in the coupe has a bit more power than the one in the sedan. All trims get a five-speed automatic only. Standard features on all models include power door mirrors with LED indicators, power windows, cruise control, CD/MP3 player with steering wheel controls, dual front airbags, ABS brakes, head restraint system and keyless entry. Optional features available in higher models include 17-inch alloys, auto-dimming rear-view mirror, sunroof, CD changer, leather, power driver's seat, fake wood trim and fog lamps.

The Lexus GS is a showcase of the Japanese company's advanced technology. It was released in 2006, it's not only loaded with more gadgetry than ever, but offers a degree of luxury that matches the best from Germany. Lexus openly admits that the BMW 5-Series was their benchmark for the new rear-wheel-drive GS. The appeal of the GS line-up lies with a fully-equipped base model. The GS 300 has most of the available features from the GS 430, except of course for the larger engine. The GS 300 gets a 3.0-litre V6 while the GS 430 gets a 4.3-litre V8, both paired with six-speed automatic with a sequential manual shift mode. Both engines lack the direct injection feature of American-spec versions apparently due to damaging high-sulphur petrol in some GCC countries, so power ratings are lower. The list of standard equipment includes leather-trimmed seats with front power adjustment, keyless entry, pushbutton starter, a premium sound system with both CD and DVD capability, Bluetooth wireless telephone technology, multiple airbags, various stability systems and a 7-inch multi-information touch screen. Options include DVD navigation, rear backup camera, moonroof, power rear sunshade, Mark Levinson audio system and adaptive front lighting.

The 207 is the redesigned replacement for the popular 206 models, available in three body styles, various trim levels and four engine choices. Derivatives include the 207 CC Cabriolet and a fast 3-door RC hatchback, alongside the regular 3-door and 5-door hatchback range. The basic 3-door and 5-door hatchbacks can be had with a 1.4-litre and a manual gearbox, or a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine with either a manual or an automatic. The 207 CC comes standard with this 1.6-litre and an automatic. A mid-range turbocharged 1.6-litre engine can also be had in the GT hatchback, but only with a manual gearbox. And there is yet another more powerful 1.6-litre turbocharged engine with a manual reserved for the sporty RC hatchback. Basic models come with front power windows, cloth interior, dual front airbags, keyless entry, ABS brakes and even a CD player as standard. Equipment in the higher models include stability and traction control, panoramic sunroof, 16-inch or 17-inch alloys, side airbags, electric mirrors, automatic a/c, rear parking sensors and more.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz A-Class Sedan came out in 2019. The A-Class now comes in two variants, the A 200 and A 250. Under the hood, is the same turbocharged 2.0-litre engine carried over from the previous generation, mated to an a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission, but gains more power. The 5-seater is offered in one loaded "Sport" spec that includes 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Honda CR-V is a roomy little soft-roader that is convenient and easy to drive on the streets, but no hero on the rough stuff. There are lots of features, and the cabin is fairly spacious. It rides as smoothly as a car, especially since it is based on the Civic. It offers the cargo versatility of a sport-utility vehicle, an upright seating position, and all-wheel drive. The styling was radically revised for 2007, with marketing folks referring to it as the "Aerosport" SUV. The CR-V comes with a 2.4-litre four-cylinder engine lifted from the Accord, with a five-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include air conditioning with micron filtration, AM/FM/CD stereo with MP3 capability and optional 6-CD changer, an adjustable steering column, power mirrors, power windows, and power outlets, along with front airbags, integrated keyless entry and alloy wheels. Side airbags are optionally available, as are a moonroof, leather seats, adaptive headlights and other features.

The Peugeot Expert offers up to 1400 kg of payload, 5.1 metre cube volume and 3.32 m of useful length, as do the Standard and Long versions. The new Peugeot Expert gets a 2.0-litre turbocharged diesel engine coupled with a choice of a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features on the Expert include cloth seats, halogen headlamps, power steering, manual A/C, 12 volt socket in cabin and cargo area, central locking, cruise control, radio with Bluetooth and USB, and 16-inch steel wheels with centre cover. Safety features include front dual airbags, stability control and ABS.

The Lexus NX 300, the Japanese brand's first entry in the compact crossover field, received a facelift for 2018. It comes with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder mated to an 8-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive. All models come with 18-inch alloys, LED headlights, synthetic or real leather, power front seats, premium multimedia system with navigation, cruise control, smart keyless entry and start, power tilt/telescoping steering wheel with buttons, Bluetooth, USB and more. The higher-spec models gain adaptive cruise, Mark Levinson stereo, wood trim, illuminated scuff plates, ventilated seats, remote starter, power-folding rear seats, wireless phone charger, power tailgate, panoramic parking cameras, heads-up display, adaptive suspension and more. The F-Sport models additionally get a mesh grille for the different front bumper, firmer suspension tuning and different wheel designs, optionally with wider tyres. Standard safety features include front, side, curtain and knee airbags as well as stability control and ABS with brake assist, with options including a pre-crash safety system, lane-change assist with blind-spot monitoring and cross-traffic alert, and lane-keeping assist with lane-departure alert and steering assist.

The Changan CS35 is the Chinese brand's sub-compact SUV offering, currently being sold only in a few GCC countries. Under the hood of the CS35 is a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to either a 5-speed manual transmission or a 4-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, central locking, manual A/C, radio with AUX/USB/CD support, 6 speakers, halogen headlamps, parking sensors, fog lamps and 16-inch alloy wheels. The higher models get sunroof, leather wrapped steering wheel and 17-inch alloy wheels. Safety features on the car include ABS, electronic brake distribution and brake assist, and front driver & passenger airbags, while higher models get side curtain airbags.

Lexus has an all-new flagship luxury sedan that is as good as the best in the business. This fourth-generation LS, dubbed the LS 460, is powered by a new 4.6-litre V8 engine without direct injection, but mated to the new 8-speed automatic. Available features include navigation, Bluetooth, ventilated seats, sunroof, cruise control and an updated Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Management system. The cabin has all the customary Lexus luxury touches, including seats covered in one of four leathers to coordinate with three woodgrain trims. A power reclining seat equipped with power leg rests and massage is available for the right rear, along with a folding table. The LS 460 also offers a nine-inch rear monitor mounted in the headliner along with a new 19-speaker Mark Levinson audio system with an onboard hard drive that holds 4000 songs. It is available in regular-length and stretched-wheelbase versions.

The Haval H9 is the Chinese brand's flagship SUV. Under the hood, it gets the 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed ZF automatic transmission. Standard features on the H9 include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push engine start-stop button, xenon headlamps, front and rear fog lamps, leather seats, infotainment system with touch screen and 10 speakers, Bluetooth, radio, AUX-in, USB, CD player and GPS. Safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD), brake assist (BA) and traction control.

The Chinese Tiggo 5 made its way to the GCC in 2015. Powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, and comes with a 4-speed automatic transmission. The five-door five-seater Tiggo gets a versatile interior, with fold-flat seats and a spacious cargo area. Features, standard or optional, include front dual airbags, rear three-point seat belts, ABS brakes with electronic brakeforce distribution, disc brakes, keyless entry, alloy wheels and a rear windshield wiper. Chery also brags that sports car maker Lotus Engineering had a hand in developing this mishmash, so we expect decent handling.

The bulbous new-for-2010 Prado is available with two petrol and two diesel engines. The GCC-spec Prado 5-door will be available in VXL, VX and TX trim levels, with the choice of a 4.0-litre V6 with a 5-speed manually-shiftable automatic or a 6-speed manual, or an underpowered 2.7-litre 4-cylinder with a 4-speed automatic or a 5-speed manual. The two diesel choices include a 3.0-litre 4-cylinder and a turbocharged 3.0-litre 4-cylinder. All models get 17-inch aluminium wheels, except for the VXL, which gets 18-inch ones. All models also have four-wheel ventilated disc brakes, independent front and live-axle rear suspension, and on higher-spec models, a "KDSS stabiliser" system to reduce body roll. The interior is available with three grades of upholstery. Basic models get fabric and mid-range versions get a better fabric, while the VXL gets leather along with wood trim and thicker-bolstered front seats. The top VXL version also gets features such as three-zone automatic a/c, 17-speaker JBL stereo with AUX input, keyless entry and starter button, front and rear parking sensors with display, electrically-operated last-row seating, Bluetooth and rear-seat DVD entertainment. Also available are front, side-curtain and knee airbags, as well as stability control and turning HID headlights. The 7-seater 5-door Prado finally gets a fold-flat third-row seat, while a 9-seater configuration is optional. The top tech feature is the optional multi-terrain system in the VX-L, with settings for mud and sand, rock, and loose surfaces, mated with air suspension, locking centre and rear diffs, four cameras and adjustable air suspension. Lower models have to cope with "active" traction control and rear diff lock, all with low-range gearing. The VX-L can also be optioned with a Pre-Crash system to hit the brakes when an imminent crash is detected, but it cannot be had with the multi-terrain option.

Acura made its entry into the Middle East market in 2015. It got a facelift for 2018, along with a new dual-screen user interface, complemented with a 7-inch touchscreen. Currently it is only being sold in Kuwait. The Acura TLX is their midsize luxury sedan offering. Under the hood, two engines are on offer - a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder motor and a 3.5-litre V6 unit. The 4-cylinder engine is mated to a 8-speed automatic, while the V6 gets a 9-speed automatic transmission. Standard features in the TLX include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, smart keyless entry, sunroof, auto-headlight system, LED daytime running lights, engine start-stop button, cruise control, power seats with lumbar support, dual-zone automatic A/C, entertainment system with AM/FM radio/CD/AUX/HDMI support, navigation, speakers & sub-woofer, hands-free telephone with voice recognition, heated & ventilated front seats, front & rear parking sensors, and rearview camera. The higher model gets push-button shifter, adaptive cruise control, and front & rear smart keyless entry. Standard safety features on the TLX include front, side curtain & knee airbags, all-wheel steering, ABS, agile handle assist (AGH), blind spot indicator, vehicle stability assist (VSA) and hill-start assist. The higher model gets lane-keeping assist system, crash mitigation brake system, forward collision warning system, road departure mitigation system and low speed following system.

The all-new Celerio is Suzuki's latest mini-car offering, launching in the middle of 2009 to be sold alongside the existing Alto. In reality, the Celerio is sold as an Alto replacement in other countries, and is built by Suzuki-Maruti in India. The Celerio offers all the styling of a modern hatchback, although its features are on the low side to keep prices down. Fitted with a standard 1.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, the tiny motor can be mated to either a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic. Touted as a "full options" hatchback, the Celerio comes with a CD stereo with MP3, dual front airbags, ABS, fog lamps, alloy wheels, keyless entry and power steering. The cabin features a hard plastic dashboard housing a minimalistic gauge cluster and various storage areas. The rear-side windows cannot be rolled down, but can slightly pop out at the edge for ventilation. While it didn't do too well in European crash tests, its lightness puts it among the most fuel-efficient cars in the GCC.

Available only in a few GCC markets, this outdated version of the Land Cruiser got a big facelift for 2008, but the mechanicals underneath remain the same. Staying alive simply because people keep buying them. The popular pickup version became known as the LC79 from 2010, by virtue of a new petrol engine. It is built to Toyota's high standard of quality so you get unsurpassed durability and reliability. Powered by either a 4.0-litre V6 petrol, or in some markets, an old 4.2-litre inline-6 diesel, mated to only 5-speed manuals, these trucks are very rudimentary, unlike the American "luxury" trucks. Standard features include a radio with cassette player and 2 speakers, manual a/c, power steering and fabric seats. Options on higher models include power door mirrors, electric winch, 16-inch steel wheels, power windows and central locking.  If you are lucky, you might get an optional CD player, but not much else. Standard safety features include nothing more than a fire extinguisher, although some markets now get optional dual front airbags. Conversely, the Saudi market gets several variations, with available features such as a 10-seater covered bed, keyless entry, cooled glove-box, heavy-duty suspension and sand tyres. Incidentally, the pickup is regionally popular for modifying into drag racers due to their durability, although the loss of the old 4.5-litre petrol engine may put a dent in that.

The Grand Vitara got a facelift for 2013. Only the 2.4-litre 4-cylinder engine is now offered, which is mated to an ancient 4-speed automatic. The Grand Vitara is among the handful of small 4WD vehicles that offers true all-round 4x4 capability thanks to its low-range gearing and truck-like construction. Suzuki offers the trucklet in 3-door and 5-door body styles. all models get four-wheel disc brakes. All Grand Vitara models come well-equipped with useful features. Some of the available features include new cabin trimmings, drive-by-wire throttle control, power windows, electric mirrors, power-adjustable front seating, CD stereo, and a keyless entry system that does not require the key to leave the pocket to unlock the doors and start the engine. Though standard equipment differs from country to country, the Grand Vitara will be offered in most markets with stability control, steel or alloy wheels, glass sunroof, in-dash 6-disc changer with MP3 compatibility, and leather seats. Safety features are also class-leading, with a full array of airbags with front, side and curtain bags for front seat passengers, plus curtain airbags for those in the back.

The all-new Chevrolet Corvette debuted as a 2020 model year. The eighth generation model, or "C8" gets an upgraded version of the 6.2-litre V8 engine, which is now located behind the passenger seat instead of in front. Power is delivered via an 8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. There will be no more manual gearbox option. The base Corvette 1LT gets a removable roof panel, Bose premium 10-speaker system, Chevrolet Infotainment 3 System, standard 8-way power GT1 seats and tilt/telescope steering wheel, rear park Assist and HD rear view camera. The Corvette 2LT adds a number of comfort and convenience features in addition to color-matched interior options. It includes front curb view cameras, Bose Performance Series 14-Speaker audio system, heated/vented seats and heated steering wheel and optional GT2 seats in Nappa leather. The Corvette 3LT gets a leather-wrapped interior. Also included is 13 interior color options, custom leather-wrapped instrument panel and door, suede microfiber upper interior trim and standard GT2 seats in Nappa leather. The Z51 Package includes summer-only performance tires, bigger brakes, eLSD, front splitter and performance exhaust.

An all-new Audi A5 came out in 2017. The Audi A5 coupe is powered by a 2.0-litre turbo 4-cylinder, available in 2 different tunes. Power is delivered through a 7-speed tiptronic auto transmission. Technology includes LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. buyers can specify the optional virtual cockpit function, which includes a 12.3-inch high-definition digital instrument panel as well as the latest evolution of Audi's MMI (Multi Media Interface) Plus infotainment system, which uses an 8.3-inch monitor and a touch-sensitive rotary controller. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Porsche 911 is all-new after spending more than a decade in its current form, with continuous updates of course. For 2012, the design incorporates a completely new platform, so now the 911 is longer and lower than before. It is still a 2+2 seater coupe. The base 911 Carrera is offered with a 3.4-litre direct-injection flat-6 engine, mated to either a world-first 7-speed manual or a 7-speed "PDK" dual-clutch automatic and rear-wheel-drive. The 911 Carrera 4, which was introduced in 2013, adds all-wheel-drive. The rear-wheel-drive 911 Carrera S upgrades the motor to a 3.8-litre, while the, new for 2013, 911 Carrera 4S adds all-wheel-drive. The Porsche 911 Targa and Targa 4S was revealed as a 2014 model year, getting the same engine specs as the Carrera 4 and 4S. The 911 Turbo and Turbo S was released in 2014. It gets a 3.8-litre turbocharged engine, and comes only with the PDK transmission. The Porsche 911 GT3 was revealed in mid 2014. It gets a 3.8-litre motor and for the first time, will not have a manual gearbox option. It will be available only with the PDK. The 911 GTS was revealed in the GCC in late 2014 and is available as rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. It is powered by a 3.8-litre motor, coupled with either a 7-speed manual or PDK transmission. As usual, everything is optional beyond the basic power accessories, touchscreen multimedia system, Bluetooth, basic keyless entry, HID headlights, electric parking brake and 19-inch wheels. Available options include different colours and materials for every interior surface, different 20-inch wheel designs, metallic paint choices, power-adjustable or sports seats, Bose or Burmester audio systems with optional voice control and TV tuner, CD changer, parking sensors, smart keyless entry and start, adaptive headlights, sunroof, electric folding mirrors, rear wiper, body kit and more. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, stability control and ABS.

The Hyundai i10 received a facelift for the 2011 model year. It also gets a new 1.2-litre 4-cylinder engine with VTVT (Variable Timing and Valve Train) technology, mated to a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic transmission. The no-frills base model comes with 14-inch steel wheels, air-conditioning, body-coloured bumpers, central locking, chrome radiator grille, electric power steering, front electric windows, and a stereo with six speakers. More available features include a CD player with MP3 compatibility and iPod input, dual front airbags, body-coloured door handles, body-coloured mirrors, driver's seat height adjustment, electric door mirrors, all-electric windows, front fog lights, remote locking, seatbelt reminder, 15-inch alloy wheels and anunderfloor rear luggage compartment. This is about as cheap as it gets for a decent new car in the GCC market. Although it is possible to go even cheaper, the i10 represents a good balance of modernity without the appearance of being a product for basic motoring.

The Audi RS 5 is being sold, but mostly only on special order. An all-new model came out in 2018. It gets a twin turbocharged 2.9-litre V6 engine with a 8-speed automatic. Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control. The exterior gets more aggressive bumpers to differentiate from the standard A5.

The 2015 Dodge Charger SRT received a significant facelift. From 2019, only the supercharged 6.2-litre V8 powered SRT Hellcat was available. For 2021, it got a host of upgrades to the interior, exterior and mechanical bits. Also a Charger SRT Hellcat Redeye was added to the lineup. Both get an 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard SRT features include leather upholstery, UConnect multimedia system with touchscreen, 20-inch wheels, rear spoiler and more, along with a unique exterior kit. The Charger SRT Hellcat receives a large, power-bulge aluminium hood, which features a dedicated air intake. Standard safety features on all models include front, side and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor and optional adaptive cruise control with auto braking.A new widebody kit version was added to the lineup in 2020.

The BMW i8 is a plug-in hybrid coupe powered by a high-performance electric motor in the front, which drives the front axle, and a mid-mounted turbocharged 3-cylinder 1.5-litre petrol engine powering the rear wheels. The petrol engine is mated to a 6-speed automatic, while the electric motor is attached to a 2-stage automatic transmission. On electricity alone, the i8 can travel about 30 Km, before the petrol engine has to intervene and recharge the batteries. Another interesting feature is the car's ability to switch between front-wheel-drive, rear-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. But that very well depends on driver mood and more importantly, the existing electric juice. The i8 features a perfect 50:50 weight distribution, which BMW claims to have achieved using lightweight materials like carbon-fibre and aluminium. Safety standards are high in the i8 as the DSC (Dynamic Stability Control) system includes the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), Cornering Brake Control (CBC), Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Brake Assist, Brake Standby, Brake Drying function, Start-Off Assistant, Fading Compensation, Active Differential Brake (ADB-x), Driving dynamic impellent torque pre-control, E-Traction, as well as the push button-activated Dynamic Traction Control (DTC) mode. Front airbags and side airbags integrated into the seat backrests, plus head/curtain airbags for both rows of seats, are all fitted as standard, as are three-point inertia-reel seatbelts including belt tensioners and belt force limiters for all seats.

The Kia Carens compact MPV is all-new for the 2007 model year, and is available with a seven-seat cabin. The new Carens is completely different from the old one, sharing only the name of the previous model. Longer, wider and taller than its goofy predecessor, the latest Carens offers more interior space than most 4WDs thanks to better packaging. Inside the cabin, the middle and rear row seats fold down to create a flat-floored luggage area. With five seats occupied, luggage space is more than 400 litres and with just the driver and front passenger on board, up to 2,106 litres of cargo can be carried. It is offered with a relatively weak 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine mated with either a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic transmission that offers sequential manual selection. The model has a hydraulic power-assisted rack and pinion steering system with relatively high gearing, requiring just 2.86 turns of the wheel from lock-to-lock with the standard 16-inch wheels. Features include front and rear disc brakes backed up by ABS with EBD, CD stereo, four forward-opening doors, and an undetermined number of airbags.

The Epica is Chevrolet's attempt at the lower end of the midsize car market, considering the Lumina is handling the slightly higher market that is occupied by the Accord and the Camry. Launched as part of a trio with the Aveo and the Optra for 2004, it is built by GM Daewoo in Korea on a front-wheel-drive platform. The car received a restyle for 2007 and maintains the traditional sedan three-box profile instead of being over-tall like the Camry, so it looks good from far away, though its details are derivative. The interior is fairly spacious considering its price. The cabin is well-designed with plenty of convenient storage spaces, while instruments and controls are well-placed. Two engines are on offer, namely a small 2.0-litre six-cylinder that works well but is fairly underpowered, and a 2.5-litre six-cylinder that has more power but only matches four-cylinder motors from Japanese midsizers. The optional four-speed automatic transmission is smooth, while a manual gearbox is also offered for that last bit of fuel efficiency. Front airbags and ABS brakes are available. The Epica competes well in a segment that only sees action from the Koreans.

The BMW X3 compact crossover grows in size for the 2011 redesign. The five-seater 5-door is now larger in size and gains a couple of new corporate engine. One is the naturally-aspirated 3.0-litre inline 6-cylinder for the xDrive28i, and the other is the turbocharged 3.0-litre inline 6-cylinder for the xDrive35i, both with 8-speed automatic gearboxes and all-wheel-drive. The new interior integrates either a 6.5-inch or an 8.8-inch screen, and new features, standard or optional depending on trim, include a heads-up display with night vision, active and passive systems such as the lane change and lane departure warnings, optional parking assistant, adaptive cruise control, surround-view cameras, Variable Damper Control to pick between Normal, Sport and Sport+, Bluetooth phone with audio connectivity, navigation, multiple front and side airbags, leather or cloth upholstery, HID headlights, keyless start, sunroof, BlackBerry smartphone connectivity to gain access to e-mails and other distractions which can be shown on the control display and read out via the optional voice output. An M package is available that adds a body kit and more.

The XLR roadster is the flagship sports car of the Cadillac range. The latest variant was the new-for-2006 supercharged XLR-V. The most expensive offering in the Cadillac lineup is based on the Chevrolet Corvette C6 platform, only shorter, narrower, and taller in height. Standard XLR models use a 4.6-litre Northstar V8 engine with a 5-speed automatic in older models, and a 6-speed in newer models since 2007. The XLR-V uses a 4.4-litre Northstar engine with a positive displacement intercooled supercharger, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Chassis modifications include larger brakes, recalibrated Magnetic Ride Control, larger front stabilizer bar and an additional rear one, stiffer rear lower control arm bushings, larger wheels and tyres, a power steering fluid cooler, and a higher-capacity fuel pump. The lightweight roof, made of composite panels, retracts in less than thirty seconds at the push of a button. Features include adaptive Xenon headlights with washers, LED taillights, rear parking assist, rain-sensing wipers, automatic dual-zone climate control, adaptive cruise control, head-up display (HUD), tyre pressure monitoring system, DVD-based navigation system,  Bose six-CD stereo, Magnasteer speed-sensitive variable-assist steering, Magnetic Ride Control, and a keyless access system. The XLR received a minor facelift inside and out for 2009, just before being killed off during the General Motors bankruptcy.

The BMW i8 is a plug-in hybrid coupe powered by a high-performance electric motor in the front, which drives the front axle, and a mid-mounted turbocharged 3-cylinder 1.5-litre petrol engine powering the rear wheels. The petrol engine is mated to a 6-speed automatic, while the electric motor is attached to a 2-stage automatic transmission. On electricity alone, the i8 can travel about 30 Km, before the petrol engine has to intervene and recharge the batteries. Another interesting feature is the car's ability to switch between front-wheel-drive, rear-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. But that very well depends on driver mood and more importantly, the existing electric juice. The i8 features a perfect 50:50 weight distribution, which BMW claims to have achieved using lightweight materials like carbon-fibre and aluminium. Safety standards are high in the i8 as the DSC (Dynamic Stability Control) system includes the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), Cornering Brake Control (CBC), Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Brake Assist, Brake Standby, Brake Drying function, Start-Off Assistant, Fading Compensation, Active Differential Brake (ADB-x), Driving dynamic impellent torque pre-control, E-Traction, as well as the push button-activated Dynamic Traction Control (DTC) mode. Front airbags and side airbags integrated into the seat backrests, plus head/curtain airbags for both rows of seats, are all fitted as standard, as are three-point inertia-reel seatbelts including belt tensioners and belt force limiters for all seats.

The Porsche 911 Turbo and Turbo S got a minor facelift in 2017, as well as a slight power upgrade, thanks to modified inlet ports in the cylinder head, new injection nozzles and higher fuel pressure. Fuel economy improves slightly as well due to further advanced electronic engine and transmission management with revised gear change mappings. The engine is a 3.8-litre turbocharged flat-6 engine, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission. Standard features on the 911 Turbo include power steering, power mirrors, keyless entry, electric sports seats, leather seats, Alcantara roof lining, multifunction steering wheel, 2-zone automatic A/C, cruise control, front and rear parking sensors with rearview camera, Porsche Communication Management (PCM) infotainment system with radio and Bluetooth, Connect Plus with Apple CarPlay, Bose sound system with 12 speakers and subwoofer, and 20-inch alloy wheels. In the Turbo S, sports bucket seats and Porsche Ceramic Composite Brake (PCCB) are standard. Optional features list is long where customers can opt for different interior packages, higher end music system, special exterior paint, different alloy rim designs, etc. Standard safety features include airbags for driver and front passenger, Porsche Side Impact Protection (POSIP), comprising side impact protection elements in the doors, thorax airbag integrated into the side bolsters of the front seats and head airbag for driver and front passenger in each door panel, traction control, stability control and lane keeping assist.

The Citroen C-Elysee is the French manufacturer's answer for the budget sub-compact segment. It's offered with a 4-cylinder 1.6-litre petrol engine, mated to a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic gearbox. The Spanish-built saloon offers several convenience and safety features, depending on trim level, including a CD/MP3 stereo, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cloth upholstery, manual or electric mirrors, power windows, manual or single-zone automatic a/c, rear parking sensors, one or two airbags, ABS with emergency brake-assist system, fog lamps and either 15-inch steel or 16-inch alloy wheels.

Launched in 2005 and facelifted for 2008, the compact S40 sedan is based on the same front-wheel-drive platform as the Mazda 3 and the Ford Focus, all of which come under the Ford umbrella. Yet Volvo claims that the S40 is a true Volvo, asserting unique premium features only found in the Volvo. The S40 is an obviously small car, but it looks a lot like its larger siblings with its signature new-age-Volvo styling. There are three engine choices, all of them the corporate oddball five-cylinder, except for the base 1.6-litre four-cylinder with manual gearbox. The range includes a basic 2.4-litre, a higher-tuned 2.4-litre and a turbocharged 2.5-litre, all offered with automatic with tiptronic in this region. Markets outside this region get all-wheel-dive models too. The interior has an ultra-slim centre console that seems to be free-floating, with extra storage space behind it. The safety package includes a patented zonal front structure using differing strengths of high-strength steel to disperse force away from passengers in a crash. Dual front airbags, SIPS side impact protection, curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection are all standard.

The Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV came to the GCC in 2020. It gets a 2.4-litre engine connected to two electric motors. Power is transmitted to the wheels via a 1-speed direct drive transmission. It comes only in all-wheel-drive format. Standard features include power steering, power mirrors, fabric seats, dual-zone A/C, audio entertainment system with CD/MP3/USB support, 6 speakers, central locking and 16-inch steel wheels. Optional features include leather seats, sunroof, centre console multi-information display screen with rear-view camera, full automatic A/C, 18-inch alloy rims and HID headlamps. Safety features include ABS brakes, electronic brake distribution (EBD), front driver and passenger side airbags.

The Kia Rio is all-new for the 2012 model year. Attractively designed, it is available in 4-door sedan and 5-door hatchback form. The only engine for the GCC is a 1.4-litre 4-cylinder with variable-valve timing, mated to a 4-speed automatic. While mechanically basic, the Rio can be had with a host of features unseen in the sub-compact segment. Standard features include 14-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, manual a/c, CD/MP3 stereo, adjustable steering wheel, central locking, power windows, electric mirrors and only one airbag. The mid-range model gets 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, centre-console armrest, fog lamps, keyless entry, USB port, Bluetooth, steering-wheel audio controls, sun-visor lights, folding mirrors with indicators and a split-folding rear seat. The top model gets rear parking sensors, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, padded leatherette door trim, LED front running lights and tail lamps, 17-inch alloy wheels, more speakers for the stereo, cruise control, cooled glovebox, auto headlights, sunroof, and finally, ABS and a passenger-side airbag in addition to the driver's one. The Rio is offered in Europe and the States with full front-side-curtain airbags and stability control, and has a 5-star crash-test rating in Europe, but that model is not sold in the GCC.

The BMW X1 is the smallest crossover SUV in the German brand. An all-new model came out in 2016. Based on the 1-Series platform, complete with four-wheel-independent suspension and disc brakes, the X1 is available in rear-wheel-drive form with the sDrive20i base model, sporting a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine. The other model in the range is the all-wheel-drive xDrive25i, also fitted with same engine but producing more power. The interior features an optional integrated iDrive that includes either the 6.5-inch Business or the 8.8-inch Professional navigation systems. Other available features, depending on trim level, includes various alloy wheels, Bluetooth phone, dual-zone a/c, sunroof, cloth or leather upholstery, HID headlights, run-flat tyres, rear parking sensors, keyless entry, cruise control, immobiliser and the usual power accessories. Standard safety features include front and side-curtain airbags, stability control, and ABS with electronic brakeforce distribution as well as cornering brake control.

Introduced in this iteration for 2009, the Mazda 6, also known as the grammatically-wrong Mazda6, has been facelifted for 2011, just like its platform-mate, the Ford Mondeo. The Mazda 6 was originally designed for the driving enthusiast, with choices of V6 and turbocharged engines, but the Middle East market only gets an upgraded new 2.0-litre "DISI" engine and a reasonable 2.5-litre engine, both of which are four-cylinder and come with a choice of 6-speed manual or 5-speed automatic. Remaining unique to the segment, the Mazda 6 is the midsize offered in sedan, liftback and wagon forms. Standard features include power windows, central locking, basic stereo system, dual airbags for driver and front passenger, and available ABS brakes with electronic brakeforce distribution. Options include a full body kit, rear spoiler, fog lamps, 6-CD changer, cruise control, alloy wheels, sunroof, stability control and leather seats. Poor marketing, average after-sales service and limited engine choices continue to doom this competent car in many GCC markets.

Almost 5 metres long with a low roofline, the Audi A7 Sportback is a full-sizer riding on 18-inch to 20-inch wheels, and as with all Audi sedans,  really rides a front-wheel-drive platform, with optional 'Quattro' all-wheel-drive tacked onto the higher trim levels. Two V6 engines are offered in the UAE - a 2.8-litre and a supercharged 3.0-litre, both of which are mated to an 'S-tronic' automatic transmission. An S7 was introduced as a 2013 model with a 4.0-litre turbocharged V8 engine. Standard options include 4-zone automatic air-conditioning, reverse-camera, MMI touch-sensitive navigation system, 10-speaker audio system. Optional equipment include interior leather packages for the seats and door trim, sports suspension, air suspension, front and reverse camera, park assist, side assist, night-vision, lane-assist and BOSE surround sound.

The Jaguar F-Type SVR convertible is the top performance model trim. Under the hood, it gets the supercharged 5.0-litre V8 engine, mated to a 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard options include engine start/stop function, bi-xenon headlamps, power windows, LED daytime running lights, 10-speaker entertainment system, USB port, Bluetooth phone and streaming, several airbags, power tailgate, retractable rear wing spoiler, sports seats, dual-zone a/c, power-adjustable seats and steering, cruise control and more. Performance upgrades include a high-performance braking system, an electronic rear-differential, and a sport-tuned suspension with adaptive dampers.

The Ferrari 488 replaced the 458 in late 2015. The 488 Spider is the hard-top convertible version of the 488 GTB coupe. Under the hood, the 488 gets a twin-turbocharged 3.9-litre V8, and power is delivered via an updated 7-speed dual clutch automatic transmission. The exterior is still pretty similar to the 458, but gets a few visual updates, most of which have been added to improve aerodynamics and performance. The interior is quite similiar to the 458 with minor tweaks such as angled air vents and improved graphics on the infotainment and instrument panel, as well as keyless start. The LCD displays in the gauge cluster serve as screens for everything from telematics to navigation. Other available features include front/rear parking sensors, cruise control, power windows and mirrors, ceramic brake discs, and selectable drive modes using the dial on the steering wheel, which loosens up the ESP to various degrees. Optional features include front and rear cameras, and an automated front-lift system to avoid scrapes.

The A3 hatchback slips into Audi's line-up as the company's smallest and cheapest model. It was introduced in 2004, received a minor facelift in 2005, and has undergone a second facelift to keep it fresh. Sharing its platform with the MKV-generation VW Golf, the main A3 models now available here are a 1.8-litre and a 2.0-litre, both turbocharged 4-cylinder engines mated to front-wheel-drive platforms and dual-clutch automanual gearboxes. Most dealers do not offer Quattro, manual or V6 models, as found in Europe, although Audi's clueless GCC-office people might argue otherwise. Since the three-door flopped here, the only bodystyle offered now is the five-door Sportback. Standard features include four-wheel disc brakes, 16-inch alloy wheels, automatic climate control, power windows, power locks with keyless remote, cloth seats and a CD player. The list of options vary, depending on who you ask. AS for the facelift, changes include new headlights, re-sculpted front bumper and possibly new tail-light lenses. The compact A3 tries to justify its high price with a well-built exterior and a pleasant interior, as well as a badge that no one respects yet.

An all-new model of the Audi A7 came out in 2019. Almost 5 metres long with a low roofline, the Audi A7 Sportback is a full-sizer and as with all Audi sedans,  really rides a front-wheel-drive platform, with optional 'Quattro' all-wheel-drive tacked onto the higher trim levels. Currently only the 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 is the only engine option available in the GCC. Standard options include 4-zone automatic air-conditioning, reverse-camera, MMI touch-sensitive navigation system, 10-speaker audio system. Optional equipment include interior leather packages for the seats and door trim, sports suspension, air suspension, front and reverse camera, park assist, side assist, night-vision, lane-assist and BOSE surround sound.

The BMW i8 is a plug-in hybrid coupe powered by a high-performance electric motor in the front, which drives the front axle, and a mid-mounted turbocharged 3-cylinder 1.5-litre petrol engine powering the rear wheels. In 2019, it got a slight facelift and a bigger battery, giving it a small bump up in horsepower. The petrol engine is mated to a 6-speed automatic, while the electric motor is attached to a 2-stage automatic transmission. On electricity alone, the i8 can travel about 30 Km, before the petrol engine has to intervene and recharge the batteries. Another interesting feature is the car's ability to switch between front-wheel-drive, rear-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. But that very well depends on driver mood and more importantly, the existing electric juice. The i8 features a perfect 50:50 weight distribution, which BMW claims to have achieved using lightweight materials like carbon-fibre and aluminium. Safety standards are high in the i8 as the DSC (Dynamic Stability Control) system includes the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), Cornering Brake Control (CBC), Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Brake Assist, Brake Standby, Brake Drying function, Start-Off Assistant, Fading Compensation, Active Differential Brake (ADB-x), Driving dynamic impellent torque pre-control, E-Traction, as well as the push button-activated Dynamic Traction Control (DTC) mode. Front airbags and side airbags integrated into the seat backrests, plus head/curtain airbags for both rows of seats, are all fitted as standard, as are three-point inertia-reel seatbelts including belt tensioners and belt force limiters for all seats.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class came out in 2019. The exterior and interior have been completely changed to incorporate their new design language, first seen on the Mercedes-Benz A-Class. New engines now power the CLS-Class which includes a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbo for the CLS 350, the 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 motor for the CLS-450 and the 3.0-litre turbo inline-6 engine coupled with an electric motor for the CLS-53 AMG. All of them get the 9-speed automatic transmission. The CLS 450 and CLS 53 AMG are available only in all-wheel-drive. Standard features are aplenty which include leather seats, keyless entry, central locking, engine stop-start button, digital instrument cluster, infotainment system with Bluetooth/USB support, cruise control, LED headlights and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment includes air suspension and a widescreen cockpit consisting of two 12.3-inch displays on the dashboard. An AMG line is also available and includes AMG body styling, a diamond pattern radiator grille, 19-inch alloy wheels, and a flat-bottomed sports steering wheel.

GM revived an old badge for the all-new Thailand-built 2013 Chevrolet Trailblazer, completely unrelated to the old American-built one. The Trailblazer comes in LT and LTZ trim levels. The Isuzu-based pickup chassis is modified to have an independent rear suspension, so it loses some off-road cred, but it does gain a 3.6-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic gearbox, with the base model being two-wheel-drive and the top model getting four-wheel-drive. Other available features include the usual split-folding second-row and cramped third-row seats, CD stereo with USB and Bluetooth, rear a/c vents, 18-inch wheels, stability control, ABS, hill-start assist, parking sensors and six airbags.

The McLaren 650S is based on the 12C but with 25% new parts. The 650S comes with a carbon-fibre tub chassis, bespoke 3.8-litre twin-turbo V8, a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox, an adaptive hydraulic suspension system, an air-brake spoiler, various driving modes and even an F1-developed brake-steer system. Using absolutely no parts from other manufacturers, the McLaren can be fully customised. Standard safety features include front, side-curtain and knee airbags, ABS and defeatable stability control. Interestingly, McLaren offers future power and feature upgrades for free to all owners. Also, the body is customisable to any unique shapes, up to a point, because they are just moulded "SMC" composite panels attached to the chassis.

The D-Max, also known by other names, is a range of light pickup trucks that are also rebadged as Chevrolet models in many markets. This "compact" pickup has grown substantially for 2013, larger in every dimension, with more cabin and cargo room. In 2016 it received a facelift. The D-Max can only be had in 4-door crew cab form in the GCC, with a range of 4-cylinder diesel engines, namely a 2.5-litre turbodiesel, a 2.5-litre intercooled turbodiesel, and a 3.0-litre intercooled turbodiesel. The folks who will drive these at work have to manage with a 5-speed manual gearbox, or if they are lucky, the optional new 5-speed automatic. It is available in economical rear-wheel-drive and capable four-wheel-drive forms, depending on the engine. Features on the basic 2WD model comes with unpainted bumpers, 15-inch or 16-inch steel wheels, cloth or vinyl seats and manual windows. Features on higher trim levels include 15-inch or 16-inch alloys, painted bumper, chrome rear bumper, higher-grade cloth seats, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, CD/MP3 stereo, power windows and mirrors, central locking, fog lamps, LED rear lights, optional rear defogger, optional dual front airbags, optional ABS brakes and more. A D-Max GT model was launched in 2014, with the 3.0-litre engine, bumper-skirts, racing stripes, optional 17-inch grey alloys, red-black seats, bedliner and stereo choices.

The CLK underwent a minor facelift for 2007, along with receiving a new range of modern engines. Available in both luxury convertible and pillar-less coupe models, the CLK-Class is an attractive extension of the C-Class platform. It packs the usual comfort and safety features typical of Mercedes-Benz, either standard or optional. Standard features include front and side airbags, ABS with Brake Assist and Electronic Stability Programme, common power features, pneumatically operated retractable rear head restraints, alloy wheels, good stereo and a host of upholstery options. The model range includes the 1.8-litre supercharged CLK 200 Kompressor, the 3.0-litre CLK 280, the 3.5-litre CLK 350, the 5.5-litre CLK 500 and the 6.2-litre CLK 63 AMG rocketship. Only the lower models have a manual gearbox option in addition to the automatic, though they make have to be special order. A new optional AMG package adds a sporty body kit, suspension and wheels to any CLK model. Other options include keyless start, navigation, an even better stereo and parking sensors.

An all-new Audi A4 came out in 2016. It is a more spacious car, while at the same time is lighter than its predecessor. Under the hood, there are 2 available engines. There is the turbocharged 1.4-litre 4-cylinder mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and is available only as front-wheel-drive. Then there is the turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and comes with all-wheel drive. Standard features include LED running lights, three-zone automatic air conditioning, front seats with lumbar support and ventilation, MMI computer control system, intelligent key that stores the vehicle's service info, and a Bang & Olufsen audio system. Also available are side-assist warning system for safe lane changes, and a parking system with a rear-view camera. The A4 also gets a dynamic system that Audi called Drive Select that manipulates transmission shifts, steering feel and suspension settings. All models get the usual power accessories as well as safety features such as multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Mercedes-Benz Sprinter can be classified as one of the largest commercial vehicles on offer in the GCC market. It comes with a range of petrol and diesel engines, with three roof heights, various wheelbase lengths, and several body trims, including panel-van, pickup and crew-bus styles. Apparently, this German-built van holds three times as much cargo as its Japanese rivals, with standard safety features to boot, such as airbags, ESP and three-point seatbelts for all passengers, and with 40,000 km service intervals for the diesel models, it ends up offering reasonable overall value.

The Opel Insignia is the German manufacturer's midsize sedan offering. It got minor exterior and interior changes for the 2015 model year. Only sold in some GCC countries, the Insignia gets a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine with front-wheel-drive. Some features include dual-zone automatic AC, sunroof, electronic parking brake, cruise control, heated leather seats with memory, AM/FM radio with MP3/AUX/USB support, front and rear parking sensors, speed-sensitive power steering, daytime running lights, fog lamps and 18-inch aluminium wheels. Safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, lane-departure warning, ESP and ABS.

New from the ground up for 2006 and much more better-looking, the M-Class, which actually uses the ML moniker, is a better on-road and off-road 4WD now. The M-Class is built for better off-road performance, with permanent all-wheel-drive plus 4ETS, a hill-start aid to help when climbing, and Downhill Speed Regulation to ensure constant speed on downhill tracks. In addition, the optional AIRMATIC package and ADS adaptive damping system so you can increase the ground clearance up to 110 millimetres at the touch of a button. Various aesthetic options include the Off-road styling package, the Chrome package, the Sports package and the Interior equipment package. Models include the 3.7-litre ML 350 and the 5.5-litre ML 500 that still uses the old V8 for now. All come with a 7-speed automatic. Features include 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, man-made leather/Aspen fabric or leather upholstery, tyre pressure loss warning system, crash sensors, front and side airbags, CD radio with pre-installation for mobile phone and more.

The Chevrolet Traverse received a facelift for 2013. It is a crossover wagon that combines the functionality of a minivan with the look of an SUV, offering three rows of seating for up to eight passengers. The design consists of polished aluminium roof rails, projector beam headlights, LED taillights and a rear spoiler. It has a 3.6-litre V6 with variable valve timing, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission, with either front-wheel-drive or optional all-wheel-drive system with no low range. The interior features a "low and away" instrument panel and a Smart Slide second-row feature allows easier access to the third row. Features include power windows, CD/MP3 stereo with six speakers, electric mirrors, keyless entry and more. Optional features include 6.5 inches touch screen for navigation, entertainment and display vehicle information, rear-seat DVD entertainment, HID headlights, sunroof, parking sensors, leather seats, tri-zone climate control and more. Standard safety features includes StabiliTrak stability control system with rollover mitigation technology, six airbags and a tyre-pressure-monitoring system. Also standard is power-assisted rack-and-pinion steering, 18-inch wheels with optional 19-inchers, and four-wheel disc brakes with ABS.

An all-new Subaru Outback came out in 2015. The base Outback 2.5i comes with a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder boxer engine mated with a CVT automatic. The top model is the 3.6R, with a turbocharged 3.6-litre 6-cylinder boxer engine mated to a CVT automatic as well. Base models get power windows, electric mirrors, ABS, front and side-curtain airbags, cloth upholstery, 16-inch wheels and a CD stereo. The top-spec trim gets stability control, SI-Drive driving mode selection system, keyless entry with starter button, cruise control, dual-zone a/c, leather interior, 10-way power-adjustable driver's seat, aluminium pedals, 6-speaker stereo with 6-CD changer, 17-inch alloy wheels, HID headlights with pop-up washers, and a sunroof.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE Coupe is an all-new model, to compete against the BMW X6. Mercedes-AMG GLE Coupe 63 is the top performance model. In 2020, it got a facelift and power upgrades. Under the hood, it comes with the 5.5-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 9-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive. A small electric motor has been added to the engine to provide better acceleration and response, as well as improve fuel economy. Available features include adjustable air suspension, adaptive cruise control and active parking assist. The exterior features HID headlights, LED running maps and 21-inch cross-spoke AMG alloy wheels. The 5-seater interior offers leather upholstery, mood lighting, HDD navigation, panoramic sunroof, rear entertainment system, keyless start, ventilated power front seats and a split-folding rear seat. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control, ABS and drowsiness monitor, with options such as a rear view camera with parking sensors, active lane assist, blind-spot monitor and automatic pre-crash braking.

The B-Series is the forgotten small pickup truck range of the Mazda line-up. No one in their right mind is going to buy one of these for personal use, but for those who want to be different, in a flamboyant American sort of way, they can pick up one of these and modify them for purposes other than hauling cargo. Engines include a 2.2-litre and a 2.6-litre petrol engines, while the diesel offering is a 2.9-litre unit, all four-cylinder motors and all with a standard five-speed manual, or even an automatic in some markets. Body styles include a single cab and a double cab shape. Key features include an AM/FM radio with cassette deck and 2 speakers, monotone or two-tone paintjob, and manually operated windows. Available accessories include overfender and side-step cladding panels, and front and rear skirt kits. Cargo-box equipment includes a single-action tailgate lock, a rear step bumper, outer and inner rope hooks, and load rests. Options, available in some markets, include front airbags, ABS brakes with electronic brake-force distribution, and even power windows.

The Q45 is Infiniti's unloved flagship fullsize sedan, available in a single trim line. It uses a 4.5-litre V8 and five-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include 18-inch chrome-finish alloy wheels, power mirrors with memory, puddle lights and driver's side auto-dimming, seriously cool seven-lens Xenon headlights, fully automatic trunk open and close function, performance-tuned active dampening suspension; tyre pressure monitoring system, dual-zone climate control; DVD-based navigation system with seven-inch LCD screen and rearview monitor; heated and cooled front seats with ten-way driver and eight-way passenger adjust, heated rear seats, six-CD/cassette Bose system with eight speakers, voice recognition system, power rear and manual rear door window sunshades, and laser-based intelligent cruise control with preview braking feature, whatever that is. Safety features include numerous front and side airbags, ABS brakes and stability control, among other things.

The new Elantra gets a sleeker yet bulbous new look. It's also taller and wider than the outgoing Elantra. There's also more interior space than before, and a higher seating position. Most people would probably consider the Elantra a compact sedan, but its new interior volume is now comparable to some midsize cars. Various trim levels are available on this front-wheel-drive sedan, including a top-of-the-line model which comes with leather seats. But all models are well-equipped with plenty of convenience features, including power windows, intermittent windshield wipers, multiple storage areas, a 60/40-split fold-down rear seatback, dual vanity mirrors, tinted windows, two 12-volt outlets and a tilt steering wheel. Engine choices include a carryover 1.6-litre four-cylinder and a revamped 2.0-litre four-cylinder. A five-speed manual comes standard with the smaller motor, while a four-speed automatic is available for both engines. Basic models get only a single airbag and steel 15-inch wheels. The top model gets dual airbags, ABS brakes, stability control, and 16-inch alloys.

The Opel Insignia is the German manufacturer's performance sedan offering. Only sold in some GCC countries, Opel Insignia OPC gets a turbocharged 2.8-litre V6 with all-wheel drive. Features include dual-zone automatic AC, sunroof, electronic parking brake, cruise control, heated leather seats with memory, AM/FM radio with MP3/AUX/USB support, front and rear parking sensors, speed-sensitive power steering, daytime running lights, fog lamps, 20-inch wheels with xenon headlights and LED daytime running lamps. Safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, lane-departure warning, ESP and ABS.

Fiat launched the compact Bravo hatchback as a new-for-2010 model, marking its return to the GCC after a gap of nearly a decade. With funky cabin materials, unique exterior, seating for five and a 500-litre boot, the Bravo goes for practicality with a bit of flair. The only GCC-spec engine is a 1.4-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder, mated to a 6-speed "Dualogic" automanual, essentially a "robotised" manual gearbox. Three trims are available, with the base model getting power windows, keyless entry, manual a/c, CD player and 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps. The mid-range Comfort Pack adds 16-inch alloy wheels, dual-zone a/c, Bluetooth phone, turning fog-lights and a Blue&Me stereo that includes voice-control options and USB connectivity. The Luxury Pack adds 17-inch alloys, cruise control, parking sensors, leather upholstery and a sunroof. Options include various cabin fabrics, carbon effect and chrome cabin trims and 18-inch alloy wheels. On the safety front, the Bravo comes with standard ABS with electronic brakeforce distribution, as well as front and side-curtain airbags. The Comfort Pack adds traction control and electronic stability control while the Luxury Pack adds a tyre pressure monitor.

The Cadillac XTS debuted in late 2012 as a new flagship, replacing the STS as well as the DTS. Based on a front-wheel-drive Chevrolet platform, the XTS is powered by a 3.6-litre direct-injection V6, mated to a 6-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive. It comes with a electronically-controlled limited-slip differential, adjustable suspension and Brembo brakes, with standard 20-inch wheels. For 2014, a V-Sport model with a turobcharged 3.6-litre V6 and all-wheel-drive joined the range. Features include leather upholstery, configurable 12.3-inch LCD display, CUE multimedia system, CD/MP3 stereo with USB and Bluetooth support, HID headlights, smart keyless entry/start and all the usual power accessories, with further available features such as heads-up display, adaptive cruise control. Safety features include multiple airbags, lane departure warning, collision alert, safety alert seat, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert and available automatic emergency braking.

The Lincoln MKZ is a midsize entry-level luxury sedan. While the name is confusing, the MKZ is supposed to bring in younger buyers to traditionally old-fashioned Lincoln. While the car is somewhat based on the older Ford Mondeo platform, classic Lincoln design elements include a "waterfall" grille and chromed 17-inch alloy wheels, while the interior features leather and real wood or aluminium trim. The standard engine is the Ford 3.5-litre V6, with a 6-speed automatic. Interestingly, all-wheel-drive is standard for the GCC market, which sets it apart from its usual competitors. Compared to the Ford Mondeo, all aspects of the Lincoln chassis, including spring rates, shocks, and bushings have been tuned for a comfortable ride, while retaining responsive handling. A number of standard features include premium leather seats, tyre-pressure-monitoring system, reverse sensing system, THX II-certified audio system, HID headlights and the usual power features. Safety features include multiple airbags and ABS brakes, but stability control is not offered.

A new generation Ford Mustang was introduced in 2015. In 2018 it received a facelift and some power upgrades. There is no more V6 engine offered, with only 2.3-litre turbo and the V8 engines carrying over. All engines can be had with either a 6-speed manual transmission or a new 10-speed automatic transmission. The interior gets the MyFord infotainment system with SYNC 3. For the first time, Ford has introduced independent rear suspension for this generation Mustang, which helps improve handling. Standard features on the 2021 Ford Mustang Convertible include power windows, power steering, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, manual A/C, fabric seats, paddle shifters and alloy rims. The higher models get navigation, rear-view camera, leather seats, more speakers, engine push-start and automatic A/C. Safety standards include driver and passenger airbags, electronic stability control, ABS brakes and traction control.

The Cadillac XT6 is the luxury brand's midsize SUV offering. It comes equipped with a 3.6-litre V6 engine, which is the only engine option, and a 9-speed automatic transmission. Standard features in the XT6 include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, push start button, AM/FM stereo with 8-inch diagonal color information display, 7 speakers, Bluetooth, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, parking sensors with rear camera, sunroof, LED headlamps and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment includes Bose Sound System, "Technology Package" which includes Air Ionizer, 8-inch diagonal color reconfigurable gauge cluster, head-up display, power rake, and telescoping steering column and wireless charging, 20-inch diamond cut alloy wheels, interior ambient lighting, navigation, AM/FM stereo with connected navigation providing real-time traffic, 8” diagonal color information display, one type A and one type C full function USBs, personalized profiles for each driver’s settings, Natural Voice Recognition (English only) and NFC (Near Field Communications) mobile device pairing. Safety features include airbags - dual-stage frontal, knee and seat-mounted side-impact for driver and front passenger; head-curtain for all outboard seating positions with rollover protection, stability control, traction control, tyre pressure monitor and ABS. Optional safety features include "Driver Awareness Package", which includes Low Speed Forward Automatic Braking, Front Pedestrian Braking, Following Distance Indicator, Forward Collision Alert, Lane Keep Assist with Lane Departure Warning and IntelliBeam. Also available is a "Driver Assist Package", which includes Adaptive Cruise Control, and Forward and Reverse Automatic Braking.

The Ford F-150 is new from the ground up for 2015. Starting from its redesigned steel ladder-frame chassis, every aspect of the truck is new, including a shift to aluminium body construction and a general push towards "EcoBoost" turbocharged engines. Available in single cab, "SuperCab" quad-cab and "SuperCrew" double-cab body styles, engines on offer include a 3.5-litre V6, a 2.7-litre turbo V6, a 3.5-litre turbo V6 and a 5.0-litre V8, all with 6-speed automatics. Further configurations include a choice of rear-wheel-drive or four-wheel-drive with low-range, while an "FX4" package can add offroad suspension, rear locking diff and skidplates to any model except the base one. Aside from the usual basic features such as power windows, keyless entry and electric mirrors, new features, depending on trim level, include remote tailgate locking and release, unique "BoxLink" tailgate attachment points that accept standard attachments used in moving trucks and trailers, stowable loading ramps that attach to the BoxLink points, optional LED headlights, optional all-around LED lighting including side-mirror "flashlights" and in-bed lighting, 170-degree opening half-doors on SuperCab models, flat rear load floor in SuperCab and SuperCrew cabins, 360-degree camera view, adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot warning and even a panoramic sunroof. And it still has that built-in step in its tailgate to climb onto the bed, aside from new pop-out steps on the sides of the bed. Standard safety features include ABS, ESP, front and side-airbags, and optional rear inflatable belts.

The Volkswagen Amarok is a mid-size pickup for the commercial sector. In 2017, it got a slight facelift. In the GCC, only the rear-wheel drive model will be sold, which comes with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbocharged engine, mated to a six-speed manual transmission. The double-cab model is only available in this region. Standard and optional equipment include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3 player with 4-speakers, manual A/C, fog lamps, 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and  cruise control. Safety features include two airbags, ABS and traction control.

The Spanish-built Seat Ibiza is based on the VW Polo and even shares engines and gearboxes, but with a completely unique exterior and interior. In the Middle East, this front-wheel-drive is offered in 3-door or five-door hatchback as well as "Ibiza ST" station-wagon body styles. As the VW-owned company is nearly inactive in promoting the brand in the GCC, drivetrain availability is vague, although numerous VW-derived powerplants can be optioned up, including a 1.4-litre and a 1.6-litre, all 4-cylinder engines, the former with a 5-speed manual and the latter with either a 5-speed manual or a 7-speed dual-clutch DSG automanual. The sporty FR and Cupra models both get 1.4-litre "twin" supercharged-turbocharged 4-cylinder engines with 7-speed DSG automanual gearboxes. Standard equipment includes ABS brakes, driver and passenger airbag, power steering, power front windows, electric mirrors, remote central locking, 15-inch to 17-inch wheels, CD stereo, height adjustable front seats, split rear seat, cloth upholstery, traction control and even an optional stability control system. These cars are quite well-packed with features for their size. Sport and FR models get larger alloy wheels, stiffer suspension, body-colour rear spoiler, sports seats and unique exhausts as standard. The limited-availability 3-door Cupra gets the top turbo engine and further sports tuning.

The VW Golf has reached its sixth generation, although receiving largely an exterior facelift on the outside. Under the skin, many new features can be found that improves the Golf MK6 as a driver's car. Most noticeable is the new corporate front-end with the black-out grille, while the rest of the car is very similar to the outgoing model. The Golf VI gets a choice of two engines on debut, namely a carryover 1.6-litre 4-cylinder and a 1.4-litre TSI 4-cylinder, the latter of which uses both supercharging and turbocharging. Both models can be had with either a manual gearbox or a new 7-speed DSG automanual transmission. The interior is very similar to the previous Golf, but some new bits include the steering wheel, 'climatronic' a/c and better noise reduction. The Golf is offered as a 2-door or a 4-door, in Trendline, Comfortline and Highline trim levels. Depending on trim, the regular Golf can be had with seven airbags including a knee airbag, stability control, adaptive cruise control, adaptive chassis control with adjustable suspension, Park Assist, alloy wheels, sunroof, and the usual power accessories.

BMW introduced the X4 in the lineup for the first time as a 2015 model. It looks like a smaller version of the X6. Under the hood, two engine choices will be available. One is a turbocharged 4-cylinder 2.0-litre engine, while the other is a turbocharged 3.0-litre inline-6 motor. The BMW X4 is equipped with BMW ConnectedDrive features that include high-resolution, full-colour Head-Up Display, which projects all important driving information and the assistance systems displays into the driver's field of view. The Navigation System Professional with ECO PRO route guidance teams up with the iDrive Touch Controller whose touchpad allows texts  e.g. a navigation destination to be easily inputted by using a finger. The tailgate can opened automatically and can be further specified with the Comfort Access Option for extra convenience, which allows it to be opened with a movement of the foot. Safety and convenience can be further enhanced by optional premium features like the anti-dazzle High Beam Assistant, Driving Assistant Plus including Pedestrian and Collision Warning, Active Cruise Control with Stop & Go function and Lane Departure Warning. Available as options are Lane Change Warning, Surround View and the Parking Assistant.

The BMW Z4 was completely redesigned for the 2009 model year, shifting focus and becoming a comfort-cruiser rather than the focused sports car that it was before. Along with all-new styling, the Z4 now sports a folding hard-top convertible roof that folds down in 20 seconds at the touch of a button. While still a two-seater, the Z4 now has more space for two passengers and their luggage, although not much cargo room is left with the roof down.
