Changes to the cabin now include more premium materials as well as an integrated iDrive multimedia computer. The Z4 comes with a choice between three inline-6 engines. The Z4 sDrive23i with a 2.5-litre, the Z4 sDrive30i with a 3.0-litre, and the Z4 sDrive35i with a turbocharged 3.0-litre, all available with a manual or automatic, with the exception of the turbo motor, which can be mated to a clutchless automanual gearbox. The Z4 comes with Dynamic Drive Control as standard, which allows NORMAL, SPORT and SPORT+ modes, each of which changes throttle response and gearbox characteristics. Other features include the iDrive system with a high-resolution display that integrates entertainment, navigation, Bluetooth phone and climate control functionality. All the usual luxury features are available, either standard or optional, such as cloth or leather upholstery, power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, powered seats, keyless entry with starter button, alloy wheels, and HID headlights, among other options. On the safety front, the Z4 Roadster comes with stability control, ABS, front airbags, head and thorax airbags, reinforced A-pillars and roll bars behind the headrests.

The Audi RS 3 is the top performance trim for the A3 model. Under the hood, the all-wheel-drive sedan gets a turbocharged 2.5-litre 5-cylinder engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic dual-clutch transmission. Standard features include a 12.3-inch LCD screen for a gauge cluster, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push start-stop engine button, Nappa leather upholstery, Bang & Olufsen sound system with sub-woofer, Bluetooth, USB/AUX support, front sports seats, front electric seats with 4-way lumbar support, rear folding back seats, fog lamps, parking sensors, rear spoiler and a pop-up MMI multimedia screen with Apple Carplay. Some optional features include Audi magnetic ride, 19-inch polished alloy wheels with matte titanium finish, 5-spoke rotor arm design, red brake calipers and roof rails with matte titanium look. Standard safety features include electronic stability control, traction control, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD), front airbags and knee airbags.

The Kia Soul is part of the Korean manufacturer's new product offensive. Being touted as a crossover, it is really a tall compact hatchback, designed to be appealing for our misguided urban youth. Featuring tons of cabin space, the front-wheel-drive Kia Soul is powered by a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic and, if you ask the dealer nicely, a 5-speed manual too. Available in two trim levels, the basic model comes with 16-inch alloy wheels, power windows, electric power steering, keyless entry, electric mirrors, a single driver's airbag, roof rack, fog lamps, CD stereo with iPod input, rear parking sensors, split-folding rear seat, black cloth upholstery and 16-inch alloy wheels. The top-spec trim gets a better CD stereo with a sub-woofer and illuminated speakers, as well as a sunroof, leather steering wheel, underfloor tray and power outlet in the boot, luggage net, some extra trim. dual front airbags and 18-inch alloy wheels, with a choice of black, beige and red two-tone interiors. Optional features are extensive, largely limited to appearance kits, such as funkier alloy wheels, stickers, chrome trim, front and rear skirts, and shiny fuel caps. In addition to front airbags, ABS is available only on the top-spec model, but stability control and side airbags are not available on GCC-spec models.

A tribute to the discontinued Hummer H1 which was based on the military Humvee, the 6.0-litre V8-powered Hummer H2 is based on the Chevrolet Tahoe platform. Technically larger than the original H1, the H2 platform has actually been modified for proper off-road duty in keeping with the Hummer name. In 2005, the Hummer H2 wagon was joined by a second model called the SUT, or Sport Utility Truck. The SUT version, as its name implies, looks like a pickup, characterized by its unique tailgate, short pickup bed, and tailgate-mounted full-size spare tyre, which makes it a few inches longer than the wagon overall. Features include air suspension, roof rack crossbars, an AM/FM 6-disc CD changer, leather seats, onboard air compressor, ESP, ABS brakes, numerous airbags and a first aid kit. Options include exterior chrome appearance package, 17-inch chrome wheels, chrome tubular assist steps, navigation and a third-row seat for the wagon. The Hummer H2 offers truly impressive off-road capabilities. However, its size makes us wish it was banned from on-road use.

BAIC is a Chinese car company which made its debut in the UAE in late 2014, followed by other GCC countries in the next few years. The BAIC A1 hatchback comes is a mini compact which comes with a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, radio with USB/AUX, 4 speakers, fabric seats, 14-inch steal wheels and driver airbag. The higher models get a remote key, CD player with touch screen, 6 speakers, sunroof, leather seats, parking sensors, rearview camera, cruise control, auto headlights, passenger side airbag and curtain airbags.They are come with standard ABS brakes and electronic brake distribution (EBD).

The MG GS is the Chinese company's compact SUV offering. It comes with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. It comes standard in front-wheel-drive format, with optional four-wheel-drive. Standard features include power steering, power windows, central locking, fabric seats, halogen headlamps, fog lamps, LED daytime running lamps, manual-adjustable seats, manual A/C, stereo with USB/AUX support, 4 speakers and 17-inch alloy wheels. Optional features include automatic headlamps, xenon headlamps, keyless entry, engine start-stop button, 18-inch alloy wheels, leather seats with lumbar support, sunroof, automatic A/C, infotainment system with 6.1-inch touch screen and 6 or 8 speakers, Bluetooth, electric folding side mirrors,  glovebox cooling and rear camera. Safety features include stability control, ABS with electronic brake distribution (EBD), brake assist, auto hold and front airbags. The higher models get additional airbags, hill descent control and anti-roll program.

The all-new Chevrolet Corvette debuted as a 2014 model year. For 2017, it got a new transmission. It features a new LT1 V8 engine, but still has the same 6.2-litre displacement. Power has gone up however, with the new Corvette Stingray producing more horsepower and torque. More interesting is the 7-speed manual transmission it has, with rev-matching technology. For customers who don't like the third pedal, there is a 8-speed automatic transmission, the same gearbox as the previous generation, but tweaked with different internals for better performance. A new electric power steering system and cylinder deactivation help to improve fuel economy, said to be now less than the previous generation. There is a Drive Mode Selector which has 5 settings Weather, Eco, Tour, Sport and Track. Looking at the exterior, we see some similar design elements from other brands such as the new 2013 SRT Viper from the front, the vents and windows of a Nissan GT-R on the side, and rear fender-top vents like that of a Ferrari 458 Italia. The rear still incorporates the trademark four-lamp design, however it looks more like a modified design from the Chevrolet Camaro. The four exhaust tips lined up together is one of those things you either love or hate. The interior is where they have made some much-needed improvements. The designers made sure they cover as much of the interior as possible with soft-touch materials. It features a more driver-focused cockpit and a smaller steering wheel. New seats with more bolstering have been added. A Z51 package adds more sporting suspension as well as extra trim such as a rear spoiler. Safety features include front and side airbags, ESP, ABS and seat-belt pretensioners.

The Hyundai i40 is a midsize station wagon. A basic, mid-range and top model are sold here. All the models get the same 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine with a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, manual a/c with rear cooling ducts, steel wheels, AM/FM radio and CD player with MP3 playback capability and six speakers. Available features, standard on higher trim levels, include parking sensors and alloy wheels. The rear seat backrests feature a 60:40 split, so you can still carry the luggage plus a rear seat passenger or two. If more space is required, rear seat backrests fold flat into the floor while the floor rail system helps keep your luggage secured.

The TrailBlazer is powerful and capable midsize off-road vehicle, which is just the right size to not be a pain on the roads. Launched in 2002, it received a minor facelift in 2006. It has a rigid chassis, good off-road suspension, powerful brakes and a spacious enough interior to compete in this class. It is stable at high speeds, wobbly around curves, and comfortable over rough surfaces, while being quite capable off-road, thanks to a proper four-wheel-drive system with low-range gearing. The TrailBlazer also comes in an EXT trim with an extended wheelbase that adds a third row seat, but it was discontinued after 2006. The TrailBlazer comes with an updated-for-2006 Vortec 4.2-litre inline 6-cylinder engine that generates very respectable numbers, similar to the V8 motors of some competitors. And then there is 5.3-litre V8 engine that can be had as an option on higher models. The V8 is equipped with GM's Displacement on Demand technology as standard which deactivates four cylinders under certain driving conditions to aid fuel efficiency, returning the full complement of power once the controller senses vehicle speed or load requires additional power. Both engines use a Hydra-Matic 4-speed auto transmission.

The MG HS is the brand's compact SUV offering. Only the 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine is sold here, mated to a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard features on the HS Comfort model include power steering, power windows, central locking, electric folding mirrors, halogen auto headlamps, cruise control, single zone electric A/C, fabric seats, driver seat manual lumbar adjustment, 7-inch display instrument cluster, 10.1-inch touch screen with USB ports, Bluetooth, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto and 6 speakers, front and rear fog lamps, roof rails, and 18-inch alloy wheels. The HS Luxury models gets all-wheel drive, leather sports seats, front driver and passenger powered seats, LED headlamps, LED taillamps, 12.3-inch instrument cluster screen, dual-zone automatic A/C and panoramic sunroof. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, side airbags, ABS, stability control, hill assist control, and tyre pressure monitor. The higher models get additional curtain airbags, blind spot monitor and lane departure warning.

The Toyota Prado got a minor facelift for 2014, with a redesigned front-end and other trim changes. The "VVT-i" engine offerings carry over, with a 2.7-litre 4-cylinder and a 4.0-litre V6. All models offer standard all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing and available locking centre-differential. The Saudi market offers both manual and automatic variants on all except the top trim level, while the UAE market only gets automatic versions. The basic Prado 2.7L, known as TX in KSA and EXR in UAE, comes with 17-inch steel wheels, black front grille, black power mirrors and door handles, rear spoiler, mud guards, fabric seating for seven, keyless entry, front and rear manual a/c, CD/MP3 6-speaker stereo, ABS with EBD and brake-assist, dual front airbags and floor-mounted spare tyre. The TX additionally gets side-steps and rear parking sensors, while the EXR instead gets a cool box, steering audio controls, USB/AUX ports and Bluetooth. The mid-range Prado 2.7L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, gets 17-inch alloy wheels, rear parking sensors, chrome front grille, body-coloured trim, side steps, leather steering wheel and shift lever, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cool box and more. The TXL additionally gets front fog lamps, front bumper guard and stability control, while the EXR instead gets dual-zone auto a/c, cruise control and a dealer-installed auto-dimming mirror with rear camera. The UAE also gets a Prado 2.7L in VXR trim that adds powered front seats, side/curtain/knee airbags, stability control and dealer-installed features such as leather upholstery and navigation with rear camera while losing steering-wheel controls. The basic Prado 4.0L, known as EXR in UAE, comes with a 6-speaker stereo withBluetooth and USB/AUX ports, steering audio controls, rear parking sensors, manual a/c, fabric seats, dual airbags, stability control, ABS, smart key with engine start/stop button, cruise control and hill start/descent assist. All UAE-bound V6 Prado models have a door-mounted spare tyre. The mid-range Prado 4.0L, known as TXL in KSA and GXR in UAE, comes with roof rails, side steps, fog lamps, front bumper guard and uphill/downhill assist on all automatic models. The TXL additionally gets a tow hitch and side mouldings, while the GXR instead gets side/curtain/knee airbags, dual-zone a/c, extra chrome trim, power front seats, rear camera and dealer-installed navigation with no steering controls. A higher-spec Prado 4.0L trim, known as TXL2 in KSA and VXR in UAE, comes with sunroof, dual auto a/c, rear camera and aftermarket audio with navigation. The TXL2 version also gets auto-levelling LED headlights, sunshades and in-car WiFi, while the VXR gets remote start, leather and power front seats. The Prado 4.0L in top VXL trim gains 18-inch alloy wheels, LED-encrusted headlights, leather seats, ventilated front seats, power front seats with memory, front and rear parking sensors with rear camera, side/curtain/knee airbags, "optitron" gauges, 14-speaker JBL stereo with voice control and steering-wheel buttons, multi-touch screen with navigation, remote engine starter and additional exterior trim. The Saudi VXL additionally gets self-leveling KDSS suspension, power-folding third row, Multi-Terrain Select with four cameras, rear DVD screen, blind-spot monitor and a tyre pressure warning system.

The S2000 is a small two-seat roadster that can easily chase the likes of the snobby Porsche Boxster. It is a technological innovation from Honda, whose aim with this car was to pump as much horsepower out of a small 2.0-litre engine as possible, without any turbo or supercharging trickery. The S2000 is said to drive like a superbike, because big horsepower from small displacement with a narrow powerband and extremely high rpm produces a very frantic experience. Driving it slowly, shifting the manual at low rpm apparently results in very weak performance in traffic. The latest model has refinements to the engine and suspension put in place back in 2005. Changes to the S2000 in 2006 include more shoulder and elbow room, and some tweaks, most notably 17-inch wheels, drive-by-wire throttle, stability control and new headlights with a triple-beam design. Early models had a plastic rear window, while 2002-plus models get a glass one. The last external facelift was in 2004. Interior features are basic, but include leather upholstery, electric power steering, starter button, power windows, power mirrors, remote central locking, air-conditioning and a pathetic radio cassette stereo with 2 speakers.

All new Kia Rio came out for the 2018 model year. It is a slightly larger car from its predecessor so interior room has marginally gone up as well. Two 4-cylinder engines are available on the front-wheel drive 2022 Kia Rio sedan - one a 1.4-litre and the other a 1.6-litre. Standard features on the Rio include power steering, power windows, central locking, halogen lamps, manual A/C, fabric seats, USB port and 15-inch steel wheels. Higher models get a 5.0-inch touchscreen audio system, 3.5-inch LCD screen on the instrument cluster, automatic A/C, leather seats, fog lamps and 15 inch or 17-inch alloy wheels. Safety features on the 2022 Kia Rio include ABS, front driver and passenger airbags, stability control, electronic brake distribution and brake assist.

The Mazda 2 gets a major makeover for 2016. Available as a hatchback and as this sedan, it now uses its own "Skyactiv" chassis and engine. The Mazda 2 gets a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine. Mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission, the front-wheel-drive Mazda 2 comes with standard features such as electric power steering, front discs and rear drum brakes, CD stereo, keyless entry, single-zone a/c and 14-inch steel wheels with hubcaps. Fog lamps, rear spoiler and 15-inch alloys are optional. Standard safety features include ABS with electronic brake-force distribution and dual front airbags.

The Fiat Fiorino is a compact commercial vehicle offering by the Italian brand. The Turkish-built Fiorino comes with a turbocharged 1.4-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed manual. Standard features include power steering, sliding side door, foldable passenger seat, adjustable driver's seat, heat reflecting windows, radio with CD/MP3 player, and ABS. It has 2.8 cubic-metre volume of cargo space with a 600 kg payload capacity.

An all-new Ford Expedition model came out as in 2018. Engine specs for the 2020 Ford Expedition include a second generation 3.5-litre twin-turbocharged "Ecoboost" engine, available in two different tunes, and connected to a 10-speed automatic transmission. The Expedition’s terrain-management system allows the driver to select from seven modes in 4WD models, so whatever terrain you’re tackling (be it sand, mud/ruts, gravel, grass or snow), there’s a mode that optimises the drivetrain for it. Needless to say that when driving in the Sport mode, you get an improved throttle response and gearbox mapping. The big Ford offers the best towing capability of any full-size SUV, and it comes with features such as Pro Trailer Backup Assist, which negates the need for repeated back- and forth when reversing with a trailer. There’s also an available hands-free, foot-activated liftgate to make loading bulky cargo into the load bay less of a back-breaking exercise. Aside from offering best-in-class second-row and third-row legroom as well as hip-room, the Expedition is also the first in this segment to feature a sliding second-row seat with tip-and-slide functionality, providing easy access to the third row without the need to first remove a child safety seat. The Expedition’s second-row and third-row seats not only provide best-in-class roominess but can be quickly folded flat with the push of a button to provide access to a cargo area wide and flat enough to handle 4×8-foot sheets of plywood and other gear. There’s no shortage of luxury kit in the Expedition, and among the goodies on offer is plush leather trim, multicontour driver seat with massage feature, a power reclining 3rd row seat, capacitive touchscreen with SYNC 3 (which also offers Arabic voice capability) and Apple CarPlay / Android Auto compatibility, adaptive cruise control with Stop-and-Go (keeps a set distance to the vehicle in front, and will automatically bring the car to a complete stop, and accelerate away again when required), dual-headrest rear entertainment system and a premium 12-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system with enough bass to make the windows reverberate. Add to that, a class-leading Panoramic VistaRoof that covers not only the 1st row but also the 2nd. Your devices are also well catered to, as there’s wireless charging, four 12-volt power points, up to six USB ports positioned across all three rows and a 230-volt outlet. The Platinum gets collision-avoidance detection (for both pedestrians and vehicles), lane-keeping system, blind-spot warning with cross-traffic alert and enhanced active park assist (for both parallel and perpendicular parking needs). There’s also a 360-degree camera to give you a bird’s eye view of the car’s immediate surrounds.

The Mazda CX-3 is the Japanese brand's smallest SUV offering. Under the hood, it comes with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features on the base 2-wheel drive model includes power steering, power windows, power mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push button start, fabric seats, halogen headlamps, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3/AUX/USB, Bluetooth, 4 speakers and alloy wheels. The mid-spec models get all-wheel drive, rear camera, auto A/C, 7-inch touch screen, 6 speakers, steering wheel with Bluetooth controls, daytime running lamps and fog lamps. The top model gets navigation, 6 Bose speakers, adaptive cruise control, leather seats, head up display, digital tachometer and DVD player. Standard safety features include front dual airbags, ABS with EBD and traction control and stability control. The higher models get blind spot monitor, auto-braking system, lane departure warning system and side curtain airbags.

The Toyota Aurion got a complete redesign for the 2012 model year alongside its Camry sibling. The Aurion is essentially a redone version of the Camry, but fitted with a V6 engine and better interior appointments. All models get a carryover 3.5-litre V6 engine with a 6-speed automatic. In the UAE, the 2012 Toyota Aurion comes in only two grades, namely Sports and Grande. In other markets such as Saudi Arabia, the grades are dubbed as Touring, SE and Grande, with a base model that isn't offered in the UAE. Only the Aurion Grande gets leather trim, 7-inch touchscreen navigation & DVD player, Bi-Xenon headlights with intelligent "AFS" and headlamp cleaner, and 8 way memory seats for the driver, all standard for the UAE. Navigation is optional in the Saudi model. The Aurion Sports model loses those features, but is instead fitted with a sport-tuned suspension, fabric sport seats with enhanced support, a newly-designed three spoke steering, paddle shifters, stereo with 6.1-inch display, 17-inch wheels and an exclusive front grille as well as sporty front and rear bumper skirts, all standard for the UAE. The moonroof and 17-inch alloys is optional on the Saudi Touring model. Other features include covered cup-holders, dual-zone auto a/c, Bluetooth, USB/AUX ports, keyless start, cruise control, rear parking sensors, front and side-curtain airbags, ABS, stability control and more.

The Chevrolet Camaro Convertible received a facelift for the 2014 model year. Aside from the pointier front-end, the generic tail lamps, the functional new bonnet vents and optional Recaro seats, there aren't any other visible changes. Powered by a 3.6-litre V6 or a 6.2-litre V8, it rides on a shortened rear-wheel-drive Lumina SS platform, with four-wheel independent suspension and 2+2 seating. The Camaro comes in V6 LT and V8 SS trims. The V6 is only available with a 6-speed paddle-shifted automatic in the GCC. The SS gets a choice of two V8 engines, each customised for use with a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic. The automatic V8 features cylinder deactivation to improve fuel economy. StabiliTrak traction control and front-side airbags are standard, while Brembo brakes are available on the SS version. The SS also gets stiffer suspension and adjustable Competitive/Sport modes for stability control and Launch Control on manual models. The ZL1 gets a supercharged 6.2-litre V8 with a 6-speed manual or automatic. The hard-plastic cabin comes with cloth or leather interior, with standard blue LED lighting and optional glow-in-the-dark trim panels. Standard features include air conditioning, power windows and lock, and keyless entry. Available features include heads-up display and a new MyLink entertainment system which includes touchscreen navigation. Standard rims include 18-inch wheels for the V6 and 20-inch ones for the V8. Safety features include front airbags, side airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Dodge Ram 1200 is a commercial pickup offering from the American brand, which is basically a rebadged Mitsubishi L200. Available in two-wheel-drive form with a 2.4-litre petrol engine or a 2.5-litre turbodiesel, or in four-wheel-drive form with the diesel engine only, it is an interesting proposition on-road, and even off-road, if equipped. Only the five-speed manual is currently offered here, with an automatic option set to come later. Choices in body styles include double cab or single cab.

The Nissan Sunny got a facelift for the 2015 model year. The Sunny sedan comes from India, and is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a CVT. The basic 'S' model comes with 14-inch steel wheels, CD/MP3 stereo, AUX jack, cloth upholstery, trip computer and a black grille surround. The 'SV' model, identified by a chrome grille surround and door handles, adds power mirrors, front power windows, keyless entry, upgraded cloth seats and hubcaps, with an optional comfort package that adds fog lights, rear power windows, rear fan vents, parking sensors, more speakers and a central rear armrest. The top 'SL' model comes only in automatic, with 15-inch alloys, Bluetooth, steering-wheel stereo controls, nicer gauges with more readings, push-start, Display Audio system with Facebook support, cloth trim on the doors, LED side mirrors, rear spoiler and mud guards. All models get dual front airbags, ABS with EBD, brake assist, and seatbelts for all five seating positions.

The Peugeot 301 is the French manufacturer's answer for the budget sub-compact segment. It's offered with a 4-cylinder 1.6-litre petrol engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic gearbox. While claiming class-leading cabin and boot space, the Spanish-built saloon offers several convenience and safety features, depending on trim level, including a CD/MP3 stereo, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth, cloth upholstery, manual or electric mirrors, power windows, manual or single-zone automatic a/c, rear parking sensors, one or two airbags, ABS with emergency brake-assist system, fog lamps and either 15-inch steel or 16-inch alloy wheels.

The new Civic is a breath of fresh air in the crowded compact class. Honda once led the class with quality and style. It lost its way for a while, but now it is back in form. The redesigned Honda Civic is the most futuristic compact car on the market. There is more power from just one 1.8-litre four-cylinder engine choice, with either a manual or an automatic. Improvements include better ride and handling, and better interior packaging. The Civic offers important safety features such ABS brakes and airbags, though not all might be standard in some markets. Standard equipment include power windows, tilt-and-telescope steering wheel, height-adjustable driver's seat, rear window-integrated radio antenna, air conditioning, power mirrors, central locking, a centre console with sliding armrest, a four-speaker AM/FM/CD stereo with MP3 and WMA playback, and the funky digital dashboard. Options include a power moonroof; a 60/40 split folding rear seatback, cruise control with steering wheel-mounted controls and 16-inch alloy wheels.

The Maserati Coupe, sometimes known as the 4200 GT, is a high-performance two-door four-seater that relaunched Ferrari-owned Maserati as a contender in the sport-luxury class. It complements the two-seater Spyder, which is a shorter-wheelbase convertible version of the Coupe. While these cars are based on the original 3200 GT which debuted in 1998, they have been receiving updates regularly. The latest variations were the GranSport Coupe and the GranSport Spyder, which feature sport-tuned suspension, aerodynamic and performance upgrades, and racier trimmings. All versions are powered by a Ferrari-tuned 4.2-litre V8, with a choice of a six-speed manual or a six-speed Cambiocorsa paddle-shifted automanual. The Gransport versions, which debuted in 2005, have slightly more power. All cars got a full suite of luxury features, such as power windows, premium CD stereo, electric mirrors, power-adjustable leather seats and more. Additional features 18-inch alloy wheels, multiple airbags, ABS brakes and stability control.

The F6 was the second model to join the Chinese BYD range. The midsize sedan is slightly smaller than the class average, even if the derivative styling uses cues from Japanese stalwarts. Powered by a choice of Mitsubishi-designed 2.0-litre or 2.4-litre 4-cylinder engines, both can be had with a 5-speed manual, although the larger engine, which comes with Mitsubishi's MIVEC variable-valve timing technology, can also be mated with an outdated 4-speed automatic with tiptronic function. Available features include an 8-way adjustable driver's seat, tilt-and-telescoping multi-function steering wheel, power windows, electric mirrors and cruise control. Also available are cloth or leather upholstery with wood trim. Safety features include ABS with EBD, dual front airbags, seat-mounted side airbags and protective beams in the doors. BYD is only available in some GCC countries, including UAE, Kuwait and Oman.

The sixth generation BMW 5-series received a facelift for the 2014 model year. The 520i gets a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder and 8-speed auto. The 535i has a turbocharged 3.0-litre 6-cylinder, mated to an 8-speed automatic with paddle-shifters. A 528i model gets a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder. The 550i with the 4.4-litre turbocharged V8 and 8-speed auto has been upgraded with more power and torque. Some of the wide range of sophisticated driving and comfort features offered in the new BMW 5-Series include Dynamic Drive Control with four modes, namely comfort, normal, sport and sport+, as well as Comfort Start, Head-Up Display, Multi-Channel Audio System, Rear Seat Entertainment, Four-Zone Automatic Air Conditioning and BMW iDrive control. BMW ConnectedDrive also offers a unique range of driver-assist technology functions for enhanced comfort and safety. The regular 5-Series can also be had with an M package that adds sports suspension and a body kit. The BMW 5-Series comes with a Parking Assistant, an optional feature that facilitates the process of parking, as well as Active Cruise Control, Surround View and Rear View Camera, Lane Departure Warning, Lane Change Warning and BMW Night Vision with pedestrian recognition.

The Trajet is Hyundai's latest attempt at conquering the world of minivans, but it is a completely typical minivan, with nothing over the competition except a lower price and an underpowered 2.7-litre V6. Standard features include power steering, front and rear a/c, roof rack, front and rear power windows, radio and cassette player with 4 speakers, central door locks, funky tail lights and an automatic transmission. Options include a sunroof, fog lamps, All models come with 15-inch wheels, though the lower model gets steel rims with plastic covers, while the top model gets alloys. Unique features include four forward-opening doors, which is a rarity in the large minivan set. The basic model actually comes with 8-seater capacity, thanks to a bunch of bench seats, but the top model is more of a 7-seater, with more comfortable accommodations. The cabin is of course versatile, with movable and foldable seats to increase or decrease luggage space as needed. Safety features are conspicuously absent in the Middle East model, though overseas versions get all sorts of airbags, traction control and ABS, some of which you could probably special-order.

An all-new Honda Pilot was released as a 2016 model. Under the hood, it gets a 3.5-liter Direct Injected V6 engine with Variable Cylinder Management (VCM), mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. The base EX model can be had in 2WD or AWD form, while the EX-L and Touring trims only come with AWD and no low-range gearing. The Pilot includes a traction management system and is featured on all models except the EX 2WD, with pushbutton mode selection and TFT mode display on the cockpit instrument panel. In addition, EX (AWD) & EXL grades offer 200 mm of ground clearance for better off-road ability. There is also a sand-mode feature. Features include halogen projector headlights in EX and EXL grades whereas LED projector headlights in Touring grade, which also gets a panoramic glass roof. Some of the other features standard in all grades includes front fog lights, LED taillights and LED daytime running lights along with Tailgate Spoiler, power door mirrors and LED turn light indicators. For the interior, an 8-inch touchscreen, standard in all grades, gives you access to audio system controls and other display features. The Touring grade includes second row captain's chairs, which provides easy walk through between the second and third row for a 7 passenger configuration. Other amenities include tri-zone automatic climate control, rear air conditioning duct in the second and third row seats, rear door sunshade, sun glass holder and conversation mirror, cargo area hidden storage for extra luggage, active noise control (ANC) for a quieter cabin, with a rear entertainment system with a 9-inch display screen available in the Touring grade. Safety features include Vehicle Stability Assist (VSA) with Traction Control Systems (TCS), Anti-Lock Brake Systems (ABS), Electronic Brake Distributor (EBD), Hill Start Assist (HSA), Agile Handle Assist (AHA) and Tyre Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS).

The Toyota Corolla is all-new for 2014, with completely-redone styling and an extended wheelbase for more cabin space. It has remained the same for the 2018 model year. Engine offerings include a 1.6-litre and a new 2.0-litre, both 4-cylinder "VVT-i" units mated to 4-speed automatics, although a base model with a 6-speed manual is available in some GCC markets. The front-wheel-drive platform still rides on independent front and torsion-beam rear suspension. The five-seater is available in various trim levels. In Saudi Arabia, there is a 1.6 XLi model with a manual or automatic gearbox, 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, black front grille, power windows and mirrors, keyless entry and a 4-speaker CD/MP3/USB/AUX stereo. Moving up to the 1.6 GLi adds fog lamps, 16-inch alloys, rear parking sensors, chrome grille, trunk liner, better upholstery with leather steering wheel, split-folding rear seats, 6-speaker touchscreen stereo with Bluetooth, smart keyless entry with starter button and several other smaller convenience features. The 2.0 GLi adds LED headlights with LED running lamps, sunroof, rear manual curtains, auto a/c and cruise control. In the UAE, there are 5 trim levels, starting with an uber-basic 1.6 S model that includes a standard automatic gearbox, 15-inch steelies, 4-speaker CD/MP3/USB/AUX stereo, power mirrors and a black grille. The next-level 1.6 SE version adds power windows, keyless entry and body-colour door handles. The 1.6 SE+ adds better upholstery with leather steering wheel, chrome grille, split-folding rear seats, LED running lamps, smart keyless entry and start, LCD info display, a better 6-speaker stereo and a few other extra bits. Moving on to the larger engine, the 2.0 SE has all the features of the 1.6 SE, but additionally gets 15-inch alloys and 6 speakers for the basic stereo. The 2.0 SE+ model gets all the features of the 1.6 SE+ model. And the 2.0 Limited gets a sunroof, auto-levelling projector headlights and cruise control. Other markets may get slightly different trim levels. All models get standard dual front airbags, ABS with brake assist and EBD, and an alarm immobiliser.

The Sirion is Daihatsu's entry in the sub-compact segment, packed with features and space. It received a minor facelift for the 2008 model year, along with a bigger 1.5-litre engine. The little Sirion offers a generous amount of space for the front passengers, including a fair bit of room between the driver seat and the front passenger seat. Rear passengers aren't so lucky, but they still get reasonable amounts of leg space between front and rear seats. The rear doors open wide to an angle of around 80 degrees, allowing easy entry and exit, and the tailgate eases handling of large luggage. There is a full 630 litres of luggage space with two people on board and the rear seats folded down. With five on board, it still has 225 litres. The top of the back door has decent head clearance and a pull handle also makes it easy to close the door. A luggage room lamp adds convenience, along with the CD/AM/FM Radio, power windows, central locking, front airbags, cup holders in the doors and the centre console, and split rear seats that are 60:40 foldable. It is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder motor, the Sirion shifts gears using a 4-speed automatic, as the manual is not offered here. 14-inch steel wheels are standard, while alloys are optional, among other things.

The fresh Mazda CX-7 five-seater crossover comes in two trim levels for the GCC market, namely a base model with front-wheel-drive and the top version with all-wheel-drive, both mated to a standard 2.3-litre turbocharged "DISI" 4-cylinder engine. The base 2WD GT model gets black fabric upholstery, CD player, manual a/c, cruise control, 18-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, basic trip computer, dual exhaust tips, rear spoiler, folding 60/40 split rear seats, power windows, electric mirrors and four-wheel independent suspension with disc brakes on all corners. The fully-optioned AWD GTX model additionally gets beige leather upholstery, intelligent keyless entry with starter button, Bose 9-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with changer, colour-screen trip computer, powered driver's seat, automatic a/c, xenon headlights, fog lamps, rain-sensing wipers, sunroof and rear-view camera. All models thankfully get ABS, stability control, front and side-curtain airbags and alarm, Mazda choosing not to skimp on safety features.

One of the longest-running nameplates in the region, the Sunny has become popular for its reasonable price and traditional reliability, all while competitors drove their own prices up. However, the Sunny soon fell behind in terms of equipment, and the all-new Tiida arrived as an unofficial replacement to the Sunny in Nissan's lineup. Nissan Middle East is openly pushing the Sunny as a fleet car now, leaving the Tiida for individual sales. That fact has led to the Sunny receiving only a facelift in its latest iteration, while having its engine lineup reduced to just one. The new car is in fact a rebadged Samsung SM3, sold only in Korea. There is good head room, but other interior dimensions fall behind its competitors. Available as a four-door sedan, the Sunny is now available only with a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine, with a manual or automatic transmissions. Standard features include electric power steering, air conditioning and a cloth interior. Options include a CD stereo system and power accessories. Optional safety features include dual front airbags and ABS brakes.

The VW Touareg is a luxurious and comfortable 4WD that is surprisingly capable both on the road and off it too. It is a practical vehicle, and on the highway, the Touareg offers a firm but smooth ride, and its handling is responsive for its mass, while in the desert, a full set of off-roading equipment comes in handy, including locking diffs and low-range gearing. The range includes a 3.2-litre V6, a 4.2-litre V8 and a very limited 6.0-litre W12. All models come with a six-speed automatic with manual shift capability. Also standard is Volkswagen's 4Motion permanent all-wheel-drive system. The Touareg seats five, and there is no third row of seats available. The Touareg comes standard with leatherette upholstery, dual-zone climate control with rear seat controls, wood trim, power windows, mirrors and sunroof, electrically adjustable front seating, alloy wheels of various sizes, ABS and many more items. Higher models get leather, auto-dimming outside mirrors with memory; and other luxuries. All models include front, side-impact and curtain airbags.

Big and conservative, the Kia Mohave is supposed to strengthen Kia's "family" SUV line-up and brand image in the world market. With a 3.8-litre V6 engine mated with the 6-speed automatic transmission, the Kia Mohave is characterized by fully-independent air suspension and its various safety systems, including the ABS brakes, electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD), brake assist, stability control, traction control, and front and side airbags. Furthermore, the Mohave is equipped with Downhill Assist Control, keeping the vehicle's speed steady while going down straight and strong slopes, while a Hill-Start Assist Control is also available. The Mohave comes with a 600W stereo with six-CD changer, seven-seater capability, cloth or leather trim, DVD player, reverse camera and all the usual power accessories. The Mohave rides on a  truck-like body-on-frame platform and comes with four-wheel-drive and low-range gearing, which allows it to be classified as an off-road vehicle by default.

The Silverado range is Chevrolet's line of full-size pickup trucks, and covers everything from passenger pickups to big honking diesel monsters with six wheels and more. The Silverado pickup is the second-best selling vehicle in the United States, behind the Ford F-150 pickup truck, and it sells more trucks there than Toyota sells Camry cars. The Silverado 1500 light pickup truck is about the only vehicle that you can drive from this range without offending anyone around you, while the Silverado HD trucks should best be used if you work at a place that requires regular hauling. The light-duty trucks generally use the 1500 name, can tow up to 4700 kg and can carry 930 kg in their beds. They are available in three cab lengths, 2-door short cab, 3 or 4-door extended cab, and front-hinged 4-door crew cab. Three cargo beds are available, including a short box, a standard box, and a long box. The short box is only available with the extended or crew cab, and is the only option on the 4-door. Engines include a Vortec 4800 V8 and a Vortec 5300 V8. The Vortec 6000 V8 is available in the Heavy Duty models but not in the 1500 models, while the Z71 signifies an off-road package.

The B-Series is the forgotten small pickup truck range of the Mazda line-up. No one in their right mind is going to buy one of these for personal use, but for those who want to be different, in a flamboyant American sort of way, they can pick up one of these and modify them for purposes other than hauling cargo. Engines include a 2.2-litre and a 2.6-litre petrol engines, while the diesel offering is a 2.9-litre unit, all four-cylinder motors and all with a standard five-speed manual, or even an automatic in some markets. Body styles include a single cab and a double cab shape. Key features include an AM/FM radio with cassette deck and 2 speakers, monotone or two-tone paintjob, and manually operated windows. Available accessories include overfender and side-step cladding panels, and front and rear skirt kits. Cargo-box equipment includes a single-action tailgate lock, a rear step bumper, outer and inner rope hooks, and load rests. Options, available in some markets, include front airbags, ABS brakes with electronic brake-force distribution, and even power windows.

The Sirion is Daihatsu's entry in the sub-compact segment, packed with features and space. It received a minor facelift for the 2008 model year, along with a bigger 1.5-litre engine. The little Sirion offers a generous amount of space for the front passengers, including a fair bit of room between the driver seat and the front passenger seat. Rear passengers aren't so lucky, but they still get reasonable amounts of leg space between front and rear seats. The rear doors open wide to an angle of around 80 degrees, allowing easy entry and exit, and the tailgate eases handling of large luggage. There is a full 630 litres of luggage space with two people on board and the rear seats folded down. With five on board, it still has 225 litres. The top of the back door has decent head clearance and a pull handle also makes it easy to close the door. A luggage room lamp adds convenience, along with the CD/AM/FM Radio, power windows, central locking, front airbags, cup holders in the doors and the centre console, and split rear seats that are 60:40 foldable. It is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder motor, the Sirion shifts gears using a 4-speed automatic, as the manual is not offered here. 14-inch steel wheels are standard, while alloys are optional, among other things.

The Lincoln MKZ made its comeback in the GCC as a 2014 model year. In 2017, it got a significant facelift, along with a new engine.The MKZ comes with a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine or a turbocharged 3.0-litre V6, both mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission with paddle shifters. The 2.0T comes in front-wheel-drive form while the 3.0T comes with all-wheel-drive for the GCC market. The MKZ will be available with SYNC3 and MyLincoln Touch as standard, along with large 10.1-inch LCD instrument cluster and an 8-inch centre touchscreen. Options include a huge opening panoramic glass roof. As for safety, there is a mono-vision camera integrated into the rearview mirror to read lane markers on the road. It will be complemented by radar sensors for the adaptive cruise control and active Collision Warning with Brake Support. Also included are wide-angle radar sensors for help with parking and backing up. It also has inflatable second-row seatbelts and eight airbags.

The Grand Marquis is the longest running Mercury-badged vehicle ever. The mechanical underpinnings date back to the 70s, but a revision in 2003 involved a new frame, a revised independent front suspension, a new steering rack and rear suspension tuning. More updates in 2005 included a facelifted exterior, interior trim changes and more convenience features.The Grand Marquis is powered by a heavily detuned version of the Mustang's 4.6-litre V8 powerplant, mated to a four-speed automatic. If not obvious yet, the Grand Marquis is just a rebadged version of the Ford Crown Victoria. Features include three-person bench seats front and back, optional leather trim, a new instrument panel, burl woodgrain, a two-tone colour package and standard power windows. It is available in the Middle East in GS, GS Convenience, GS-L, LS Premium, LSE and LS Ultimate trims, at last count. A handling package, optional on GS and LS series, aims to improve the boat-like drive with 16-inch  aluminium wheels, a 3.27 axle, heavy duty rear stabiliser bar and rear air suspension with unique springs. Safety features include dual front airbags and ABS brakes.

An all-new model of the Acura RDX was released in 2020. Under the hood, it gets a 3.5-litre V6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. The all-wheel-drive RDX comes in one trim. Standard features in the RDX include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, LED headlights, daytime running lights, sunroof, engine start-stop button, cruise control, front power driver's seat, dual-zone automatic A/C, leather interior, premium audio system with 10 speakers, front & rear smart keyless entry, front heated & ventilated seats, front & rear parking sensors and real wood dashboard, adaptive cruise control, bird's eye view camera. Standard safety features on the RDX include front, side curtain and knee airbags, ABS, electronic brakeforce distribution (EBD), vehicle stability assist (VSA), and traction control.

An all-new model of the BMW X3 came out for the 2018 model. The X3 20i feature a turbocharged 2.0-liter 4-cylinder engine, and the X3 xDrive30i comes with the turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-6 motor. All are available with a standard 8-speed sport automatic. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, leather seats, automatic A/C and FM radio and entertainment system with USB/iPod/Bluetooth support. Optional features include a new generation of BMW Navigation System, full-color BMW Head-Up Display, Driving Assistant Plus which warns the driver of a potential collision with a pedestrian and BMW Active Cruise Control with Stop & Go. Safety features are always good with BMW and standard equipment include driver and passenger airbags, ABS and dynamic stability control (DSC).

The Volvo S60 Polestar, available only in certain GCC markets. It comes with a 3.0-litre turbocharged 6-cylinder engine and all-wheel-drive. It comes with a 6-speed automatic transmission. The cabin features extensive soft-touch materials and Volvo's trademark 'floating' console. Features include leather upholstery, power windows, electric mirrors, alloy wheels, CD/MP3 stereo, front and side-curtain airbags, keyless entry with starter motor, navigation, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitor, adaptive HID headlights, sunroof and more. Volvo's unique 'City Safety' feature is standard, whereby the system brakes by itself to avoid hitting cars and pedestrians.

The Maserati Coupe, sometimes known as the 4200 GT, is a high-performance two-door four-seater that relaunched Ferrari-owned Maserati as a contender in the sport-luxury class. It complements the two-seater Spyder, which is a shorter-wheelbase convertible version of the Coupe. While these cars are based on the original 3200 GT which debuted in 1998, they have been receiving updates regularly. The latest variations were the GranSport Coupe and the GranSport Spyder, which feature sport-tuned suspension, aerodynamic and performance upgrades, and racier trimmings. All versions are powered by a Ferrari-tuned 4.2-litre V8, with a choice of a six-speed manual or a six-speed Cambiocorsa paddle-shifted automanual. The Gransport versions, which debuted in 2005, have slightly more power. All cars got a full suite of luxury features, such as power windows, premium CD stereo, electric mirrors, power-adjustable leather seats and more. Additional features 18-inch alloy wheels, multiple airbags, ABS brakes and stability control.

The VW Multivan is the range-topping minivan based on the T5 Transporter work-van platform. The outdated front-wheel-drive van is powered by an equally-outdated 3.2-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic. Available with 6 or 7 seats, it has a unique rail feature in which seats can slide forward and backward into any configuration. Offered in base Comfortline and upgraded Highline trim, the Multivan can be had with features such as power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, and a CD stereo. It can be optionally outfitted with cloth or leather seats, HID headlights, wood cabin trim, rear DVD entertainment system, sunroof, alloy wheels and automatic doors. A wide range of accessories are available, like tables and refrigerators which fit onto the rails, all movable. The Multivan has safety features as standard such as front and side-curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.

Hyundai has upped its game considerably, and sister-company Kia benefits too. The new-for-2011 Kia Optima is based on the latest Sonata and therefore a larger car than its predecessor. Styled like a European sedan, the midsize Optima will receive two economy-biased engines in the GCC, mainly a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder, with some countries receiving a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder. Both are available with 6-speed manual and 6-speed automatic transmissions, though some countries will only get a standard automatic with paddle-shifters. The base model comes with power steering, power windows, manual a/c with rear cooling ducts, automatic headlights, paddle shifters, power mirrors with indicators, fog lamps, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, cruise control, CD/MP3 stereo with 6 speakers, USB and AUX ports with iPod cable, steering wheel buttons, 16-inch steel wheels and a single airbag. The mid-range model gains a panoramic glass roof, with automatic rolling cloth roof-shades, as well as 17-inch alloy wheels and ABS. The fully-optioned model is loaded with intelligent keyless entry with start button, power-folding mirrors, HID headlights, chrome door handles, automatic a/c, rear parking sensors, overhead 'map' lights up front, excellent leather upholstery, driver's power-adjusted seat, trip computer, slightly-tinted glass, 6-CD changer, ventilated seats, 18-inch alloys, navigation, Bluetooth, six airbags, and stability control with hill-start assist and brake assist. Kia is offering proper safety features only in the top model.

The Ford Fusion is back in a new skin for 2014. Still powered by a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, the front-wheel-drive midsize sedan only comes with a 6-speed automatic. An Ecoboost engine option may become available later. Available in two trim levels, the Fusion S comes with independent front and rear suspension, torque-vectoring control, electric parking brake, trip computer, steering wheel with cruise and audio buttons, power windows with one-touch open/close, capless fuel filler, auto halogen headlights, LED tail lamps, speed-sensitive wipers, 4-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with AUX/USB ports, SYNC with MyFord multimedia system with 4.3-inch screen, Bluetooth, 16-inch steel wheels and blind-spot mirrors. The Fusion SE adds power-adjustable driver's seats, rear armrest, 6-speaker stereo, outside temperature display and compass, rear a/c vents, mirror-mounted indicators, additional body-colour trim, keypad lock and 17-inch alloys. Options include 18-inch alloys, parking sensors, sunroof, fog lamps, rear spoiler, premium floor mats, auto a/c, rear camera, 8-inch touchscreen with additional 4.2-inch gauge-cluster LCD displays, front memory power seats, rain-sensing wipers, leather upholstery and navigation. Standard safety features include front and side/curtain airbags, knee airbags, ABS with EBD, stability control, tyre pressure monitor, hill-start assist, and alarm. Optional safety features include auto high beams, blind-spot monitors, cross-traffic alert and lane-keeping assist.

The Getz, new in 2003 and facelifted in 2006, is known for offering "European" levels of refinement. We feel it is let down only by its weak range of engines, namely a tiny 1.1-litre, followed by a 1.4-litre and a 1.6-litre, all four-cylinder units, some with a manual gearbox and others with an automatic. This front-wheel-drive hatchback comes standard with very little, but includes air-conditioning, a rear wiper with washer, a radio and cassette player with 4 speakers, and wind-up windows. Options in the higher trim levels include power steering, ABS brakes, a single airbag, power windows, central door locks, electric mirrors, sunroof, rear spoiler, fog lamps, keyless entry system, a radio and cassette player and fake carbon-fibre trim. The interior is well-made, with good materials. It is not too cramped inside either, with seating for five and decent legroom both front and back. All trim levels come with a cloth cabin and a useful rear luggage area with a lift-up tailgate. Small 14-inch steel wheels with plastic hubcaps.

The Subaru XV debuted in its current form in 2013. Known also as Crosstrek elsewhere, it is a based on the Impreza platform, but with hatchback styling, raised suspension, and roof rails. While appearing tough, this compact crossover is powered by a small 2.0-litre 4-cylinder mated to a CVT automatic and all-wheel-drive. The standard XV 2.0i comes with the usual power options, cloth upholstery, auto a/c, CD/MP3 stereo with USB and AUX ports, Bluetooth, 17-inch alloys, cruise control and halogen headlights. The 2.0i-S Premium adds smart keyless entry and start, rear camera, aluminium pedals, dual-zone auto a/c, HID headlights with washers, power-folding mirrors with LED indicators, and a sunroof. Front and side-curtain airbags, ABS with EBD, and stability control are standard on all models.

An all-new Honda Pilot was released as a 2016 model. It got a facelift for the 2019 model year. Under the hood, it gets a 3.5-liter Direct Injected V6 engine with Variable Cylinder Management (VCM), mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. The base EX model can be had in 2WD or AWD form, while the EX-L and Touring trims only come with AWD and no low-range gearing. The Pilot includes a traction management system and is featured on all models except the EX 2WD, with pushbutton mode selection and TFT mode display on the cockpit instrument panel. In addition, EX (AWD) & EXL grades offer 200 mm of ground clearance for better off-road ability. There is also a sand-mode feature. Features include halogen projector headlights in EX and EXL grades whereas LED projector headlights in Touring grade, which also gets a panoramic glass roof. Some of the other features standard in all grades includes front fog lights, LED taillights and LED daytime running lights along with Tailgate Spoiler, power door mirrors and LED turn light indicators. For the interior, an 8-inch touchscreen, standard in all grades, gives you access to audio system controls and other display features. The Touring grade includes second row captain's chairs, which provides easy walk through between the second and third row for a 7 passenger configuration. Other amenities include tri-zone automatic climate control, rear air conditioning duct in the second and third row seats, rear door sunshade, sun glass holder and conversation mirror, cargo area hidden storage for extra luggage, active noise control (ANC) for a quieter cabin, with a rear entertainment system with a 9-inch display screen available in the Touring grade. Safety features include Vehicle Stability Assist (VSA) with Traction Control Systems (TCS), Anti-Lock Brake Systems (ABS), Electronic Brake Distributor (EBD), Hill Start Assist (HSA), Agile Handle Assist (AHA) and Tyre Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS).

The Toyota Corolla is all-new for 2014, with completely-redone styling and an extended wheelbase for more cabin space. Engine offerings include a 1.6-litre and a new 2.0-litre, both 4-cylinder "VVT-i" units mated to 4-speed automatics, although a base model with a 6-speed manual is available in some GCC markets. The front-wheel-drive platform still rides on independent front and torsion-beam rear suspension. The five-seater is available in various trim levels. In Saudi Arabia, there is a 1.6 XLi model with a manual or automatic gearbox, 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, black front grille, power windows and mirrors, keyless entry and a 4-speaker CD/MP3/USB/AUX stereo. Moving up to the 1.6 GLi adds fog lamps, 16-inch alloys, rear parking sensors, chrome grille, trunk liner, better upholstery with leather steering wheel, split-folding rear seats, 6-speaker touchscreen stereo with Bluetooth, smart keyless entry with starter button and several other smaller convenience features. The 2.0 GLi adds LED headlights with LED running lamps, sunroof, rear manual curtains, auto a/c and cruise control. In the UAE, there are 5 trim levels, starting with an uber-basic 1.6 S model that includes a standard automatic gearbox, 15-inch steelies, 4-speaker CD/MP3/USB/AUX stereo, power mirrors and a black grille. The next-level 1.6 SE version adds power windows, keyless entry and body-colour door handles. The 1.6 SE+ adds better upholstery with leather steering wheel, chrome grille, split-folding rear seats, LED running lamps, smart keyless entry and start, LCD info display, a better 6-speaker stereo and a few other extra bits. Moving on to the larger engine, the 2.0 SE has all the features of the 1.6 SE, but additionally gets 15-inch alloys and 6 speakers for the basic stereo. The 2.0 SE+ model gets all the features of the 1.6 SE+ model. And the 2.0 Limited gets a sunroof, auto-levelling projector headlights and cruise control. Other markets may get slightly different trim levels. All models get standard dual front airbags, ABS with brake assist and EBD, and an alarm immobiliser.

The Carnival, also known as Grand Carnival or Sedona in some markets, is undoubtedly Kia's largest non-commercial vehicle, being a full-size minivan. With three rows of seats, there is no shortage of space. Powered by a 3.8-litre V6, it comes with limited standard features, which include 16-inch alloy wheels, AM/FM radio with CD, front and rear a/c with tri-zone control, battery saver, electric mirrors, central door locks, ABS brakes, power windows with driver-side auto down, variable intermittent wipers, hidden radio antenna, power sunroof and an automatic gearbox. Higher trim levels get additional features such as an AM/FM radio with cassette player, CD and MP3, automatic light control system, audio remote controls on the steering wheel, reverse warning system, electric folding mirrors, cruise control, keyless entry system, roof rack, front fog lamps, power sliding doors and tailgate, 8-way power driver's seat and finally, dual front airbags. Safety features are surprisingly limited to only ABS brakes, the optional airbags and an energy-absorbing steering column.

The Lexus LX 570, which was all-new for 2008, received a minor facelift for 2012. Heavily based on the Toyota Land Cruiser, new model gets a new front-end, bi-xenon headlights, new 18-inch or 20-inch wheels, new tail-lamp clusters and a couple of features such as "overturn" assist and new interior colours. The Lexus is powered by a 5.7-litre V8 mated with a 6-speed automatic transmission. In 2014, a limited-to-200 LX 570 Supercharged was offered exclusively for the Middle East market, with a 5.7-litre supercharged V8. The full-time all-wheel drive features a new 2-speed transfer case, Torsen centre differential and a crawl-control feature when in low range. The "overturn" assist feature can lock one inside rear tyre to help make slow turns tighter in offroad conditions. The LX has a vehicle "posture control" system with four-wheel active height control and adaptive variable suspension that reacts more quickly and allows for a greater range of adjustment than the system it replaces. Active safety features include stability control, ABS brakes and traction control, as well as multiple airbags. The leather interior can be had in tan, beige or black. The plush interior is covered in leather and wood, with seating for at least seven, and features such as ventilated front seats, power-folding third-row seating, sunroof, navigation, Mark Levinson CD/DVD stereo, front-rear-side-view cameras and all the usual power accessories. A "Sport" kit with a unique front bumper was introduced for 2013 in the top models. The touchscreen computer gets a new interface for 2012.

In 2014, the BMW 4 Series Convertible replaced the 3-series convertible model. It is offered as two variants in the GCC. The 428i features a turbocharged 2.0-liter 4-cylinder engine and the 435i comes with the turbocharged 3.0-litre inline-6 motor. Both are available with a standard 8-speed sport automatic or a six-speed manual transmission. Only real-wheel drive versions will be offered here. The new BMW 4 Series Coupe is visibly larger in width and wheelbase than the outgoing BMW 3 Series Coupe. The BMW 4 Series Coupe gets "Air Breathers", which are positioned rearwards of the front wheel arches to reduce drag. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, leather seats, automatic A/C and FM radio and entertainment system with USB/iPod/Bluetooth support. Optional features include a new generation of BMW Navigation System, full-color BMW Head-Up Display, Driving Assistant Plus which warns the driver of a potential collision with a pedestrian and BMW Active Cruise Control with Stop & Go. Safety features are always good with BMW and standard equipment include driver and passenger airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Audi A8 is the German manufacturer's flagship full-size luxury sedan. Of course, that means the list of options will be long for this car. It got a minor facelift, as well as engine updates in 2014. Only the long-wheel base makes its way to the UAE. There are three engine variants - the 3.0-litre supercharged V6, 4.0-litre turbocharged V8 and the 6.3-litre W12. They are all equipped with all-wheel drive systems. Some basic options include four-zone automatic air-conditioning, Bluetooth, xenon-head lamps, start-stop engine system, parking-aid, rear-view camera, adaptive air-suspension, leather seats, navigation and sunroof. Customers can add different equipment packages which can add rear-entertainment systems, individual rear power seats, seat ventilation and massage function for both front and rear, alcantara trim, 20-inch alloy wheels, panoramic sunroof and electronically opening and closing bootlid. However, adding options to the A8 L creeps up the price further.

For 2016, the 300 SRT got a minor facelift. It got some new safety features, updated entertainment system and a new automatic transmission. Under the hood is a 6.4-litre V8 mated to a 8-speed automatic. Standard SRT8 features include leather upholstery, UConnect multimedia system with touchscreen, 20-inch wheels, rear spoiler and more, along with a unique exterior kit. Standard safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor, adaptive cruise control with auto braking, lane departure warning and forward collision warning.

The Sportage is another of Kia's long-running nameplates, though the crossover itself has changed over time. Whereas the original Sportage was unreliable but could do basic off-roading, the new one is much more dependable but is allergic to sand dunes. It is even offered in a front-wheel-drive model alongside the four-wheel-drive, to dilute the nameplate further. Powered by either a 2.0-litre four-cylinder with a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic, or a 2.7-litre V6 with a four-speed automatic, it is interesting to note that Kia and parent Hyundai are the first ones to officially offer a V6-powered small 4WD in the region. Standard features include manual air-conditioning, height-adjustable driver seat, power windows, front and rear power outlets, immobiliser, 60/40 split-folding rear seat, front and rear cup holders, 16-inch alloy wheels, radio cassette stereo with 4 speakers and a roof antenna. We could not verify what safety features are available on the Sportage, though ABS brakes and front airbags might possibly be options.

The Mercedes-Benz A35 AMG 4Matic joined the lineup for the first time in 2019. It is a new performance variant, sitting below the A45 AMG. It uses the same 2.0-litre turbocharged engine as the standard version, but tuned to produce more horsepower. Power is delivered via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The 5-seater hatchback's features include 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

An all-new Hyundai Tucson debuted in 2016 and received a facelift in 2019. It got upgrades inside and out, including a new cascading grille, new center stack design, more advanced safety features and available Qi wireless charging. Standard features on the 2020 Hyundai Tucson include standard projector headlights, LED tail lamps, shark-fin antenna and wheels upto 19-inch in size. The 2020 Hyundai Tucson is powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive, and a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder with all-wheel-drive. Both engines are mated to a 6-speed automatic. The base 2.0-litre FWD model comes with power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth seats, fog lamps, USB port, Bluetooth, manual a/c, rear spoiler, roof rails, ABS and more. Things get better in the higher trim levels, with the top 2.4-litre 4WD model additionally outfitted with dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, cruise control, smart key with starter button, leather upholstery, power driver-side seat, front and rear sensors and camera, chrome door handles, electric folding mirrors, and improved safety features such as ABS with stability control, active headrests and two front airbags and side airbags. Other optional safety features on the 2020 Hyundai Tucson include Smart Parking Assist, Autonomous Emergency Braking, Lane Keeping Assist System, Rear Traffic Cross Alert, Blind Spot Detection, Speed Limit Information Function and Active Bonnet System which will automatically raise the hood to cushion the impact shock in case of a frontal collision.

The Nissan Patrol Pickup is the commercial version of the more popular Nissan Patrol Safari model. It gets the 4.8-litre inline-6 cylinder engine, mated to a 5-speed manual transmission.  It comes with a Straight-line drive transfer which allows on-the-fly shifting from 2WD to 4WD with one touch of a lever. The Patrol Pickup has a baisc interior featuring cloth upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo, manual a/c, and16-inch steel wheels. Front airbags, EBD, VDC and ABS are standard.

An all-new Jeep Wrangler Unlimited came out in 2018. It is slightly bigger, faster and lighter than the previous generation. The engine has been carried over from the older model, the 3.6-litre V6 “Pentastar” motor. Acceleration and fuel economy numbers have been improved, thanks to the new 8-speed automatic transmission replacing the ancient 5-speed. Manual gear lovers will be left disappointed though, as it is not offered anymore in this region. The electronically assisted steering has replaced the hydraulic steering. The interior has more quality materials than the older model, with the Sahara and Rubicon models getting more of the leather treatment. Even the standard equipment has improved, with the Wrangler Unlimited Sport getting a touchscreen for the infotainment system. Safety features include four airbags, ABS, stability control, and brake assist. Optional safety features include blind spot monitor, and rear cross path detection.

The Mitsubishi Attrage is the Japanese brand's sub-compact sedan offering, introduced in 2014 GCC market. The Thai-built Attrage gets a 1.2-litre 3-cylinder engine, mated to either a 5-speed manual in fleet-spec trim or a CVT in all other versions. The small engine, combined with the lightweight body makes it very fuel-efficient. Standard features include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, keyless entry with central locking, fabric seats, manual a/c, AM/FM radio with CD player and 4 speakers, tachometer and 14-inch steel wheels. Optional equipment include a full-auto a/c, better entertainment system, leather-strapped steering wheel and gear knob, 15-inch alloy wheels and USB port. For safety, only the top model gets 2 airbags for the driver and passenger, whereas as the rest get only one for the driver. All models get ABS with EBD.

As evolutionary developments of the America's most popular minivan, the latest model features a more square design, optional power operation of the sliding side doors, dual front airbags, a power rear liftgate and revised interiors that are quieter, nicer and more comfortable. The new Grand Voyager comes with a 3.8-litre V6 with a 6-speed automatic. It also features Stow 'n' Go rear seats, giving the ability to easily fold the second and third-row seats into the floor in as little as 30 seconds with a simple one-hand operation. More options include a rear-seat audio system, traction control, parking sensors, side-curtain airbags, a tyre-pressure warning system, electronically adjustable pedals and a rear-seat DVD entertainment. Chrysler minivans, in various shapes and names, are best sellers in the United States, but failed to make any headway in this region because minivans are not popular here.

Completely revamped for the 2012 model year, the Ford Focus now becomes the best compact car available in the GCC, if a tad higher-priced than some competitors. That's because it offers optional tech features that no other player has. Available in sedan, station-wagon and hatchback forms, the latter 5-door is being pitched as a high-end model. There is a base 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a 6-speed dual-clutch automanual, available in the "Ambiente" and "Trend" trim levels. In fact, the sedan and the wagon will only be available in the basic "Ambiente" trim level alongside the hatchback. The hatchback can be had in all trim levels, including "Trend", "Sport" and "Titanium" editions. Only the "Sport" and the "Titanium" get the 2.0-litre direct-injected 4-cylinder "GDI" engine, mated to a 6-speed dual-clutch automanual. While all models in the UAE get the manually-shiftable automatic, some other GCC markets may get a 5-speed manual option as well. Standard features include four-wheel-independent suspension, power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth upholstery, CD stereo with USB/AUX port, capless fuel filler, 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, and a manual a/c. Other features, available on higher models, include 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, keyless start, leather upholstery, dual-zone auto a/c, rain-sensing wipers, auto headlights, "sports" front seats, cruise control with speed limiter, sunroof, Bluetooth, "premium" centre-console storage, fog lights, LED tail lamps, footwell courtesy lights, and an optional park-assist system with parking sensors and the ability to control the steering automatically during parallel-parking. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, as well as ABS, stability control with hill-start assist, and a torque-vectoring system for better handling.

The first product from the takeover of Chrysler by Daimler-Benz was the Crossfire, a stylish sports coupe that rides on the old Mercedes-Benz SLK platform, while sharing many of its components with other Mercedes models, and built in Germany too. The Crossfire has a long hood with streaks on it, while the fastback roofline ends with a "boat tail." The car also has a centre spine that runs the length of the car, from the grille in front to between the dual, centre-mounted rear exhausts. The Crossfire's stance is enhanced by rear tyres that are larger than those in front, and by its broad shoulders, tall body sides and minimal glass area. The car's central spine reappears as an element in the car's interior design. The car's two bucket seats are trimmed in two-tone leather. Gauges have white-on-black faces with metallic bezels and chrome trim rings, while the centre console has a metallic look too. Other features for the two-seat coupe include a speed-activated rear spoiler and six-speaker audio system with dual subwoofers. By now, it would seem like the Crossfire is more of a design exercise than an attempt to build a true sports car. This is confirmed by the old 3.2-litre V6 that doesn't pull the car with enough verve.

The new-for-2011 Mitsubishi ASX is a 5-seater sub-compact crossover based on the Outlander platform and actually shares the exact same wheelbase, but is shorter at the front and especially the rear. The standard engine is a 2.0-litre DOHC 4-cylinder with MIVEC variable valve timing, CVT transmission and either front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. The all-wheel-drive has 2WD, 4WD and 4WD Lock modes. The base model comes with 16-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, cloth seats, soft-touch dash and front door surfaces, CD/MP3 player with AUX and USB ports, ABS-assisted disc brakes, four-wheel independent suspension, up to seven airbags including a knee bag, and an optional panoramic glass roof with mood lighting along the sides. The top model gets 17-inch alloys, a front lip spoiler, intelligent entry with starter button, HID headlights, leather upholstery and a 7-speaker stereo with subwoofer, among other items. Available safety features include the aforementioned airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, hill start assist and emergency braking blinkers.

The range-topping M6 arrived for 2006, in coupe and convertible form, using the same V10 engine as the M5. Unlike that of the new 5-Series and 7-Series models, the styling of the new 6 Series has generally received a warm welcome from the public, for unknown reasons. The new 6-Series was designed to look like a shark, and really does remind you of one, but it is far from good-looking. The controversial "Bangle-butt" rear styling works somewhat better on the shapely 6-Series than on other BMW models though. The 6-Series has become the vehicle of choice for rich town-cruising yuppies, but it is actually an excellent performance car, available with a 7-speed SMG automanual in the M6. A mild facelift came for the 2008 model, adding minor gadgetry updates.

The Jaguar XFR-S is the top performance model in the XF lineup. It gets a supercharged 5.0-litre V8 and is mated to a 8-speed automatic with manual-shift capability. The most interesting feature of the car is its simplistic interior which consists of toys such as a rotary-dial gear selector and hideway a/c vents. It features include power seats with memory, a split-folding rear seat, automatic dual-zone climate control, trip computer, sunroof and adaptive cruise control. Safety features include stability and traction control, ABS brakes and numerous airbags. Other available features include satellite navigation, in-dash 7-inch screen, power-adjustable foot pedals, self-leveling xenon headlights, rain-sensing wipers, front and rear parking sensors, leather upholstery, keyless entry and start, and other options. The audio unit comes with 30GB of storage and a standard 400-watt system, an optional 600-watt system, or a 1200-watt system which features 17-speakers with subwoofer from Bowers & Wilkins. The XFR-S gets unique bumpers, skirts, wheels and interior upholstery, as well as sports suspension and drivetrain components.

The ZNA Yumsun is a 7-seater minivan that turns out to be the unlikely flagship, with its 2.5-litre Nissan 4-cylinder engine. The single trim level includes soft-touch cabin trim, 4-speed automatic, 15-inch alloy wheels, front-disc rear-drum brakes with ABS, power steering, fake wood and leather trim, CD/MP3 stereo with steering controls and 6-CD changer, remote locking, power windows and mirrors, table on the backrest of front seats, 3.9-inch LCD screen with rear audio controls and 6 speakers, automatic antenna, rear parking sensors, auto front and rear a/c, and two airbags.

The Nissan Altima has been completely redesigned for the 2008 model year, with slightly more sporty handling and a little more extrovert styling than the competition. The Altima sits at the top of the class in terms of power. Available in the GCC with only a 3.5-litre V6, both with a choice of six-speed manual or CVT automatic transmissions, the Altima Coupe is a true 5-seater. The Altima offers standard features such as power windows, keyless entry and start, tilt and telescoping steering wheel, power steering, and an in-glass antenna for the nine-speaker Bose CD/MP3 stereo with iPod connectivity. Also available are power mirrors, optional electric seats, sunroof, cruise control, leather, 17-inch alloy wheels and HID headlights. ABS brakes with Electronic Brake-force Distribution and Brake Assist are standard, as are front airbags. Side and curtain airbags are also available.
