Even the standard equipment has improved, with the Wrangler Unlimited Sport getting a touchscreen for the infotainment system. Safety features include four airbags, ABS, stability control, and brake assist. Optional safety features include blind spot monitor, and rear cross path detection.

The Genesis G90 is the the first model to be released after its parent company Hyundai decided to make Genesis a separate luxury brand. The G90 is their flagship sedan and it comes in the GCC with three engine options. In 2021, it got a major facelift incorporating their new design language. The base engine is the 3.8-litre V6 which was found in the Centennial, while the other two new additions are the turbocharged 3.3-litre V6 motor and the 5.0-litre V8. Standard options in the G90 include power steering, power windows, electric folding mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push engine start-stop, leather upholstery, memory and ventilated seats, audio system with AUX/USB support, auto A/C, navigation, auto defog system, rain sensors, sunroof, parking assist system, rear electric curtain, xenon headlamps, LED headlights and taillights with LED daytime running lamps, front and rear camera, air suspension and 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include 9 airbags, lane keep assist, adaptive cruise control, ABS, traction control, stability control, brake assist, blind spot detection and autonomous emergency braking (AEB).

New from the ground up for 2006 and much more better-looking, the M-Class, which actually uses the ML moniker, is a better on-road and off-road 4WD now. It received a few visual changes in 2008. The ML 63 AMG is the top performance variant and it uses a 6.2-litre V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic. Features include AMG alloy wheels, leather upholstery, tyre pressure loss warning system, crash sensors, front and side airbags, CD radio with pre-installation for mobile phone and more.

The new Skoda Yeti is a sub-compact crossover SUV, and it comes standard with a 1.8-litre turbo 4-cylinder engine coupled to a 6-speed DSG automatic gearbox and an all-wheel-drive system that adapts for driving on rough terrain. Available in Comfort and Adventure trim levels, features are largely similar between the two. On the Comfort, these include 17-inch alloy wheels, fabric seating, black roof rails, auto a/c, cruise control, electric mirrors, folding table on rear-seat centre armrest and on the rear of front seats, cooled storage compartment, rear parking sensors, CD/MP3 stereo, Bluetooth and turning fog lamps. The Adventure gets different 17-inch wheels, silver roof rails, 6-CD changer with SD card reader, and a panoramic glass roof. Safety features include standard front airbags, side-curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, hill-descent assist, and a whole host of electronics.

The Chevrolet Tahoe got a new 6-speed transmission from 2009 onward. A beefy  Vortec 5.3-litre V8 powers the Tahoe. The V8 powers the rear wheels on the road, or through all four wheels when the standard 4WD system is engaged. Features include the usual power features and three rows of seats. Power-adjustable brake and accelerator pedals are standard on the higher models and optional on the base versions. New features also include power folding rear seats, among other things. On the road, the Tahoe is smooth and stable in a straight line, hopeless in the corners and strong off the road. The Suburban is the long-wheelbase version of the Tahoe, and offers more room in the back. Rear passengers can enjoy an optional package that includes a DVD system with flip-down seven-inch colour monitor, six-disc in-dash audio player and Bose speakers. New versions added later include the Tahoe Z71 off-road package with lifted suspension.

The Cadillac XT5 debuted in 2017 as an all-new model and is considered a luxury midsize crossover. Under the hood, it gets a 3.6-litre V6 engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The V6 engine features cylinder deactivation and engine stop/start when idle to improve fuel economy. A 2.0-litre turbocharged engine debuted in the 2020 model year. The all-wheel-drive is powered by a "twin-clutch" system which is capable of sending 100-percent torque to the front or rear axle. Standard features include power windows, power mirrors, LED headlights and tail lamps and fog lamps. Optional equipment include Cadillac's CUE entertainment system with BOSE speakers, magnetic ride control, alloy wheels and adaptive forward lighting. Safety features include ABS and traction control, sensors to warn driver of potential dangers, safety seat alert which sends immediate impulse through the seat cushion from the direction of the potential hazard.

An all new Mercedes-Benz SL Class was released for 2012. The new design features a complete new aluminium body, so it is lighter than its predecessor. Also the new generation SL Class is wider and longer. In 2017, it got a facelift and a new base engine. Engine choices include the SL 400 with a 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 and SL 500 with a 4.7-litre V8. Both are mated to a 9-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include front airbags and head-thorax sidebags, ABS brakes, automatic climate control with dust filter and air recirculation, automatic steering wheel with adjustment on entry and exit, brake assist, central locking, cruise control with variable speed limiter, stability control, xenon headlights, leather upholstery, light-alloy wheels, CD radio with 8 speakers and more.

Quietly put on the showroom floor by local Hyundai dealers, the unknown i30 is a new-for-2008 hatchback alternative to the Elantra. Powered by a 1.6-litre or a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, the i30 is being positioned as a cheaper alternative to better-equipped compact Japanese and European rivals. It is available with only a 4-speed automatic gearbox. The i30 benefits from a spacious-enough interior and the flexibility of a hatchback cargo area, especially with the folding rear seatback. Standard features are limited, with height-adjustable front seats, 60/40 split rear seats, cloth or partial leatherette seats, power windows, electric mirrors, body-coloured exterior trim and LED cabin lighting. Other available features include keyless entry, CD/MP3 stereo with USB support, fog lights, sunroof and 16-inch alloy wheels. The i30 was originally designed to compete in the European market, so it benefits from tighter suspension tuning and better cabin materials. Sadly, GCC-spec cars are underequipped, especially in terms safety, as there is only one standard airbag and no ABS brakes.

The Espace is famous for being the first minivan to grace European roads back in the 1980s. Packed with abundant space and numerous safety features, it has the maximum rating in crash tests conducted by European governmental agencies. It comes in short-wheelbase and long-wheelbase body styles, all seating as many as seven passengers, with luggage space to spare. With the new slide and lock seating system, the latest Espace can offer even greater versatility. At the rear, passengers can adjust the position of their seat for better legroom. Whether the cargo is a large number of passengers or a large load, switching between 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 or even 2 seat configurations is a simple affair. Standard features include a stereo, power windows and more. It is equipped with ABS brakes and Emergency Brake Assist, plus an Electronic Stability Programme with understeer control, as well as ASR traction control. Passive safety features eight airbags, including thorax airbags in the second row of seats.

The Cadillac XT5 is an all-new model and is considered a luxury midsize crossover. Under the hood, it gets a 3.6-litre V6 engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The V6 engine features cylinder deactivation and engine stop/start when idle to improve fuel economy. A 2.0-litre turbocharged engine could debut later. The all-wheel-drive is powered by a "twin-clutch" system which is capable of sending 100-percent torque to the front or rear axle. Standard features include power windows, power mirrors, LED headlights and tail lamps and fog lamps. Optional equipment include Cadillac's CUE entertainment system with BOSE speakers, magnetic ride control, alloy wheels and adaptive forward lighting. Safety features include ABS and traction control, sensors to warn driver of potential dangers, safety seat alert which sends immediate impulse through the seat cushion from the direction of the potential hazard.

The Bentley Continental GTC received a facelift for the 2016 model. Two engines are available, one a turbocharged 4.0-litre V8 model and the other a turbochrged 6.0-litre W12 engine. They both come with an 8-speed automatic transmission. The Bentley does not skimp on luxury, with a handcrafted wood and leather interior, complete with all the requisite gadgets such as navigation and a killer stereo. Instrumentation is provided by classic dials that live in deep recesses ahead of the steering wheel, while a small screen directly in the driver's line of sight monitors all relevant in-car systems. The two-door Continental GT convertible is equipped with the full suite of passive safety equipment, including two front airbags, four side airbags and two side curtain bags. And the GTC Speed, with the same W12 engine, adds more power, reduced weight and an aluminium cabin trim package, while improving performance and handling.

The ninth generation Chevrolet Malibu made its debut in the GCC as a 2017 model year. It got a slight facelift in 2019, along with a new base engine and improved tech. Under the hood the base model now gets a turbocharged 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed transmission. The other engine on offer is a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine. That one gets an 6-speed auto transmission. Standard features on the 2022 Chevrolet Malibu LS model include power steering, electric windows, central locking, halogen headlamps, LED daytime running lamps, single zone A/C, 6-speaker audio system, 7-inch touch screen with Bluetooth, phone projection and navigation, keyless entry, engine push start, fabric seats, cruise control and 16-inch steel wheels. The Malibu LT gets additional remote vehicle starter and 17-inch alloy wheels. The sunroof, 8-inch touch screen, and power seats are optional on the LT. On the Malibu Premier, additional features include dual exhausts, HID headlamps, LED tail lamps, auto headlight leveling function, dual-zone A/C, 9-speaker Bose audio system, 8-inch touch screen with navigation, USB charge port, leather seats, power seats and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional features on the Premier include sunroof, rearview camera and adaptive cruise control. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS), and traction control. The Premier gets side airbags as well. Other optional safety equipment include lane-keeping assist, blind spot monitor, forward collision alert and rear cross traffic alert.

The Renault Duster, a rebadged Dacia, has been designed to suit all types of roads across the world's less-developed countries. This new sub-compact SUV is based on a stretched Nissan Tiida platform, and comes with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, available in either a two-wheel-drive 4-speed automatic form or in an all-wheel-drive 6-speed manual form, the latter capable of locking the diff for a 50:50 front/rear torque split. Interestingly, the 2WD model comes with a torsion-beam rear suspension, while the 4WD model gives up some boot space to make way for an independent rear suspension. The rear seats fold down as standard, and split-folding on all but the base model, while you can transport longer items if the front passenger seat is folded down as well. The basic PE version comes with two-wheel-drive, 4-speed automatic, cloth upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo with USB port and Bluetooth with buttons behind steering wheel, unpainted bumpers, 16-inch steel wheels, front power windows, keyless entry, folding rear bench seat, power steering and manual a/c. Early models came with one airbag, but by mid-2012, all models had two standard airbags. The higher-spec SE can be had in 2WD automatic or special-order 4WD manual drivetrains, and adds standard fog lamps, trip computer, ABS with Emergency Brake Assist, extra front-passenger airbag, rear power windows, electric mirrors, 16-inch alloy wheels, painted bumpers, leatherette steering wheel and extra chrome trim. The SE version can be further upgraded with leather seats with additional pyrotechnic pre-tensioners on the front seatbelts as well as side airbags. The exterior package on the SE version also adds standard chrome door mirrors, longitudinal roof rails, front/rear skid plates and side-skirt covers. Extra tinted rear windows, rear quarter glass and rear windscreen round up the list, as is a split-folding rear seat, height adjustable driver's seat and height-adjustable steering wheel. A comprehensive range of accessories,including wind reflectors, side steps, wheel arch mouldings, chrome exhaust trim and mudflaps, is also available.

The Lumina is the only rear-wheel-drive sedan in the affordable midsize segment, which is about the only reason why we do not want to see this aging car fail. Well that, and the available V6 and V8 motors that no one can match in terms of price. Built in Australia alongside the Caprice, it has been receiving minor updates every year since a major facelift in 2003, with an updated front end and new gearbox for 2005. The Lumina comes in five variants, namely the LS, LTZ, S, SS, SS Coupe and the new Royale. The power for the LS, LTZ and body-kitted S comes from the Alloytec 3.6-litre V6 engine, while the 5.7-litre V8 does its work in the Royale, the SS sedan and the SS Coupe. The base LS and LTZ models fulfil the basic needs of a commuter car that doubles as a family vehicle, with decent space and adequate power, while the SS models merge muscle-car attitude with a traditional sedan.The Royale attempts to be a luxury sports sedan with a host of luxury styling cues. The V8-powered Coupe is great value for money, though it goes for more money than the equally fast sedan. The Australians already had a 6.0-litre V8 downunder while we here still played with the old 5.7-litre.

The all-new 6-Series  was introduced in 2003, filling the hole in the line-up left since the end of the 8-Series. The last actual 6-Series was around back in the 1980s. Based on the underpinnings of the 5-Series, the new 6-Series was introduced with a 4.4 L V8 engine for the 645Ci, which has since been replaced by the 650Ci with a 4.8-litre V8 in 2006. In 2004, a more affordable inline 6-cylinder engine was introduced in the 630i. This was soon followed by a convertible model. Unlike that of the new 5-Series and 7-Series models, the styling of the new 6 Series has generally received a warm welcome from the public, for unknown reasons. The new 6-Series was designed to look like a shark, and really does remind you of one, but it is far from good-looking. The controversial "Bangle-butt" rear styling works somewhat better on the shapely 6-Series than on other BMW models though. The 6-Series has become the vehicle of choice for rich town-cruising yuppies, but it is actually an excellent performance car, available with a six-speed manual or a six-speed automatic.

In 2015, the Audi A7 Sportback got a facelift. It remains the same for the 2018 model year. Almost 5 metres long with a low roofline, the Audi A7 Sportback is a full-sizer riding on 18-inch to 20-inch wheels, and as with all Audi sedans,  really rides a front-wheel-drive platform, with optional 'Quattro' all-wheel-drive tacked onto the higher trim levels. Three engines are on offer - 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder, 2.8-litre V6 and a 3.0-litre supercharged unit, all of which are mated to an 'S-tronic' 7-speed automatic transmission. Standard options include 4-zone automatic air-conditioning, reverse-camera, MMI touch-sensitive navigation system, 10-speaker audio system. Optional equipment include interior leather packages for the seats and door trim, sports suspension, air suspension, front and reverse camera, park assist, side assist, night-vision, lane-assist and BOSE surround sound.

The VW Polo recently received a fresh redesign and upgraded equipment. The Polo, though simply a sub-compact hatchback, has a more upmarket feel, thanks to judicious use of materials. High quality interiors are synonymous with Volkswagen, and the high quality plastics and fabrics found in the Polo is no exception. Standard equipment includes a CD stereo system, along with power windows and other electricals. Sadly, the only available powerplant in the Polo is the 1.4-litre four-cylinder unit. Available with a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic gearbox, this engine kills the upscale illusion. The new Polo includes standard safety systems such as ABS brakes, Hydraulic Brake Assist, and dual front airbags. Side airbags, a curtain airbag system and Electronic Stabilisation Programme are optional. The Polo also has high levels of torsional rigidity, leading to improved crash performance, impressive refinement and driving dynamics.

The BT-50 is the forgotten small pickup truck range of the Mazda line-up. No one in their right mind is going to buy one of these for personal use, but for those who want to be different, in a flamboyant American sort of way, they can pick up one of these and modify them for purposes other than hauling cargo. Engines for the B-Series include 2.2-litre and 2.6-litre petrol engines, all four-cylinder motors and all with a standard five-speed manual. Body styles include a single cab and a double cab shape. Key features include an AM/FM radio with cassette deck and 2 speakers, monotone or two-tone paintjob, and manually operated windows. Available accessories include plastic fender and side-step cladding panels, and front and rear skirt kits. Cargo-box equipment includes a single-action tailgate lock, a rear step bumper, outer and inner rope hooks, and load rests. Options, available in some markets, include front airbags, ABS brakes with electronic brake-force distribution, and even power windows.

The 360 is a mid-engined two-seater sports car, designed as a high-tech replacement for the simplistic F355, while itself being replaced by the F430 for 2005, effectively giving the 360 the short shelf-life. For this model, occasionally known as the F360, Ferrari partnered with Alcoa to produce an all-aluminium space-frame chassis. Also new was the Pininfarina styling that gave up flip-up headlights, replacing them with rounded fixed units. The new 3.6-litre V8 engine came with either a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed F1-style automanual. The cabin was sparse on gadgets, but the basics were standard, including leather, CD stereo, power windows, electric mirrors, front airbags, ABS brakes, and stability control. The coupe version was called the 360 Modena, while the new-for-2001 convertible was called the 360 Spider. The lightweight 360 Challenge Stradale came later, with  110 kg shaved off, a bump up in power from the upgraded V8, and featuring 19-inch BBS wheels, carbon-fibre side-mirrors, updated front bumper, lower ride height, and a black mesh grille at the rear.

The BAIC BJ40 is the Chinese brand's offroad-capable SUV. Sharing a lot of design cues from the Jeep Wrangler, the BJ40 Plus is a 5-door version. Under the hood is 2.3-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, radio with USB/AUX, remote key, CD player with touch screen, 6 speakers, leather seats, parking sensors, rearview camera, cruise control and auto headlights.They come with standard front two airbags, ABS brakes and electronic brake distribution (EBD).

The C-Class Coupe was introduced new in 2012. Featuring a wide range of engines that just confuses the average consumer, the C-Class can be optioned out as a bare commuter car or a beefy sports car. For the coupe is a 4-cylinder turbocharged 1.8-litre "BlueEfficiency" engine in the C 250. The 3.5-litre V6-powered C 350 round off the standard range, on which the C 63 AMG version is based. All models come with a 7-speed automatic. An auto start-stop feature allows for low fuel-consumption ratings. All cars come with a full set of safety features, including electronic nannies and multiple airbags, but many premium features, such as 16-inch to 18-inch wheels, navigation and even leather are optional on the base models. The "Sport" models offer stiffer suspension and quicker-shifting transmission. The optional AMG sports package offers stiffer suspension, 18-inch light-alloy wheels and cosmetic add-ons to most non-AMG models. Depending on dealer, prices might be much higher in some countries.

The Hyundai Accent is longer, wider and lower than the previous generation model. It features Hyundai's swoopy new corporate styling and superb build quality. The spacious sub-compact 4-door sedan comes with a choice of 1.4-litre and 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engines, both with 5-speed manual and 4-speed automatic geabox options. The basic front-wheel-drive Accent comes with 14-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, cloth upholstery, six cup-holders, power windows and mirrors, CD/MP3 stereo, keyless entry, power steering, four-wheel-disc brakes, and a single airbag. Features on higher models include 14-inch or 16-inch alloy wheels, leather steering wheel with stereo controls, fog lamps, centre-console storage cubby, rear parking sensors with camera, auto-dimming mirror, split-folding rear seat, Bluetooth and sunroof. Safety features, all optional, includes stability control, ABS and a full set of front and side airbags, though it depends on the local dealer if they want to offer these options.

The SL has undergone numerous design and interior improvements in its facelifted-for-2007 iteration. Models include the new 3.5-litre SL 350, the new 5.5-litre SL 500 and the twin-turbo 5.5-litre SL 600 rocketship. Upping the ante are two sport-tuned models, namely the upgraded supercharged 5.5-litre SL 55 AMG and the twin-turbo 6.0-litre SL 65 AMG. Second-generation Active Body Control and the more direct steering improve handling without compromising the comfort aspects of the SL. The redesigned front, new rear light units and new light-alloy wheels of the revised SL are hardly noticeable compared to the previous version. New interior appointments include new materials and colour schemes. Standard features include front airbags and head-thorax sidebags, ABS brakes, automatic climate control with dust filter and air recirculation, automatic steering wheel with adjustment on entry and exit, brake assist, central locking, cruise control with variable speed limiter, Electronic Stability Program, Xenon headlights, leather upholstery, light-alloy wheels, CD radio with 8 speakers and more.

The Murcielago, named after a famous matador, is the truest of the current Lamborghinis, with traditional scissor doors and a massive V12 engine sitting between the front and rear wheels. It was also the first Lamborghini to be developed under new parent Audi, and is available in a hard-top coupe and a soft-top Roadster trim. The upgraded LP640 model with a larger 6.5-litre V12,  with a unique body kit and more power, is the only version on sale now. Power is fed to the all-wheel-drive system through a standard six-speed manual or an optional E-gear sequential manual transmission on all versions. High-tech features include active spoilers and air intakes that adjust according to speed, while the suspension can be adjusted for ride height to clear bumpy roads. The Murcielago Roadster has a cut-down windscreen so overall height is 70 mm lower than the coupe. Standard features include dual front airbags, ABS with EBD, massive four-wheel disc brakes, power windows, air suspension and 18-inch alloy rims, while the Roadster has built-in rollover hoops.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class is essentially the new facelifted M-Class following the German brand's new nomenclature. From 2017 onwards, this midsize SUV came in three versions. The GLE 400 comes with a 3.0-litre turbo engine, the hybrid GLE 500e gets the 3.0-litre turbo V6 combined with an electric motor and the GLE 500 has the 4.7-litre V8. Both engines get a 7-speed automatic transmission. Available features include adjustable air suspension, adaptive cruise control and active parking assist. The exterior features HID headlights, LED running maps and a choice of 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels. The revamped 5-seater interior offers, depending on trim level, leather upholstery, wood trim, mood lighting, Harmon-Kardon Logic7 surround sound, HDD navigation, optional panoramic sunroof, rear entertainment system, optional keyless start, optional ventilated power front seats and a split-folding rear seat. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control, ABS and drowsiness monitor, with options such as a rear view camera with parking sensors, active lane assist, blind-spot monitor and automatic pre-crash braking. An AMG package is optional, and it adds a body kit and sportier suspension.

The Sorento is an attractive entry into the crowded affordable 4WD market. Offering either a 2.4-litre four-cylinder with a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic, or a new 3.3-litre V6 with a five-speed automatic, the facelifted-for-2007 Sorento offers decent off-road ability and a fair bit of interior space, making it a good buy, given its price. Standard features include 16-inch alloy wheels, radio cassette with antenna and 6 speakers, manual air-conditioning, power steering, 8-way adjustable driver seat, 4-way adjustable passenger seat, power windows, 60/40 split folding rear seat, battery saver, driver airbag, proper rear lift gate, power door locks, and limited slip differential. Available features in higher models include a CD player with power antenna and 8 speakers, ABS brakes, power folding mirrors and cruise control. Four-wheel independent suspension and four-wheel disc brakes make it a good road cruiser, unlike truck-based 4WDs, although it is still no sports car.

Mercedes-Benz GLC replaced the GLK and also added a Coupe model in 2017. It got a slight facelift in 2020. Under the hood, the GLC 63 S AMG Coupe sports a twin-turbocharged 4.0-litre V8 engine, mated to the 4Matic all-wheel-drive system. Power is delivered via a 9-speed automatic transmission. Features include AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

An identical replica of the Porsche 356 Speedster from the 1960s, the new-age Speedster II is hand-built by French outfit Pierre GÃ©rard Organisation, also known as PGO. Changes to the basic design include higher-positioned mirrors, modern tail-lights and stylish 16-inch or 17-inch rims. The chassis is made of composite materials, is attached to a steel frame. The engine, a Peugeot-sourced 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, is mounted in the rear, while the small luggage compartment is in the front. Standard setup include rear-wheel-drive, a 5-speed manual gearbox and a cloth soft top. Features of the original include a cloth or leather interior, electric mirrors, basic CD stereo and as many as eight whole gauges, but not much else. The windows are of the removable variety, and the soft top is manual. The car stays true to its roots and therefore has no ABS brakes, no airbags and not even power steering. However, the 2008 model features luxuries such as power windows, a/c, electric mirrors, CD/MP3 stereo and keyless entry, as well as a 4-speed automatic gearbox. Sold only in a few GCC countries, the Speedster offers a pure driving experience few cars offer, but it can only be regarded as an expensive toy.

The BMW 8-Series, also known by its chassis code E31, is a Grand Tourer developed as a flagship for the German carmaker in its time. While it replaced the original E24 6-Series in 1991, the 8-Series was not a successor, but rather an entirely new class with a substantially higher price. Initially, the only engine on offer was a 5.0-litre V12, for the 850i, which was later renamed 850Ci by 1993. The 1993 model-year also saw the introduction of the 4.0-litre V8 with an 840Ci model, which was later replaced by a 4.4-litre V8 for 1995. Also for 1995, a new 5.4-litre V12 replaced the old engine for the 850Ci. All models were offered with a choice of manual and automatic transmissions. From 1992 to 1996, an M-tuned 850CSi model was also offered, identified by its frontal chin spoiler, unique wheels and manual-only gearbox, and powered by a 5.6-litre V12. The cars at the time were loaded with features such as leather upholstery, power windows and mirrors, power-adjustable seats, premium stereo, LCD info displays, airbags, ABS and more.

The X-Trail is Nissan's entry for the small road-going 4WD market, though for a long time we thought it was really a midsize comparable to the old Pathfinder in size. Developed to attract young adventurous buyers, we find the X-Trail particularly unattractive, but it has proved to be a runaway success with older people just looking for a conservative vehicle that looks like a 4WD. The X-Trail has undergone only slight exterior redesigns and interior upgrades ever since it was launched years ago and is beginning to look dated. Powered by a 2.5-litre four-cylinder engine coupled with a 4-speed automatic or a 5-speed manual transmission, it isn't particularly fast, but a reasonable long-distance cruiser. Full-time four-wheel drive is available when the computer system senses the need for all wheels to be driven to suit demand, but it will get stuck if you take it beyond the beach. The interior is full of storage spaces, including cup-holders, centre console box and other nooks and crannies. ABS brakes and 2 airbags are standard.

The Swift offers eye-catching looks, quality and good driving dynamics all in an affordable sub-compact package. Built and sold in many countries, this "world car" is a break from previously dull Suzuki iterations and adopts a muscular body with bold sides, spread-out wheels, and a broad-shouldered beltline that continues all the way to the tail lights, while the roof's rear edge is shaped as a spoiler to improve aerodynamics. The Swift has one of the widest bodies in its class, and together with a long wheelbase, permits a spacious enough cabin. The functional interior uses aluminium-look trim highlights, tight fit and finish, and high-grade hard plastics. The little Suzuki is powered by a 1.5-litre four-cylinder powerplant, while power is sent to the front-wheels using either the standard five-speed manual transmission or a four-speed automatic with a gated shift lever option. Standard features include power windows, CD/MP3 player, power steering and more, positioning the Swift as a semi-upscale runabout in the GCC. An expensive body kit is optional. All models have standard driver and passenger front and side airbags, as well as available full-length curtain airbags.

The 206 is one of Peugeot's more popular models, with a wide range of body styles, trim levels and engine choices. Its design has changed little since its launch in 1999, although new derivatives such as the 206 CC Cabriolet joined the line-up in 2001. There are various petrol engines in the range, although after 2006, the local offerings had decreased. The standard five-door hatchback can be had with a 1.4-litre or a 1.6-litre four-cylinder engine with either a manual or an automatic. The 206 CC coupe-cabriolet can only be had as a 1.6-litre automatic in the later years, although the manual 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre CC models were available here for a few years in between. There is a more powerful 2.0-litre engine with a manual offered in three-door RC hatchback form, which is a true sporting contender. The tuned RC debuted in 2003, replacing the competent GTi 2.0-litre model. All models come with front power windows, a cloth interior, driver's airbag and other basics as standard. Comprehensive safety equipment such as ABS with electronic brakeforce distribution, Emergency Brake Assist, ESP and traction control, along with passenger front airbag, were all optional. Available features included a CD player, alloy wheels and more.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE Coupe is an all-new model, to compete against the BMW X6. Mercedes-AMG GLE Coupe 63 is the top performance model. There are two variants, which includes the standard GLE 63 and then the GLE 63 S. Under the hood, both come with the 5.5-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive. Available features include adjustable air suspension, adaptive cruise control and active parking assist. The exterior features HID headlights, LED running maps and 21-inch cross-spoke AMG alloy wheels. The 5-seater interior offers leather upholstery, mood lighting, HDD navigation, panoramic sunroof, rear entertainment system, keyless start, ventilated power front seats and a split-folding rear seat. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control, ABS and drowsiness monitor, with options such as a rear view camera with parking sensors, active lane assist, blind-spot monitor and automatic pre-crash braking.

The Audi Q5 is the compact class offering in the VW-owned German manufacturer's SUV range. In 2018, an all-new model was released. In 2021, it got a facelift and new tech inside. Under the hood, the only engine on offer is a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder motor, mated to an 7-speed automatic transmission. It is available with the all-wheel-drive "Quattro" system, and will be available with the Audi 'Drive-Select' system to change its settings. While exterior does not have a whole lot of changes from its predecessor, the interior has been fully revamped. It also weighs less than the previous generation. Features include LED running lights and taillights, alloy wheels of up to 20 inches in size, seating for five with folding rear bench and a foldable front seat, and the usual power accessories. The Q5 will be available in several different trim options, including an 'S-Line' trim option with aggressive body mouldings and mesh foglight grills. Other available features, whether standard or optional, include a roof load sensor to adjust the stability control for the higher centre of gravity, rearview camera, navigation, high-beam assistant that automatically switches between the high and low beams, blind-spot monitor, adaptive cruise control, triple-zone climate control, intelligent keyless entry, electric parking brake, multiple airbags, MMI multimedia with speech control system, Bluetooth telephone and Apple CarPlay

The X-Trail is Nissan's entry for the small road-going 4WD market, though for a long time we thought it was really a midsize comparable to the old Pathfinder in size. Developed to attract young adventurous buyers, we find the X-Trail particularly unattractive, but it has proved to be a runaway success with older people just looking for a conservative vehicle that looks like a 4WD. The X-Trail has undergone only slight exterior redesigns and interior upgrades ever since it was launched years ago and is beginning to look dated. Powered by a 2.5-litre four-cylinder engine coupled with a 4-speed automatic or a 5-speed manual transmission, it isn't particularly fast, but a reasonable long-distance cruiser. Full-time four-wheel drive is available when the computer system senses the need for all wheels to be driven to suit demand, but it will get stuck if you take it beyond the beach. The interior is full of storage spaces, including cup-holders, centre console box and other nooks and crannies. ABS brakes and 2 airbags are standard.

An all-new model of the Kia Cadenza came out in 2017. It remained the same for 2018. It comes with two engine options, one the 3.3-litre "MPI" V6 and a 6-speed automatic gearbox, and the other more powerful 3.3-litre "GDI" V6 with an 8-speed automatic transmission. Features, standard or otherwise, include cloth or leather upholstery, power front seats, intelligent keyless entry with starter button, HID headlights, fake wood grain, fog lamps, power windows, electric mirrors, immobilizer, 17-inch, 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels, dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, electric rear curtains, auto-dimming mirror, rain-sensing wipers, cruise control, 8-inch screen with navigation, ventilated front seats, rear camera and interior lighting. It gets Kia's UVO system featuring Android Auto and Apple CarPlay as standard, while a 12-speaker Harman/Kardon system is an option. Safety features include stability control, eight airbags, active headrests and ABS for the four-wheel-disc brakes. Higher models get Kia's "Drive Wise" semi-autonomous self-driving tech. The self-driving suite includes emergency braking, radar cruise control that can function in stop-and-go traffic, and lane keep assist tech.

Yet another entry into Daihatsu's sub-compact range, this one is a unique little number. Daihatsu advertising is so poor in this region that we only came across this specialty machine by mistake. Some prefer to call it a mini MPV, but it is really a hatchback. The little boxy car offers oodles of space thanks to the tall shape and long wheelbase. It is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, with a choice of a five-speed manual or a four-speed automatic. The rear doors open wide to allow easy entry and exit, and the rear seat can be optioned to slide front and back. Luggage capacity is hihgly flexible, with folding front seats and split-folding rear seats, while pockets are all over the place. This Toyota-derived vehicle has its annoying gauge cluster in the centre, and the interior treatment is all hard plastic, except for interesting touches such as illuminated speakers and handles. Other available features include with a CD/AM/FM radio, power windows, remote central locking, ABS brakes and at least dual front airbags if not more.

The X5 M debuted in late 2009, with a higher-tuned turbocharged 4.4-litre V8 than the regular X5. The M has a 6-speed auto with proper paddle-shifters. Features include iPod / USB adapter interface, Active Cruise Control with Stop and Go, Lane Departure Warning, Active Steering, running boards, Head-Up Display, 4-zone automatic climate control, side-view cameras, top-view camera, leather-covered dashboard, full keyless entry, and smartphone integration. The M gets 20-inch wheels with performance tyres, Adaptive Drive system, aluminium roof rails, M door sill plates, M driver footrest, M steering wheel and M aerodynamic enhancements. It also gets  features such as sports suspension, 'M' driving mode, paddle-shifted quicker-response automatic, launch control and a body kit.

The Mercedes-Benz A35 AMG 4Matic joined the lineup for the first time in 2019. It is a new performance variant, sitting below the A45 AMG. It uses the same 2.0-litre turbocharged engine as the standard version, but tuned to produce more horsepower. Power is delivered via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The 5-seater hatchback's features include 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Subaru WRX is in its fifth generation, debuting in 2015 and getting a facelift for 2018. Redesigned 18-inch wheels, revised electric power steering and optional turning LED headlights are also new for 2018. Under the hood, it gets a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder Boxer engine with a twin-scroll turbocharger and intercooler. It will be coupled to a 6-speed manual transmission. There's a new Sport Lineartronic CVT as an option, which also comes with 6-speed and 8-speed paddle-shifter mode. The new lighter engine ensures that this WRX with the manual gearbox is 30 kg heavier than the previous 2014 model. Of the two alternatives, torque will be equally (50:50) distributed to all four wheels in the 6-speed manual variant and the CVT will receive a torque distribution split of 45:55 with Subarua's Variable Torque Distribution system. The new WRX is 25 mm longer wheelbase than the previous generation. So rear seat passengers gain nearly 51 mm of extra legroom. It also has a bigger boot and 60/40-split fold-down rear seats. Inside, the Subaru gets a leather-wrapped steering wheel and sports seats covered in high-grip fabric. Buyers can also opt for leather seats and 8-way adjustable driver seat. Among other features is a power sunroof, a dual gauge instrument layout with a 3.5-inch LCD central screen displaying various functions and a new 4.3-inch multi-information central display providing a multitude of vehicle system functions. Safety features include driver and passenger airbags, ABS, traction control and stability control.

Just 40 examples of the Bugatti Divo are going to be built and sold (five units are bound for the Middle East), with the entire production run already spoken for well before the first car rolled out of the Molsheim factory. The Divo was offered only to existing Bugatti customers. Apart from the Divo’s low-volume status, its main drawcards are bespoke bodywork that reprises Bugatti’s coachbuilding tradition, plus sharpened dynamics that stem from fettled suspension and a comprehensive aero package that delivers almost 500 kg of downforce at the car’s 380 kph v-max.The Divo is actually slower than the 420 kph Chiron it’s derived from, in terms of outright straight-line speed as its high downforce and the aggressive negative camber it runs on the front and rear tyres necessitated a drop in ultimate velocity. But the payoff of these modifications, in addition to stiffer springs and dampers, is that the Divo serves up sharper steering response and corner-devouring capabilities that eclipse the Chiron – it’s eight seconds a lap quicker than the latter around the 6.2 km Nardo handling circuit.

Toyota created the IMV platform to serve its budget-oriented lineup, and one of the products of this venture is the Innova. The IMV platform consists of a body-on-chassis setup, offering more refinement in its larger vehicles. The Innova attempts to resemble a 4WD in height, with a high waistline and four forward-opening doors, but it ends up looking like a van. The only engine is a 2.7-litre four-cylinder straight from the Fortuner, offered with a manual or automatic. All versions are well-equipped, seat eight people and get a rear seat slide mechanism to improve legroom, along with infinitely-configurable seats. Standard features include a cassette/MP3/CD player with 6 speakers, dual-zone a/c, power & tilt steering, power windows, keyless entry, central locking, multi-information display, fabric seats, probably fake wood trim, airbags for driver and front passenger, and ABS brakes. The big van rides on comparatively tiny 15-inch alloy wheels. Ironically, the Innova is considered a luxury vehicle in third-world markets.

The fourth-gen Audi A8 debuted as a 2018 model, lighter and filled with even more complicated technology than before. The initial powertrain offering for the GCC will be a 3.0-litre "TFSI" turbo V6, but a 4.0-litre TFSI turbo V8 follows later, and there will also be a 6.0-litre W12 for those who want one on special order. The new A8 has a suspension system that uses actuators to individually raise and lower each wheel to keep the car as flat as possibly over bumpy roads, and uses a camera that scans the road ahead to basically pre-set the suspension accordingly. Audi claims the new A8 is the first production car to offer Level 3 automated driving at speeds of up to 60 kph, but only on highways where a physical barrier separates you from cars travelling in the opposite direction. Other features include variations of adaptive cruise control, lane-departure assist and all that. Up front, Audi has more or less done away with buttons and switches via a 10.1-inch touchscreen display which, when off, blends almost invisibly into the high-gloss black surround. The user interface comes to life as soon as the car is opened. There’s also a secondary touchscreen display in the centre console to control air-con functions and make text inputs. Audi is also offering an optional ‘relaxation seat’ in the A8 L that adjusts four ways and has a footrest that incorporates both warming and massaging functions for aching soles. Other rear-seat features include matrix reading lights, in-seat massage function and a smartphone-mimicking remote control.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG Coupe made its debut as a 2015 model year. In 2018, it got a facelift and interior upgrades, but no mechanical changes. The Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG Coupe comes with a twin-turbocharged 6.0-litre V12 engine. Inside, the traditional instrument cluster from the previous generation is gone and is replaced by two high-resolution 8:3 format colour displays, 12.3-inch in size, for controlling comfort settings and infotainment purposes. Seats are fitted with 14 actuated air bladders in the backrest with six different massage programs. For safety the S65 AMG Coupe gets "beltbags", which are airbags in the seatbelt webbing, and "cushionbags", which prevent occupants from sliding under the belt. A new climate control, called "thermotronic" features improved filtering of outside air and also an "active perfuming system" for customising the smell of the interior. The new S65 AMG Coupe gets "Magic Body Control" which uses cameras to scan the road in advance and adjust the suspension accordingly. Safety features include Active Parking Assist, Active Lane Keeping Assist, Night View Assist Plus, Distronic Plus with Steering Assist, Brake Assist Plus with Cross-Traffic Assist and Pre-Safe Brake with pedestrian recognition.

The redesigned 2014 Kia Carens is a seven-seater MPV, smaller than typical minivans. The Carens can be had with two 4-cylinder engines, one a direct-injection 1.6-litre "GDI" in LX and EX trim, and the other a fuel-injected 2.0-litre "MPI" in LX and two EX trims. All models get a 6-speed automatic, front-wheel-drive, fog lamps, cooled glovebox, CD/MP3 stereo, Bluetooth, roof rack and keyless entry. Base models get 16-inch steel wheels and a vinyl steering wheel. Higher trim levels get 17-inch alloy wheels, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, parking sensors, cruise control and more. Only the top model gets a panoramic glass roof. All models get ABS and only one airbag, except for the top model, which gets two front airbags to go with that glass roof.

The second-generation Peugeot 308 was released in 2014, but only went on sale in the GCC in 2015. The same  is turbocharged 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engines carried over from the previous shape, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Even the most basic model gets driver & passenger airbags, ABS brakes with EBD, trip computer, AM/FM Radio with CD/MP3 player with remote stalk, speed-sensitive power steering, electric windows and mirrors, cooling vent inside the glove compartment, height-adjustable headlights, split-folding rear seats, remote key with central locking, and 15-inch wheels. Moving up to the higher trim levels adds items such as side-curtain airbags, stability control, navigation system, dual-zone automatic a/c with rear vents, CD/MP3 player with bluetooth and AUX input, 5-CD changer, panoramic sunroof with automatic curtain, cruise control, automatic headlights, rain-sensing wipers, leather seats with chrome interior trim, auto-dimming mirror, foldable door mirrors, fog lights, parking sensors, front and rear armrests,  16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and automatic tyre pressure sensors. Inside and out, it is a classy hatchback for its category, making it almost as good as any of the premium-branded compacts.

The undeniable mascot of the VW range, the car popularly known as the New Beetle isn't that new anymore, but still a weird head-turning cruiser. Launched in 1999, it hass received a few facelifts over the years, but is still essentially the same. Passengers must make some concessions for retro style. Interior ergonomics are not as good as that in a traditional car, and there isn't a lot of trunk space. But the Beetle does come in an assortment of bright colours, including sunflowery yellow and limey green. Its exterior and interior design details are fun and creative, but very much on the feminine side. On the road, the Beetle is smooth and handles fairly okay. The convertible adds to the fun with its ability to drop the top. But the New Beetle hardly offers blistering performance, with a choice of 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre four-cylinder engines, with either a manual or an automatic. All Beetles are well equipped, with an AM/FM/cassette stereo, central locking with keyless remote, anti-theft system, four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, dual airbags, power exterior mirrors and windows, among others. Options include a CD changer and electronic stability control.

The Traverse is a crossover wagon that combines car-like handling with the utility of a 4WD wagon, offering three rows of seating for up to eight passengers. The design consists of polished aluminium roof rails, projector beam headlights, LED taillights and a rear spoiler. It has a 3.6-litre V6 with variable valve timing, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission and an optional all-wheel-drive system with no low range. The interior features a "low and away" instrument panel and a Smart Slide second-row feature allows easier access to the third row. Features include power windows, CD/MP3 stereo with six speakers, electric mirrors, keyless entry and more. Optional features include rear-seat DVD entertainment, HID headlights, sunroof, parking sensors, leather seats, tri-zone climate control and more. Standard safety features includes StabiliTrak stability control system with rollover mitigation technology, six airbags and a tyre-pressure-monitoring system. Also standard is power-assisted rack-and-pinion steering, 18-inch wheels with optional 19-inchers, and four-wheel disc brakes with ABS.

The new Elantra gets a sleeker yet bulbous new look. It's also taller and wider than the outgoing Elantra. There's also more interior space than before, and a higher seating position. Most people would probably consider the Elantra a compact sedan, but its new interior volume is now comparable to some midsize cars. Various trim levels are available on this front-wheel-drive sedan, including a top-of-the-line model which comes with leather seats. But all models are well-equipped with plenty of convenience features, including power windows, intermittent windshield wipers, multiple storage areas, a 60/40-split fold-down rear seatback, dual vanity mirrors, tinted windows, two 12-volt outlets and a tilt steering wheel. Engine choices include a carryover 1.6-litre four-cylinder and a revamped 2.0-litre four-cylinder. A five-speed manual comes standard with the smaller motor, while a four-speed automatic is available for both engines. Basic models get only a single airbag and steel 15-inch wheels. The top model gets dual airbags, ABS brakes, stability control, and 16-inch alloys.

The Isuzu MU-X is the brand's only SUV offering. It is basically a rebadged Chevrolet Trailblazer, but with a diesel engine. It gets the 2.5-litre turbodiesel engine, mated to a 5-speed automatic transmission. It is available in economical rear-wheel-drive and capable four-wheel-drive forms.Features on the higher trim levels include 16-inch alloys, higher-grade cloth seats, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, CD/MP3 stereo, power windows and mirrors, central locking, fog lamps, LED rear lights, optional rear defogger, optional dual front airbags, optional ABS brakes and more.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz E-Class Coupe made its debut as a 2018 model year. It adopted the new design culture already first seen on the S-Class, and followed by the C-Class. Three models were introduced - the E200 and E300 which get the 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and the all-wheel drive E400 which gets the 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 motor. All models get the 9-speed automatic transmission. Inside, most dashboard buttons have been replaced by a screen which can be accessed via a rotary controller or an optional touchpad. For the first time, air suspension is now offered. Standard safety features include multiple airbags, stability control and traction control. Various optional safety systems include Active Parking Assist, Adaptive Highbeam Assist Plus, Traffic Sign Assist with Wrong-Way Alert, Drive Pilot and Evasive Steering Assist.

The Infiniti Q70 received a facelift for the 2015 model year. Available with a 3.7-litre V6 or with a 5.6-litre V8, all the rear-wheel-drive cars feature a 7-speed automatic, with optional paddle shifters. There are three versions of the 3.7-litre Q70 available, namely Excellence, Luxury and Sport; and two of the 5.6-litre, called Luxury and Sport. Some markets, such as the UAE, have only the V6 model available, in limited trim levels. Available features, depending on trim level, include "˜Infiniti Drive' which has four different settings for the throttle delivery and power mapping; Bose Surround Sound CD/MP3 stereo with iPod connectivity, DVD navigation, 9.3GB hard drive and speakers even in the front seats; rear-wheel active steering with Sport models; adaptive cruise control, turning HID headlights, 18-inch or 20-inch wheels, rear camera with front and rear parking sensors, Bluetooth phone, intelligent keyless entry and start, power-adjustable ventilated front seats, dual-zone automatic a/c with optional 'forest air' setting, leather upholstery with choice of wood trim, full power accessories and more. Sport models get aluminium pedals and magnesium paddle shifters. Safety features include front airbags, side and curtain airbags, pre-crash automatic braking, lane departure warning, lane departure prevention, intelligent brake assist, blind-spot monitoring, tyre pressure monitor, and seat-belts that become tighter on hard braking.

The Q50 is also longer, wider and sits lower than the previous generation, which was the G37. For 2017, it got new engines. As for the interior, it now has the Infiniti's new InTouch system a touch screen which displays information and navigation. Owners will also be able to download, update and synch personal apps through their smartphones and USB drives.  The standard motor is a Mercedes-sourced 4-cylinder 2.0-litre turbocharged unit which made its debut in 2015. In 2017, a 3.0-litre turbocharged engine was introduced, available in two different tunes. There is also a 3.5-litre V6 engine coupled with an electric motor, which will be available in select markets. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, leather seats, LED headlights and taillights, automatic headlights, LED daytime running lamps, LED fog lights, twin exhaust pipes, dual-touch screens, Bluetooth, front and rear parking censors with rearview camera, dual-zone adaptive climate control with rear vents, AM/FM audio system with USB/iPod support, Bluetooth and 6 speakers, and 17-inch alloy rims. Optional equipment include sunroof, navigation system, 19-inch alloy rims, sports seats and sports suspension. Standard safety features include tyre pressure monitor, ABS, electronic brake force distribution (EBD), traction control, stability control, hill-start assist and 6 airbags. Optional safety equipment include Active Lane Control, which uses a camera-based straight-line stability system which is included as part of the Lane Departure Prevention system. The Lane Departure Prevention system makes small steering input angle adjustments if the car undergoes minor direction changes due to road surface changes or crosswinds. Another optional safety feature is the Direct Adaptive Steering system which allows independent control of the Q50's tire angle and steering inputs, transmitting the driver's intentions to the wheels faster than a mechanical system.

The Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class is a compact crossover offering. It is powered by a direct-injection 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder mated to a 7-speed "DCT" dual-clutch automanual and a front-wheel-drive or all-wheel drive platform. The 5-seater is offered in one loaded "Sport" spec that includes 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

An all-new Nissan Pathfinder was introduced in 2013, when it ditched its body-on-frame chassis and gained some length to compete in the hotly-contested midsize crossover segment. In 2018 it got a facelift, along with engine and interior upgrades. The 7-seater Pathfinder is powered by a 3.5-litre V6, mated to a CVT and a choice of either front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive in all trim levels. The hybrid model is powered by a 4-cylinder 2.5-litre supercharged engine combined with an electric motor. The all-wheel-drive model gets a selector for choosing 2WD, 4WD or Auto. The base Pathfinder S comes standard with a second-row 60/40-split fold-flat bench seat, a third-row 50/50-split fold-flat reclining bench seat, LED running lights, 18-inch alloys, tri-zone automatic a/c, keyless entry with push-button ignition, power windows, CD/MP3/DVD/HDD audio system with 8-inch screen and 6 speakers, USB/AUX ports, Bluetooth phone, auto headlights, 6 airbags, stability control, tyre-pressure monitor and apparently a standard power liftgate in some markets. The Pathfinder SV adds power-adjustable front seats, rear camera, 20-inch alloy wheels, remote starter, auxiliary audio/video input jack, power windows with front one-touch auto-up/down, front fog lamps, chrome body side trim, welcome lighting, stainless-steel kick plates, speed-sensitive intermittent wipers, illuminated sun-visor mirrors, sunroof, wood-tone trim, leather-wrapped steering wheel and shift knob, leather seats, and a tow hitch receiver with 7-pin trailer tow wiring harness on the rear bumper. The top-spec Pathfinder SL further adds a key-linked memory seat and other settings for individual drivers, side-curtain airbags front and rear, digital compass, 9GB hard drive, 8-inch VGA colour monitor with navigation, Bose audio system with 13 speakers, climate-controlled front seats, and a power-tilt/telescoping steering column. An around-view four-camera parking aid is optional, as is a rear DVD entertainment system with 2 screens. Available accessories include roof rail bars, rear-installing tent and more.

When the new Nissan Patrol was launched in 2010, the carmaker elected to keep producing the older-generation Patrol Safari alongside the new one. The long-running Safari continues to be Nissan's best four-wheel-drive model. For 2010, it only became available as a 5-door model with the 4.8-litre inline 6-cylinder engine as standard, with the choice of a 5-speed automatic with tiptronic or a proper 5-speed manual. By the middle of 2011, a 3-door short-wheelbase model became available with the same drivetrain, as a 2012 model. Straight-line drive transfer allows on-the-fly shifting from 2WD to 4WD with one touch of a lever. The Patrol also has a decent interior featuring quality materials, wood trim, cloth upholstery, CD/MP3 stereo, manual a/c, fog lamps, 16-inch wheels and other equipment. Along with two foldout cargo-area seats, the wagon model has room for seven. Front airbags and ABS are standard, among other features.

The VW Passat offered in the GCC is unique in that it's designed and built in the United States specifically for that market, and is larger as well as cheaper than the European version. It is currently offered with one 2.5-litre 5-cylinder engine option mated to a 6-speed automatic. Offered in four trim levels, namely S, SE, SEL and SPORT, the 4-door sedan boasts class-leading space and respectable cabin trim. The entry-level S is designed specifically for fleet customers, and features ABS, ESP, dual front airbags, curtain and side thorax airbags, Bluetooth with voice command, multifunction steering wheel with audio and phone controls, cruise control, CD/MP3 stereo, 60/40 folding rear seat, and electronic vehicle immobilisation. The SE model includes a six-CD changer, leather steering wheel, rear a/c vents and 16-inch "San Jose" alloy wheels. In addition to the features seen on the S and SE models, the SEL has 17-inch "Sonoma" alloy wheels, leatherette seats and a high-end Fender sound system with a subwoofer in the boot. A media input with iPod cable is also standard on the SEL, as is a powered driver's seat, front fog and cornering lamps, keyless entry, pushbutton start, a sunroof and dual-zone climatronic air conditioning with air quality sensors. The flagship SPORT model adds part-leather seats, 18-inch "Bristol" alloy wheels, touch-screen navigation system, 30GB hard disc, SD card reader and DVD drive, memory function for the driver's seat and a powered front passenger seat. Other features include tyre-pressure sensors, insulating glass and a special acoustic film integrated into the windscreen to help keep out external noise.

The redesigned-for-2008 Mondeo is an attractive midsize car built in Europe that shares a Mazda platform. It looks excellent inside and out, but loses out to the Japanese with a weak combination of carryover engines, along with the stigma of expensive dealer maintenance charges. It was facelifted a bit for 2011, with a new front bumper and grille. The Mondeo is largely avaliable as a family sedan, but it is also available in sporty liftback and practical wagon form in some markets. The Mondeo is a tremendous success in Europe though, simply because its handling is outstanding, rivalling more expensive cars like Alfa Romeo, all for an affordable price. The interior is especially attractive and put together well. The base Mondeo is powered by the 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, available with a 5-speed manual. A 2.3-litre 4-cylinder engine is coupled with a 6-speed automatic transmission in the higher model. Various trim levels are available, all with power windows, trip computer, ABS brakes, front airbags, CD stereo with MP3 connector and more. Options include stability control, CD changer, keyless starter button, Xenon adaptive headlights, tyre pressure monitor, sunroof, fog lights, variable suspension settings, hill launch assist and adaptive cruise control.

The sub-compact Figo is Ford's smallest offering in the GCC. Intended to be a cheaper motoring option than even the Fiesta, the Figo is built in India, based on a shortened older-generation Fiesta, and comes in 5-door hatchback form. It comes with a choice of 1.4-litre 4-cylinder with a manual gearbox and 1.6-litre 4-cylinder with an automatic. All cars get independent MacPherson strut front suspension and a semi-independent rear twist beam. The Figo is available in Ambiente and Trend trims, both getting cloth-upholstered interiors with features that include manual windows, power mirrors, 2-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with USB/AUX ports, power steering, fold-flat second-row seating, intermittent wipers, dual front airbags, soft-touch dashboard and a claimed "best-in-class" manual a/c. Also available on the higher model are 14-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, fog lamps, ABS brakes, front power windows and height-adjustable driver's seat.

The first to adopt Infiniti's new naming system, the Q50 replaces the G25 and G37 model. A complete new design, the Q50 does not disappoint in the looks department. It now has the signature Infiniti "double arch" grille, along with the horizontal headlights and taillights. The Q50 is also longer, wider and sits lower than the outgoing G. As for the interior, it now has the Infiniti's new InTouch system a touch screen which displays information and navigation. Owners will also be able to download, update and synch personal apps through their smartphones and USB drives. As per the new naming system, the numbers in model names don't designate the engine capacity any more. The same engine is carried over from the Infiniti G37 in the Q50, the 3.7-litre V6, which is mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. However, there is a new entry-level engine, a Mercedes-sourced 4-cylinder 2.0-litre turbocharged unit which made its debut as a 2015 model year. The top model is the Q50 S Hybrid, with a 3.5-litre V6 boosted by an electric motor, and mated to a 7-speed automatic. Lot of new technologies have been added to improve driver safety. One of them, Active Lane Control, uses a camera-based straight-line stability system which is included as part of the Lane Departure Prevention system. The Lane Departure Prevention system makes small steering input angle adjustments if the car undergoes minor direction changes due to road surface changes or crosswinds. It also gets Direct Adaptive Steering system which allows independent control of the Q50's tire angle and steering inputs, transmitting the driver's intentions to the wheels faster than a mechanical system.

The redesigned CTS 4-door sedan in 2008 spawned the Cadillac CTS-V sedan from 2009 to 2013. Powering the rear-wheel-drive CTS-V is the supercharged 6.2-litre V8 that can be had with a 6-speed manual or automatic. The exterior is characterized by a larger chrome-trimmed grille, vertical-shaped headlights and vertical taillights with LED lighting. Inside, the interior is luxurious enough and has standard or optional technological features including DVD-based navigation with telescoping touch-screen, Bose 5.1 Cabin Surround audio system, front and side-curtain airbags, leather trim, adaptive HID headlights, an Easy Key system with Smart Remote Start, 19-inch alloy wheels, Bluetooth, optional limited-slip diff and an optional panoramic sunroof. For maximum comfort, heated and ventilated seats is fitted with new "thin-seat" technology and rear-seat leg, knee and foot room has been enhanced. The CTS-V also gets extra bodywork, better brakes, stiffer suspension and Recaro sports seats alongside the Corvette-derived supercharged V8.

The Accent is Hyundai's long-running sub-compact nameplate, though it could be more successful than it is. The new model is a decent upgrade over the old Accent, though still using lightly-modifed carryover engines. Now available in 5-door sedan and 3-door hatchback form in this region, the most basic Accent thankfully comes with power steering, air-conditioning, AM/FM radio and cassette player with 4 speakers and a 1.4-litre four-cylinder engine with a manual or automatic gearbox at a dirt-cheap price. Step up to the higher models, and buyers are treated to a 1.6-litre four-cylinder with a manual or an automatic, power windows, central door locks, electric mirrors, fog lamps, better cloth seats, a 60/40 split-folding rear seat with centre armrest and cup holders, and not much else. An agreeably spacious interior and steel 14-inch wheels with plastic covers are standard on all trim levels, but there is no mention of airbags or ABS brakes in the spec sheet on cars bound for the Middle East market.

The unimaginatively-named Pickup is a midsize pickup that is designed to be a workhorse rather than a lifestyle vehicle, but we are listing it here anyway as it is practical enough to serve as personal transport for someone who absolutely needs to drive a pickup. Powered by a 2.4-litre four-cylinder petrol engine mated to a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic, or a 2.5-litre four-cylinder turbodiesel mated to a five-speed manual, it recently received a facelift that gives the truck a corporate front end. It is available in single cab and quad cab configurations. Features, most of them optional, include air conditioning, a reclining split bench seating in front, power steering, 4-speaker AM/FM radio cassette audio system with CD player, power windows and auto door lock, airbags, dual cup-holders and a sliding rear window. A bunch of bed accessories are also available. The four-wheel-drive models have better ground clearance and a pumped-up look compared to the rear-wheel-drive models. It seems not all models are available in all local markets.

The Veyron 16.4 was a long-running pet project by Volkswagen to create the fastest production car in the world at the time, reintroducing the Bugatti badge in style. Goofy looks notwithstanding, the styling is an essential part of the design to ensure total stability at top speed. The car is powered by an 8.0-litre quad-turbo W16 engine derived from Volkswagen designs, mated to all-wheel-drive and a seven-speed direct-shift automanual gearbox. The fully customisable interior is covered in leather and metal, with numerous features such as CD stereo, navigation and more. The single-piece carbon-fibre monocoque does well in crash tests, while airbags give the driver and passenger additional protection. The high-speed tyres designed specially for the Veyron 16.4 incorporate the PAX System that ensures safe handling even after sudden pressure loss. Another safety element is the rear spoiler that acts as a "˜parachute brake' during emergency braking. A second key must be engaged when stopped to initiate "top speed" mode, when the rear spoiler sets itself to a lower position, the front air diffusers close and the vehicle lowers to further improve aerodynamic downforce. A limited-to-150-pieces Grand Sport model was released in mid-2008 with a removable targa-roof panel.

An all-new Chevrolet Camaro was launched in 2016. While the exterior may not be that different from the previous generation, under the hood the 3.6-litre V6 and 6.2-litre V8 engines have been upgraded with more power. The Camaro also has a new 4-cylinder 2.0-litre turbocharged engine, but it is not sold in the GCC. They can all be had with either a 6-speed manual or an 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include air conditioning, power windows and lock, and keyless entry. Available features include heads-up display, sunroof and the MyLink entertainment system which includes touchscreen navigation. Standard rims include 18-inch wheels for the V6 and 4-cylinder, and 20-inch ones for the V8. Safety features include front airbags, side airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Ford Ecosport is a new addition to the American brand's increasingly international line-up. Built in several countries around the world, this little crossover comes from India for the GCC market. The standard engine is a simple 1.5-litre 4-cylinder mated to either a 5-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic gearbox, and it only comes in front-wheel-drive form with SUV-like ground clearance. Measuring only a little more than a sub-compact hatchback in length, the Ecosport seats five, with a small boot behind the sideways-opening tailgate. Standard features on the base Ambiente trim include a 2-way manual-adjustable driver's seat, 60:40-split folding rear seat, electric power steering, front-disc rear-drum brakes, 4-speaker CD/MP3 stereo, power windows, front floor mats, adjustable steering column, rear wiper, rear fog lamp, cooled glovebox, basic keyless entry, and 15-inch steel wheels with covers or optional 16-inch alloys. The mid-range Trend trim adds a 4-way manual-adjustable driver's seat, additional storage spaces, 6-speaker stereo, voice-activated SYNC multimedia system, USB port, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel with audio controls, one-touch function on power windows, standard 16-inch alloys, body-colour trim, light-coloured grille, front fog lamps, roof rack, and cruise control with the optional automatic transmission. The top Titanium model additionally gets a lumbar-adjustable driver's seat with armrest, standard automatic gearbox, unique 16-inch alloys, Bluetooth, extra map lights, climate control, rain-sensing front wipers, auto headlights, smart keyless entry with starter button, extra power-point in the boot, rear floor mats, rear parking sensors, chrome grille, silver roof rack, trip computer, auto-dimming rearview mirror, and a seatbelt warning for front passengers, with optional features such as leather upholstery and soft-touch door armrests. All versions get dual front airbags, ABS, stability control and engine immobiliser, with the Trend and Titanium further getting side and curtain airbags as well as a perimeter alarm. Optional accessories include roof-rack crossbars, spare wheel cover, metal pedal covers, carpeted floor mats, rear spoiler, mud guards and more.

The Chinese Chery Tiggo received a makeover for its 2016 model year and a rebranding to Tiggo 3, while also making it the second facelift for this aging crossover. Powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, it comes with a CVT automatic now. The five-door five-seater Tiggo 3 gets a versatile interior, with fold-flat seats and a spacious cargo area. Features, standard or optional, include front dual airbags, rear three-point seat belts, ABS brakes with electronic brakeforce distribution, disc brakes, keyless entry, alloy wheels and a rear windshield wiper. Chery also brags that sports car maker Lotus Engineering had a hand in developing this mishmash, so we expect decent handling.

The Magna was an all-new model back in 1997, replacing Mitsubishi's Sigma as their top-of-the-line sedan. Competing in the near-luxury segment against upscale brands, it never stood a chance, but soldiered on anyway unchanged right up to 2003, at which point it got a facelift. The Magna features a standard 3.5-litre V6 engine, a 4-speed automatic gearbox, a modern-at-the-time dashboard, decent suspension tuning and improvements in body structure that promise fair handling. Offered only as a sedan, the fairly-large Magna rode on a front-wheel-drive platform, and didn't overlap with the more-popular Galant, which was originally in between a compact and a midsize at that time. The Magna was available in essentially two flavours, namely a standard model and a sportier VR-X version. The Magna VR-X upgrades include a mesh grille, colour-keyed rear spoiler, aerodynamic side skirts, wheel lip moldings, sport-style bucket seats, unique seat fabric, and possibly sportier suspension tuning with slightly-increased engine power. Standard features on this redesigned sedan include dual airbags, 16-inch alloy wheels, tinted glass, a power driver seat, an AM/FM stereo with cassette and CD player, remote keyless entry, optional leather, optional ABS and a security system. A minor facelift came for 2000, before the major one in 2004.

The Pagani Huayra supercar made its debut in 2012, to succeed the company's previous offering, the Zonda. Powering the Huayra is a bespoke 6.0-litre twin-turbo, V12 engine developed by Mercedes-AMG.  It uses a 7-speed sequential gearbox and a single disc clutch. The choice not to use a dual-clutch in an oil bath was due to the increase in weight of over 70 kg, thus negating any advantage of the faster gear changes in a double-clutch transmission. As a result, the entire transmission weighs 96 kg. The car is equipped with Brembo brake calipers, rotors and pads. The calipers have four pistons in front and four in the rear. The rotors are drilled carbon ceramic.

The Veracruz is a midsize crossover 4WD that aims for luxury and onroad performance. Hyundai positions the Veracruz as an alternative to luxury crossovers but with a lower price. However, it is still the company's most expensive 4WD model, and base models are pretty bare on safety. The Veracruz is longer and wider than the Santa Fe, and comes standard with three rows of seats for seven passengers on all but the base model. The Veracruz comes in three trim levels here. All are powered by the same 3.8-litre V6 engine mated to a six-speed automatic. All models ride on 17-inch wheels, and come standard with all-wheel-drive and ABS with EBD. Basic features include power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, alarm, CD/MP3 with 6 speakers, manual air-conditioning, side steps, and only a single airbag. The mid-level model adds cruise control, faux leather and a power liftgate. The top model adds xenon headlights, power driver seat, sunroof, rain-sensing wipers, six-CD changer and more speakers, dual-zone a/c, stability control, dual airbags, side airbags and curtain airbags. Navigation is optional, but there is no low-range gearing.

The Cadillac CT5-V is the performance version of the CT5 midsize sedan. Under the hood, gone are the big V8 engines of the old CTS-V and now comes with a 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 engine, mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission. Standard features for the real-wheel-drive CT5 include power windows, power mirrors, LED headlights and tail lamps and fog lamps. Available equipment include Cadillac's updated CUE entertainment system with 10-inch screen and BOSE speakers, magnetic ride control, alloy wheels and adaptive forward lighting. Safety features include ABS and traction control, sensors to warn driver of potential dangers, safety seat alert which sends immediate impulse through the seat cushion from the direction of the potential hazard.

The Mercedes-Benz R-Class got a facelift in 2011. Packed under the hood are rather powerful engines, but that hardly makes it a sporting vehicle. Models from 2011 onwards include the new R 300, the R 350 and the upgraded R 500, most available only in long-wheelbase trim here. Amazingly, it is very hard to tell the difference between long and short models. Originally available only as a luxurious six-seater, the R-Class is now optionally available with five or seven seats too. Sadly, few on the road recognise its eccentricity and price tag, so it gets as much respect in public as a typical cargo hauler. Features include a 7-speed automatic transmission, cruise control with variable speed limiter, automatic climate control and all-wheel-drive. Options include a panoramic sunroof, air suspension and navigation. Standard safety features include the anticipatory occupant protection system PRE-SAFE, a complete restraint system with eight airbags, crash-responsive NECK-PRO front head restraints, a tyre pressure loss warning system and adaptive brake lights.
