The GLS uses 4MATIC, the permanent Mercedes-Benz four-wheel drive system, with special off-road features such as Downhill Speed Regulation (DSR), hill-start assist and off-road ABS assist. The package includes a two-speed transfer case with a low range ratio and 100 percent differential locks for the transfer case and the rear axle. The GLS 63 AMG comes with a 5.5-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. Equipped with the third-row individual seats, the GLS-Class is a full-size seven-seater. Either one or both seats can be electrically folded to create a continuously level load floor. All the usual Mercedes-Benz safety and luxury power features are included in this one too.

The Patrol is Nissan's most capable 4WD in its lineup. It is a big 4WD that dates back to the 1992 version, relaunched with a new skin in 1998. It has garnered a reputation as an excellent off-road vehicle in the Middle East, even though it has been fighting a losing battle with the overrated Toyota Land Cruiser for decades now. It is also popular for its reasonable on-road ride, though its handling leaves a lot to be desired. The 4.8-litre inline six-cylinder came for 2002, alongside the older 4.5-litre inline-six which eats more fuel, and the frugal diesel 4.2-litre inline-six. A 4-speed automatic with manual sequential shift facility is available on petrol models alongside the 5-speed manual. The latest updates give the Patrol an edgier new front end and freshened rear end. Straight-line drive transfer allows on-the-fly shifting from 2WD to 4WD with one touch of a lever. The latest Patrol has an all-new interior featuring better quality materials and more equipment. Along with two foldout cargo-area seats, it has room for seven. Front airbags are standard, among other features.

The Mercedes-Benz S 63 AMG Coupe made its debut as a 2015 model year and replaces the CL65 AMG. It is still motivated by a 5.5-litre twin-turbocharged V8, but produces more power than its predecessor. The engine can be coupled with rear-wheel-drive, as well as an AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 7-speed automatic transmission. There's also an AMG sports exhaust system with logic-controlled exhaust flaps that produces the desired sound according to the situation. Safety features include Active Parking Assist, Active Lane Keeping Assist, Night View Assist Plus, Distronic Plus with Steering Assist, Brake Assist Plus with Cross-Traffic Assist and Pre-Safe Brake with pedestrian recognition.

PGO proclaims itself to be a 'French automobile craftsman' to highlight their hand-crafted aspect and small-scale production. The CÃ©vennes got slight facelift and improvements in 2013. Both share the same technical foundation and differ only in style, with the CÃ©vennes looking more modern with restyled bumpers and trim. Indeed, the overall styling is still based on the 1950s Porsche 356. However, it is powered by a recent 2.0-litre 4-cylinder Peugeot engine, with no additional tuning. The rear-mounted motor is mated to a rear-wheel-drive platform and a choice of 5-speed manual or 4-speed automatic. While the car is very basic and very expensive, customisation options offer 15 paintjobs, 8 soft-top colours, 14 types of leather and 10 types of carpet. Standard features include a basic a/c, power windows, 17-inch alloy wheels, CD/MP3 stereo with 2 speakers, keyless entry, electric mirrors, black manual soft top and a set of eight instrumentation gauges. Options include chrome wheels, two-tone leather, CD changer, alarm and more.

The Altima received a face-lift for the 2013 model. They still get the same 2.5-litre 4-cylinder and 3.5-litre V6 engine from the previous shape, along with CVT transmissions. Features included in the base 2.5 S include ABS, traction-control, vehicle stability control, remote keyless entry with Push Button Ignition, radio with CD player with Aux-in and 4 speakers, audio controls on steering wheel and dual airbags. The 2.5 SV adds to that cruise control, 6-speaker audio system with 5-inch display, bluetooth, USB port with iPod connectivity, rear-view camera, auto-headlamps, parking sensors, fog lamps and 17-inch alloy rims. Moving up to 2.5 SL,  additional features include 6-way power seats, dual zone auto A/C, side and curtain airbags and remote engine start. For the V6, the 3.5 SV is the same options as 2.5 SV but included are paddle shifters on the steering column. The 3.5 SL gets leather seats, driver 8-way power seat, lumbar support, Bose audio system with 9 speakers, sunroof, xenon head lamps and LED tail lamps. The top SL versions can be specced out with a navigation system.

Finally making its official debut in the GCC, the rally-bred Subaru Impreza WRX STI landed for the 2008 model year with a hatchback-only body and no warranty. By 2010, it could finally be bought with a warranty. The sedan came for 2011. The standard engine is a 2.5-litre turbocharged and intercooled horizontally-opposed 4-cylinder, mated to a 6-speed manual and Subaru's 'symmetrical' all-wheel-drive system. In 2011, a minor range-wide facelift debuted along with the sedan, as well as a 5-speed automatic option. An SI-DRIVE system offers three modes, namely Intelligent, Sport, and Sport Sharp, with the first mode reducing power and improving fuel economy. The 'Driver Controlled Center Differential,' also known as DCCD, has three automatic modes in addition to allowing manual torque-split adjustment. The VDC stability control system can be left on, fully turned off, or set to a sport mode. Features include ABS-assisted Brembo brakes, LED tail lamps, torque-sensitive limited slip differential, 18-inch alloy wheels, front airbags, side-curtain airbags, keyless entry with starter button, retractable headlight washers, common power accessories and a CD stereo, with options such as Recaro sport seats and navigation. However, options lists keep changing every year, depending on what the dealers choose to bring in.

The SC 430 switches from luxury hardtop coupe to open roadster at the touch of a button. Dropping the power hardtop turns it into a true convertible, but the SC is far from a sporting vehicle. Its exterior and interior were freshened for 2006. This rear-wheel drive car is powered by a 4.3-litre V8 engine mated to a new six-speed automatic transmission and soft comfort-biased suspension. It comes as one model that features a power retractable hardtop, soft leather with wood and chrome accents, a navigation system and a Mark Levinson audio with nine speakers, 6-CD changer, a/c system that auto-adjusts temperature for top-up and top-down, eight-way power adjustable front seats with memory function, power door mirrors, Bluetooth mobile phone, HID headlamps with adaptive front-lighting system and auto-leveling system, LED tail lamps, rear spoiler, front and rear corner sensors, and 18-inch aluminium wheels. Safety features include dual front & side airbags, whiplash injury lessening concept seats, ABS brakes with EBD and Brake Assist, Vehicle Stability Control, traction control, and a tyre pressure warning system.

The new-for-2008 A5 is an all-new four-seater coupe by Audi that is based on the new stretched A4 platform. The A5 incorporates many elements from the Nuvolari concept of 2003, including Audi's trademark loudmouth grille framed by rectangular headlights, a very thick C-pillar, frameless windows, and a waistline that flows upwards around the wheel arches to give the car a dynamic, sporty character. The Audi A5 is powered by a 3.2-litre FSI V6 engine. Power is delivered through a CVT transmission for the front-wheel-drive version, and a 6-speed tiptronic auto transmission for the Quattro all-wheel-drive version. Technology includes partial LED lighting, an electromechanical parking brake, an all-plastic key and three-zone climate control, along with all the usual luxury features, such as power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and leather upholstery. Safety features include multiple airbags, ABS and stability control. The new platform moves the engine more rearward in relation to the front axle for better balance and handling, but ultimately the car loses out on the fun factor in any form, either due to its front-driven underpinnings or to its overly-safe Quattro system.

The Jeep Grand Cherokee SRT gets a name-change to only "SRT" for 2014, as well as a 6.4-litre V8, 8-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive with no low-range. In 2020, it got a minor facelift in front, along with a slight power bump. Other features include an 8.4-inch touchscreen display and 7-inch customer configurable multiview cluster display. The 2020 Jeep Grand Cherokee SRT features include real leather upholstery, stitched-leather dash trim, ventilated power-adjustable front seats, 9-speaker audio with subwoofer and 20-inch wheels, with various options and accessories available. The SRT8 version gets a unique body kit, sports suspension, sports seats and other trim bits. Safety features in the 2019 Jeep Grand Cherokee SRT include standard active head restraints, front airbags, full-length side-curtain and seat-mounted side airbags, stability control, electronic roll mitigation, hill-start assist and optional trailer-sway control. An optional blind-spot/rear cross-path detection system and adaptive cruise control with forward collision warning are also available.

The Cadillac XT4 is the luxury brand's compact SUV offering. It comes equipped with a 2.0-litre turbocharged engine, which is the only engine option, and a 9-speed automatic transmission. Standard features in the XT4 include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, push start button, AM/FM stereo with 8-inch diagonal color information display, 7 speakers, Bluetooth, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, parking sensors with rear camera, sunroof, LED headlamps and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment includes Bose Sound System, "Technology Package" which includes Air Ionizer, 8-inch diagonal color reconfigurable gauge cluster, head-up display, power rake, and telescoping steering column and wireless charging, 20-inch diamond cut alloy wheels, interior ambient lighting, navigation, AM/FM stereo with connected navigation providing real-time traffic, 8” diagonal color information display, one type A and one type C full function USBs, personalized profiles for each driver’s settings, Natural Voice Recognition (English only) and NFC (Near Field Communications) mobile device pairing. Safety features include airbags - dual-stage frontal, knee and seat-mounted side-impact for driver and front passenger; head-curtain for all outboard seating positions with rollover protection, stability control, traction control, tyre pressure monitor and ABS. Optional safety features include "Driver Awareness Package", which includes Low Speed Forward Automatic Braking, Front Pedestrian Braking, Following Distance Indicator, Forward Collision Alert, Lane Keep Assist with Lane Departure Warning and IntelliBeam. Also available is a "Driver Assist Package", which includes Adaptive Cruise Control, and Forward and Reverse Automatic Braking.

The Patrol is Nissan's most capable 4WD in its lineup. It is smaller than the Armada, but still big enough to qualify as a big 4WD. It has garnered a reputation as an excellent off-road vehicle in the Middle East, even though it has been fighting a losing battle with the overrated Toyota Land Cruiser for decades now. It is also popular for its smooth on-road ride, though its handling leaves a lot to be desired. The latest engine is a 4.8-litre inline six-cylinder, alongside the older 4.5-litre inline-six which eats more fuel, and the frugal diesel 4.2-litre inline-six. A new five-speed automatic with manual sequential shift facility is available on petrol models alongside the manual. The latest updates give the Patrol an edgier new front end and freshened rear end. Straight-line drive transfer allows on-the-fly shifting from 2WD to 4WD with one touch of a lever. The latest Patrol has an all-new interior featuring better quality materials and more equipment. Along with two foldout cargo-area seats, it has room for seven. Front airbags are standard, among other features. After the launch of the all-new 2010 model, this older version continued to be sold briefly in a stripped-down format at a lower base price.

Built by Noble Automotive, the M600 is a handbuilt British supercar that debuted in 2009. Utilising materials such as stainless steel, aluminium and carbon-fibre, the M600 is powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.4-litre V8 from the Volvo XC90 that was originally developed by Yamaha. There are driver-selectable settings that vary the power, fed through an Italian-sourced 6-speed manual to the rear wheels. The 2-seater cabin is tight and impractical, while using premium leather upholstery and offering a basic stereo. Wheels are 19-inch up front and 20-inch in the back. Safety features are lacking, with traction control and nothing else, not even airbags or ABS for the mildly-assisted steel brakes.

The Nissan Patrol was redesigned from the ground up for 2010, and has been mildly facelifted for 2014. In 2017, the major change was the new V6 engine and no manual option was available. In 2018, everything was pretty much the same. In 2019, the Patrol got a host of new accessories which include fender flares, front and rear diffusers and different roof rails. For 2020, it got a major facelift for the front and back, along with major interior tech upgrades and new exterior colour choices. Engine options include a base 4.0-litre V6 with a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol XE or SE, as well as a 5.6-litre V8 with direct injection and a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol LE. Depending on trim level, the 7-seater Patrol can be had with standard or optional features such as all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing, hydraulic body motion control system for the suspension, computerised terrain response system, climate-controlled leather seats, infotainment with touchscreen, Apple Carplay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, power rear liftgate, keyless start, adaptive cruise control, 20-inch alloy wheels, power-folding 3rd-row seat, around-view cameras, and a centre console cool-box that can be opened from both 1st & 2nd-row seats. Also available is an Off-road Monitor that provides real-time information such as tyre conditions involving steer angle, slip and pressure, as well as hill start, hill descent, and an electronically-locking rear diff. Most models get a regular offroad-ready front bumper, while the top Platinum "City" trim gets a slightly-lower unique bumper. Safety features include two front airbags and numerous side-curtain airbags, stability control and ABS, as well as optional lane-departure warning, tyre-pressure monitor and auto-braking systems.

The Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class is a compact crossover offering. It is powered by a direct-injection 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder mated to a 7-speed "DCT" dual-clutch automanual and a front-wheel-drive or all-wheel drive platform. The 5-seater is offered in one loaded "Sport" spec that includes 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Toyota Hiace has been the market leader for years in the UAE and continues to be a popular choice in the commercial sector, whether for transporting the work-force or cargo. An all-new model came out in 2019. The engine now moves to the front, thereby increasing noise and vibration, as well as heat generated inside the cabin. There is only one engine choice in the Hiace, a 3.5-litre V6 petrol engine mated to a standard 6-speed manual or an optional 6-speed automatic transmission. The Saudi market additionally gets a 2.7-litre turbocharged diesel engine model with a 6-speed manual. It comes in two variants, the Hiace Panel Van version for carrying cargo and the Hiace Commuter which gets back seats to act as a people carrier. Standard features include dual front/rear a/c, an AM/FM cassette player with 2 speakers, power steering, power door locks, toolbox, halogen headlamps, and 15-inch steel wheels. Some markets get optional features such as remote locking. Depending on the market, consumers have the choice of a normal roof or high-roof with a standard or long wheel base-wide body.

The Civic grew up in 1984, in terms of size as well as image. The larger new model looked very modern for its time, making Civic four-doors and wagons identical to the Accord in wheelbase. A new 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine was offered alongside a 1.3-litre 4-cylinder unit on base models. Transmission choices included 4-speed and 5-speed manuals and a 3-speed automatic. The revamped suspension was a temporary step backwards for Honda, since it didn't have an independent rear setup, like in previous and later Civics. But this offered a space-efficient cabin design while retaining reasonable ride and handling characteristics. The lineup consisted of a hatchback, a sedan, a tall Shuttle wagon, and separately, a new CRX sports coupe. The base models were barren, but higher models had sport seats, reclining rear seats, a rear stabilizer bar and more. The Shuttle wagon was later available with all-wheel drive and a six-speed manual gearbox. Changes  in 1986 included a 4-speed automatic. The top-spec Civic hatchback included a removable glass sunroof, a full-width tail-light panel and colour-keyed front airdam and roof spoiler.

The E-Class is the bestseller in the Mercedes-Benz line-up, with its perfect size and luxurious accessories, if optioned out properly. Available in sedan and unpopular wagon body styles, the E-Class comes with a range of petrol and diesel engines, though the diesel engines are close to unwanted in this region. It underwent a pointless facelift recently, but features the same carryover internals. Models include the 1.8-litre supercharged E 200 Kompressor, the 3.0-litre E 280, the 3.5-litre E 350, the new 5.5-litre E 500 and the new 6.2-litre E 63 AMG. All come with automatic transmissions officially, though the base model can be had with a manual. Options include bi-xenon headlamps with Active Light System and cornering light function, COMAND control and display system for radio and navigation, Distronic proximity control, upholstery options, headlamp cleaning system, keyless start, parking sensors, semi-active air suspension, four-zone automatic climate control and a tyre pressure-loss warning system. A new AMG sports package is also available for sedans makes any trim look like the AMG model.

The Dodge Challenger received a minor facelift and new engine upgrades in 2015. The interior has been significantly improved as well. The Challenger utilises retro styling that is largely a rethinking of the original 1970s Challenger's 2-door design. The interior gets upgraded with a bit more gadgetry in the form of an 8.4-inch Uconnect infotainment system and 7-inch customization display between the retro-inspired speedometer and tachometer. With a high-sill center aluminium gauge bezels makes the revamped interior extremely pleasing to the eyes. Through the Uconnect interface, you can now access the all-new Dodge performance pages that allows you to select different driving modes to adjust steering effort, engine and transmission response, electronic stability and traction controls, and standard launch control. It can also be optioned with a forward collision warning, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring and rear cross path detection.Sharing its platform, engine and mechanicals with other fullsize rear-wheel-drive Chrysler cars, the Challenger can be had with a 3.6-litre V6 or a 5.7-litre V8. Standard features in the V6 include sporty suspension, cloth upholstery, alloy wheels, keyless entry with starter button, CD/MP3 stereo, power accessories and not much else. Also available are a sunroof, racing stripes, rear sensors with camera, and the UConnect touchscreen multimedia system with voice controls as well as navigation, hard drive and Bluetooth phone. Safety features include ABS, stability control, front,side and curtain airbags.

The Volvo S60 got a facelift for the 2014 model year. The S60 straddles the line between compact and midsize. Available in the GCC with three engine choices, the entry-level S60 1.6T model comes with a 1.6-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder and front-wheel-drive, available only in certain GCC markets. There is a T5 2.0T which gets a 4-cylinder 2.0-litre turbocharged engine, also in front-wheel drive. The top-spec model is the S60 T6 AWD, with a 3.0-litre turbocharged 6-cylinder engine and all-wheel-drive, and available only in loaded 'Prestige' trim in certain GCC markets.  They all get a 6-speed automatic transmission. The cabin features extensive soft-touch materials and Volvo's trademark 'floating' console in a choice of wood, metal and graphite colours. Base features include cloth upholstery, power windows, electric mirrors, alloy wheels, CD/MP3 stereo, front and side-curtain airbags, keyless entry with starter motor and more. The 'Prestige' model gets larger wheels, leather, navigation, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitor, adaptive HID headlights, sunroof and more. A simple silver body kit is optional. Volvo's unique 'City Safety' feature is standard, whereby the system brakes by itself to avoid hitting cars and pedestrians. A software-based Polestar power upgrade is also offered, adding 20-30 hp, depending on the model.

The new-for-2012 Honda CR-V is an all-new design that is slightly lighter and apparently more aerodynamic. Built in the United States, it comes in LX, EX and EX-Leather flavours. It is still powered by a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder engine with a basic 5-speed automatic transmission, but power has been bumped up a fair bit. Honda now tacks on an improved all-wheel-drive system that still drives the front wheels most of the time but can send torque to the rear wheels anytime, instead of like the old system that used to wait for the front wheels to lose traction and spin first. The 5-seater cabin comes with a quick 60:40 fold-flat rear bench. The LX gets 17-inch alloys, a 4-speaker CD stereo with AUX port, mirror-mounted indicators, ABS, stability control and front airbags. Only the EX and EX-L models get 18-inch wheels, a 6-speaker stereo with USB/AUX ports, cruise control, HID headlights, fog lamps, dual-zone auto a/c, sunroof, Bluetooth, rear camera and an 'i-MID' LCD display. The EX-L itself further gets side-curtain airbags, leather and a power driver's seat.

The Ford Mustang is an icon of American something-or-the-other since its 1964 introduction, popular for its bold style and affordable price. The Mustang started the "pony car" genre, and now it has gone back to its old styling. The Mustang rides on rear-wheel-drive platform, but it still doesn't have independent rear suspension to the detriment of handling compared to other sports cars. The interior looks good, but is full of cheap plastics. But this car is one of the best performance bargains in town. The Mustang GT boasts a powerful 4.6-litre V8, available with a 5-speed manual or a 5-speed automatic. The new-for-2005 Mustang was sold only in GT form here. Standard equipment includes four-wheel disc brakes with four-channel ABS and all-speed traction control, dual exhausts, front fog lamps, a rear spoiler, tilt steering wheel, 17-inch painted cast aluminium wheels with Z-rated performance tyres, power mirrors, AM/FM stereo with a single-CD player, air bags, power door locks with remote keyless entry, and power windows. Options include the Shaker 500-watt audio system with 6-disc CD player and MP3 capability, among other things.

The MG RX5 is the Chinese-British brand’s offering of a compact crossover. There will be a choice of two well-equipped trims with two available powertrains, namely a 1.5-litre with a 7-speed automatic and a 2.0-litre with a 6-speed automatic, both turbocharged. The front-wheel-drive 2019 MG RX5 is available with LED headlamps, two-tone 18-inch rims, high-quality cabin finish including soft-touch surfaces, opening panoramic sunroof, adjustable fold-flat rear seats with split/fold function, power tailgate, keyless entry, a start button and an auto-hold brake function. A remote smart app allows the driver to operate vehicle functions such as remote start and stop air conditioning, vehicle tracking and aftersales appointments, even reminding owners of the services needed for the car. There is a 10.4-inch high-definition infotainment touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and navigation on the 2.0T version and an 8-inch colour navigation system for 1.5T models. The 2019 MG RX5 comes with standard ESP and traction control, a curving braking control system and more. Passive safety features include a strengthened body structure that uses thermal formed steel, multiple airbags, automatic unlocking in the event of a collision and a collapsible steering column, all of which has helped the MG RX5 earn a 5-star rating in the Chinese C-NCAP crash tests.

The GAC GS5 is the Chinese brand's compact crossover SUV offering. Under the hood, it gets two 4-cylinder engine choices, which is the naturally aspirated 2.0-litre motor and the turbocharged 1.8-litre unit. They both can be had in either a 5-speed manual transmission or a 5-speed automatic transmission. While the 2.0-litre version is front-wheel drive, the 1.8-litre turbocharged version can be had in four-wheel-drive as well. Standard feature for the GS5 include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, fog lamps, parking sensors, AM/FM radio with CD/AUX/USB support, 6 speakers, fabric seats, automatic A/C with dual-zone, rear A/C vents and manual seats. The higher models get leather seats, power seats, sunroof and audio controls on steering wheels. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, ABS brakes and EBD.

After a decade, Toyota launched a redesigned Land Cruiser for the 2008 model year, and 2012 marked its first major makeover. The updated Land Cruiser comes with the choice of an upgraded 4.0-litre "Dual VVT-i" V6 with either a 5-speed manual or a 5-speed auto, an all-new 4.6-litre "Dual VVT-i" V8 with a 6-speed auto, and a 5.7-litre version with a 6-speed automatic. A rare 4.5-litre turbodiesel V8 is discontinued in UAE, but continues to be offered in Saudi Arabia, with the 6-speed automatic version getting more power than the 5-speed manual version. The Land Cruiser can transport as many as eight or nine passengers with its variable seating configurations. Available features include power windows and mirrors, cruise control, sunroof, 17-inch alloy or steel wheels on lower models, standard smart keyless entry with start/stop button, standard parking sensors with optional rear camera, multi-information display, optional cooler box, three rows of seats, optional four-zone climate control, optional leather, standard CD/MP3 stereo with CD changer, optional rear DVD screens, and Bluetooth among other items. New features for 2012 include bi-xenon headlights with integrated LEDs, new rear lights and new front bumper on all models, as well as a front chin spoiler, 18-inch wheels and a new multimedia system on V8 models. Higher models get navigation, crawl control with tight-turn assist, four-camera view and a multi-terrain selection system. In the UAE, there are three trim levels as well as a stripped-down safari fleet model. Dual front airbags and ABS are standard, with side-curtain airbags available on all but the most basic models, while knee airbags and stability control with hill-assist are available on V8 models only.
For 2021, an all-new Mercedes-Benz S-Class came out.

An all new Mercedes-Benz SL Class was released for 2012. The new design features a complete new aluminium body, so it is lighter than its predecessor. Also the new generation SL Class is wider and longer. The SL 65 AMG comes with a turbocharged 6.0-litre V12, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include front airbags and head-thorax sidebags, ABS brakes, automatic climate control with dust filter and air recirculation, automatic steering wheel with adjustment on entry and exit, brake assist, central locking, cruise control with variable speed limiter, stability control, xenon headlights, leather upholstery, light-alloy wheels, CD radio with 8 speakers and more.

The Clio was completely redesigned in 2006, but this new version is only available in the GCC in sporting form. The two versions available are the Renault-Sport Clio 197 RS and the Renault-Sport Clio F1 Team R27. As confusing as the naming system is, the RS is the generic model and the F1 is a special-edition model with red Brembo four-piston brake calipers, yellow paint and various "F1 Team" and "world champion" stickers. Both the RS and the F1 versions of the Clio Renault-Sport models will be sold in limited numbers across the GCC, due to low demand rather than to maintain exclusivity. Derived from the basic New Clio available in Europe, both the Renault-Sport cars are powered by a highly-tuned 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with a 6-speed manual gearbox. Renault says the cars were apparently tested locally to ensure suitability for local driving conditions, and fitted with air-conditioning systems to suit the local heat. Apart from the bright yellow paint finish which is exclusively for the R27 model, both cars will also be available in various colours. The yellow paint finish, red Brembo four-piston brake calipers at the front, Recaro seats and its exclusive stickers are the only differences that set the Clio F1 Team R27 apart from the RS 197. The F1 also benefits from BeBop 17-inch smoked wheels and a numbered plate alongside the handbrake. There is no spare tyre due to the dual-exhaust setup. Safety features include stability and traction control with "off" switch, ABS brakes, up to eight airbags, and energy-absorbing head restraints.

The Jaguar F-Type Coupe hit showrooms in mid-2014, joining the range almost a year after the Roadster's launch. In 2020, it got a facelift, along with power and interior upgrades. It comes with a supercharged 3.0-litre engine V6 as well as with a supercharged 5.0-litre V8. A new detuned version of the V8 was introduced in 2020 but currenly not available in the GCC. In 2018, a 2.0-litre turbo joined the lineup as well. The F-Type comes standard in rear-wheel drive from, but from 2016, the R versions were available in optional all-wheel-drive, then later on as only all-wheel drive. Components include adaptive dampers and adjustable suspension settings, several aluminium body bits, rear-wheel-drive and a unique 8-speed automatic with paddle-shifters. Standard options include engine start/stop function, bi-xenon headlamps, power windows, LED daytime running lights, 8 or 10-speaker entertainment system, USB port, Bluetooth phone and streaming, several airbags, power tailgate and a retractable rear wing spoiler. Further available features include optional sports seats, dual-zone a/c, customisable colours for cabin trim, power-adjustable seats and steering, cruise control and more. The F-Type R Coupe additionally gets a new electronic active differential and a torque vectoring system, as well as larger brakes with optional carbon-ceramic discs.

Tougher than most compact 4WDs, the Jeep Cherokee, also known as the Liberty in some markets, seats five people and can carry their gear too. Powered by a 3.7-litre V6, it is just about adequate for the streets. Early models got a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic, while post-facelift models got the automatic or a 6-speed manual. Fold the rear seats and it can move two people and some serious cargo. Turn off the pavement, and it can negotiate most trails with confidence. All-new for 2002, the Cherokee was extensively updated for 2005. From 2006, all models come with Jeep's Electronic Stability Program, ABS brakes, Electronic Roll Mitigation, and all-speed traction control. Standard on all models is Command-Trac, a conventional part-time four-wheel-drive system with a two-speed transfer case. Full-time Selec-Trac is optional, and retains a low range for serious off-roading. Standard features also include power windows, power mirrors, remote keyless entry, six-speaker AM/FM/CD stereo, grey fender flares, 16-inch steel wheels and traction control. Options include leather, cruise control, 16-inch aluminium wheels, fog lamps, body-colour fender flares, roof rails, functional rock rails and more.

The Volvo V40 is the Swedish company's 5-door hatchback offering, facelifted for 2017 with new headlights and other minor trim changes. The only version offered in most GCC markets is the V40 T5 now, fitted with a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder for the Middle East. Variants beyond the regular V40 include the V40 R-Design model with a sporty body kit and unique wheels and a Polestar version with more power. All versions are front-wheel-drive. Features include fuel-saving auto start-stop tech, power windows, electric mirrors, CD/MP3 stereo, cloth or leather upholstery, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and other basics, with options such as HID headlights, sunroof, navigation and all that. Safety standards are always high in Volvos, and the V40 is no exception. Safety features, aside from the standard front and side-curtain airbags, include a world-first pedestrian airbag, blind spot monitoring, lane-keeping aid with haptic auto steering, pedestrian detection with auto braking, and a Park Assist Pilot system that makes parallel parking easy.

The Rio is Kia's sub-compact nameplate that started life in 2000. It can always be depended on for the most unique exterior designs in this segment. This generation of the Rio debuted in 2006 and received a minor frontal facelift in 2010, before being replaced in 2012. The interior offers decent space for its size, although the cabin is a hard plastic tomb, like most others in its class. Powered by a 1.4-litre four-cylinder engine mated to either a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic, this front-wheel-drive runabout comes in either sedan or hatchback body styles. Standard features include manual air-conditioning, 14-inch steel wheels with full wheel covers, battery saver, wind-up windows and AM/FM radio cassette player. Higher models add a few items, such as body-coloured outer trimmings and power windows, along with electric mirrors, front fog lamps, driver's seat height adjustability, luggage undertray and central door locks. We could not verify what safety features are available besides seat belts, although we believe many markets get ABS brakes and front airbags, standard or otherwise.

The F430 is heavily influenced by F1 Racing technology, and makes it known to everyone openly. The F430's compact 4.3-litre V8 engine offers blistering high-revving performance, and the experience is enhanced by an optional F1-style paddle-shifting gearbox which has made its way to every other Ferrari model too. The F430's aerodynamics are honed to generate special flows to increase downforce and improve cooling. One technical feature is the electronic differential, transferring massive torque levels to the track under high cornering g-forces, and guarantees maximum grip out of bends, eliminating wheel spin. The larger interior can be personalized with carbon-fibre or aluminium inserts, with space behind the seats accessed using an electrically operated compartment. The standard electric seats can be substituted by more sporting items with four-point harnesses to order. Even with all this the interior is noticeably barebones in keeping with its sporting nature. For 2008, a more powerful, lighter and track-focussed F430 Scuderia was introduced, with a faster clutchless-manual gearbox and other chassis enhancements.

The Renault Koleos is a compact SUV designed by Renault and developed by Nissan. It is manufactured by Renault Samsung Motors, a subsidiary of Renault, at its plant in South Korea. Based on a Nissan platform, the Koleos was facelifted with a new front-end for 2012, but still uses a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder mated to a CVT automatic gearbox. Though it may look like an offroader, this mildly-lifted crossover comes standard with front-wheel-drive in the base trim, while basic all-wheel-drive system is standard on the higher trim levels, with 50:50 lock but without low-range gearing. Available equipment, depending on trim level, includes cruise control, alloy wheels, CD/MP3 sound system, automatic air-conditioning, rain-sensing wipers, automatic headlights, rear parking sensors, power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and an automatic electronic parking brake. Stability control, ABS, front airbags and side-curtain airbags helped the Koleos achieve a 5-star crash test rating in Europe.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class is essentially the new facelifted M-Class following the German brand's new nomenclature. Mercedes-AMG GLE 63 is the top performance model and gets more power and torque in 2016. There are two variants, which includes the standard GLE 63 and then the GLE 63 S. Under the hood, both come with the 5.5-litre turbocharged V8 engine, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive. Available features include adjustable air suspension, adaptive cruise control and active parking assist. The exterior features HID headlights, LED running maps and 21-inch cross-spoke AMG alloy wheels. The 5-seater interior offers leather upholstery, mood lighting, HDD navigation, panoramic sunroof, rear entertainment system, keyless start, ventilated power front seats and a split-folding rear seat. Safety features include nine airbags, stability control, ABS and drowsiness monitor, with options such as a rear view camera with parking sensors, active lane assist, blind-spot monitor and automatic pre-crash braking.

The Scirocco is revival of Volkswagen's odd-shaped 1970s model that attempted to bridge the gap between a hatchback and a coupe. It last died out in 1992, until its revival as a concept car in 2006 and a production car by 2008. Debuting in the GCC as a 'sportier' alternative to the VW Golf, the Scirocco lifts platforms, engines and even interior panels from the Golf. However, the cabin itself has a lower roofline while retaining seating for four. Engine for the Scirocco R is a higher tuned 2.0-litre FSI turbocharged 4-cylinder. It first became available in 2012, with more power, a body kit and firmer suspension. This Portugese-built front-wheel-drive hatchback gets the usual power accessories, along with available panoramic sunroof, CD/MP3 stereo, HID headlights, front-side airbags, climate control, keyless entry, stability control, ABS and such. The VW Scirocco also gets an optional three-mode adaptive chassis control, offering the driver a choice of sport and comfort that affects suspension and steering tune.

Originally introduced in Malaysia back in 1993, the Wira was based on the early-90s Mitsubishi Lancer, and continued in its early form all the way to the new century, and ending up being the most outdated car on the market. Available as a sedan or a liftback, the engine and gearbox were sourced from Mitsubishi, namely a 1.5-litre and a 1.6-litre, both 4-cylinder. The smaller engine came with a 5-speed manual or a 3-speed automatic, while the larger one came standard with a 4-speed auto. Features included cloth interior, manual or power windows, radio-cassette player, optional sunroof, optional spoiler, and not much else. Safety features were limited to seat-belts in early models, with later ones receiving a driver-side airbag, ABS brakes and safety-bars in the doors. As unrefined as the car is, proven Mitsubishi mechanicals under the skin means on-road reliability is as good as most Japanese cars, although the car itself will be falling apart from the inside out, starting with the cheap cabin trim. The car flopped in the GCC region, except in places like Kuwait, where it was marketed as a commercial vehicle.

The Australian-built Chevrolet Caprice remains largely unchanged since a redesign in 2007, and currently only one engine is on offer, namely the 6.0-litre V8 with cylinder-deactivation. There are four variants to choose from, starting with the LS and the LTZ, and topping out with the sport-tuned SS and the more luxury-inclined Royale. The Caprice gets a 6-speed automatic transmission for all their models. The Royale has a chrome grille while the SS has a monochromatic paint job, whilst all models now have LED brake-lamps that increase in intensity depending upon the brake pressure applied. Available features include front and rear proximity sensors, optional twin DVD screens, satellite navigation, power features, leather interior, 16-inch to 18-inch alloy wheels, AM/FM radio with CD/MP3/USB support, Bluetooth and more. The Chevrolet MyLink infotainment system is standard on SS and Royale models, and includes a 7-inch touchscreen with stereo, navigation, CD/MP3 player and a USB port. Safety features include driver and passenger side airbags, ABS brakes and traction control.

The Nissan Micra made its entry into the GCC market for the first time in 2012. A facelifted version became available for 2019. Based on a shortened Sunny sub-compact platform, the Micra hatchback comes only in 5-door form, with a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a 4-speed automatic. The base model gets 14-inch steel wheels, folding rear bench seat, rear fog lamp, intermittent front and rear wipers, basic CD/MP3 stereo with AUX port, trip computer, manual a/c, power steering with tilt adjustment, alarm and fabric upholstery. There are fewer trim levels from 2014 onwards, with higher trims having features such as power windows, split-folding rear seat with three headrests, 15-inch alloy wheels, chrome exterior trim, auto headlights, remote locks or smart keyless entry with starter button, auto wipers, front fog lamps, tachometer, height-adjustable driver's seat with centre armrest, rear window defroster, 12V power outlet, and sunvisors with vanity mirrors. Optional accessories include a chrome grille, body kit, chrome exhaust tip, rear spoiler, mirror-mounted indicators, mud guards and floor mats. Standard safety features include ABS with EBD, brake assist, dual front airbags, and 3-point seatbelts for all five seats.

The M6 Coupe uses a twin-turbocharged 4.4-litre V8, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automanual gearbox. Fuel economy is apparently better by 30% compared to the old V10-powered model. Other mechanical features include BMW's electronically-controlled Active M Differential, massive 16.1-inch carbon-ceramic rotors in front with blue 6-piston calipers, 15.6-inch rotors in the back with a single-piston caliper, M-specific 19-inch alloys with 265/40 ultra-high performance tyres in front and 295/35 tyres in the rear, with 20-inch available as an option, and a carbon-fibre roof. The M6 features both Brake Energy Regeneration and the Auto Start-Stop function. It comes equipped with Cornering Brake Control, Dynamic Brake Control, Brake Assistant, Brake Fade Compensation function, a Brake Drying function and Start-off Assistant.

The Liana is pitched into the ultra-competitive compact segment. It was introduced as a 2002 model, and mildly facelifted for 2005. The only model offered here is the 1.6-litre four-cylinder version with either a manual or an automatic. It can be fully equipped with air-conditioning, ABS brakes, dual airbags, CD stereo, full electrics, keyless entry and an engine immobiliser. The interior has undergone a respectable makeover, with a new quality look, new materials and better bolstered front seats. Front seat occupants will enjoy the airy cabin. The seats are supportive and well contoured, and even rear passengers are not lacking for headroom or legroom. The high seating position contributes to good visibility. The luggae trunk is not particularly roomy, but split-fold rear seats allow more load space. There are faux aluminium and chrome highlights all over, while optional accesories include a rear spoiler and alloy wheels. The Liana used to come in sedan and hatchback body styles in other markets, but in its final years, only the sedan survived in most markets. European and American markets get larger engine choices.

The range-topping M6 arrived for 2006, in coupe and convertible form, using the same V10 engine as the M5. Unlike that of the new 5-Series and 7-Series models, the styling of the new 6 Series has generally received a warm welcome from the public, for unknown reasons. The new 6-Series was designed to look like a shark, and really does remind you of one, but it is far from good-looking. The controversial "Bangle-butt" rear styling works somewhat better on the shapely 6-Series than on other BMW models though. The 6-Series has become the vehicle of choice for rich town-cruising yuppies, but it is actually an excellent performance car, available with a 7-speed SMG automanual in the M6. A mild facelift came for the 2008 model, adding minor gadgetry updates.

The Acadia is GMC's first crossover wagon that combines car-like handling with the utility of a 4WD wagon, offering three rows of seating for up to eight passengers. The design consists of polished aluminium roof rails, projector beam headlights, LED taillights and a rear spoiler. First introduced in 2007, the Acadia got an upgrade under the bonnet in 2009, with a slightly more powerful 3.6-litre V6 with variable valve timing, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission and an optional all-wheel-drive system with no low range. The interior features a "low and away" instrument panel and a Smart Slide second-row feature allows easier access to the third row. Features include power windows, CD/MP3 stereo with six speakers, electric mirrors, keyless entry and more. Optional features include rear-seat DVD entertainment, HID headlights, sunroof, parking sensors, leather seats, tri-zone climate control and more. Standard safety features includes StabiliTrak stability control system with rollover mitigation technology, six airbags and a tyre-pressure-monitoring system. Also standard is power-assisted rack-and-pinion steering, 18-inch wheels with optional 19-inchers, and four-wheel disc brakes with ABS. An Acadia Denali version debuted for 2011, with identical drivetrains as the base model, but with 20-inch wheels, unique front and rear bumpers, chrome mesh grille and upgraded interior trim.

The new Challenger marked the return of the legendary muscle-car nameplate from Dodge. Unfamiliar to GCC residents, but revered by American enthusiasts, the Challenger utilises retro styling that is largely a rethinking of the original 1970s Challenger's 2-door design. Sold only in top-spec SRT-8 trim with a steep GCC price tag, the Challenger isn't the affordable muscle it used to be back in the day. Sharing its platform, engine and mechanicals with other fullsize rear-wheel-drive Chrysler cars, the Challenger packs a 6.1-litre Hemi V8 mated to an aging 5-speed automatic with manual-shift functionality. Standard features include sporty suspension, bi-xenon headlights, leather-alcantara sport seats, keyless entry with starter button, CD stereo, and 20-inch aluminium-alloy wheels, along with the usual accessories such as automatic a/c, cruise control, power windows and electric mirrors. Also available are a sunroof, racing stripes, rear sensors with camera, and the UConnect touchscreen multimedia system with voice controls as well as navigation, hard drive and Bluetooth phone. Safety features include ABS, stability control, front and side airbags, and big honking Brembo brakes. Too bad a high price and a non-existent marketing campaign will make the Challenger a rarity on local roads.

The Volkswagen Jetta underwent a full redesign for 2011, growing in size to offer class-leading interior space. The only engine on offer is an old 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a manually-shiftable 6-speed automatic transmission and front-wheel-drive. There are three trim levels, named Trendline, Comfortline and Comfortline Plus. The base Trendline comes with keyless entry, 8-speaker CD/MP3 stereo, power windows, electric mirrors, cloth upholstery and 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps. The Comfortline additionally comes with chrome trim, 16-inch alloy wheels, dual-zone a/c, steering-wheel buttons, fog lamps, alarm system and parking sensors. The top Comfortline Plus version comes with 17-inch alloys, intelligent keyless entry and starter button, electric-adjustable sports seats with partial leather, and a touchscreen audio system. All VW Jetta models come with ABS, traction control, six airbags and auto hazard lights as standard.

The Mountaineer is supposed to be a more upscale version of the Ford Explorer, and it certainly looks like it from the outside. It shares its structure and most major components with the Explorer, but apparently it shares a lot of the interior as well, thus diminishing brand differences. The Mountaineer is also powered by the Explorer's 4.0-litre V6, mated to a five-speed automatic, but it loses low-range gearing for its four-wheel-drive system The interior theoretically offers seating for up to eight people with three rows of seats, with a third-row seat that can fold flat. Standard interior features include a CD stereo, power windows and mirrors, available CD changer and sunroof, cruise control, available leather upholstery, and standard alloy wheels. The Mountaineer also builds on Ford's strong safety offerings, offering standard AdvanceTrac with Roll Stability Control, ABS brakes, dual front airbags and a tyre-pressure monitoring system, while the Safety Canopy side-curtain airbag system is optional.

The MX-5, also known as the Miata, is a popular rear-wheel-drive roadster from Mazda. Completely overhauled for the 2016 model year, this purebred sports car is now powered by an all-new SkyActiv-G 2.0-litre four-cylinder motor, and mated to a 6-speed SkyActiv-Drive automatic transmission with paddle-shifters. There is a 6-speed manual variant available elsewhere, which is not offered in the GCC at the moment. Featuring the usual soft-top passed down from its predecessors, there is also a retractable hard-top variant known as the MX-5 RF (Retractable Fastback) available from 2017 model year. Besides a few kilos of weight, there are no significant differences between the soft and hard top variants, even in terms of performance. Interior features include CD/MP3 stereo with six-disc changer and 9 Bose speakers, power windows and mirrors, auto a/c, power steering, leather seats, smart-key for keyless entry and ignition, auto-dimming rear-view mirror, navigation, and cruise control. Additional features include chrome outer door handles, LED headlights, fog lamps, dual exhaust tips, and 17-inch alloy wheels with run-flat tyres. Safety features include dual front airbags and side airbags, ABS brakes, traction control, blind-spot monitoring, stability control, tyre pressure monitor, burglar alarm with immobiliser, and rollover hoops behind the seats.

The Expedition is a full-size 4WD that has yet to blaze a trail in the Middle East. It's smooth, stable and refined for the most part, and this new version goes head-to-head with Chevrolet's non-descript Tahoe for top honours among American 4WDs. Its four-wheel-independent suspension is unusually sophisticated in this class, providing better ride and handling, on-road and off. The Expedition comes with a 5.4-litre V8 engine mated to an automatic gearbox. Expedition is loaded with safety features, and offers an available Roll Stability Control system, which is designed to sense an approaching rollover situation then take action to help prevent it. What the Expedition does best is move large quantities of people and gear, with its perfectly flat cargo area and available PowerFold third-row seat that folds perfectly flat with the press of a button. Able to carry up to eight passengers, the second row features a small center seat that slides forward to give parents in the front seat access to a small child. Options include a rear-seat DVD system and the reverse sensors, among the many standard power features. The longer Expedition EL model has a stretched wheelbase to offer more space.

The 2-door Cerato Koup comes with a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with a 4-speed automatic. In 2011, it got a 6-speed automatic. The interior feature in the Cerato that Kia is proud of seems to be a new "super vision" LCD cluster with reddish lighting with warning-message and trip-computer functionality. at the bottom of the cluster. Also available is a basic four-speaker audio system, with the option of six-speaker system that adds tweeters, plus a choice of three radio/CD players and the option of MP3 and iPod connectivity. Standard are power windows, electric mirrors, 15-inch wheels with hubcaps, cloth upholstery and central locking. Other available features in higher models include 17-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry with starter button, automatic a/c, some chrome exterior trim, "super vision" gauge cluster, fog lamps, sunroof, leather steering wheel with audio controls, rear parking sensors, aluminium pedals and automatic headlights. Safety is being downplayed again, as the basic Cerato comes with a single driver's airbag. The higher model gets ABS, active headrests and rear disc brakes instead of drums. Side-curtain airbags and stability control, though not initially available, became standard on the top-spec model later.

The second-generation SLK, a hard-top convertible, boasts a better-looking design than its limited competition from Germany. Several details take their cue from Formula 1, like its arrow-shaped nose. The range starts with the 1.8-litre supercharged SLK 200 Kompressor, and goes up to V6 models such as the 3.0-litre SLK 280 and the new 3.5-litre SLK 350, while Mercedes-AMG builds the top 5.4-litre SLK 55 AMG. Standard equipment includes light-alloy wheels of various sizes, projection-beam headlamps, LED tail-lights, manual six-speed transmission on non-AMG models, stability control, remote control locking system and cruise control. Options, standard on high-spec models, include 18-inch alloy wheels, AMG bodystyling, Designo upholstery, sports suspension, speed-sensitive power steering, steering wheel gearshift buttons for the optional automatic transmission, bi-xenon headlamps with cornering light, parking sensors, electric seats with memory function, infrared remote control for the vario-roof, COMAND navigation system with DVD player, and a Harman/Kardon LOGIC7 surround-sound system with 11 speakers.

All-new in 2007 and facelifted for 2010, the Q7 is the first proper SUV to bear the Audi name. It is based on the same platform as the Volkswagen Touareg and Porsche Cayenne, though it shares mostly drivetrain components. The Q7 is larger in all dimensions than its relatives, and is named after its Quattro all-wheel drive system. The Q7 is available with a 3.6-litre V6 and a 4.2-litre V8 in the GCC, now available with an energy recovery system to run the electrical system. Both come with a six-speed automatic with Tiptronic manual mode. However, both engines were cancelled by 2011 in favour of two 3.0-litre supercharged V6 "TFSI" engines, one more powerful than the other, with only the higher-powered one getting a "supercharged" title. There is a 4.2-litre turbodiesel V8 and a 6.0-litre turbodiesel V12 "TDI" engine available for order as well, for whatever reason. Features include seven-passenger seating which can be optioned to six-passenger by changing the second-row bench to two individual seats. Changes to the 2010 Audi Q7 include new LED headlights and indicators, LED taillights, a chromed front grille, new bumpers, new instrument cluster, ambient lighting and new cabin trim choices, along with new paint colours. Standard features include bi-Xenon headlamps, leather seating surfaces, MMI computer with colour screen, in-dash six-CD changer and Bose premium sound system. Available items include 18-inch and 19-inch alloy wheels, three-panel panorama sunroof, advanced parking system with rearview camera, keyless lock and ignition system, and parking sensors. The Q7 is a proper luxurious 4WD  that can also go off-road, in the vein of the Range Rover models, though it looks a lot like a minivan.

The Pathfinder can be considered a proper off-roading 4WD. It is built on a fullsize pickup platform, thereby offering good off-road capability but marginal on-road handling. The current Pathfinder is significantly larger than previous models. It offers more interior space and more convenience features. It also offers third-row seating to carry up to seven people. The 4.0-litre V6 that powers the Pathfinder is a larger, retuned version of the engine that powers the 350Z. Its five-speed automatic transmission is geared to use the engine's torque characteristics. The 4WD features optional Hill Descent Control, which limits downhill speed without driver intervention, and Hill Start Assist, which briefly holds the Pathfinder on a slope while the driver releases the brake pedal and applies the accelerator. Standard features include fabric upholstery, cruise control, power mirrors, windows and door locks with keyless remote, CD stereo with six speakers, reclining backs on the middle row seats, front and side airbags, ABS and alloy wheels. Options include power seats, halogen foglights, running boards, roof rack cross bars and leather seating. For 2008, the Pathfinder received a very minor facelift, while gaining new available features such as Bluetooth, navigation, rear-seat DVD entertainment and intelligent keyless entry.

An all new Mercedes-Benz SL Class was released for 2012. The new design features a complete new aluminium body, so it is lighter than its predecessor. Also the new generation SL Class is wider and longer. In 2017, it got a slight facelift and power upgrade. The SL 63 AMG comes with a turbocharged 5.5-litre V8 mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include front airbags and head-thorax sidebags, ABS brakes, automatic climate control with dust filter and air recirculation, automatic steering wheel with adjustment on entry and exit, brake assist, central locking, cruise control with variable speed limiter, stability control, xenon headlights, leather upholstery, light-alloy wheels, CD radio with 8 speakers and more. An optional performance package bumps up power by 25 hp, and removes the speed limiter.

The Cerato is Kia's improved new entry in the popular compact field. The front-wheel-drive Cerato can be had as a four-door sedan or a five-door hatchback that looks more like a wagon. Powered by a 1.6-litre four-cylinder or optionally a 2.0-litre four-cylinder, both with either a manual or an automatic, this barebones commuter car has basic standard features like 15-inch steel wheels, radio cassette player with power antenna and 6 speakers, manual cloth seats, halogen headlamps, air-conditioning, front cup holders, intermittent wipers and not much else. Available features include front and rear power windows, central door locking, full wheel covers, impact sensor auto door unlocking, body colour trim, battery saver, and a rear spoiler. We are not quite sure what safety features are available, other than the usual door beams and seat belts. It seems ABS brakes and front airbags might be optional in some markets, standard in others, and not available at all in some places.

The BMW M5 is the performance version of the 5-series and a new model debuted in late 2011 with a highly-tuned 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard equipment include head-Up display, multi-channel audio system, four-zone automatic air conditioning and BMW iDrive control. The M5 gets a unique body kit, hydraulic steering, and simpler sports suspension. The redesigned BMW 5-Series comes with a parking assistant, as well as active cruise control, surround view and rear view camera, lane departure warning, lane change warning and night vision with pedestrian recognition.

From 2014, the Infinti FX model became the QX70 to follow the Japanese brand's new naming structure, but has since remained unchanged. The QX70 is available in four trim levels and two different engines. The Excellence, Luxury and Elite Sport get a 3.7-litre V6 engine, while the Luxury Sport variant gets the 5.0-litre V8, with both engines mated to 7-speed automatic transmissions. Built on the all-wheel-drive front-midship platform, the the QX70 features an extensive list of available equipment. Available features include Continuous Damping Control, Rear Active Steer, and 21-inch lightweight aluminium-alloy wheels designed by Enkei. Inside, the interior has available "sport" seating and advanced audio, optional navigation and technology ranging from an 11-speaker Bose-developed audio system to the intelligent key, available active cruise control and available around-view monitor system. The QX70 offers numerous safety and convenience technologies such as intelligent brake assist, distance control assist, adaptive front lighting system, standard HID headlights, integrated fog lights, rear LED taillights, functional side air vents, aluminium roof rails, leather and wood trim, sunroof, "self-healing" clearcoat paint finish, stability control, and the usual power accessories and multiple airbags. A V6 "Limited" trim was offered in 2018 in some markets, with LED fog lamps, dark outer trim and painted wheels. Available safety features include object-detection for the around-view parking camera system as well as voice instructions on how to parallel-park into a specific space.

An all-new Chevrolet Camaro Convertible was launched for the 2017 model year. It has remained unchanged for the 2018 model year. While the exterior may not be that different from the previous generation, under the hood the 3.6-litre V6 and 6.2-litre V8 engines have been upgraded with more power. The Camaro also has a new 4-cylinder 2.0-litre turbocharged engine, but it is not sold in the GCC. They all get either a 6-speed manual or an 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include air conditioning, power windows and lock, and keyless entry. Available features include heads-up display, sunroof and the MyLink entertainment system which includes touchscreen navigation. Standard rims include 18-inch wheels for the V6 and 4-cylinder, and 20-inch ones for the V8. Safety features include front airbags, side airbags, ABS and stability control.

Available only in a few GCC markets, this outdated version of the Land Cruiser got a big facelift for 2008, but the mechanicals underneath remain the same. Staying alive simply because people keep buying them. The popular pickup version became known as the LC79 from 2010, by virtue of a new petrol engine. It is built to Toyota's high standard of quality so you get unsurpassed durability and reliability. Powered by either a 4.0-litre V6 petrol, or in some markets, an old 4.2-litre inline-6 diesel, mated to only 5-speed manuals, these trucks are very rudimentary, unlike the American "luxury" trucks. Standard features include a radio with cassette player and 2 speakers, manual a/c, power steering and fabric seats. Options on higher models include power door mirrors, electric winch, 16-inch steel wheels, power windows and central locking.  If you are lucky, you might get an optional CD player, but not much else. Standard safety features include nothing more than a fire extinguisher, although some markets now get optional dual front airbags. Conversely, the Saudi market gets several variations, with available features such as a 10-seater covered bed, keyless entry, cooled glove-box, heavy-duty suspension and sand tyres. Incidentally, the pickup is regionally popular for modifying into drag racers due to their durability, although the loss of the old 4.5-litre petrol engine may put a dent in that.

The Porsche Cayenne was redesigned for 2011, and continues with minor changes for 2013. The entry-level Cayenne gets a 3.6-litre V6 engine, the Cayenne S gets a 4.8-litre V8 engine, whereas the Turbo gets a 4.8-litre V8 with twin-turbochargers. New for 2014 is a Turbo S model with an upgraded turbo engine. A hybrid model, the Cayenne S Hybrid, is fitted with a 3.0-litre supercharged engine and electric motor. There is also a Cayenne Diesel model now with a 3.0-litre turbodiesel V6. By 2013, a Cayenne S Diesel model was introduced with a 4.2-litre turbodiesel V8. The Cayenne GTS, a lowered sporty model powered by a higher-tuned 4.8-litre V8, came in mid-2012. All the models get a new 8-speed Tiptronic S automatic transmission and an Automatic Start-Stop function. Only the base V6 can be had with a 6-speed manual. There were Platinum versions for the V6 and Diesel models, which were simply special trim choices. Porsche claims the Cayenne is a capable off-roader, but there isn't even a low-range gearing option any more. A feature called Porsche Traction Management manages the permanent all-wheel-drive, self-locking centre differential, automatic brake differential, stability control and on-demand hill control. A PASM air suspension controls the damping firmness, and available as standard or optional, depending on model. As usual, everything on a Porsche is largely optional, with few exceptions. Features available on the Cayenne include a 7-inch TFT touchscreen, optional two-tone or body-colour leather upholstery, 40:20:40 split rear seat with front-back movement, power front-seat adjustment with optional memory feature, optional adaptive sports seats, cruise control, navigation, Bluetooth, cruise control with optional distance-control function, optional lane-change monitor, parking sensors with optional back-up camera, wheel sizes from 18-inch to 21-inch, and a choice of an optional 14-speaker BOSE CD stereo or an optional 16-speaker Burmester CD stereo, both with USB and iPod support. Safety features are thankfully standard, including front and side airbags, tyre pressure monitor, ABS and stability control, with various other optional electronic aids.

The VW Multivan is the range-topping minivan based on the T5 Transporter work-van platform. The outdated front-wheel-drive van is powered by an equally-outdated 3.2-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic. Available with 6 or 7 seats, it has a unique rail feature in which seats can slide forward and backward into any configuration. Offered in base Comfortline and upgraded Highline trim, the Multivan can be had with features such as power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, and a CD stereo. It can be optionally outfitted with cloth or leather seats, HID headlights, wood cabin trim, rear DVD entertainment system, sunroof, alloy wheels and automatic doors. A wide range of accessories are available, like tables and refrigerators which fit onto the rails, all movable. The Multivan has safety features as standard such as front and side-curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Toyota Hiace has been the market leader for years in the UAE and continues to be a popular choice in the commercial sector, whether for transporting the work-force or cargo. There is only one engine choice in the Hiace, a 2.7-litre four cylinder petrol engine mated to a standard 5-speed manual, while some markets such as UAE occasionally get a 4-speed automatic option. The Saudi market additionally gets a 2.5-litre diesel model with a 5-speed manual. It comes in two variants, the Hiace Panel Van version for carrying cargo and the Hiace Commuter which gets back seats to act as a people carrier. Standard features include dual front/rear a/c, an AM/FM cassette player with 2 speakers, power steering, power door locks, toolbox, halogen headlamps and 15-inch steel wheels. Some markets get optional features such as remote locking. Depending on market, consumers have the choice of a normal roof, mid-roof or high-roof with a standard, long or super long wheel base-wide body.

The Mitsubishi Montero Sport is the Japanese brand's midsize SUV offering, replacing the Pajero Sport for 2016. Carrying over unchanged for 2018, it gets a 3.0-litre V6 engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The base model comes with side steps, leather-wrapped steering wheel with audio controls, multi-mode dash display, CD/MP3 stereo with 4 speakers, manual a/c with rear vents, dual airbags, power windows, keyless entry, chrome-plated power mirrors, 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, ABS with EBD, immobilizer, front skid plate, and three rows of cloth-upholstered seating. The higher models gets cruise control, fog lamps, upgraded stereo with 8 speakers, automatic a/c, leather upholstery, sunroof and 18-inch alloy wheels.

The Z4 debuted for 2003 as a replacement for the outgoing Z3. Freshened styling, M models and the introduction of a hatchback coupe marked major changes in 2006 and 2007 for BMW's little sports car. The convertible Z4 has a fabric top with heated glass rear window, while the new hatchback coupe has a fixed top. The Z4 can be had with two versions of the 2.5-litre six-cylinder in the 2.5i and the 2.5si respectively, and a 3.0-litre six-cylinder in the 3.0si, all in convertible and coupe form. The high-performance Z4 M convertible and coupe get the 3.2-litre six-cylinder from the outgoing M3. All come with a 6-speed manual transmission. Optional is a 6-speed automatic with steering wheel paddles for manual operation. ABS and traction control. The M convertibles have a power top that is otherwise optional. A navigation system is optional. BMW revives the hatchback coupe style with their fixed-top Z4, and unlike their ugly Z3 predecessors, the new Z4s have a sloped rear roofline. In most other respects, they are identical with the roadsters, except for a more rigid body. The M Roadster and M Coupe are some of the most hardcore sports cars in the current market. The SMG clutchless manual is seemingly not offered in this region, and neither is the base 2.0i model.

The Mitsubishi ASX is a 5-seater sub-compact crossover based on the Outlander platform and actually shares the exact same wheelbase, but is shorter at the front and especially the rear. It got a facelift for its 2017 model, along with interior upgrades and it carries over to 2018 unchanged. The standard engine is a 2.0-litre DOHC 4-cylinder with MIVEC variable valve timing, CVT transmission and either front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive. The all-wheel-drive has 2WD, 4WD and 4WD Lock modes. The base model comes with 16-inch alloy wheels, keyless entry, cloth seats, soft-touch dash and front door surfaces, CD/MP3 player with AUX and USB ports, ABS-assisted disc brakes, four-wheel independent suspension, up to seven airbags including a knee bag, and an optional panoramic glass roof with mood lighting along the sides. The top model gets 17-inch alloys, a front lip spoiler, intelligent entry with starter button, HID headlights, leather upholstery and a 7-speaker stereo with subwoofer, among other items. Available safety features include the aforementioned airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, hill start assist and emergency braking blinkers.

The Mitsubishi Pajero is a true off-roader, and a legend in its own right. It received a massive revamp for 2007, with an all-new interior, and can be had in either three-door or five-door body styles. From 2010, powertrain options were either a 3.5-litre V6 mated to a 4-speed automatic, or a 3.8-litre V6 engine mated to a 5-speed auto. A minor frontal facelift and other trim changes marked the changes for 2012. Both engines started getting the 5-speed automatic transmission from 2017. The standard package in the 2021 Mitsubishi Pajero includes ActiveTrac four-wheel-drive with rear-wheel, full-time all-wheel and 4WD high and low range with locked centre differential. The short-wheelbase three-door Pajero holds five passengers, while the long-wheelbase model holds seven, with a third-row seat that can be folded into a well in the cargo area floor, or removed entirely. Standard features in the 2021 Mitsubishi Pajero include an RV meter showing external temperature, time, date, compass, pressure, altitude and maintenance intervals. Also standard are a radio cassette player with 6 speakers, automatic a/c, front dual airbags, keyless entry, power windows and mirrors, and 16-inch alloy wheels. Higher models get a 6-disc CD changer, fake wood interior trim, sunroof, front and rear automatic a/c, traction control, ABS with EBD, cruise control, cool box, leather seats and 17-inch wheels. Only the top-level 3.8 models get side airbags as standard. From early 2012, a few hundred 30th Anniversary edition models were offered, signified by LED lights in the bumpers and a few other trim bits.

The luxury car of the Kia range, the Opirus is a large front-wheel-drive sedan aiming for the entry-level luxury segment. Its most obvious feature is the mixed-salad styling, though it has been improved for 2007, with a less prominent grille and a redesigned rear end. This front-wheel-drive comes with a new 3.8-litre V6 and a five-speed automatic gearbox with manual shift capability. Features, standard or otherwise, include a radio cassette player with MP3 and 8 speakers, ABS brakes, standard front and side airbags, leather, power driver's seat with electric lumbar support, power passenger's seat, electric power steering, keyless entry system, auto light control system, fake wood grain, front fog lamps, power door locks, power windows, power mirrors, audio controls on the steering wheel, immobilizer, battery saver, active head restraint, cup holders front and back, body-coloured  exterior trim, 17-inch alloy wheels, and automatic air-conditioning with dual independent controls.

Launched back in 2001, redone mechanically in 2004, and facelifted in 2007, the S60 is tuned to be a sports sedan, but though it is betrayed by a front-wheel-drive chassis in all but the R model, it looks like a sleek sports coupe from afar. The interior is fairly spacious even with the swooping roofline, and it offers more of a midsize package than a compact one, even though it is occassionally pitted against smaller German rivals in comparisons. For the Middle East market, there are five powerplants. These include a basic 2.0-litre turbo and a 2.5-litre turbo for the run-of-the-mill S60 sedan models, a 2.4-litre turbo for the sporty front-wheel-drive T5 and a highly-tuned 2.5-litre turbo for the all-wheel-drive S60 R. All engines are five-cylinder, and have an automatic with tiptronic, although some can be had with a manual too. Maintaining Volvo tradition, safety features include dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags and WHIPS whiplash protection.

The Tata Xenon is the Indian manufacturer's answer to commercial vehicles which is currently dominated by the Japanese. Featuring a 2.2-litre 4-cylinder diesel engine, the Xenon comes standard with power steering, power windows and air-conditioning. Unlike the name, it does not come with xenon headlamps. The Xenon can be had in either single cab or double cab, with the option of two-wheel drive or four-wheel-drive.

The redesigned-for-2011 Chrysler 300C looks similar to the old model, and still uses a lot of the same underpinnings, but in reality has many major changes, including a sharper-sloping windshield and a lower belt-line for better visibility. The new 300C thankfully remains rear-wheel-drive and features updated suspension, upgraded engine and a much nicer interior. The new 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 version, mated to an 8-speed automatic with manual capability, debuted in 2012. The base model gets cruise control, cloth upholstery, 18-inch alloy wheels, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with 4.3-inch touchscreen and USB port, auto headlights, intelligent keyless entry and other standard features. Higher trim levels additionally come with an 8.4-inch touchscreen, stereo amplifier, auto a/c with rear vents, power seats, heated/cooled cup-holders, leather, remote start, Bluetooth, HID headlights, sunroof and more. The 5.7-litre Hemi V8 model, with a 5-speed automatic with manual capability, comes in three trim levels. Standard features include cruise control, 18-inch alloy wheels with optional 20-inch wheels, CD/MP3 stereo with touchscreen and USB port, auto headlights, intelligent keyless entry with starter button. Other available features, depending on trim level, includes an 8.4-inch touchscreen, stereo amplifier, auto a/c with rear vents, power seats, heated/cooled cup-holders, leather, remote start, Bluetooth, HID headlights, sunroof and more. The top model, the 300C SRT8, was released in 2012 with a 6.4-litre V8 mated to a 5-speed automatic. Standard SRT8 features include leather upholstery, UConnect multimedia system with touchscreen, 20-inch wheels, rear spoiler and more, along with a unique exterior kit. Standard safety features include front, side and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor and optional adaptive cruise control with auto braking.

The all-new Kia Stinger came out as a 2018 model year and is the Korean brand's grand tourer model on offer. Under the hood, the 2020 Kia Stinger gets two engine choices - the standard engine is a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder motor and the higher option is the 3.3-litre turbocharged V6 unit. Both engines are mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. The 2020 Kia Stinger comes as rear-wheel drive standard and optional all-wheel-drive. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, remote locking, central locking, leather seats, and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional equipment include real leather upholstery, 8-inch screen with navigation, 19-inch alloy wheels, heads up display, ventilated front seats and remote start. Safety features in the 2020 Kia Stinger include front, side and knee airbags, ABS, ESP, traction control and brake assist. Optional safety features include blind spot monition, front collision warning, parking distance warning front and back and rear cross-traffic alert.

The Haval Jolion is the Chinese SUV brand's smallest offering. It comes with a turbocharged 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, central locking, steering wheel with audio and cruise control buttons, keyless entry, push-start engine, fabric upholstery, manual seats, bluetooth, audio system with CD player and AUX support, 4 speakers, halogen headlamps with daytime running lamps, fog lamps. manual AC, rear parking sensors and alloy wheels. Higher models get sunroof, audio system with 6 speakers and MP3/USB support, electric foldable mirrors and reverse camera. Safety features include dual airbags in the front, while the higher models get side airbags as well. Other standard safety features include ABS, electronic brake distribution, brake assist, tyre pressure monitor and traction control.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle.
