The only powerplant is the 2.0-litre four-cylinder with front-wheel-drive and an automatic gearbox. The sloping front end offers a commanding driving position. The dash-mounted shifter is within easy reach and the digital instrumentation is clear. The cabin is filled with accessories like cup-holders, fold-down aeroplane-style tables in the back, and a low luggage floor for easy loading, with numerous other stowage facilities and cubby holes, including huge door pockets and under-floor storage boxes. Safety features include the requisite airbags and ABS brakes.

All new Kia Rio came out for the 2018 model year. It is a slightly larger car from its predecessor so interior room has marginally gone up as well. Two 4-cylinder engines are available on the front-wheel drive 2019 Kia Rio hatchback - one a 1.4-litre and the other a 1.6-litre. Standard features on the Rio include power steering, power windows, central locking, halogen lamps, manual A/C, fabric seats, USB port and 15-inch steel wheels. Higher models get a 5.0-inch touchscreen audio system, 3.5-inch LCD screen on the instrument cluster, automatic A/C, leather seats, fog lamps and 15 inch or 17-inch alloy wheels. Safety features in the 2019 Kia Rio hatchback include ABS, front driver and passenger airbags, stability control, electronic brake distribution and brake assist.

The 2015 Dodge Charger received a significant facelift. The previous engines are there, which includes the 3.6-litre V6 and 5.7-litre V8, aside from the SRT models. They all get the 8-speed automatic transmission. The base SE V6 model gets a manual a/c, cruise control, cloth upholstery, 18-inch alloy wheels, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with 4.3-inch touchscreen and USB port, auto headlights, intelligent keyless entry and other standard features. The SXT V6 trim level additionally comes with an 8.4-inch touchscreen, stereo amplifier, auto a/c with rear vents, power seats, heated/cooled cup-holders, leather, remote start, Bluetooth, HID headlights, sunroof and more, with some of these features reserved for the SXT Plus version offered in certain markets such as the UAE. The Rallye V6, available only in some markets such as KSA, comes with an appearance package. The 5.7-litre Hemi V8 model, comes in three trim levels. The base "Full House" V8 trim, available in some markets such as KSA, gets almost all the features of the top V6 model except for leather and fancy cup-holders, but gains sportier suspension and brakes, with options such as power seats, the fancy cup-holders, premium audio and a few other features, depending on market. The top "R/T" model gets the "Road and Track" performance package with sportier suspension, steering, exhaust, grille, spoiler and 20-inch alloys. Standard SRT features include leather upholstery, UConnect multimedia system with touchscreen, 20-inch wheels, rear spoiler and more, along with a unique exterior kit. Standard safety features on all models include front, side and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor and optional adaptive cruise control with auto braking.

The Chinese Tiggo beautifully illustrates the Koreans' fight for dominance in the small-4WD segment over the Japanese. The Tiggo has a bit of the Kia Sorento front end slapped onto the body of a previous-generation Toyota RAV-4. It kind of reminds us of a fake Rolex watch that has a Swatch lookalike face--a bit of the best and a bit of the average, but still ultimately neither. The five-door five-seater Tiggo does benefit from a versatile interior though, with fold-flat seats and a spacious cargo area. Features, standard or optional, include front dual airbags, rear three-point seat belts, ABS brakes with electronic brakeforce distribution, disc brakes, keyless entry, alloy wheels and a rear windshield wiper. Powered by a 2.4-litre Mitsubishi-sourced 4-cylinder engine, it comes with either a four-speed auto with two-wheel-drive, or a five-speed manual gearbox with all-wheel-drive. Chery also brags that sports car maker Lotus Engineering had a hand in developing this mishmash, so we expect decent handling. Don't put too much faith in the incredibly low manufacturer-quoted fuel consumption numbers though.

The Jeep Grand Cherokee SRT gets a name-change to only "SRT" for 2014, as well as a 6.4-litre V8, 8-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive with no low-range. Other features include an 8.4-inch touchscreen display and 7-inch customer configurable multiview cluster display. Other features include real leather upholstery, stitched-leather dash trim, ventilated power-adjustable front seats, 9-speaker audio with subwoofer and 20-inch wheels, with various options and accessories available. The SRT8 version gets a unique body kit, sports suspension, sports seats and other trim bits. Safety features available include standard active head restraints, front airbags, full-length side-curtain and seat-mounted side airbags, stability control, electronic roll mitigation, hill-start assist and optional trailer-sway control. An optional blind-spot/rear cross-path detection system and adaptive cruise control with forward collision warning are also available.

The Toyota Hiace has been the market leader for years in the UAE and continues to be a popular choice in the commercial sector, whether for transporting the work-force or cargo. There is only one engine choice in the Hiace, a 2.7-litre four cylinder petrol engine mated to a standard 5-speed manual, while some markets such as UAE occasionally get a 4-speed automatic option. The Saudi market additionally gets a 2.5-litre diesel model with a 5-speed manual. It comes in two variants, the Hiace Panel Van version for carrying cargo and the Hiace Commuter which gets back seats to act as a people carrier. Standard features include dual front/rear a/c, an AM/FM cassette player with 2 speakers, power steering, power door locks, toolbox, halogen headlamps and 15-inch steel wheels. Some markets get optional features such as remote locking. Depending on market, consumers have the choice of a normal roof, mid-roof or high-roof with a standard, long or super long wheel base-wide body.

The 1-Series is the smallest range in BMW's line-up. Completely redesigned for 2012, it remains the only vehicle in its class featuring rear-wheel-drive and is offered in the GCC as a 5-door hatchback alongside the older-generation 1-Series coupe and convertible that carried on into the 2012 model year. Petrol versions now include the 1.6-litre 116i, the 2.0-litre 118i and the turbocharged 2.0-litre 125i, although all models are not offered in all GCC markets. All models come with a choice of 6-speed transmissions, both manual or automatic, although only the automatic version is offered here. An M 135i model was offered from 2013, in 5-door form, with a 3.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder and a choice of 6-speed manual or 8-speed automatic. While the hatchback was completely redesigned for 2012, the coupe and convertible continued unchanged for one more year. To differentiate the sub-models, BMW offers Sport Line and Urban Line models which differ by alloy wheels, kidney grille and other appearance-related features. All trims come standard with common power accesories, cloth or leather upholstery, front and side airbags, stability control and ABS, alongside various optional features such as HID headlights, "active" steering, stereo choices and various wheel sizes. BMW claims to have improved cabin materials from the last 1 series. All models are equipped with start-stop and a/c as standard. Higher trims will include a 8.8-inch LCD monitor and Bluetooth hands-free with USB connectivity. BMW's Drive Performance Control is standard on all models. Drive Performance Control allows the driver to select one of four modes. These include Comfort, Sport, Sport+, and ECO PRO. ECO PRO aims to save fuel by adjusting throttle response to encourage slower acceleration and by limiting the use of accessories like air-conditioning, heated mirrors and seats.

This generation of the Genesis G80 sedan debuted in 2015 model year as the Hyundai Genesis, before the rebranding in 2017 as a separate marque. The Genesis can be had with a choice of either a 3.8-litre V6 or 5.0-litre V8. Both engines are mated to a Hyundai-designed 8-speed automatic transmission. Rear-wheel-drive is standard in both models. An "Intelligent Drive Mode" system offers Normal, Eco, Sport and Snow settings that alter transmission mapping, throttle responsiveness, stability control to suit driving conditions. The Genesis V8 can be optioned with an adaptive damping suspension that promises both sportier roadholding and a cushier ride. It, too, can be controlled by Intelligent Drive Mode.  The Genesis 3.8 is fitted as standard with leather upholstery, 12-way power-adjustable front seats, a navigation system with an 8.0-inch screen, a seven-speaker AM/FM/CD radio stereo with AUX and USB input jacks, auto on/off headlight, LED headlight accents, LED taillights, rain-sensing windshield wipers, automatic climate control, Bluetooth connectivity, cruise control, hands-free trunk opening capability, a 4.3-inch instrument cluster TFT LCD display and 18-inch alloy wheels. To those features, the Genesis 5.0 adds or substitutes a Lexicon Discrete Logic 7 surround sound system with 14 speakers, premium leather upholstery, genuine matte wood trim, 16-way power adjustable front seats, HID headlights with auto-leveling, high-beam assist, LED fog lights, a rear-view camera, front and rear parking sensors, automatic emergency braking, blind spot detection with rear cross traffic alert and lane change assist, lane departure warning system with lane keep assist, a 7.0-inch instrument cluster TFT LCD display, manual rear side window sunshades, a power rear sunshade, memory functionality for power driver's seat and outside mirrors and steering column, adaptive cruise control and 19-inch alloy wheels. Much of the 5.0's features can be added to the 3.8 in the form of optional extras. All Genesis models come with dual front, front side, rear side and full-length side curtain airbags in addition to a driver's knee airbag and traction and stability control systems. Optional equipment includes an automatic emergency braking system that applies the brakes if it detects an impending collision; a blind spot warning system with a rear cross traffic alert system that warns the driver of approaching traffic in backup situations; a lane departure warning system with lane keep assist setup that warns the driver if the Genesis begins to wander into an adjacent lane and provides slight steering corrections to bring the sedan back on course; and an emergency steering support mode that automatically changes the setting of suspension and electronic stability control in the direction suitable for emergency steering, to help avoid frontal crash situations.

The Porsche Macan is a second SUV for the German premium brand and hopes to replicate the success of the Cayenne, albeit in the compact crossover segment. Taking the front fascia from its elder brother, the Macan doesn't disappoint in terms of looks. The rear of the vehicle however, is unique and could be termed as a love-or-hate affair. But the wide tyres which range from 18-inch to 21-inches do complement the somewhat muscular stance of the Macan. But it must be noted that it stands shorter and is marginally longer than its Q5 counterpart. As for the variants, Porsche has four. The first being the Macan S, which is equipped with a 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6 engine. It also features an active all-wheel-drive and a 7-speed double-clutch transmission. The second variant in the lineup is the Macan Turbo which gets a 3.6-litre turbocharged pertrol engine. Porsche claim that it is set to be the most powerful vehicle in the compact SUV segment. The third variant is the Macan Diesel which features a 3.0-litre turbo diesel engine, mated to a 7-speed transmission as well. The Diesel is not available in all GCC markets, unless special-ordered. The fourth is the Macan GTS which was introduced in 2017. It gets the same 3.0-litre turbo V6, but with more power. Height-adjustable air suspension is optional on the S and standard on the GTS and Turbo. As with any Porsche, the interior is carefully setup. It follows the generic Porsche cockpit, but there happens to be a new steering wheel which is a welcome change from the one on the Cayenne. The Macan's interior comes in a variety of colours, but there also happens to be a Piano Black interior package with Alcantara inserts for the seats on the S variant. Available features include a multimedia touchscreen, navigation, rear camera, power seats, panoramic glass roof and much more from a long list of options. Safety features include Porsche Stability Management (PSM), as well as airbags for driver and passenger all around the vehicle.

The Volvo XC60 was launched with high hopes for the Swedish company, capitalising on the small crossover vehicle market. The XC60 is a 5-seater crossover SUV that is aimed at attracting luxury-brand buyers. The XC60 T6 is powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic with manual-shifting capability, and an all-wheel-drive system without low-range gearing. The XC60 T5 model comes with a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder with a 6-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive. The smallest XC model includes safety technology, Volvo's City Safety system, designed to help a driver avoid a collision at under 30 kph, or reduce the speed of impact at higher speeds by hitting the brakes if the vehicle in front suddenly stops and City Safety determines that a collision is likely. Other safety features on the XC60 is Pre-Prepared Restraints that uses a laser sensor that interacts with other technology to control the airbags and adaptive seatbelt load limiters. Other features, depending on trim level, include cloth or leather upholstery, blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, reverse camera, keyless entry, sunroof, alloy wheels, common power accessories and a CD/MP3 stereo. An R-Design body kit is optional. Standard safety features include front and side-surtain airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, and whiplash-protection headrests. A software-based Polestar power upgrade is also offered, adding 20-30 hp, depending on the model.

The Pathfinder is a 4-door, 5-passenger luxury 4WD, and a popular performer. This unit-body shape was introduced in 2000, but got the newer 3.5-litre V6 only in 2002. This model range ran till 2005. A 5-speed manual is standard while a 4-speed automatic transmission with overdrive is optional. The manual-mated V6 is slightly more powerful than the automatic-mated V6. Later models also have an optional package consisting of electronic stability control, ABS brakes, traction control, and a tyre-pressure monitoring system. The top Pathfinder models got six-spoke 17-inch wheels and a leather interior in the later years, while lower models have 16-inch wheels and a cloth cabin. Exterior paint-jobs were two-colour for base models and monotone for upper models. Available features included a cassette or CD player, power windows, electric mirrors, sunroof and power front seats, among other accessories.

A new generation of the Mazda 3 came out in 2020. Mechanically, the engines have carried over from the previous model. One engine is offered in the GCC, a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder unit with a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard safety features include dual front airbags, ABS with EBD and an immobiliser, side airbags, "smart" brake support and blind-spot monitoring.

The Scirocco is revival of Volkswagen's odd-shaped 1970s model that attempted to bridge the gap between a hatchback and a coupe. It last died out in 1992, until its revival as a concept car in 2006 and a production car by 2008. Debuting in the GCC as a 'sportier' alternative to the VW Golf, the Scirocco lifts platforms, engines and even interior panels from the Golf. However, the cabin itself has a lower roofline while retaining seating for four. Engines include a 1.4-litre TSI 4-cylinder with both a supercharger and a turbocharger, as well as a 2.0-litre FSI turbocharged 4-cylinder. The GCC dealers will be pushing the automatic version locally, with the 'DSG' automanual gearbox, but it can be special-ordered with a 6-speed manual. This Portugese-built front-wheel-drive hatchback gets the usual power accessories, along with available panoramic sunroof, CD/MP3 stereo, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, HID headlights, front-side airbags, climate control, keyless entry, stability control, ABS and such. The VW Scirocco also gets an optional three-mode adaptive chassis control, offering the driver a choice of sport and comfort that affects suspension and steering tune.

The Chevrolet Malibu is unchanged for 2015. Built in Korea and based on the front-wheel-drive Opel Insignia platform, the new Malibu is offered with a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder and a 3.0-litre V6, mated to 6-speed automatics. Aside from common features such as power windows, cloth or leather upholstery, keyless entry and CD/MP3 stereo, available options include HID headlights and a choice of 16-inch, 17-inch or 18-inch wheels. Standard safety features include 6 airbags, ABS, available stability control with brake assist, and options such as rear-view camera with parking sensors.

The Chevrolet Impala is a large sedan designed to slot in just above the Malibu. The front-wheel drive Impala comes to the GCC with a 3.6-litre V6 engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic. Along with the usual power steering, power windows and power mirrors, other features include 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels, HID headlights, LED daytime running lights, optional multimedia-navigation system with pop-up screen, Bluetooth and a six-speaker audio entertainment system with CD/MP3/AUX support. Safety features include 10 standard airbags, and options include adaptive cruise control, collision mitigation braking, forward collision alert, lane departure warning, side blind zone alert, rear cross traffic alert, rear camera and rear-park assist.

The Volvo V40 is the Swedish company's latest hatchback offering, replacing the C30 with this new 5-door model. The base engine offered here, for the V40 T4, is a turbocharged 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic. The other version is the V40 T5, fitted with a turbocharged 2.0-litre 5-cylinder for the GCC market. Available with either engine, variants beyond the regular V40 include the V40 R-Design model with a sporty body kit and unique wheels, as well as the V40 Cross Country model with faux skid-plates and a slightly-raised suspension. All versions are front-wheel-drive, although the Cross Country can be had with all-wheel-drive as well. Features include fuel-saving auto start-stop tech, power windows, electric mirrors, CD/MP3 stereo, cloth or leather upholstery, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and other basics, with options such as HID headlights, sunroof, navigation and all that. Safety standards are always high in Volvos, and the V40 is no exception. Safety features, aside from the standard front and side-curtain airbags, include a world-first pedestrian airbag, blind spot monitoring, lane-keeping aid with haptic auto steering, pedestrian detection with auto braking, and a Park Assist Pilot system that makes parallel parking easy.

The Savvy is the third car developed by Proton itself, after the Waja and the Gen2. This five-door hatchback is sized somewhere between a mini hatchback and a sub-compact, thus making this entry level Proton one of the larger offerings in this market segment. Hilariously touted as a cheap "Lotus" in early marketing materials, the Savvy benefits from numerous unique features, such as actual suspension tuning by Lotus, stepped side windows and a clamshell-style hood. Lifting the hood reveals a Renault 1.2-litre four-cylinder engine, mated to either a five-speed manual or a five-speed automatic. Standard features include cloth upholstery, 50:50 flat folding rear seats, keyless entry, power steering, rear window wiper, 14-inch steel wheels and a CD player with four speakers. Options include front power windows, 15-inch alloy wheels and metallic paint. The Savvy is available with ABS brakes and dual front airbags. The Savvy is not available in all GCC markets.

The A4 has been completely redesigned for the 2009 model year, featuring a new and improved platform, shared with the A5 coupe, that moves engine further back in the engine compartment for better handling balance. The new model is bigger than its predecessor in most dimensions, thus improving cabin space to almost midsize levels. Arriving in the GCC during the first quarter of 2008 only in sedan form, available engines include the weak "1.8T" with two versions of the 1.8-litre turbo 4-cylinder, mated to front-wheel-drive and a CVT automatic, and a "3.2 Quattro" with a 3.2-litre V6 with all-wheel-drive and 6-speed automatic. A couple of "2.0T" models joined the line-up by 2010, with two different 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engines, one with front-wheel-drive and the other with more power and all-wheel-drive. Standard features include LED running lights, three-zone automatic air conditioning, front seats with lumbar support and ventilation, MMI computer control system, intelligent key that stores the vehicle's service info, and a Bang & Olufsen audio system. Also available are side-assist warning system for safe lane changes, and a parking system with a rear-view camera. The A4 also gets a new dynamic system that Audi called Drive Select that manipulates transmission shifts, steering feel and suspension settings, with up to 24 combinations available to create individual driving profiles. All models get the usual power accessories as well as safety features such as multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The rear-wheel-drive H1 is a contender to be the van of choice for families, assuming you are looking just for a whole lot of space and not much luxury features. Its tough looks are misleading, as it appeals more to corporate groups as staff transportation rather than the jalopy of choice for large families who would like to travel in style and comfort. Still, Hyundai is promoting it as such. Powered by a 2.4-litre four-cylinder, it is available in various configurations, ranging from a 3-seater all the way to a 12-seater. The top spec is actually a 9-seater with power front windows, electric mirrors, an automatic gearbox and a two-tone paint job. The other models don't get any of those features, and manage with a manual gearbox. All trims get power steering, radio cassette player and air-conditioning, some even with rear a/c. Boasting uniquely configurable seats and extensive luggage space, other standard features include cloth seat coverings, while options include central door locks and front fog lamps.

The Dodge Challenger SRT received a minor facelift and new engine upgrades in 2015. The interior has been significantly improved as well. The Challenger utilises retro styling that is largely a rethinking of the original 1970s Challenger's 2-door design. From 2020 onwards, Dodge Challenger SRT interior gets upgraded with a bit more gadgetry in the form of an 8.4-inch Uconnect infotainment system and 7-inch customization display between the retro-inspired speedometer and tachometer. With a high-sill center aluminium gauge bezels makes the revamped interior extremely pleasing to the eyes. Through the Uconnect interface, you can now access the Dodge performance pages that allows you to select different driving modes to adjust steering effort, engine and transmission response, electronic stability and traction controls, and standard launch control. It also gets forward collision warning, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring and rear cross path detection. The 2020 Dodge Challenger SRT gets the 6.4-litre V8, while the SRT Hellcat gets the 6.2-litre supercharged V8 motor. All SRT models gets a flat-bottomed steering wheel, bi-xenon headlights, heated and ventilated seats wrapped in Nappa leather and Alcantara and 20-inch aluminium-alloy wheels, along with the usual accessories such as automatic a/c, cruise control and fog lamps. Also available are a sunroof, racing stripes, rear sensors with camera, and the UConnect touchscreen multimedia system with voice controls as well as navigation, hard drive and Bluetooth phone. An optional widebody kit is also available on the SRT Hellcat. Safety features include ABS, stability control, front,side and curtain airbags, and SRT-exclusive Brembo brakes.

The Subaru WRX STi  was all-new in 2015 and got a minor facelift for 2018. It is available only as a sedan. Under the hood, it gets a 2.5-litre 4-cylinder Boxer engine with a twin-scroll turbocharger and intercooler. It is coupled to a 6-speed manual transmission as standard. It is 25 mm longer wheelbase than the previous generation. So rear seat passengers gain nearly 51 mm of extra legroom. It also has a bigger boot and 60/40-split fold-down rear seats. Inside, the Subaru gets a leather-wrapped steering wheel and sports seats covered in high-grip fabric. Buyers can also opt for leather seats and 8-way adjustable driver seat. Among other features is a power sunroof, a dual gauge instrument layout with a 3.5-inch LCD central screen displaying various functions and a new 4.3-inch multi-information central display providing a multitude of vehicle system functions. Safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, traction control, stability control and ABS.

The VW Multivan is the range-topping minivan based on the T5 Transporter work-van platform. The outdated front-wheel-drive van is powered by an equally-outdated 3.2-litre V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic. Available with 6 or 7 seats, it has a unique rail feature in which seats can slide forward and backward into any configuration. Offered in base Comfortline and upgraded Highline trim, the Multivan can be had with features such as power windows, electric mirrors, cruise control, and a CD stereo. It can be optionally outfitted with cloth or leather seats, HID headlights, wood cabin trim, rear DVD entertainment system, sunroof, alloy wheels and automatic doors. A wide range of accessories are available, like tables and refrigerators which fit onto the rails, all movable. The Multivan has safety features as standard such as front and side-curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Wrangler has been redesigned for 2007, with a stiffer frame, revised suspension, a new engine, and fresh styling. The all-new real jeep is longer and wider, more refined, and for the first time, offered with four doors. Now powered by a 3.8-litre V6, with a manual or automatic, it still offers low-range gearing and off-road capability. In 2011, the interior was redesigned completely, with a new dashboard and door panels, while body-coloured exterior plastic trim and roof were offered. The lengthened four-door wheelbase also provides room for a three-wide rear seat in the new Unlimited, making for five-passenger capability. It also offers more ground clearance, more wheel articulation and some new suspension hardware. For the first time, the Wrangler offers an optional electronic-disconnecting front stabiliser bar. This Active Sway Bar System allows more front-wheel travel over obstacles. Also available is the Command-Trac part-time four-wheel-drive system. A Trak-Lok limited slip differential and Rock-Trac with special off-road tyres also are available. Comfort features include power windows, CD/MP3 stereo, and even a voice-controlled 'UConnect' Bluetooth telecom system. Safety includes stability control, ABS brakes, front airbags and seat-mounted side-airbags. It can be equipped with a new three-piece hardtop with removable panels. Also available is a Sunrider soft top with a sunroof feature. The dealer also offers a huge catalogue of original offroad accessories, such as lift kits, metal bumpers, monster tyres and the like, which can get quite expensive if every add-on is chosen.

An all-new generation of Honda Accord came for the 2018 model year. The naturally-aspirated engines has been replaced by two 4-cylinder turbocharged motors - a 1.5-litre, mated to CVT and a 2.0-litre connected to a 10-speed automatic transmission. Features on the standard 2018 Honda Accord LX model include power windows, power mirrors, remote engine start, push button start, dual-zone automatic A/C, cruise control, 160-watt audio system with 4 speakers, 7-inch audio display, Bluetooth, USB, LED headlights, LED taillamps, dual exhausts and 17-inch alloy wheels. The 2018 Honda Accord Sport variant gets additional power seats with lumbar support, aluminium sports pedals, paddle shifts, 2-mode drive system (ECO/Sport), LED fog lamps, sunroof, dark chrome front grille, spoiler and 18-inch alloy wheels. The 2018 Honda Accord EX gets additional leather seats, 180-watt audio system with 8 speakers, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto and 8-inch audio display. The top 2018 Honda Accord 2.0T Sport gets additional 450-watt audio system with 10 speakers and subwoofer and head-up display. Standard safety features on the 2018 Honda Accord include front,side, curtain and knee airbags (total 8 airbags), ABS, EBD, brake assist, stability control, emergency stop signal, brake booster and tyre pressure monitoring system. The Honda EX and 2.0T Sport get additional Honda Lane Watch and rear-view camera.

The Continental GTC made its debut as a 2006 model. It gets the same twin turbocharged 6.0-litre W12 engine as the coupe and all-wheel drive is standard. It comes with a handcrafted wood and leather interior, complete with all the requisite gadgets such as navigation and a killer stereo. Instrumentation is provided by classic dials that live in deep recesses ahead of the steering wheel, while a small screen directly in the driver's line of sight monitors all relevant in-car systems. The two-door Continental GT convertible is equipped with the full suite of passive safety equipment, including two front airbags, four side airbags and two side curtain bags.

Finally making its official debut in the GCC, the rally-bred Subaru Impreza WRX STI landed for the 2008 model year with a hatchback-only body and no warranty. By 2010, it could finally be bought with a warranty. The sedan came for 2011. The standard engine is a 2.5-litre turbocharged and intercooled horizontally-opposed 4-cylinder, mated to a 6-speed manual and Subaru's 'symmetrical' all-wheel-drive system. In 2011, a minor range-wide facelift debuted along with the sedan, as well as a 5-speed automatic option. An SI-DRIVE system offers three modes, namely Intelligent, Sport, and Sport Sharp, with the first mode reducing power and improving fuel economy. The 'Driver Controlled Center Differential,' also known as DCCD, has three automatic modes in addition to allowing manual torque-split adjustment. The VDC stability control system can be left on, fully turned off, or set to a sport mode. Features include ABS-assisted Brembo brakes, LED tail lamps, torque-sensitive limited slip differential, 18-inch alloy wheels, front airbags, side-curtain airbags, keyless entry with starter button, retractable headlight washers, common power accessories and a CD stereo, with options such as Recaro sport seats and navigation. However, options lists keep changing every year, depending on what the dealers choose to bring in.

The Suzuki Vitara is a completely new model, making its debut in the GCC in 2016. Smaller, lighter and losing its offroad capabilities, the new Vitara is designed to compete in the road-going crossover segment and is a separate vehicle line from the existing Grand Vitara. It is only available as a 5-door wagon, and gets a 1.6-litre engine, mated to either a 5-speed manual transmission or a 6-speed automatic transmission. It is available in both two-wheel drive and four-wheel drive. In the UAE, two trims are available, the GLX and GLX+, all of which come with automatic transmission as standard. Standard features include power steering, power mirrors, central locking, keyless push start system, sunroof, LED daytime running lamps, leather seats, cruise control,  automatic A/C, roof rails, front & rear parking sensors, front skid plate, chrome front grille and alloy wheels. The higher GLX+ model gets panoramic roof and polished aluminium wheels. Standard safety features include 6 airbags, electronic brake distribution (EBD), ABS and brake assist.

The Nissan Sunny got a facelift for the 2015 model year. It remained the same for the 2018 model year. The Sunny sedan comes from India, and is powered by a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a CVT. The basic 'S' model comes with 14-inch steel wheels, CD/MP3 stereo, AUX jack, cloth upholstery, trip computer and a black grille surround. The 'SV' model, identified by a chrome grille surround and door handles, adds power mirrors, front power windows, keyless entry, upgraded cloth seats and hubcaps, with an optional comfort package that adds fog lights, rear power windows, rear fan vents, parking sensors, more speakers and a central rear armrest. The top 'SL' model comes only in automatic, with 15-inch alloys, Bluetooth, steering-wheel stereo controls, nicer gauges with more readings, push-start, Display Audio system with Facebook support, cloth trim on the doors, LED side mirrors, rear spoiler and mud guards. All models get dual front airbags, ABS with EBD, brake assist, and seatbelts for all five seating positions.

The Lexus CT 200h is the first hybrid in the small-car segment to debut in the GCC. It got a facelift in 2014, getting the new front "spindle grille" design. This premium hatchback comes only in front-wheel-drive hybrid form, with a 1.8-litre 4-cylinder mated to a self-charging electric motor and a CVT automatic. The platform has its roots in Toyota models, but the suspension is fully independent, MacPherson-strut front and double-wishbone rear. Standard features include an info display to show battery usage, 16-inch alloy wheels, leather steering wheel with cloth upholstery, dual-zone auto a/c, cruise control, smart keyless entry with starter button, parking sensors, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with USB port, split-folding rear seat, sunroof, LED side and tail lamps, LED front driving lamps, fog lamps and alarm. The top trim additionally gets leather upholstery, wood trim, power-adjustable driver's seat with memory, front seat heaters, navigation system with flip-up 7-inch LCD screen, rear camera, Bluetooth, auto-levelling LED headlights, rain-sensing wipers, sport front bumper, and a 10-speaker audio system. Standard safety features include front, side, curtain and knee airbags, stability control, and ABS with EBD and brake-assist.

The Porsche 911 Cabriolet is all-new after spending more than a decade in its current form, with continuous updates of course. For 2012, the design incorporates a completely new platform, so now the 911 is longer and lower than before. It is still a 2+2 seater convertible. The base 911 Carrera is offered with a 3.4-litre direct-injection flat-6 engine, mated to either a world-first 7-speed manual or a 7-speed "PDK" dual-clutch automatic and rear-wheel-drive. The 911 Carrera 4 Cabriolet, which was introduced in 2013, adds all-wheel-drive. The rear-wheel-drive 911 Carrera S Cabriolet upgrades the motor to a 3.8-litre, while the, new for 2013, 911 Carrera 4S Cabriolet adds all-wheel-drive. The 911 Turbo Cabriolet and Turbo S Cabriolet was released in 2014. It gets a 3.8-litre turbocharged engine, and comes only with the PDK transmission. The 911 GTS was revealed in the GCC in late 2014 and is available as rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. It is powered by a 3.8-litre motor, coupled with either a 7-speed manual or PDK transmission. As usual, everything is optional beyond the basic power accessories, touchscreen multimedia system, Bluetooth, basic keyless entry, HID headlights, electric parking brake and 19-inch wheels. Available options include different colours and materials for every interior surface, different 20-inch wheel designs, metallic paint choices, power-adjustable or sports seats, Bose or Burmester audio systems with optional voice control and TV tuner, CD changer, parking sensors, smart keyless entry and start, adaptive headlights, electric folding mirrors, rear wiper, body kit and more. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, stability control and ABS.

The Hyundai Azera, fills the gap between the Sonata and the Genesis sedan. It received a facelift for the 2015 model year. The front-wheel-drive full-size sedan comes with two engine choices, a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder and a 3.0-litre V6, but some GCC markets get only the V6. Both engines get a standard 6-speed automatic. The 2.4-litre version gets smart keyless entry with starter button, mood lighting, available panoramic sunroof, fake wood trim, rear sunshade, CD/MP3 stereo, auto-dimming mirror, electric parking brake with auto hold, leather powered seats, fog lamps, parking sensors, and 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels. The 3.0-litre version additionally gets xenon lights, memory and seat massage for driver, Infinity stereo, heating & cooling for front seats, electric tilt & telescopic steering wheel, Bluetooth, tyre pressure monitoring system, electric folding mirrors, adaptive cruise control, rain sensor and dual-zone a/c. The top model gets a navigation and DVD entertainment system with rear camera. All models get 8 airbags and ABS with EBD, while only the V6 gets stability control.
An all-new new model of the Kia Carnival came out in 2021.

The Brilliance FRV is the Chinese company's sub-compact hatchback offering.  The FRV Cross has been around since 2009, but only made its debut in the UAE in 2013. It comes with 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 4-speed automatic. Standard features in the FRV include power steering, power windows, fabric seats, radio with single CD player and MP3/USB support, and steel wheels. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, ABS and electronic brake distribution (EBD).

The Maserati Quattroporte became larger and lighter in 2013, and for 2015, is offered with three engine options, namely two versions of a 3.0-litre V6 in the base Quattroporte and the mid-range Quattroporte S, and a 3.8-litre V8 in the Quattroporte GTS, all twin-turbocharged direction-injection units built by Ferrari, but using some Chrysler-derived parts. Both have an 8-speed automatic transmission and rear-wheel-drive for the GCC market. Later on, an all-wheel-drive version for the Quattroporte S was available. The all-new architecture retains its 50:50 weight distribution, double-wishbone front suspension, and a five-link rear suspension. The more-spacious interior can be had with both four-seat and five-seat layouts. Cabin features include a Chrysler-sourced 8.4-inch touchscreen, adjustable pedals, reversing cameras and the optional 15-speaker Bowers & Wilkins audio system, as well as WLAN-based WiFi and Bluetooth compatibility. The screen includes navigation, reverse camera, DVD player, audio and ventilation functions. Adaptive cruise control, smart key with push-button start, front-side airbags and a dual-zone climate control system with 13 ventilation ports, complete the list of standard features.

This mini-car, also known as the Atos Prime occassionally, is in such a rare category that few people heard about it, and even fewer have bought one. It is amazingly cheap, but even more amazingly small, which seems to be to its detriment in this region. Powered by either 1.0-litre or 1.1-litre four-cylinder engines, the smaller engine can be had with a manual or automatic, while the slightly larger engine gets only an automatic as well as better fuel economy, Standard features include air- conditioning, seat under-tray for the front passenger, AM/FM radio and cassette player, a fold-down rear seat and, of course, wind-up windows. Move up to the better trims, and available features include power steering, front fog lamps, central door locking, power windows, rear wiper with washer, seat back pockets, better cloth upholstery, body-coloured door handles and outside mirrors, and the all-important seat under-tray both under the passenger as well as the driver's seat, to store your dirty magazines. Safety features include nothing more than the metal holding up the body panels.

The Toyota Yaris Sedan received a facelift in 2009. The sedan comes with either a very weak 1.3-litre or a 1.5-litre engine mated to either a five-speed manual or a four-speed auto. From 2012 however, only the 1.3-litre has been available. Standard items include power steering, a tilt-adjustable steering wheel, front and rear cupholders, two airbags, radio cassette player, 14-inch steel wheels, and ABS brakes. The suspension is independent in front and torsion beam in the rear. Options include a CD player with MP3 capability, a 60/40 split fold-down rear seat, 15-inch alloy wheels and a rear spoiler.

In 2021, a new generation of the Porsche 911 Targa was revealed. The 2+2 seater coupe gets an updated exterior design, along with updates to the engine. The 911 Carrera and Carrera S is offered with a 3.0-litre turbocharged flat-6 engine, mated to a 8-speed "PDK" dual-clutch automatic and rear-wheel-drive. The Targa 4 and 4S are all-wheel drive. As usual, everything is optional beyond the basic power accessories, touchscreen multimedia system, Bluetooth, basic keyless entry, HID headlights, electric parking brake and 19-inch wheels. Available options include different colours and materials for every interior surface, different 20-inch wheel designs, metallic paint choices, power-adjustable or sports seats, Bose or Burmester audio systems with optional voice control and TV tuner, CD changer, parking sensors, smart keyless entry and start, adaptive headlights, sunroof, electric folding mirrors, rear wiper, body kit and more. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, stability control and ABS.

The Tiguan, small in size and conservative in design, was mildly facelifted for the 2012 model year to incorporate the latest VW design cues, mostly involving LEDs and a new grille. Three different trim levels include the Trend&Fun, the Sport&Style and the Track&Style, the latter of which is supposedly tuned for offroading, given its underbody plates and higher front bumper, though there is no low-range gearing for the 4Motion all-wheel-drive vehicle. There are two turbocharged engines, both 2.0-litre and in different states of tune. The engines are mated to a 6-speed automatic. The Tiguan has seating for five, with a split-folding 60:40 rear bench, and has multiple position settings for the seatback. For additional cargo area, there is also an optional double-floor trunk-floor setup, including a cargo management system. The cabin can be had in cloth or leather, and features include power windows, electric mirrors, multiple airbags, stability control, ABS brakes, cruise control and CD stereo with a dash-mounted touchscreen. An automatic parallel parking system is also available, as are parking sensors and a rear camera.

The Subaru Impreza got a complete redesign for 2012, and is only offered in sedan form in the GCC. Interestingly, the WRX versions have spun off into a separate model line and continue unchanged from their pre-2012 forms, at least until 2014. The Impreza is now offered with either a 1.6-litre or a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder boxer engine, both mated to a CVT automatic and all-wheel-drive. Standard features in the 1.6i model include 15-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, power windows and mirrors, multi-function display, automatic a/c, CD/MP3 stereo with AUX port, 60/40 folding rear seats and cloth upholstery. The 2.0i model adds the larger engine, 16-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, fog lamps, faux paddle-shifters and a rear-seat centre armrest with cup-holders. Standard safety features include front dual airbags, stability control and ABS with EBD, along with the all-weather traction of asymmetrical all-wheel-drive.

The Mitsubishi Lancer EX, first introduced in 2008, got some minor trim changes for 2010. From 2013 onwards, it comes with a choice of two four-cylinder engines, namely a new 1.6-litre and a carryover 2.0-litre. In 2016, it got another facelift. The smaller engine gets a 4-speed automatic and the larger one gets a CVT auto transmission. Offering a choice of either engine, features in the most basic GLX model includes power steering, locally-installed CD/MP3 player with 4 speakers, manual a/c, keyless entry, 16-inch steel wheels with covers, power windows and even colour-coded bumpers, but only a driver's airbag. The mid-range GLS model can only be had with the larger engine, and includes a sporting body kit, rear spoiler, leather-wrapped steering wheel, cruise control, rain-sensing wipers, smart key with starter button, sunroof, 6-speaker stereo with USB port, rear camera and faux-wood panelling. The top GT model adds adaptive headlights which turn with the steering wheel, fog lamps, Rockford Fosgate premium CD audio system with six-CD changer and 9 speakers, "sport-type" front seats, rear split seats with centre armrest, colour-keyed power mirrors, ABS brakes with EBD and Brake Assist, 18-inch alloy wheels and just two front airbags.

The Fortuner, Toyota's cheapest SUV, has received a minor facelift, giving it a new face and other minor detail updates. The Fortuner is the product of Toyota's International Multi-Purpose Project family, which also includes the new Hilux pick-up and the Innova. These three vehicles all share the new platform and are built in Indonesia, so any thought about this Toyota being purely Japanese is an allusion. Although this 4WD is based on a pickup, its styling is very softly finished, with none of its truck-like toughness showing. It has true off-road ability, thanks to four-wheel-drive with low-range gearing. It also has space for five, or optionally seven, and its value-packed price has attracted families rather than desert junkies. The Fortuner is available here with a 2.7-litre 4-cylinder as well as two 4.0-litre V6 engines, one with manual and a higher-torque one with the automatic. The Fortuner sits high up from the ground, so it can be a bit of a climb for the kind of people who are expected to buy it. It has space for five adults and two kids. Features include power windows, dual front airbags, keyless entry and fabric upholstery. Higher trim levels get fake wood, cruise control, chrome body trimmings, navigation, 17-inch alloy wheels, rear diff lock, ABS, multi-information display, and a CD stereo with changer and AUX input as well as Bluetooth.

This generation of the S-Class is among the top-selling luxury cars in the Middle East thanks to its mix of luxury and road presence. The S 65 AMG gets a twin turbocharged 6.0-litre V12 engine, mated to a 5-speed automatic. The new model features new steps in road safety with the second generation of the PRE-SAFE occupant protection system that predicts accidents and prepares the car's occupants for the crash by initiating safety measures such as pre-tensioning seatbelts, raising seat backs to the optimum position and even closing the sunroof. In addition, it also has optional Night View Assist which is an advanced after-dark vision system. Other features include enhanced COMAND system with 8-inch display and a controller on the centre console, Airmatic adaptive suspension and adaptive brake lights. It also  includes a reversing camera, panoramic sunroof, AMG bodykit and AMG light-alloy wheels.

The son of the Orient is the most impressive to look at. The design seems derivative, but is largely original and non-offensive, though what is under the hood is outsourced from Mitsubishi. Boasting the most advanced engine in this raggedy range, it comes with only an automatic transmission in this region. The underpowered 2.4-litre engine is of the same design as the one that did duty in various large Mitsubishi models in the past. There is also a 2.0-litre engine that has almost as much power as the 2.4-litre. With a Delphi ABS system and four airbags, it does not skimp on safety items, and with options such a visual reverse sensor, a 3-screen DVD stereo system, a CD changer, an automatic thermostatic air-conditioner and 8-way adjustable power leather seats, you'd be hard-pressed to find better value anywhere else, even among the Koreans. Other options on this front-wheel-drive compact include an electric sunroof, keyless entry and even GPS navigation. We just hope it is not loaded with a map of mainland China.

The Maybach was originally built for the ultra-rich back before World War II. Mercedes-Benz has revived the brand for the ultra-rich of today, as "a business jet on wheels," according to the company, and quite rightly so. The Maybach is offered in three versions currently. The Maybach 62 is the long wheelbase version of the 57, which is quite large already, and this body style comes in either standard 62 trim with a 5.5-litre turbocharged V12, or in a new-for-2008 62 S trim with a 6.0-litre turbocharged V12. All models utilise a five-speed automatic and rear-wheel-drive. Standard features include massive seats, leather interior and wood all over. The cars can be customised according to fat-cat customer wishes, including real gold interior trim, special paint finishes, TV tuner, DVD player, CD changer, telephone, Dolby surround sound system, panoramic glass roof, and, especially for the 62, reclining rear seats. Safety features include all the requisite equipment, including a multitude of airbags and electronic stability systems. A handful of limited-edition Landaulet four-door convertible models were built in 2010 for a four times higher price.

An all-new Nissan Navara Pickup was released as a 2017 model year. In the GCC, the engines are carried over from the previous generation but with new transmissions. It is offered with a 2.5-litre four-cylinder petrol engine or a 2.5-litre turbodiesel engine, both of which come with either a 6-speed manual or 7-speed automatic transmission. The two versions share the same features that include 16-inch alloy wheels, bedliner, power door locks, front fog lamps,audio system with CD player, power windows, chrome door mirrors, dual power outside mirrors with LED turn signal lamps, keyless entry, chrome rear bumper and speed-sensing wipers. Safety features include dual front airbags and ABS brakes. Climate control, premium trim and special upholstery are optional equipment.

Hyundai redesigned the Sonata from the ground up in 2011, and facelifted it for 2013. It takes on a 'four-door coupe' profile but without the impracticality or high price. The GCC market receives a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder with a 6-speed automatic transmissions with available paddle-shifters. The base model comes with power steering, power windows, manual a/c with rear cooling ducts, automatic headlights, paddle shifters, power mirrors with indicators, fog lamps, leatherette-wrapped steering wheel, cruise control, CD/MP3 stereo with 6 speakers, USB and AUX ports with iPod cable, steering wheel buttons, 16-inch steel wheels and a single airbag. The mid-range model gains a panoramic glass roof, with automatic rolling cloth roof-shades, as well as 17-inch alloy wheels and ABS. The fully-optioned model is loaded with intelligent keyless entry with start button, power-folding mirrors, HID headlights, chrome door handles, automatic a/c, rear parking sensors, overhead 'map' lights up front, excellent leather upholstery, driver's power-adjusted seat, trip computer, slightly-tinted glass, 6-CD changer, 'amplitude selective' dampers, 18-inch alloys, navigation, Bluetooth, six airbags, and stability control with hill-start assist and brake assist.

The Navigator is the Lincoln-badged luxury version of the Ford Expedition, a full-size 4WD known to be smooth, stable and refined for the most part. Mildly facelifted for 2005, its four-wheel-independent suspension is sophisticated, providing better on-road ride and handling, while low-range gearing is available for off-roading. The standard engine for 2005 onwards was a revised 5.4-litre V8 engine mated to a 6-speed automatic gearbox. What the Navigator does best is move large quantities of people and gear, with its perfectly flat cargo area and third-row seat, with the ability to carry up to eight passengers. The interior was different from its Ford cousin, with faux satin-nickel trim and real wood inserts. Other features include 18-inch wheels, optional power-folding running boards, power liftgate, leather seats and wood trim. Options included a voice-activated touchscreen navigation system, THX audio system, rear-seat DVD player, and HID headlights. Multiple airbags, a tyre-pressure monitor and stability control were standard, with Roll Stability Control an option.

For 2016, the 300 SRT got a minor facelift. It was pretty much the same for 2017. It got some new safety features, updated entertainment system and a new automatic transmission. Under the hood is a 6.4-litre V8 mated to a 8-speed automatic. Standard SRT8 features include leather upholstery, ventilated seats, UConnect multimedia system with touchscreen, 19 Harmon Kardon speakers, dual-pane panoramic sunroof, 20-inch wheels, rear spoiler and more, along with a unique exterior kit. Standard safety features include front, side, knee and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor, adaptive cruise control with auto braking, lane departure warning, blind spot monitor, cross path detection and forward collision warning.

The X5 M debuted in late 2009, with a higher-tuned turbocharged 4.4-litre V8 than the regular X5. The M has a 6-speed auto with proper paddle-shifters. Features include iPod / USB adapter interface, Active Cruise Control with Stop and Go, Lane Departure Warning, Active Steering, running boards, Head-Up Display, 4-zone automatic climate control, side-view cameras, top-view camera, leather-covered dashboard, full keyless entry, and smartphone integration. The M gets 20-inch wheels with performance tyres, Adaptive Drive system, aluminium roof rails, M door sill plates, M driver footrest, M steering wheel and M aerodynamic enhancements. It also gets  features such as sports suspension, 'M' driving mode, paddle-shifted quicker-response automatic, launch control and a body kit.

Almost 5 metres long with a low roofline, the Audi A7 Sportback is a full-sizer riding on 18-inch to 20-inch wheels, and as with all Audi sedans,  really rides a front-wheel-drive platform, with optional 'Quattro' all-wheel-drive tacked onto the higher trim levels. Two V6 engines are offered in the UAE - a 2.8-litre and a supercharged 3.0-litre, both of which are mated to an 'S-tronic' automatic transmission. An S7 was introduced as a 2013 model with a 4.0-litre turbocharged V8 engine. Standard options include 4-zone automatic air-conditioning, reverse-camera, MMI touch-sensitive navigation system, 10-speaker audio system. Optional equipment include interior leather packages for the seats and door trim, sports suspension, air suspension, front and reverse camera, park assist, side assist, night-vision, lane-assist and BOSE surround sound.

An all-new Hyundai Tucson came out in 2022. Under the hood, the base model gets a 2.0-litre engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. The higher model gets a 1.6-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder motor, connected to a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Standard features in the 2022 Tucson include power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth seats, fog lamps, USB port, Bluetooth, manual a/c, rear spoiler, roof rails and 17-inch alloy wheels. Things get better in the higher trim levels, with the top 4WD model additionally outfitted with dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, cruise control, smart key with starter button, leather upholstery, power driver-side seat, front and rear sensors and camera, chrome door handles, electric folding mirrors and 18 or 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features on the 2022 Hyundai Tucson include Smart Parking Assist, Autonomous Emergency Braking, Lane Keeping Assist System, Rear Traffic Cross Alert, Blind Spot Detection, Speed Limit Information Function and Active Bonnet System which will automatically raise the hood to cushion the impact shock in case of a frontal collision.

The all-new Chevrolet Sonic is a sub-compact replacement for the Aveo. Available in sedan and hatchback body-styles, the Sonic was sold in the GCC with a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic with tiptronic function, while a 5-speed manual available in some markets. The base model comes with 5-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, manual a/c, fold-down rear seat, 4-speaker CD/MP3 stereo, optional keyless entry and only one airbag. The mid-range LS model additionally gets steel wheels or optional 15-inch alloy wheels, optional sunroof, power windows, 4-way manually-adjustable driver's seat, better stereo with Bluetooth and more optional speakers, split-folding rear seat, optional parking sensors, optional ABS and two airbags. The top LT model additionally gets 16-inch alloy wheels, cruise control, standard ABS, 6-speaker stereo, and front as well as side airbags.

The small EX35 is what Infiniti likes to call a coupe-crossover, although it is really a compact five-door wagon. Powered by a 3.5-litre V6, it comes with a new 7-speed automatic for 2011, as well as standard all-wheel-drive. It has an excellent leather interior, power front seats, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, sunroof, automatic headlamps, Bluetooth hands-free phone system, power tilt and telescopic wheel, six-CD/MP3 Bose stereo, power mirrors, stability control, intelligent keyless entry and start and an advanced front-side-curtain airbag system. There is no low-range gearing as the EX35 sits low and the chassis is tuned for on-road dynamics. The EX35 also comes with nifty features such as a seven-inch colour display with Infiniti controller for the trip computer and additional vehicle information, including the Infiniti DVD navigation system. But the most interesting feature by far is the around-view parking system that uses four cameras to simulate a 360-degree image of what is around the vehicle, thereby making parking easier in tight spots.

For 2016, the 300 SRT got a facelift, giving it a more aggressive look. It got some new safety features, updated entertainment system and a new automatic transmission. Under the hood is a 6.4-litre V8 mated to a 8-speed automatic. Standard SRT8 features include leather upholstery, ventilated seats, UConnect multimedia system with touchscreen, 19 Harmon Kardon speakers, dual-pane panoramic sunroof, 20-inch wheels, rear spoiler and more, along with a unique exterior kit. Standard safety features include front, side, knee and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor, adaptive cruise control with auto braking, lane departure warning, blind spot monitor, cross path detection and forward collision warning.

Powered by a 3.5-litre V6, it comes with a new 7-speed automatic for 2011, as well as standard all-wheel-drive. It has an excellent leather interior, power front seats, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, sunroof, automatic headlamps, Bluetooth hands-free phone system, power tilt and telescopic wheel, six-CD/MP3 Bose stereo, power mirrors, stability control, intelligent keyless entry and start and an advanced front-side-curtain airbag system. But the most interesting feature by far is the around-view parking system that uses four cameras to simulate a 360-degree image of what is around the vehicle, thereby making parking easier in tight spots.

The Jaguar XK received a face-lift for 2012. The XK Coupe and Convertible are powered by a 5.0-litre V8 direct-injection engine, while a supercharged version of the same V8 powers the high-performance XKR. That too can be had in either coupe or convertible format. Both engines are mated to a six-speed automatic gearbox with paddle shifters. An even more powerful XKR-S was released in 2012 with the same supercharged 5.0-litre engine but producing even more horsepower. Changes include a new wider front grille, enlarged vents in the lower grille with chrome accents, LED daytime running lights and slightly thinner headlamps. Its rigid chassis and CATS adaptive suspension aim for a smooth ride and sporty cornering. Standard equipment includes DVD navigation, keyless entry and keyless start, a seven-inch video display, Bluetooth capability, cruise control, a 6-CD/MP3 player, rear park assist, cruise control, and electronic parking brake. Options include adaptive cruise control with a forward-alert system that sounds an audible warning, full soft leather upholstery, and a CD stereo system. Safety feature include front and side airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, dynamic stability control with a track feature, and electronic rollover mitigation.

Mercedes-Benz GLC replaced the GLK and also added a Coupe model in 2017. Under the hood, the GLC 43 AMG Coupe sports a twin-turbocharged 3.0-litre V6 engine, mated to the 4Matic all-wheel-drive system. Power is delivered via a 9-speed automatic transmission. Features include AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Dodge Charger received a significant facelift in 2015. The previous engines are there, which includes the 3.6-litre V6 and 5.7-litre V8, aside from the SRT models. They all get the 8-speed automatic transmission. In 2019, Dodge added the 6.4-litre V8 engine from the SRT models into the R/T line. The base Dodge Charger model gets a manual a/c, cruise control, cloth upholstery, 18-inch alloy wheels, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with 4.3-inch touchscreen and USB port, auto headlights, intelligent keyless entry and other standard features. The 2020 Dodge Charger SXT V6 trim level additionally comes with an 8.4-inch touchscreen, stereo amplifier, auto a/c with rear vents, power seats, heated/cooled cup-holders, leather, remote start, Bluetooth, HID headlights, sunroof and more, with some of these features reserved for the SXT Plus version offered in certain markets such as the UAE. The GT and GTS V6 models comes with an appearance package. The 2020 Dodge Charger R/T model comes in different trim levels. The base R/T gets almost all the features of the top V6 model except for leather and fancy cup-holders, but gains sportier suspension and brakes, with options such as power seats, the fancy cup-holders, premium audio and a few other features, depending on market. The top R/T Scat Pack model gets the bigger 6.4-litre V8 engine, sportier suspension, steering, exhaust, grille, spoiler and 20-inch alloys. Standard safety features on all models include front, side and curtain airbags, ABS, stability control, tyre pressure monitor and optional adaptive cruise control with auto braking.

The Veracruz is a midsize crossover 4WD that aims for luxury and onroad performance. Hyundai positions the Veracruz as an alternative to luxury crossovers but with a lower price. However, it is still the company's most expensive 4WD model, and base models are pretty bare on safety. The Veracruz is longer and wider than the Santa Fe, and comes standard with three rows of seats for seven passengers on all but the base model. The Veracruz comes in three trim levels here. All are powered by the same 3.8-litre V6 engine mated to a six-speed automatic. All models ride on 17-inch wheels, and come standard with all-wheel-drive and ABS with EBD. Basic features include power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, alarm, CD/MP3 with 6 speakers, manual air-conditioning, side steps, and only a single airbag. The mid-level model adds cruise control, faux leather and a power liftgate. The top model adds xenon headlights, power driver seat, sunroof, rain-sensing wipers, six-CD changer and more speakers, dual-zone a/c, stability control, dual airbags, side airbags and curtain airbags. Navigation is optional, but there is no low-range gearing.

The Pilot is Honda's midsize 4x4 offering, and their largest offering at this time. The facelifted-for-2012 SUV attempts to move slightly upscale with its available luxury options. The new look features a new standard grille, new front and rear bumpers, and optional new wheels, along with a few other cabin additions. The Pilot can seat eight people at a pinch. The standard 3.5-litre V6 engine features Variable Cylinder Management (VCM) which allows it to operate on half the cylinders when power is not needed, improving fuel economy. Also standard is a basic 5-speed automatic. Based on the same platform as the Odyssey minivan, the Pilot claims to be an off-roader, but only succeeds moderately, with an all-wheel-drive system that can lock itself in a 50:50 front/rear power split, but with no low-range gearing. Standard features include cloth upholstery, fog lights, roof rails, cruise control, tri-zone auto a/c, 7-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with USB/AUX ports, auto headlights, rear parking sensors, split-folding rear seats and 17-inch alloy wheels. The top Touring model can be had with leather upholstery, 10-speaker stereo with hard-drive navigation, rear DVD entertainment, rear camera, rear sun blinds, powered front seats, sunroof and 18-inch alloy wheels. Standard safety features include ABS, traction control, stability control, front-side airbags and curtain airbags.

An identical replica of the Porsche 356 Speedster from the 1960s, the new-age Speedster II is hand-built by French outfit Pierre GÃ©rard Organisation, also known as PGO. Changes to the basic design include higher-positioned mirrors, modern tail-lights and stylish 16-inch or 17-inch rims. The chassis is made of composite materials, is attached to a steel frame. The engine, a Peugeot-sourced 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, is mounted in the rear, while the small luggage compartment is in the front. Standard setup include rear-wheel-drive, a 5-speed manual gearbox and a cloth soft top. Features of the original include a cloth or leather interior, electric mirrors, basic CD stereo and as many as eight whole gauges, but not much else. The windows are of the removable variety, and the soft top is manual. The car stays true to its roots and therefore has no ABS brakes, no airbags and not even power steering. However, the 2008 model features luxuries such as power windows, a/c, electric mirrors, CD/MP3 stereo and keyless entry, as well as a 4-speed automatic gearbox. Sold only in a few GCC countries, the Speedster offers a pure driving experience few cars offer, but it can only be regarded as an expensive toy.

An all-new Lincoln Navigator debuted for 2018, still a rebodied version of the new-for-2018 Ford Expedition. The Navigator L is the long-wheelbase version, with more boot space. All new Navigators make extensive use of high-strength aluminium-alloy to lose weight while offering more space inside. Power continues to be provided by an uprated twin-turbo V6 and mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission, similar to the Ford F-150 Raptor. The top model is known as the Signature. Inside, both front seats feature heating/cooling/massaging functions and are adjustable in 30 ways. Rear seats have a recline function. Available rear-seat entertainment features include 10-inch adjustable screens. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are part of the standard SYNC 3 touchscreen system, along with navigation, Bluetooth, phone, etc. A total of 20 speakers with the optional Revel II audio system can create distinct listening modes including audience, on-stage, and stereo. A Lincoln “welcome mat” will illuminate on the ground beneath the front doors, and the Lincoln star badge in the grille lights up too. Other available notable features include powered side-steps, heads-up display, customisable LCD gauge cluster and USB ports for the power-adjustable third row. Safety features are extensive, with a full set of airbags, ESP, ABS, lane-departure warning, blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, al-round parking sensors with cameras and all that.

A new generation Nissan X-Trail debuted in the GCC in 2015. It got a facelfit for the 2018 model year. Featuring a completely revised exterior and interior, it gets a 2.5-litre 4 cylinder engine, mated to a CVT gearbox. The base model is front-wheel-drive, but all other trim levels are all-wheel-drive with an electronic 4x4 lock feature. There's also a choice of 5-seater and 7-seater layouts. Standard features include power windows, power steering, electric mirrors, fabric seats, keyless entry with central locking, manual A/C, AM/FM radio with CD/USB/AUX, cruise control, smart keyless entry with starter button, and steel or 17-inch alloy wheels. Optional features include better entertainment system with screen and more speakers, bigger alloy wheels, parking sensors, rear camera, panoramic glass roof, leather, power front seats, navigation, 18-inch alloys and automatic a/c, among other things. Standard safety features include driver and passenger airbags with optional side airbags, ABS brakes, electronic brake distribution (EBD) and Brake Assist (BA).

The all-new 6-Series was introduced in 2003, filling the hole in the line-up left since the end of the 8-Series. The last actual 6-Series was around back in the 1980s. Based on the underpinnings of the 5-Series, the new 6-Series was introduced with a 4.4 L V8 engine for the 645Ci, but this has since been replaced by the 650Ci with a 4.8-litre V8 in 2006. In 2004, a more affordable inline 6-cylinder engine was introduced in the 630i, upgraded in power for 2006. This was soon followed by a convertible model. Unlike that of the new 5-Series and 7-Series models, the styling of the new 6 Series has generally received a warm welcome from the public, for unknown reasons. The new 6-Series was designed to look like a shark, and really does remind you of one, but it is far from good-looking. The controversial "Bangle-butt" rear styling works somewhat better on the shapely 6-Series than on other BMW models though. The 6-Series has become the vehicle of choice for rich town-cruising yuppies, but it is actually an excellent performance car, available with a six-speed manual or a six-speed automatic, with an available six-speed SMG automanual in the V8. A mild facelift came for the 2008 model, adding minor gadgetry updates.

An all-new Audi S4 made its debut in the UAE and GCC in 2020. Under the hood, the all-wheel-drive S4 gets a 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 engine, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include LED running lights, three-zone automatic air conditioning, front seats with lumbar support and ventilation, MMI computer control system, intelligent key that stores the vehicle's service info, and a Bang & Olufsen audio system. Also available are side-assist warning system for safe lane changes, and a parking system with a rear-view camera. The S4 also gets a dynamic system that Audi called Drive Select that manipulates transmission shifts, steering feel and suspension settings. All models get the usual power accessories as well as safety features such as multiple airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Kia Seltos is a generically handsome sub-compact crossover that debuted for 2020. The LED headlamps, DRLs and fog lamps adorn the front and rear, at least in top-trim models. The UAE and GCC markets will get a non-turbo 1.6-litre and a turbo 1.4-litre, both mated to a 6-speed automatic and front-wheel-drive, although other markets get better engines and options. Inside, the GCC-spec 2021 Kia Seltos is offered with an 8-inch infotainment screen, basic cruise control, sunroof, rear camera, manual or automatic a/c, 3.5-inch or 7-inch gauge cluster screen, and up to 6 airbags. Android Auto and Apple CarPlay are not offered.

The Lotus Elise is a super-light sports convertible with a supercharged 1.8-litre 4-cylinder engine. It gets go-kart like handling, thanks to its light weight, as well as its aerodynamics and aluminium chassis. The soft-top is standard on the Elise, with the option of a hard-top as well. It can be had with either a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard options include light weight aluminium passenger foot-rest, proBax seats, plain black leather sun-visors, light weight aluminium foot-well divider, black leather steering wheel, black leather gear lever gaiter, polished aluminium gear-knob and hand break sleeve, radio and single CD/MP3 player with 4 speakers, immobiliser with remote activated alarm and central door locking. Upgrade packages are offered for the Elise - the Touring Pack offers leather ProBax seats, leather door panels, perforated leather door inserts, leather trimmed centre console, handbrake gaiter, black carpet mats with embroidered Elise logo, noise insulation paneling, auxiliary driving lights, iPod stereo connection, trinket tray divider and cup holder. The Sport Pack offers Bilstein sports dampers, twin oil coolers, 7-twin-spoke ultra light weight forged alloy wheels in Hi-power silver and ProBax sports seats. Safety features include driver and passenger front airbags, traction control system (TCS) and torque-sensing limited slip differential.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz E-Class Coupe made its debut as a 2018 model year. It adopted the new design culture already first seen on the S-Class, and followed by the C-Class. Three models were introduced - the E200 and E300 which get the 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and the all-wheel drive E400 which gets the 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 motor. All models get the 9-speed automatic transmission. Inside, most dashboard buttons have been replaced by a screen which can be accessed via a rotary controller or an optional touchpad. For the first time, air suspension is now offered. Standard safety features include multiple airbags, stability control and traction control. Various optional safety systems include Active Parking Assist, Adaptive Highbeam Assist Plus, Traffic Sign Assist with Wrong-Way Alert, Drive Pilot and Evasive Steering Assist.

Changes to the basic design include higher-positioned mirrors, modern tail-lights and stylish 16-inch or 17-inch rims. The chassis is made of composite materials, is attached to a steel frame. The engine, a Peugeot-sourced 2.0-litre 4-cylinder, is mounted in the rear, while the small luggage compartment is in the front. Standard setup include rear-wheel-drive, a 5-speed manual gearbox and a cloth soft top. Features of the original include a cloth or leather interior, electric mirrors, basic CD stereo and as many as eight whole gauges, but not much else. The windows are of the removable variety, and the soft top is manual. The car stays true to its roots and therefore has no ABS brakes, no airbags and not even power steering. However, the 2008 model features luxuries such as power windows, a/c, electric mirrors, CD/MP3 stereo and keyless entry, as well as a 4-speed automatic gearbox. Sold only in a few GCC countries, the Speedster offers a pure driving experience few cars offer, but it can only be regarded as an expensive toy.

The Audi Q3 is the German manufacturer's 'baby SUV' offering. It got a facelift for the 2015 model year. There are three engine options, namely the turbocharged 1.4-litre with a 6-speed automatic, and two tunes of the 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbocharged powerplant mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission and "Quattro" all-wheel drive. The Q3 gets a lot of the standard features in the base model such as automatic xenon headlamps, LED rear lights, 17-inch alloy rims, automatic air-conditioning, 8-speaker audio system, AUX-IN port, front and side airbags, hill-start assist and ESC. The higher spec model gets hill-hold assist, parking sensors, driver information system, Bluetooth and cruise control.

The GMC Yukon got a new 6-speed automatic transmission from 2009 onward and also the Yukon Denali got a slight power increase. A beefy Vortec 5.3-litre V8 powers the Yukon, with better fuel economy to boot. The V8 powers the rear wheels on the road, or through all four wheels when the standard 4WD system is engaged. Features include power windows, electric mirrors and additional power equipment, along with a folding third-row seat. Power-adjustable brake and accelerator pedals are standard on the higher models and optional on the base versions. New features also include power folding rear seats, among other things. On the road, Yukon is smooth and stable in a straight line, hopeless in the corners and strong off the road. The Yukon XL is the long-wheelbase GMC version of the Suburban, and offers more room in the back. Rear passengers can enjoy an optional package that includes a DVD system with flip-down seven-inch colour monitor, six-disc in-dash audio player and Bose speakers. The Denali version adds a 6.2-litre V8 with a 6-speed auto, chrome trim and some luxury interior features, but loses off-road gearing.

Based on the E-Class platform, the Mercedes-Benz CLS continues the trend of offering a repackaged midsize luxury sedan in a prettier suit. Facelifted for 2015, the CLS 63 AMG comes with a new 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 and a 7-speed automatic mated to a rear-wheel-drive base. Standard features include leather upholstery, active parking assist, memory electric front seats, COMAND multimedia system, electric rear-window blinds, automatic a/c and LED exterior running lamps, sunroof, active shape-shifting front seats with fans, rear camera, intelligent keyless entry, DVD changer, Harman Kardon stereo, TV tuner and more. The CLS 63 AMG can be had with a limited-slip rear diff, adjustable suspension, carbon-fibre trim inside and out, ceramic brakes and other optional items at extra cost, including an AMG performance package that adds additional horsepower.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it is not really that good off-road, but gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. It is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. This wagon offers room for five passengers, with the option of two additional rear-facing seats in the luggage area. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, cruise control, electric driver's seat, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, a power front passenger seat,  16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, and WHIPS whiplash protection.
