Standard options in the G90 include power steering, power windows, electric folding mirrors, central locking, keyless entry, push engine start-stop, leather upholstery, memory and ventilated seats, audio system with AUX/USB support, auto A/C, navigation, auto defog system, rain sensors, sunroof, parking assist system, rear electric curtain, xenon headlamps, LED headlights and taillights with LED daytime running lamps, front and rear camera, air suspension and 19-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include 9 airbags, lane keep assist, adaptive cruise control, ABS, traction control, stability control, brake assist, blind spot detection and autonomous emergency braking (AEB).

The Cadillac CT6 is the American luxury brand's flagship sedan. It takes on the Germans, but it weighs less than a 5-Series and an E-Class. Under the hood, there are three engine choices available. The standard model gets the turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine, which is currently not sold in the GCC. Then there is the naturally aspirated 3.6-litre V6 engine and the current top trim gets a turbocharged 3.0-litre V6 unit. All motors get a 8-speed automatic transmission. Standard features for the rear-wheel drive CT6 include power windows, power mirrors, LED headlights and tail lamps and fog lamps. Optional equipment include Cadillac's CUE entertainment system with 34 BOSE speakers, rear seat infotainment system with 10-inch-diagonal screens that retract into the front seatbacks, quad-zone climate control, bigger alloy wheels and adaptive forward lighting. Safety features include ABS and traction control, sensors to warn driver of potential dangers, safety seat alert which sends immediate impulse through the seat cushion from the direction of the potential hazard.

The Canadian-built MKX is the Lincoln-badged version of the Ford Edge, an all-new soft-roader that debuted for the 2007 model year. The Edge features a car-derived platform, a raked windshield, a fast-sloping back window, a high-mounted rear spoiler, a high beltline and standard 18-inch alloy wheels. The interior features seating for five and cargo space can be maximized when the rear seats are folded. The Edge is powered by a new 3.5-liter V6 mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Available with an intelligent all-wheel-drive system in the GCC, the MKX is not equipped with low-range gearing. The interior features a center console that can fit a laptop computer and a number of standard features including leather upholstery, a panoramic Vista Roof, rear DVD screen, an MP3 audio jack and six-way power-adjustable front seats. Standard safety features include Advance Trac with Roll Stability Control, seat-mounted side airbags and Safety Canopy air curtain system with rollover detection and side-curtain airbags.

Created by Ford's SVT team, the updated-for-2010 Shelby GT500 is the most powerful car you can buy at its price. Powered by a supercharged and intercooled 5.4-litre DOHC V8 engine, it comes with a 6-speed manual,and a new final drive ratio changed from 3.31 to 3.55 for better acceleration. For 2011, Ford switched to an aluminium engine block, making it 55 kg lighter while adding 10 hp. Features include a twin-disc clutch to improve driveability, a resonator to reduce the supercharger whine, a domed aluminium bonnet to help in cooling, and a conical air filter for better breathing. The suspension system remains independent at the front and live-axle at the rear. Brakes, suspension and steering have also been improved. The GT500 gets Goodyear F1 Supercar tyres and aluminium wheels. The coupe gets forged 19-inch rims while the convertible gets cast 18-inch ones. A redesigned front splitter, a revised duck-tail spoiler, and a fake rear diffuser housing large dual exhaust tips complete the exterior package for the beefed-up facelifted Mustang. The interior uses genuine leather, real aluminium trim and upscale Alcantara inserts. Convenience features include Ford's SYNC voice-activated hands-free in-car communication and entertainment system, Bluetooth, power windows and mirrors, customisable ambient lighting and cruise control. The GT500 also features safety devices such as stability control with sport mode, ABS, dual front airbags, side-impact airbags and more. It might be available through special order in GCC markets.

The 5-seater Jeep Grand Cherokee got a second facelift for the 2017 model year. Offered with a choice of the 3.6-litre "Pentastar" V6 or the 5.7-litre "Hemi" V8, both come with a new 8-speed automatic, four-wheel-drive with low-range and four trim levels. The base Laredo is V6 only, the Limited can be V6 or V8, and the Overland is V8 only. Another trim level introduced for 2014 is the Summit which also comes in only V8 form. The SRT8 version gets a name-change to only "SRT" for 2014, as well as a 6.4-litre V8, 8-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive with no low-range. For non-SRT versions, depending on trim level, there is a choice of two 4x4 systems, Quadra-Lift air suspension on the Overland, and a new Selec-Terrain system with crawl control. The Mercedes-Benz-derived platform has independent front and rear suspension, stiffer new body structure and more space. Another feature on all models is the new 8.4-inch touchscreen display and 7-inch customer configurable multiview cluster display. Even the Laredo is well-equipped, with body-colour bumpers, 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, power driver's seat, dual-zone manual a/c, keyless start, CD/MP3 stereo, cloth upholstery, HID automatic headlights, fog lamps, and the usual power accessories. The Limited adds leather, Alpine premium audio, automatic a/c, panoramic roof, 18-inch wheels, rain-sensing wipers, navigation, 30GB hard drive and UConnect Bluetooth phone. The Overland adds chrome bumper trim, painted wheel arches, real leather, real wood trim, stitched-leather dash trim, ventilated power-adjustable front seats, 9-speaker audio with subwoofer and 20-inch wheels, with various options and accessories available. The Summit has similar options to the Limited, with the addition of a unique SRT-like front bumper, more premium leather and wood panels for the interior. The SRT8 version gets a unique body kit, sports suspension, sports seats and other trim bits. Safety features available include standard active head restraints, front airbags, full-length side-curtain and seat-mounted side airbags, stability control, electronic roll mitigation, hill-start assist and optional trailer-sway control. An optional blind-spot/rear cross-path detection system and adaptive cruise control with forward collision warning are also available.

The  Milan is Mercury's new midsize five-passenger sedan that is designed to appeal to a younger audience and provides a new entry point to the Mercury brand, as Mercury's first vehicle in this segment in more than a decade. It is based on a modified Mazda 6 platform, but features signature Mercury design cues including waterfall grille and satin aluminium trim. It is powered by a Mazda-derived 2.3-litre four-cylinder, mated to a 5-speed automatic. The premium interior features upgraded materials such as leather seats and either Satin Metallic or Wales Mahogany wood trim, and available two-tone leather seating surfaces with contrast stitching. Standard equipment includes power windows, electric mirrors, an auxiliary audio input jack, fold-down passenger seat, front-seat side airbags, side-impact air curtains, ABS brakes, traction control, and a security package highlighted by side-impact airbags, side-curtain airbags for all rows, and an anti-theft alarm system. Options include some sort of appearance package, rear spoiler, and more.

The new-for-2011 Kia Sportage has been redesigned from the ground up, barely larger than the outgoing model, and based on Hyundai underpinnings. Now powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive, and a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder with all-wheel-drive, both engines are mated to a 6-speed automatic. The base 2.0-litre FWD model comes with power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth seats, fog lamps, manual a/c, rear spoiler, roof rails, CD/MP3 stereo with 6 speakers and USB/AUX inputs, 17-inch steel wheels, ABS and only a single driver-side airbag. Things get better in the higher trim levels, with the top 2.4-litre AWD model additionally outfitted with dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, cruise control, smart key with starter button, leather upholstery, power driver-side seat, stereo with subwoofer and iPod cable, rear sensors and camera, chrome door handles, electric folding mirrors, 18-inch alloy wheels, and improved safety features such as ABS with stability control, active headrests and two front airbags, though still no side airbags. The Sportage received high ratings in European crash tests, but keep in mind that they apply to a model with six airbags.

The X6 is what you get when you chop the top off an X5. It is dubbed the world's first "Sport Activity Coupe," which unfortunately abbreviates down to "SAC." While still technically a 4WD, the new-for-2009 X6 comes in two models, namely the XDrive35i and the XDrive50i, both being powerful high-end models, in keeping with its exclusive nature. It is therefore powered by either a 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-6 or a 4.4-litre turbocharged V8, both mated to 6-speed manually-shiftable automatics. The X6 gets a new all-wheel drive system, without low-range gearing, but improving on-road handling. Redesigned to be shorter in height than its practical sibling, the X6 offers seating for only four in its chop-top cabin. A whole host of features include standard bi-xenon headlights, BMW's controversial iDrive computer, 19-inch alloy wheels, run-flat tyres, tyre-pressure monitor, 10-way power front seats, and new leather colour schemes. Other available features include active steering, automatic tailgate, adaptive headlights, rear-mounted DVD system, reverse-view camera, satellite-navigation, four-zone air-conditioning, and bigger rims. Standard safety features include front, side and side head airbags, and crash-activated front-seat headrests, as well as stability control, ABS and a fancy new driving aid called Dynamic Performance Control.

The budget APV multi-purpose people carrier has a name that stands for All-Purpose Vehicle and offers up to eight seats or a panel-van body. That makes the APV one of the few passenger vehicles sold here that have more than seven seats. Built on a ladder frame chassis, the APV is supposed to be tough and affordable. It is designed in Japan and assembled in Indonesia. Although production costs were kept low, Suzuki engineers tried not to cut corners when it came to safety. The APV has Suzuki's proprietary TECT body, which is a structural design that's supposed to redirect collision energy away from occupants. The doors are reinforced with side impact beams and there are two front airbags that come as standard. Externally, the APV looks clean and distinctive in an oddball kind of way. It's dimensions translate into a roomy interior, but having eight adults in the APV is possible for average-sized people who just manage to fit. Luggage space is limited with the third-row seats up, but can be expanded by folding the rear seats forward, which then liberates enough space to allow you to transport something as big as a washing machine. Available features include rear air-conditioning, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking with remote control, 15-inch alloy wheels and a 1.6-litre engine with either a manual or an automatic.

The Jimny is a longstanding Suzuki 4WD dating back to the 1980s Samurai. With its rounded 1999 facelift, it entered the modern age in with a lot of enthusiasm. Powered by a 1.3-litre four-cylinder engine, it can be had with either a five-speed manual or four-speed automatic. For what it's worth, the manual version is much quicker than the automatic one, though both are still painfully slow. Off-road, the Jimny holds its own against bigger 4WD vehicles. A separate chassis means that the Jimny has been constructed with serious off-road use in mind. Four adults can be carried on short journeys as long as they don't bring any luggage, but even then, front seat occupants will probably be called upon to sacrifice some legroom. When carrying rear passengers, the luggage area behind them is tiny. It is better to think of this vehicle as a two-seater with a fold-down rear bench. Driver and passenger airbags are available, as are ABS brakes. The Jimny is outdated, but finding another off-roader at this price is an unrealistic idea.

The undeniable mascot of the VW range, the car popularly known as the New Beetle isn't that new anymore, but still a weird head-turning cruiser. Launched in 1999, it hass received a few facelifts over the years, but is still essentially the same. Passengers must make some concessions for retro style. Interior ergonomics are not as good as that in a traditional car, and there isn't a lot of trunk space. But the Beetle does come in an assortment of bright colours, including sunflowery yellow and limey green. Its exterior and interior design details are fun and creative, but very much on the feminine side. On the road, the Beetle is smooth and handles fairly okay. The convertible adds to the fun with its ability to drop the top. But the New Beetle hardly offers blistering performance, with a choice of 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre four-cylinder engines, with either a manual or an automatic. All Beetles are well equipped, with an AM/FM/cassette stereo, central locking with keyless remote, anti-theft system, four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, dual airbags, power exterior mirrors and windows, among others. Options include a CD changer and electronic stability control.

The Morris Garages nameplate, an off-shoot of the defunct Rover brand, has been resurrected by the Chinese SAIC group, and their first product is the MG 750, midsize front-wheel-drive sedan based fully on a facelifted Rover 75. The MG 750 comes with an updated 183 hp 2.5-litre V6, 5-speed automatic, 16-inch alloy wheels, independent suspension, four-wheel ventilated disc brakes, cruise control, dual front airbags, stability control, ABS with EBD, leather seats, power-adjustable driver's seat, adjustable steering wheel, steering-mounted radio controls, automatic climate control a/c, CD/MP3 stereo with 8 speakers, CD changer, sunroof, keyless entry, auto headlights, cooled central cubby box, illuminated sunshade mirrors and parking sensors. Options such as GPS and side airbags are apparently not yet available in GCC-spec models, but may be offered later.

The Lincoln Continental is the Ford-owned luxury brand's all-new flagship sedan. Three engine choices are available - the base model gets 3.7-litre V6 engine, while there is a turbocharged 2.7 V6 and turbocharged 3.0 V6 motors on offer as well. All engines are mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission. Only the all-wheel drive models are available in the GCC but other markets get a front-wheel drive option as well. Standard features on the Continental include adaptive power steering, power windows, adaptive HID headlamps and LED daytime running lamps, power mirrors, premium sound system with 10 speakers, 8-inch touchscreen with SYNC 3, 2 USB ports, push start engine, push button shift transmission, front and rear parking sensors, rearview camera, leather seats, and 19-inch alloy wheels. Higher models get more interior trim choices, premium LED headlamps, massage seats for the rear, better sound system with 19 speakers, more adjustable power seats for the front, voice activated touch screen, 360 camera for parking and 20-inch alloy rims. Standard safety features include front, side and knee airbags, stability control, brake assist, ABS, electronic brake distribution (EBD) and ABS. Higher models get lane-keeping assist, blind spot monitor and driver alert system.

The Silverado range is Chevrolet's line of full-size pickup trucks, and covers everything from passenger pickups to big honking diesel monsters with six wheels and more. The Silverado pickup is the second-best selling vehicle in the United States, behind the Ford F-150 pickup truck, and it sells more trucks there than Toyota sells Camry cars. The Silverado 1500 light pickup truck is about the only vehicle that you can drive from this range without offending anyone around you, while the Silverado HD trucks should best be used if you work at a place that requires regular hauling. The light-duty trucks generally use the 1500 name, can tow up to 4700 kg and can carry 930 kg in their beds. They are available in three cab lengths, 2-door short cab, 3 or 4-door extended cab, and front-hinged 4-door crew cab. Three cargo beds are available, including a short box, a standard box, and a long box. The short box is only available with the extended or crew cab, and is the only option on the 4-door. Engines include a Vortec 4800 V8 and a Vortec 5300 V8. The Vortec 6000 V8 is available in the Heavy Duty models but not in the 1500 models, while the Z71 signifies an off-road package.

Based on the latest E-Class platform, the Mercedes-Benz CLS continues the trend of offering a repackaged midsize luxury sedan in a prettier suit. The CLS 63 AMG comes with a new 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 and a 7-speed automatic mated to a rear-wheel-drive base. Standard features include leather upholstery, active parking assist, memory electric front seats, COMAND multimedia system, electric rear-window blinds, automatic a/c and LED exterior running lamps, sunroof, active shape-shifting front seats with fans, rear camera, intelligent keyless entry, DVD changer, Harman Kardon stereo, TV tuner and more. The CLS 63 AMG can be had with a limited-slip rear diff, adjustable suspension, carbon-fibre trim inside and out, ceramic brakes and other optional items at extra cost, including an AMG performance package that adds additional horsepower.

The top-spec IS-F sports sedan model finally debuted in 2011 in the GCC with a 5.0-litre V8 and paddle-shifted 8-speed automatic. The rear-wheel-drive IS comes with an impressive set of standard features that includes a premium sound system with CD auto-changer MP3 and WMA compatibility along with 13 speakers, power windows and front seats, keyless entry and start, cruise control, HID headlamps with auto-leveling system, and a fabric interior. The numerous options include a Mark Levinson premium surround sound system with DVD and 14 speakers, moonroof, ventilated front seats, navigation system, power rear window sunshade, auto wiper system, adaptive front-lighting system, rear view monitor system and park assist system. Safety features that come standard include numerous airbags, electronic stability control, traction control, ABS, and electronic brake-force distribution. Lexus's Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Management system, which includes traction control, vehicle stability control and ABS with electronic brake-force distribution, is standard. Options include a "Pre-Crash" safety system and two-tone leather seats. The IS-F comes with lowered sports suspension, special wheels, sports seats, special cabin trim and a body kit along with the uniquely-tuned V8.

An all-new Dodge Ram was released for 2019. Available only in the four-door crew-cab body style for now, the new Ram 1500 is offered in Big Horn, Rebel, Laramie and Limited trims for the GCC region. The exterior styling is a departure from the Ram’s previous three generations’ “big rig” looks, with a selection of grille designs and headlight configurations based on the trim you buy. The top-dog Limited features the most chrome, and also comes with 22-inch wheels and electric-folding side-steps. The Rebel gets a black plastic-cladded look with 18-inch wheels, slightly lifted ride height and fixed side steps. Inside, the abundantly-spacious Ram features stitched-leatherette on the dash, doors and sides of the centre-console as well as a huge 12-inch touchscreen in the Limited version. The screen is fairly responsive, and there are still physical buttons for the main a/c controls along the sides. The Rebel gets an 8.4-inch touchscreen. Aside from the wonderfully-configurable centre-console storage and two glove-boxes, there are also underfloor and underseat storage compartments in the rear-seat area. The useful lockable RamBox feature in the bed is carried over from the previous model and remains optional. The bed itself has LED lights and the tailgate is damped so it doesn’t slam open. It is still powered by a 5.7-litre “Hemi” V8 and mated to a knob-controlled 8-speed automatic. The motor has cylinder-deactivation tech. A 3.6-litre V6 will be offered later on the base trim. Underneath, the Ram’s ladder frame is held up by coil-spring rear suspension in contrast to rivals’ rear leaf springs. Height-adjustable air suspension is optional, as is a locking rear differential.

The undeniable mascot of the VW range, the car popularly known as the New Beetle isn't that new anymore, but still a weird head-turning cruiser. Launched in 1999, it hass received a few facelifts over the years, but is still essentially the same. Passengers must make some concessions for retro style. Interior ergonomics are not as good as that in a traditional car, and there isn't a lot of trunk space. But the Beetle does come in an assortment of bright colours, including sunflowery yellow and limey green. Its exterior and interior design details are fun and creative, but very much on the feminine side. On the road, the Beetle is smooth and handles fairly okay. The convertible adds to the fun with its ability to drop the top. But the New Beetle hardly offers blistering performance, with a choice of 1.6-litre and 2.0-litre four-cylinder engines, with either a manual or an automatic. All Beetles are well equipped, with an AM/FM/cassette stereo, central locking with keyless remote, anti-theft system, four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, dual airbags, power exterior mirrors and windows, among others. Options include a CD changer and electronic stability control.

The five-door Leon is arguably the sportiest model in the Seat line-up, and the best interpretation of the new Seat design language yet. Named after a Spanish city, yet based on the VW Golf, the Leon offers an array of engines, including a 1.6-litre, a 2.0-litre and three turbocharged 2.0-litre units, all from Volkswagen. Depending on model, there are manual, automatic or DSG automanual gearboxes available. Standard features include power front windows, electric mirrors, cloth upholstery, keyless entry, ABS brakes, traction control, electronic stability control and anti-slip regulation. Also available are front airbags, side and curtain airbags, a tyre pressure sensor, electric mirrors and a quality CD audio system. Basic models get 16-inch steel wheels with hubcaps, while climbing up the model range allows for 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels. Options include special upholstery, cruise control, onboard computer, rear power windows and side mirror with electric parking position. The sporty FR gets the first turbo engine, sports seats, lowered suspension and other trim bits. The Cupra carries the FR concept further with an upgraded turbo engine and a body kit, among other changes. The Cupra R replaced the Cupra later on with more power.

Mini released an all-new Cooper and Cooper S 5-door hatchback model in 2015 model. The Mini Cooper will be getting a twin-turbocharged 1.5-litre 3-cylinder engine, while the Cooper S gets a twin-turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine. They can both be had in either a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, fabric seats and alloy rims. Optional features include rain sensor, Park Distance Control, Comfort Access, electrically operated glass roof, roof rails, electrically heated and folding exterior mirrors, interior and exterior mirrors with automatic anti-dazzle function, seat heating, 2-zone automatic air conditioning, rear spoiler in John Cooper Works design, large selection of decorative roof and exterior mirror options, bonnet stripes, seat upholsteries, interior surfaces and Colour Lines, MINI navigation system, MINI Radio Visual Boost and Harman Kardon hi-fi speaker system.Standard safety systems include front and side airbags, ABS brakes and stability control. Driver assistance systems package includes MINI Head-Up-Display, Driving Assistant including camera-based active cruise control, collision and pedestrian warning with initial brake function, high beam assistant and road sign detection, parking assistant; rear view camera.

The BMW X6 M got a new model for the 2015 model year. Under the hood, it comes with a twin-turbocharged 4.4-litre V8 engine, mated to a 8-speed Steptronic automatic transmission. Standard features in the X6 M include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, Merino leather sports seats,  leather wrapped M-steering wheel with aluminium paddle shifters, leather-wrapped dashboard, Alcantara roof liner, M-branded door sill plates, aluminium trim, contrast stitching, a 4-zone automatic climate control system, Harman Kardon audio system, xenon headlamps and 21-inch alloy wheels. Standard safety features include front driver and passenger airbags, curtain airbags, dynamic stability control (DSC), rollover sensors and tyre defect sensors.

The CL-Class, the coupe version of the S-Class on which it is based, received a minor facelift for the 2011 model. This coupe features numerous innovative safety technology, such as up-front sensors which make it possible to assess the impact severity at an early stage during a crash and activate the front passenger airbag in two stages depending on the severity of the accident. Other features include Active Body Control for better handling, Intelligent Light System using bi-xenon headlights with five different lighting functions to match weather conditions. Options include night-view assist with infrared headlamps, reversing camera, voice control for car radio, DVD changer and navigation as well as tyre pressure monitoring system. Some new engines were introduced as well. Models include the CL 500 with a 4.7-litre V8, mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission. The CL 600 has the same 5.5-litre twin-turbocharged V8 carried over, which is mated to the old 5-speed automatic transmission. The performance model CL 63 AMG gets the new twin-turbocharged 5.5-litre V8, mated to 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The CL 65 AMG still has the same 6.0-litre V12 bi-turbo engine, connected to a 5-speed automatic, but tweaked to give more power.

The GMC Acadia received a facelift for its 2013 model. The crossover offers three rows of seating for up to eight passengers. The design consists of polished aluminium roof rails, projector beam headlights, LED taillights and a rear spoiler. The Acadia gets a 3.6-litre V6 with variable valve timing, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission and an optional all-wheel-drive system with no low range. The interior features a "low and away" instrument panel and a Smart Slide second-row feature allows easier access to the third row. Features include power windows, CD/MP3 stereo with six speakers, electric mirrors, keyless entry and more. Optional features include rear-seat DVD entertainment, HID headlights, sunroof, parking sensors, leather seats, tri-zone climate control and more. Standard safety features includes StabiliTrak stability control system with rollover mitigation technology, six airbags and a tyre-pressure-monitoring system. Also standard is power-assisted rack-and-pinion steering, 18-inch wheels with optional 19 or 20-inchers, and four-wheel disc brakes with ABS.

The Accord is of one the best midsize sedans available. It does everything well and is popular for doing so. It may not be best in class for every little thing, but it is more of an all-round package than its competitors. There are two engines, the standard 2.4-litre four-cylinder with a manual or automatic, and the optional 3.0-litre V6 with an automatic only. The popular sedans are great everyday cars with comfort and convenience features. Available optional features include cruise control, power locks, keyless entry, 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, four-wheel-disc brakes with Electronic Brake-force Distribution (EBD), in-dash six-CD changer, steering wheel audio controls, leather upholstery, a power glass sunroof, side mirrors with integrated turn signals, and VSA stability control. Safety is enhanced on all Accords by available side-impact and curtain airbags, in addition to the required dual front airbags. Anti-lock brakes (ABS) with Electronic Brake-force Distribution (EBD) come standard. All V6 models come with Vehicle Stability Assist (VSA) and Brake Assist with traction control.

The TrailBlazer is powerful and capable midsize off-road vehicle, which is just the right size to not be a pain on the roads. Launched in 2002, it received a minor facelift in 2006. It has a rigid chassis, good off-road suspension, powerful brakes and a spacious enough interior to compete in this class. It is stable at high speeds, wobbly around curves, and comfortable over rough surfaces, while being quite capable off-road, thanks to a proper four-wheel-drive system with low-range gearing. The TrailBlazer also comes in an EXT trim with an extended wheelbase that adds a third row seat. The early TrailBlazer comes with a Vortec 4.2-litre inline 6-cylinder engine that generates very respectable numbers, similar to the V8 motors of some competitors. And then there is 5.3-litre V8 engine that can be had as an option only on the EXT. The V8 is equipped with GM's Displacement on Demand technology as standard which deactivates four cylinders under certain driving conditions to aid fuel efficiency, returning the full complement of power once the controller senses vehicle speed or load requires additional power. Both engines use a Hydra-Matic 4-speed auto transmission.

In addition to a sedan version, the Impreza has now become a hatchback for 2008, with interior and exterior styling solidly in the mainstream of conservative design. It remains the only car in its class with standard full-time all-wheel drive. Subaru likes to tout their rally heritage, but none of the Middle East models are anywhere near rally cars. The models offered here are the new 1.5-litre, known as the 1.5i, and the 2.0-litre, known as the 2.0R. Both have flat 4-cylinder "boxer" engines, and both mated to either a 5-speed manual or an outdated 4-speed automatic. Base models have a standard AM/FM stereo system, cloth upholstery, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking and steel wheels, along with dual front airbags. The full-spec 2.0R model features the same full power options, alloy wheels, rear spoiler, ABS brakes, dual front airbags, fog lamps, sunroof and not much else. Western and Eastern world markets receive turbocharged WRX sports models, but local dealers do not officially offer them in the GCC.

The BMW X2 is a brand new model introduced as a 2018 model year. It is based on the X1 and Mini Countryman chassis, but offers the "SUV" coupe design. An optional M sport package consisting of sporty suspension, cabin trim and body kit is also offered. The new engines available include the entry-level sDrive18i getting a new 1.5-litre 3-cylinder turbocharged engine. The sDrive20i and sDrive28i gets a new 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbocharged unit.  The X2 M35i gets a turbocharged 6-cylinder 3.0-litre all-aluminum motor. An 8-speed automatic gearbox with auto start-stop tech is offered, although there is also a 6-speed manual available that will likely never be shipped here by local dealers.The interior features an optional integrated iDrive that includes either the 6.5-inch Business or the 8.8-inch Professional navigation systems. Other available features, depending on trim level, includes various alloy wheels, Bluetooth phone, dual-zone a/c, sunroof, cloth or leather upholstery, HID headlights, run-flat tyres, rear parking sensors, keyless entry, cruise control, immobiliser and the usual power accessories. Standard safety features include front and side-curtain airbags, stability control, and ABS with electronic brakeforce distribution as well as cornering brake control.

The Mountaineer is supposed to be a more upscale version of the Ford Explorer, and it certainly looks like it from the outside. It shares its structure and most major components with the Explorer, but apparently it shares a lot of the interior as well, thus diminishing brand differences. The Mountaineer is also powered by the Explorer's 4.0-litre V6, mated to a five-speed automatic, but it loses low-range gearing for its four-wheel-drive system The interior theoretically offers seating for up to eight people with three rows of seats, with a third-row seat that can fold flat. Standard interior features include a CD stereo, power windows and mirrors, available CD changer and sunroof, cruise control, available leather upholstery, and standard alloy wheels. The Mountaineer also builds on Ford's strong safety offerings, offering optional AdvanceTrac with Roll Stability Control, ABS brakes, dual front airbags and a tyre-pressure monitoring system, while the Safety Canopy side-curtain airbag system is optional.

The Maserati Ghibli was revived by Fiat as a 2014 model and is intended to compete in the luxury midsize segment which is dominated by the Germans. The rear-wheel drive Ghibli gets two 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 engines in different states of tune. Both versions get an 8-speed automatic transmission. In 2015, the Ghibli S was also available with all-wheel-drive. In 2019, a Gran Lusso trim was introduced with a body kit, sports seats and steering wheel, and full-LED adaptive Matrix headlights. Standard options include power windows, electric mirrors, power steering, cruise control, leather seats, infotainment screen with navigation, parking sensors, reverse camera and 19-inch alloy rims. The higher models get a better audio entertainment system, 20-inch alloys and all sorts of cabin trim choices. Standard safety features include dual front airbags, side and curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Nissan Patrol was redesigned from the ground up for 2010, and has been mildly facelifted for 2014. In 2017, the major change was the new V6 engine and no manual option was available. In 2018, everything was pretty much the same. In 2019, the Patrol got a host of new accessories which include fender flares, front and rear diffusers and different roof rails. In 2020, it got a major facelift for the front and back, along with major interior tech upgrades and new exterior colour choices. Engine options for the 2022 Nissan Patrol include a base 4.0-litre V6 with a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol XE or SE, as well as a 5.6-litre V8 with direct injection and a 7-speed automatic, known as the Patrol LE. Depending on trim level, the 7-seater Patrol can be had with standard or optional features such as all-wheel-drive with low-range gearing, hydraulic body motion control system for the suspension, computerised terrain response system, climate-controlled leather seats, infotainment with touchscreen, Apple Carplay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, power rear liftgate, keyless start, adaptive cruise control, 20-inch alloy wheels, power-folding 3rd-row seat, around-view cameras, and a centre console cool-box that can be opened from both 1st & 2nd-row seats. Also available is an Off-road Monitor that provides real-time information such as tyre conditions involving steer angle, slip and pressure, as well as hill start, hill descent, and an electronically-locking rear diff. Most models get a regular offroad-ready front bumper, while the top Platinum "City" trim gets a slightly-lower unique bumper. Safety features in the 2022 Nissan Patrol include two front airbags and numerous side-curtain airbags, stability control and ABS, as well as optional lane-departure warning, tyre-pressure monitor and auto-braking systems.

The Opel Corsa is the smallest offering from the German manufacturer in the Middle East market. The base model comes with a 4-cylinder 1.4-litre engine, mated to a 5-speed manual or a 4-speed automatic transmission. There is a 3-door and 5-door hatchback version to choose from. Standard options include power steering, power windows, power mirrors, manual A/C, AM/FM radio, cloth upholstery and steel wheels. The higher models get a better entertainment system with a CD player and MP3/iPod/AUX support, and alloy wheels. All Corsa variants are also equipped with ABS brakes, featuring brake assist and electronic brakeforce distribution.

The Lincoln debuted for the 2007 model year, and has been heavily revised for 2011, with a new face, higher-quality interior and better entertainment features, while still looking like a Ford Edge derivative, on which is based. The updated MKX features a new chrome grille, along with new headlights, tail lamps and wheel designs externally. The newly-designed interior still features seating for five with a fold-down rear seat to maximise cargo room, as well as soft-touch materials, mood lighting and wood trim. The MKX features a standard 3.7-litre V6, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission, and available with front-wheel-drive or an all-wheel-drive system without low-range gearing. Available features include leather upholstery, rain-sensing wipers, 18-inch or optional 20-inch alloy wheels, dual-zone automatic a/c, power accessories, panoramic glass roof, six-way power-adjustable front seats with heating and cooling, adaptive HID turning headlights, MyTouch touchscreen with SYNC voice-controlled multimedia computer and Sony stereo, optional THX-certified audio system, USB and SD card ports, Bluetooth phone, dual-zone a/c, remote starter, keyless entry with starter button, power-operated tailgate and more. Standard safety features include Advance Trac with Roll Stability Control, front and side airbags, Safety Canopy side-curtain airbags with rollover detection, hill start assist, tyre pressure monitor and ABS, as well as blind-spot monitor, rear camera, adaptive cruise control with collision warning and brake support, and cross-traffic detection.

The Kia Niro is the Korean brand's hybrid sub-compact SUV offering. Under the hood, it gets a 1.6-litre engine coupled with an electric motor, mated to a 6-speed dual-clutch transmission. Standard features include power steering, power windows, halogen headlamps, cruise control, fabric seats, 8.0-inch screen with the infotainment system, Android Auto, Apple CarPlay, automatic AC and 16-inch alloy wheels. Standard safety features include front airbags, tyre pressure monitor, stability control and rear camera.

The Audi RS 7 is the top performance variant of the A7, the German brand's "4-door coupe" offering. In 2015, the RS 7 got a minor facelift. Under the hood is a turbocharged 4.0-litre V8, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. It is available only in all-wheel drive format, as with all RS models. Standard options include 4-zone automatic air-conditioning, reverse-camera, MMI touch-sensitive navigation system, 10-speaker audio system, interior leather packages for the seats and door trim, sports suspension, air suspension, front and reverse camera, park assist, side assist, night-vision, lane-assist and BOSE surround sound. Safety standards are high as expected with front and side airbags all around, along with traction control and stability control.

The Hyundai Kona is a sub-compact crossover with no offroad abilities whatsoever, although it sports black plastic cladding and half-baked roof rails to imitate it. Powered by either a 2.0-litre with a 6-speed automatic or a turbocharged 1.6-litre with a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic, both 4-cylinder and with either front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive, the Kona seems to rival the company's own Creta crossover. Available features include LED running lights and tail lights, alloy wheels, cruise control, and an LCD multimedia touchscreen with Bluetooth, USB and all that. Safety features include at least 2 airbags, ABS with EBD, ESP and a tyre-pressure monitor. It has a 5-star EuroNCAP crash-test rating, but only when equipped with side airbags in full-option trim.

The Chevrolet Corvette C6 is the most capable Corvette ever. The LS2 V8 powerplant has grown to 6 litres for 2005, with power and torque that is killer at the track and useable in regular driving. The standard tranny is the Tremec T56 six-speed manual gearbox, while an outdated four-speed automatic is optional. Large 18-inch wheels at the front and 19-inch at the rear and exposed headlamps with fixed Xenon High-Intensity Discharge lamps now define the Corvette. Available as a hatchback coupe with a lift-off roof panel or as a convertible with a fabric soft-top and heated glass rear window, while a power top is also available. The new race-bred Corvette Z06 packs a massive 7.0-litre V8 engine, and comes in coupe form only and offers performance that rivals Ferrari. Even though its dimensions have shrunk, the C6 has as much room inside as the C5. The only letdown is an interior that could easily have been in the Aveo, although GM does try to make up for it with gadgets such as keyless start and a heads-up display. We'd say America's favourite sports car is now as good as anything from Italy.

The first ever Opel-badged compact 4WD isn't even a real Opel. The Antara is a Korean product built at the Daewoo factory, and also sold in the GCC as a GMC Terrain. However, it does complete the dying Opel range, giving dealers their very own small soft-roader. Unlike the Terrain, the Antara is available with only one engine, namely a 3.2-litre V6 with a standard 5-speed automatic transmission offering basic manual-shift capability. All-wheel-drive is standard, but there is no low-range gearing. The Antara seats five and does not offer third-row seating. However, the rear seat folds flat to extend the cargo area. Active and passive safety systems include stability control, hill descent control and active rollover protection, as well as dual-stage front and side-impact airbags, as well as head-curtain airbags. Th high-quality interior offers numerous soft-touch surfaces and available two-tone leather upholstery. Standard features include power windows, electric mirrors, CD player, keyless entry, alloy wheels and more.

The XC70 was Volvo's first attempt at a 4WD vehicle. Based on a jacked-up V70 wagon with all-wheel-drive, it had been somewhat redesigned for 2008, and then mechanically upgraded for 2012. Although it is still not really that good off-road as we know it, the XC70 gets by on gravel and flat sand, given its fairly impressive ground clearance. Available only in T6 trim now, it is powered by a turbocharged 3.0-litre 6-cylinder engine, with an automatic offering tiptronic manual shifting. The second-row has a three-section bench seat with removable centre position for various setups. Standard features include keyless entry, CD player, trip computer, air-conditioning, xenon headlights, power windows, doors, locks, sunroof and mirrors. Available features also include leather or vinyl seats, ventilated front seats with perforated leather, 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, an in-dash computer system with USB and Bluetooth support, and an optional rear-seat entertainment system. Safety features include ABS brakes, stability control, dual front airbags, side impact airbags for SIPS, inflatable curtain airbags, WHIPS whiplash protection, collision Warning with brake support and emergency brake lamps, adaptive cruise control helps keeping a safe distance to vehicles ahead, hydraulic brake assist, optimised hydraulic brakes and fading brake support. An optional Polestar ECU upgrade is available to bump up the power by 25 hp.

A new generation Ford Mustang was introduced in 2015. In 2018 it received a facelift and some power upgrades. There is no more V6 engine offered, with only 2.3-litre turbo and the V8 engines carrying over. All engines can be had with either a 6-speed manual transmission or a new 10-speed automatic transmission. The interior gets the MyFord infotainment system with SYNC 3. For the first time, Ford has introduced independent rear suspension for this generation Mustang, which helps improve handling. Standard features include power windows, power steering, electric mirrors, keyless entry, central locking, manual A/C, fabric seats, paddle shifters and alloy rims. The higher models get navigation, rear-view camera, leather seats, more speakers, engine push-start and automatic A/C. Safety standards include driver and passenger airbags, electronic stability control, ABS brakes and traction control.

A new-generation Honda CR-V made its debut in 2017. No changes have been made for the 2018 model year. Under the hood, the same engine remains, which is a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder direct-injection engine mated to a CVT that can simulate a 7-speed in 'sport' mode. The DX and LX trims come in 2WD form, while the EX and Touring trims come in AWD form. Standard features on the base two-wheel-drive CR-V model include power steering, power windows, electric mirrors, central locking, remote key, halogen headlights, daytime running lamps, single-zone A/C, rear camera, fabric seats, 5-inch audio screen, 1 USB, 4 speakers, cruise control and 17-inch alloy wheels. Higher models gets all-wheel-drive, LED headlights, fog lamps, paddle shifters, engine push start, 7-inch screen, 8 speakers, 4 USB ports, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, dual-zone A/C, and 18-inch alloy wheels. Safety features include ABS, vehicle stability assist, traction control system, tyre pressure monitor, hill start assist, electric brake force distribution, and driver attention monitor. The AWD models get Honda's LaneWatch side camera. The top model gets side and curtain airbags as well.

An all-new Mercedes-Benz A-Class came out in 2019. The A-Class now comes in two variants, the A 200 and A 250. Under the hood, a new 1.3-litre turbocharged engine sit in the A 200, while for the A 250 it is the same turbocharged 2.0-litre engine carried over from the previous generation, mated to an a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission, but gains more power. The 5-seater is offered in one loaded "Sport" spec that includes 18-inch AMG alloys, sporty bumpers, power windows, electric mirrors, multimedia screen, navigation, CD/MP3 stereo, USB port, Bluetooth, cruise control, keyless entry and other features. Standard safety features include front airbags, side-curtain airbags, radar-based collision-prevention assist, attention assist, stability control and ABS. Other available features include LED xenon headlights, active parking assist, rear camera, hill-start assist and a interior ambient-lighting pack. Additional safety options include adaptive cruise control, adaptive highbeam assist, speed-limit sign assist, blind-spot assist and lane-keeping assist.

The Lancer Evolution is Mitsubishi's rally-inspired high-performance all-wheel-drive sedan based on the Lancer compact sedan. The redesigned 2008 Lancer Evolution is the tenth generation of the rally car for the street, and hence it is called the Evolution X. The all-new Evo X is offered in one trim level in the GCC, known as GSR, with different levels of equipment. Standard is the turbocharged and intercooled 2.0-litre 4-cylinder that now gets either a 5-speed manual gearbox or a new 6-speed paddle-shifted Twin-Clutch Sportronic Shift Transmission (TC-SST) with Normal, Sport and S-Sport modes. Both versions include the Super All-Wheel Control (S-AWC) all-wheel-drive system with Active Center Differential (ACD), Active Yaw Control (AYC), Active Stability Control (ASC), and Sport ABS brakes. Features include automatic climate control, Recaro bucket seats, 18-inch Enkei alloy wheels, various aluminium body panels, cruise control, adaptive HID headlights, foglamps, tyre pressure gauge, power windows and electric mirrors. Safety includes ABS-assisted Brembo brakes, front airbags, side-curtain airbags and a knee airbag for the driver. Leather, keyless entry and a Rockford Fosgate stereo are optional. These latest models come with a GCC warranty, which become void if the car even touches the track. An optional performance kit was offered in 2009 to boost power by 37 hp.

The F430 is heavily influenced by F1 Racing technology, and makes it known to everyone openly. The F430's compact 4.3-litre V8 engine offers blistering high-revving performance, and the experience is enhanced by an optional F1-style paddle-shifting gearbox which has made its way to every other Ferrari model too. The F430's aerodynamics are honed to generate special flows to increase downforce and improve cooling. One technical feature is the electronic differential, transferring massive torque levels to the track under high cornering g-forces, and guarantees maximum grip out of bends, eliminating wheel spin. The larger interior can be personalized with carbon-fibre or aluminium inserts, with space behind the seats accessed using an electrically operated compartment. The standard electric seats can be substituted by more sporting items with four-point harnesses to order. Even with all this the interior is noticeably barebones in keeping with its sporting nature. For 2008, a more powerful, lighter and track-focussed F430 Scuderia was introduced, with a faster clutchless-manual gearbox and other chassis enhancements.

The Chevrolet Tahoe got a new 6-speed transmission from 2009 onward. A beefy  Vortec 5.3-litre V8 powers the Tahoe. The V8 powers the rear wheels on the road, or through all four wheels when the standard 4WD system is engaged. Features include the usual power features and three rows of seats. Power-adjustable brake and accelerator pedals are standard on the higher models and optional on the base versions. New features also include power folding rear seats, among other things. On the road, the Tahoe is smooth and stable in a straight line, hopeless in the corners and strong off the road. The Suburban is the long-wheelbase version of the Tahoe, and offers more room in the back. Rear passengers can enjoy an optional package that includes a DVD system with flip-down seven-inch colour monitor, six-disc in-dash audio player and Bose speakers. New versions added later include the Tahoe Z71 off-road package with lifted suspension.

The Mercedes-Benz Vito is a midsize commercial van that can be outfitted as a cargo carrier or as a passenger transport. Changes were made in 2015 which included standard Attention Assist and Crosswind Assist, optional Intelligent Light System which included LED indicators, LED daytime running lamps, LED low-beam headlamps, and main beam with cornering light function. There were no changes for the 2017 model year. The cargo vans can be had with three turbocharged 2.1-litre 4-cylinder diesel engines with different states of tune, mated to either a 6-speed manual or a 5-speed automatic transmission. The UK-built luxury passenger carrier version gets a 3.5-litre V6 engine, mated to a 5-speed automatic. All models are rear-wheel-drive. Basic options include power steering, front power windows and central locking with remote control. Safety features include ESP, driver-side airbag, third brake light and three-point seatbelts for all seats.

BMW's American-built 4WD comes in three models in this region, namely the 3.0i with a 6-cylinder engine, the 4.4i with a V8, and the 4.8is with a bigger V8. Debuting in 2000 and receiving a facelift in 2004, the X5 has all-wheel drive without low-range gearing, but does come with ABS and traction control. The 3.0i offers manual and automatic transmissions, but the V8 models only come with an automatic. The automatics do have a manual shift gate, but they are still essentially automatics. Standard on V8s and optional on the 3.0i are load-leveling suspension, leather upholstery, front and rear obstacle detection, and steering-linked xenon headlights. Other available features include adjustable ride-height suspension, heated rear seats, navigation system and sunroof. The X5 is far from an off-roader, but it has built up a reputation for excellent on-road driving dynamics for a 4WD, and has become popular with rich people who like to terrorise other road users with some deft moves. The V8 models drive more like sport wagons rather than any 4WD, though it seems a little pointless when BMW itself has much more capable V8-powered 5-Series wagons in its European stable.

The Jeep Renegade is the smallest SUV offering from the brand. It gets 2.4-litre 4-cylinder engine under the hood, mated to a 9-speed automatic transmission. The base Renegade Sport model comes in front-wheel-drive format, while the Latitude, Trailhawk and Limited models are all-wheel drive platforms. Standard options include power windows, power steering, electric mirrors, fabric seats, manual A/C, FM radio with AUX/USB support and alloy wheels. Higher options include automatic A/C, Infotainment system with screen, navigation, automatic A/C and leather seats. Safety features include driver and passenger airbags, traction control and vehicle stability control.

Receiving a minor frontal facelift for 2013, the sixth-generation Nissan Z continues to be a focussed sports car that is now affordable. The 370Z Roadster includes a 3.7-litre V6 engine with VVEL variable-valve timing, lightweight 4-wheel independent suspension with extensive use of aluminum components, 19-inch staggered lightweight alloy wheels, and a 7-speed automatic with paddle shifters. The powered soft top model almost have the same rigidity as the coupe. Features include power windows and mirrors, 'intelligent' keyless entry and starter button, 6-speaker CD/MP3 stereo with two subwoofers, Bluetooth, optional navigation touchscreen system, various dashboard-top gauges and available leather upholstery in various colours. Optional NISMO factory accessories include an exhaust system, body kit, rear spoiler, suspension sway bars, S-tune shocks and springs, and NISMO alloy wheels. Standard safety features include front and side-curtain airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Nissan Pathfinder Classic is a return of the old-shape model to some GCC markets. This one is made in Spain, rather than the United States. Now only available as a basic model, it is built on a body-on-frame platform, offering good off-road capability but marginal on-road handling. The Pathfinder Classic offers third-row seating to carry up to seven people. A 4.0-litre V6 powers the SUV and its five-speed automatic transmission is geared to use the engine's torque characteristics. Standard features include fabric upholstery, cruise control, power mirrors, windows and door locks with keyless remote, CD stereo with six speakers, reclining backs on the middle row seats, front airbags, ABS and steel wheels.

The Toyota Hiace has been the market leader for years in the UAE and continues to be a popular choice in the commercial sector, whether for transporting the work-force or cargo. An all-new model came out in 2019. The engine now moves to the front, thereby increasing noise and vibration, as well as heat generated inside the cabin. There is only one engine choice in the Hiace, a 3.5-litre V6 petrol engine mated to a standard 6-speed manual or an optional 6-speed automatic transmission. The Saudi market additionally gets a 2.7-litre turbocharged diesel engine model with a 6-speed manual. The 2020 Toyota Hiace comes in two variants, the Hiace Panel Van version for carrying cargo and the Hiace Commuter which gets back seats to act as a people carrier. Standard features include dual front/rear a/c, an AM/FM cassette player with 2 speakers, power steering, power door locks, toolbox, halogen headlamps, and 15-inch steel wheels. Some markets get optional features such as remote locking. Depending on the market, consumers have the choice of a normal roof or high-roof with a standard or long wheel base-wide body.

The Camaro received a facelift for the 2014 model year. Aside from the pointier front-end, the generic tail lamps, the functional new bonnet vents and optional Recaro seats, there aren't any other visible changes. Powered by a 3.6-litre V6 or a 6.2-litre V8, it rides on a shortened rear-wheel-drive Lumina SS platform, with four-wheel independent suspension and 2+2 seating. The Camaro comes in V6 LT and V8 SS trims. The V6 is only available with a 6-speed paddle-shifted automatic in the GCC. The SS gets a choice of two V8 engines, each customised for use with a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automatic. The automatic V8 features cylinder deactivation to improve fuel economy. StabiliTrak traction control and front-side airbags are standard, while Brembo brakes are available on the SS version. The SS also gets stiffer suspension and adjustable Competitive/Sport modes for stability control and Launch Control on manual models. The ZL1 gets a supercharged 6.2-litre V8 with a 6-speed manual or automatic. The hard-plastic cabin comes with cloth or leather interior, with standard blue LED lighting and optional glow-in-the-dark trim panels. Standard features include air conditioning, power windows and lock, and keyless entry. Available features include heads-up display, sunroof and a new MyLink entertainment system which includes touchscreen navigation. Standard rims include 18-inch wheels for the V6 and 20-inch ones for the V8. Safety features include front airbags, side airbags, ABS and stability control.

The Lexus RX continues its grip on womenly drivers everywhere, with a new design for 2010 that isn't a radical change compared to the outgoing model. The RX 350 still comes with only one engine, namely a 3.5-litre V6 with VVT-i variable valve timing, mated to a 6-speed automatic and all-wheel-drive platform. The basic model includes front-side airbags, curtain and knee airbags, rear-side airbags, cruise control, CD changer with 9 speakers, powered front seats, wood trim, fabric seats, smart entry and start system, ABS, stability control, 18-inch alloy wheels, front and rear parking sensors, and HID headlights. The mid-range model adds Mark Levinson audio with 15 speakers, DVD changer, Bluetooth, heads-up display, rear entertainment system, navigation system, rear camera, leather seats, Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Management, 19-inch alloy wheels, sunroof, adaptive headlights and hill-start assist. The top model adds better leather, panoramic sunroof and a pre-crash safety system. The optional Vehicle Dynamics Integrated Management is a system that coordinates the stability control system with Active Torque Control to offer better handling in emergency situations. A front lower-bumper spoiler is optional. On debut in 2010, three trim levels were offered, namely the Premium, Premium Plus and Luxury. For 2011, the trim levels changed to Premier, Vogue, Prestige and Platinum, as a well as a mid-range 'Stone Designs' edition with a custom red-beige cloth interior.

The Acadia is GMC's first crossover wagon that combines car-like handling with the utility of a 4WD wagon, offering three rows of seating for up to eight passengers. The design consists of polished aluminium roof rails, projector beam headlights, LED taillights and a rear spoiler. The Acadia is powered by a new 3.6-litre V6 with variable valve timing, mated to a six-speed automatic transmission and an optional all-wheel-drive system with no low range. The interior features a "low and away" instrument panel and a Smart Slide second-row feature allows easier access to the third row. Features include power windows, CD/MP3 stereo with six speakers, electric mirrors, keyless entry and more. Optional features include rear-seat DVD entertainment, HID headlights, sunroof, parking sensors, leather seats, tri-zone climate control and more. Standard safety features includes StabiliTrak stability control system with rollover mitigation technology, six airbags and a tyre-pressure-monitoring system. Also standard is power-assisted rack-and-pinion steering, 18-inch wheels with optional 19-inchers, and four-wheel disc brakes with ABS.

The Mini Paceman is just a 3-door chopped-top version of the Countryman. Under the bonnet are the same 1.6-litre engines that power the smaller Minis, with Cooper and Cooper S variants, all with a 6-speed automatic gearbox. All-wheel-drive is optional on the Cooper S variant. A John Cooper Works model is also available, with lowered sports suspension as well as 18-inch and 19-inch alloy wheel options. Options include various CD/MP3 audio and navigation systems, a panoramic glass roof, adaptive HID headlights, towbar, and alloy wheels from 16-inch to 19-inch in size, as well as a range of John Cooper Works performance accessories. Safety features include front and side-curtain airbags, stability control, and ABS with electronic brake-force distribution.

The Lumina remains the only rear-wheel-drive sedan in the affordable midsize segment. The available 3.6-litre V6 and 6.0-litre V8 motors offer value no one can match. Built in Australia alongside the Caprice, it is brand new from the ground up, and comes in four-door trim only. The Lumina comes in four variants, namely the LS, LTZ, S and SS. The power for the LS, LTZ and body-kitted S comes from the Alloytec 3.6-litre V6 engine with an automatic transmission. The 6.0-litre V8 does its work in the SS sedan with either a 6-speed manual or new 6-speed automatic that replaced the old 4-speed automatic since 2008. The base LS and LTZ models fulfil the basic needs of a commuter car that doubles as a family vehicle, with decent space and adequate power, while the SS models merge muscle-car attitude with a traditional sedan. Available features, standard or optional depending on model, include an MP3-capable CD stereo, CD changer, stability control, ABS brakes, traction control, 16-inch, 17-inch or 18-inch wheels, comfort or sports suspension, trip computer, Bluetooth, cloth or leather upholstery, and various power features.

The Previa is roomy, comfortable and does everything well. It is easy to live with if you learn how to park it, and it comes loaded with features that make life easier and more convenient. Everything operates exactly as expected, so equipment struggles are rare. Its smoothness and convenience allows the vehicle to fade into the background while you go about your life, even though it looks like a space ship. On the road, the Previa delivers a smooth ride and decent handling. Its 2.4-litre four-cylinder engine and four-speed automatic transmission offer adequate throttle response and fuel economy, though given its weight, it is far from quick. The 3.5-litre V6 with six-speed automatic, new for 2007, improves straight-line power. Standard features include seating for either seven or eight, a radio cassette player, power windows, cloth seats, keyless entry and central locking, along with ABS and two airbags. Optional features include HID headlamps with adaptive light system and auto leveling, front fog lamps, 17-inch alloy wheels, CD player with 6 speakers, cruise control and automatic rear doors.

The Lexus LX 570, which was all-new for 2008, received a minor facelift for 2012. Heavily based on the Toyota Land Cruiser, new model gets a new front-end, bi-xenon headlights, new 18-inch or 20-inch wheels, new tail-lamp clusters and a couple of features such as "overturn" assist and new interior colours. The Lexus is powered by a 5.7-litre V8 mated with a 6-speed automatic transmission. In 2014, a limited-to-200 LX 570 Supercharged was offered exclusively for the Middle East market, with a 5.7-litre supercharged V8. The full-time all-wheel drive features a new 2-speed transfer case, Torsen centre differential and a crawl-control feature when in low range. The "overturn" assist feature can lock one inside rear tyre to help make slow turns tighter in offroad conditions. The LX has a vehicle "posture control" system with four-wheel active height control and adaptive variable suspension that reacts more quickly and allows for a greater range of adjustment than the system it replaces. Active safety features include stability control, ABS brakes and traction control, as well as multiple airbags. The leather interior can be had in tan, beige or black. The plush interior is covered in leather and wood, with seating for at least seven, and features such as ventilated front seats, power-folding third-row seating, sunroof, navigation, Mark Levinson CD/DVD stereo, front-rear-side-view cameras and all the usual power accessories. A "Sport" kit with a unique front bumper was introduced for 2013 in the top models. The touchscreen computer gets a new interface for 2012.

The Nissan Micra makes its entry into the GCC market for the first time in 2012. Based on a shortened Sunny sub-compact platform, the Micra hatchback comes only in 5-door form, with a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a 4-speed automatic, although a 5-speed manual is also available in the most basic model. The base model gets 14-inch steel wheels, folding rear bench seat, rear fog lamp, intermittent front and rear wipers, basic CD/MP3 stereo with AUX port, trip computer, manual a/c, power steering with tilt adjustment, alarm and fabric upholstery. There are four further trim levels, progressively adding features such two or four power windows, split-folding rear seat with three headrests, 15-inch alloy wheels, chrome exterior trim, auto headlights, remote locks or smart keyless entry with starter button, auto wipers, front fog lamps, tachometer, height-adjustable driver's seat with centre armrest, rear window defroster, 12V power outlet, and sunvisors with vanity mirrors. Optional accessories include a chrome grille, body kit, chrome exhaust tip, rear spoiler, mirror-mounted indicators, mud guards and floor mats. Standard safety features include ABS with EBD, brake assist, dual front airbags, and 3-point seatbelts for all five seats.

The Nissan Micra made its entry into the GCC market for the first time in 2012. It remains the same for the 2014 and 2015 model year. Based on a shortened Sunny sub-compact platform, the Micra hatchback comes only in 5-door form, with a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder engine mated to a 4-speed automatic. The base model gets 14-inch steel wheels, folding rear bench seat, rear fog lamp, intermittent front and rear wipers, basic CD/MP3 stereo with AUX port, trip computer, manual a/c, power steering with tilt adjustment, alarm and fabric upholstery. There are fewer trim levels from 2014 onwards, with higher trims having features such as power windows, split-folding rear seat with three headrests, 15-inch alloy wheels, chrome exterior trim, auto headlights, remote locks or smart keyless entry with starter button, auto wipers, front fog lamps, tachometer, height-adjustable driver's seat with centre armrest, rear window defroster, 12V power outlet, and sunvisors with vanity mirrors. Optional accessories include a chrome grille, body kit, chrome exhaust tip, rear spoiler, mirror-mounted indicators, mud guards and floor mats. Standard safety features include ABS with EBD, brake assist, dual front airbags, and 3-point seatbelts for all five seats.

The Honda CR-V is a roomy little soft-roader that is convenient and easy to drive on the streets, but no hero on the rough stuff. There are lots of features, and the cabin is fairly spacious. It rides as smoothly as a car, especially since it is based on the Civic. It offers the cargo versatility of a sport-utility vehicle, an upright seating position, and all-wheel drive. The styling was radically revised for 2007, with marketing folks referring to it as the "Aerosport" SUV. The CR-V comes with a 2.4-litre four-cylinder engine lifted from the Accord, with a five-speed automatic transmission. Standard features include air conditioning with micron filtration, AM/FM/CD stereo with MP3 capability and optional 6-CD changer, an adjustable steering column, power mirrors, power windows, and power outlets, along with front airbags, integrated keyless entry and alloy wheels. Side airbags are optionally available, as are a moonroof, leather seats, adaptive headlights and other features.

The Mercedes-Benz A 45 AMG is the range-topping variant of the A-Class line. If features a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine mated to a 7-speed automatic and an all-wheel-drive platform. Externally, it can be identified by its AMG-specific bumpers and wheels, although these are also available with lower-spec A-Class models with an AMG package as well. Other AMG-specific features include a conservative "twin-blade" grille, black side-sills and trim, and squared-off exhaust tips. Further features include sports seats, stiffer suspension, sports exhaust system, speed-sensitive sports steering, transmission oil cooler, bigger brakes and an AMG-tuned ESP system. Other available features include HID headlights, smart keyless entry and start, cruise control, navigation and more. The pricier A 45 AMG "Edition 1" model includes white body colour, sports stripes in matte grey, red highlights on certain trim bits, red brake calipers, 19-inch AMG light-alloy wheels in matte black, AMG "Night" and "Aerodynamics" packages, black and red interior, special seat upholstery, AMG Performance steering wheel and other doodads.

The Jaguar F-Pace is the British luxury brand's first SUV in their lineup. It comes with a 3.0-litre supercharged V6 engine with two different tunes. Later on, a 2.0-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder engine joined the lineup. Power is delivered via an 8-speed automatic transmission for all motors. A limited production "First Edition" model was released initially. The Pure, Prestige, R-Sport and Portfolio models get the standard 2.0-litre and 3.0-litre engines, while the F-Pace S and the First Edition trims get the more powerful 3.0-litre engine. Standard options on the all-wheel drive F-Pace include power windows, power mirrors, power steering, speed proportional steering, electric parking brake, hill launch assist, LED taillights, 2-zone climate control, paddle shifters,  5-inch screen, Bluetooth connectivity and 18-inch alloy wheels. Optional features include 19-inch rims, luxury sports seats, electric seats with lumbar support, sliding panoramic roof, interior mood lighting, body kit, and Meridian Digital sound system. Safety features include front and rear parking sensors, rearview camera, 360-degree parking view, valet mode, blind spot monitor, traction control, front and curtain airbags.

The Navigator is the Lincoln-badged luxury version of the Ford Expedition, a full-size 4WD known to be smooth, stable and refined for the most part. Heavily facelifted and revised for 2007, its four-wheel-independent suspension is sophisticated, providing better on-road ride and handling, while low-range gearing is available for off-roading. The standard engine is a 5.4-litre V8 engine mated to an automatic gearbox. The Navigator is loaded with safety features, and offers an available Roll Stability Control system, which is designed to sense an approaching rollover situation then take action to help prevent it. What the Navigator does best is move large quantities of people and gear, with its perfectly flat cargo area and available PowerFold third-row seat that folds perfectly flat with the press of a button, with the ability to carry up to eight passengers. Other features include HID headlights, 18-inch wheels, power-folding running boards, leather seats and wood trim. Options include 20-inch wheels, a rear-seat DVD system and more power features. Also new to the range is the Navigator L, an extended version which has a longer wheelbase and additional cargo space.

In 2019, a new generation of the Porsche 911 was revealed. The 2+2 seater coupe gets an updated exterior design, along with updates to the engine. The 911 Carrera and Carrera S is offered with a 3.0-litre turbocharged flat-6 engine with two different tunes, mated to a 8-speed "PDK" dual-clutch automatic and rear-wheel-drive. The Carrera 4 and 4S is all-wheel drive. As usual, everything is optional beyond the basic power accessories, touchscreen multimedia system, Bluetooth, basic keyless entry, HID headlights, electric parking brake and 19-inch wheels. Available options include different colours and materials for every interior surface, different 20-inch wheel designs, metallic paint choices, power-adjustable or sports seats, Bose or Burmester audio systems with optional voice control and TV tuner, CD changer, parking sensors, smart keyless entry and start, adaptive headlights, sunroof, electric folding mirrors, rear wiper, body kit and more. Standard safety features include front and side airbags, stability control and ABS. The Carrera S and Carrera T models also have the option of all-wheel-steer.

The new-for-2008 Volvo C30, the Swedish firm's entry-level attempt at capturing younger buyers, received a frontal facelift for 2010. This sporting hatchback has room for four average-sized adults and a range of competitive engines. It offers a fair bit of space inside, at least for the front passengers, and features very basic interior styling, save for a few unique touches such as the floating centre console. Available for 2010 are only two engines, both 5-cylinder, one being a 2.4-litre and the other a turbocharged 2.5-litre, both with automatic gearboxes and tiptronic functionality. By 2012, the only version available was the T5 R-Design. All versions are front-wheel-drive. Standard features include cloth upholstery, power windows, trip computer and CD audio. Standard safety features typical of Volvo include ABS brakes, front airbags, side-curtain airbags, and a whiplash protection system. Options include alloy rims between 15-inch and 18-inch sizes, three levels of audio equipment, customisable centre console trim, stability control and a blind-spot warning system for inattentive drivers. A new R-Design package adds sportier suspension and a body kit.

The Altima received a face-lift for the 2013 model. They still get the same 2.5-litre 4-cylinder and 3.5-litre V6 engine from the previous shape, along with CVT transmissions. Features included in the base 2.5 S include ABS, traction-control, vehicle stability control, remote keyless entry with Push Button Ignition, radio with CD player with Aux-in and 4 speakers, audio controls on steering wheel and dual airbags. The 2.5 SV adds to that cruise control, 6-speaker audio system with 5-inch display, bluetooth, USB port with iPod connectivity, rear-view camera, auto-headlamps, parking sensors, fog lamps and 17-inch alloy rims. Moving up to 2.5 SL,  additional features include 6-way power seats, dual zone auto A/C, side and curtain airbags and remote engine start. For the V6, the 3.5 SV is the same options as 2.5 SV but included are paddle shifters on the steering column. The 3.5 SL gets leather seats, driver 8-way power seat, lumbar support, Bose audio system with 9 speakers, sunroof, xenon head lamps and LED tail lamps. The top SL versions can be specced out with a navigation system.

The Mercedes-Benz AMG GT Roadster, or Mercedes-AMG GT Roadster as the marketeers like to call it now, is the first car entirely developed in-house by AMG. Two variants of the AMG GT Roadster are available as of 2018, all with the same V8 4.0-litre twin-turbocharged engine but with different tunes. Power is delivered in both variants through a 7-speed dual clutch automatic transmission. The standard AMG GT Roadster gets a mechanical rear-axle locking rear differential while the AMG GT C gets an electronic locking rear differential. The GT C also has an AMG RIDE CONTROL suspension with electronically controlled dampers with three different modes - Comfort, Sport and Sport Plus. The AMG GT doesn't weigh so much for its size, thanks to the body structure being built through a mixture of steel, aluminium and magnesium. Safety standards are high in the AMG GT with front and side airbags, traction control, ABS brakes and stability control.

The Lincoln MKZ made its comeback in the GCC as a 2014 model year, with a major frontal facelift and new engine coming in 2017. The MKZ comes with a turbocharged 2.0-litre 4-cylinder engine or a turbocharged 3.0-litre V6, both mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission with paddle shifters. The 2.0T comes in front-wheel-drive form while the 3.0T comes with all-wheel-drive for the GCC market. The MKZ will be available with SYNC3 and MyLincoln Touch as standard, along with large 10.1-inch LCD instrument cluster and an 8-inch centre touchscreen. Options include a huge opening panoramic glass roof. As for safety, there is a mono-vision camera integrated into the rearview mirror to read lane markers on the road. It will be complemented by radar sensors for the adaptive cruise control and active Collision Warning with Brake Support. Also included are wide-angle radar sensors for help with parking and backing up. It also has inflatable second-row seatbelts and eight airbags.

The  new-for-2007 Nitro is somewhere between a compact and a midsize in terms of size, but is actually based on the Jeep Cherokee, but without low-range gearing. It is a useful wagon  with room for five passengers, innovative cargo features, and hit-and-miss styling. Typically American in its outlook, the Austrian-built Nitro comes across as a vehicle with attitude, though for this region, it is powered by either a 3.7-litre V6 mated to a 4-speed automatic for the base model or, new for 2008, a 4.0-litre V6 with a 5-speed for the R/T. The Nitro's unique fold-flat first-row passenger seat and usual fold-flat second-row seats offer a variety of loading options. Also new is the "Load N Go" cargo floor, which slides half-a-metre rearwards for easy loading and unloading, holding up to 181 kg when pulled out. With full power features, 16-inch steel wheels, keyless entry, a CD entertainment system, and a long list of standard safety and security features that include airbags, ABS brakes and more, the Dodge Nitro offers value for money in the confusing yet competitive compact-to-midsize 4WD segment.

The new-for-2010 Hyundai Tucson has been redesigned from the ground up, only slightly longer than the outgoing model, but 27 kg lighter than before. Now powered by a 2.0-litre 4-cylinder with front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive, and a 2.4-litre 4-cylinder with all-wheel-drive, both engines are mated to a 6-speed automatic. The base 2.0-litre FWD model comes with power windows, electric mirrors with indicators, keyless entry, cloth seats, fog lamps, manual a/c, rear spoiler, roof rails, CD/MP3 stereo with 6 speakers and USB/AUX inputs, 17-inch steel wheels, ABS and only a single driver-side airbag. Things get better in the higher trim levels, with the top 2.4-litre 4WD model additionally outfitted with dual-zone automatic a/c, panoramic glass roof, cruise control, smart key with starter button, leather upholstery, power driver-side seat, stereo with subwoofer and iPod cable, rear sensors and camera, chrome door handles, electric folding mirrors, 18-inch alloy wheels, and improved safety features such as ABS with stability control, active headrests and two front airbags, though still no side airbags.

European motorcycle-maker KTM, introduced their first ever car with the X-Bow. KTM basically transferred its principles from two wheels to four, with a track-biased car that can be driven on the street.
